# Decisions scratchpad — autonomous calls for Alex to review

Running log of judgment calls made while you were away. Newest at the bottom.
Format: **D# — decision** · rationale · revisit?

---

**D1 — Setup action budget (64) + deterministic auto-fix.** Random/untrained agents livelock in the setup phase (can't randomly satisfy "exactly 11, 3+ on LoS, ≤2 per wide zone" and pick DONE). Real BB has setup clocks; FUMBBL enforces them. After 64 placement actions, only `SETUP_DONE` is legal and the engine deterministically repairs the formation (no dice → replay-safe). Full setup expressiveness retained below the budget. *Revisit:* budget size; whether RL policies should see a penalty signal for hitting autofix.

**D2 — `BB_LEGAL_MAX` = 4096.** Setup enumerates ~3000 player×square placements. The RL action heads never materialize this list (factored heads); it's for replay validation/fuzzing/tests. 16KB stack per enumeration is fine.

**D3 — Starter skill set in Phase 2 core** (loner, dodge, block, tackle, guard, thick_skull, stunty, sure_feet, sure_hands, pass, catch, sprint) wired through `bb_skills.h` hooks; everything else lands Phase 3 through the same hooks. Wrestle/Frenzy/Mighty Blow/apothecary deliberately deferred (decision windows not yet modeled) — each marked `TODO(phase3)` in source.

**D4 — Kickoff events: 4 of 11 implemented** (Time-Out, Brilliant Coaching, Changing Weather, Pitch Invasion); the decision-heavy ones (Solid Defence, Quick Snap, High Kick, Charge, Cheering Fans→prayers, Get the Ref→bribes, Dodgy Snack) are rule-shaped no-ops marked `TODO(phase3)`. Phase 4 differential validation will quantify the gap.

**D5 — Pass mechanics v1 approximations** (flagged for the rulebook-test campaign to correct): Euclidean range bands; natural-1≈fumble folded into the inaccurate path; interception deferred. The rulebook tests being written right now will force exactness; FUMBBL replays are the final word.

**D6 — Golden traces: 8 matchups committed** (incl. Ogre vs Snotling for stunty/big-guy coverage). Regenerating goldens is an explicit `make goldens` — rules fixes are EXPECTED to break goldens; that's their job.

**D7 — Vast.ai**: key stored at `~/.vast_api_key`, verified live ($96.26 credit). Spend capped at your authorized $50. No GPU spend until the PufferLib binding smoke test (Phase 5).

**D8 — GitHub remote deferred.** Repo is local-only so far; creating a private GH repo is outward-facing and can wait for your morning review (CI workflow file is ready to go when pushed).

**D9 — Wrestle auto-applies on Both Down.** Rules make it optional ("may choose"); since declining is almost never right and the rulebook tests expect auto-application, the engine applies it when either player has it. Revisit if FUMBBL replays show declines.
**D10 — Single-candidate interceptions auto-attempt.** Attempting is cost-free (no failure penalty), so with one eligible interceptor there's no real decision; with several, the defending coach chooses. Matches the rulebook tests.
**D11 — Crowd-push dice order.** Crowd injury + throw-in resolve at relocation time, BEFORE the follow-up decision — FFB's order, and what the blocking tests encode. GAME/FOLLOW-UP's "decision before any other dice" reading is a known minor divergence to check against FUMBBL replays.
**D12 — Pitch Invasion victim selection** uses the raw PRNG (not the scripted dice stream) — FUMBBL records selections as separate commands, so replay alignment handles it at the harness level. Fan-factor modifiers TODO with the fans/inducements work.
**D13 — Secure the Ball failure = bounce + turnover** (consistent with the failed-pickup family). Rule text doesn't settle it; flagged for FFB differential adjudication.
**D14 — Test-vs-test conflicts resolved toward the mirror**: throw-in direction die is a D6 over the 3 template arrows (corners: D3); distance counts the boundary square as the first; no bounce on an empty landing square. Two agent tests written with d3/full-distance/bounce assumptions were corrected.
**D15 — BB2025 team re-rolls are UNLIMITED per turn** (the BB2020 once-per-turn cap is gone) and replenish at half-time; skill re-rolls (Dodge/Sure Feet/...) are once per TURN per player. Engine restructured accordingly.
**D16 — Mighty Blow auto-policy.** MB(+1) is rules-wise a choice of armour OR injury roll. Engine auto-applies: to the armour roll only when that converts a miss into a break, otherwise to the injury roll — the strictly dominant line in >99% of cases (exception: fishing for specific injury bands). Claws+MB on the same roll disallowed per rules; Claws' 8+ auto-break consumes the slot. Revisit if FUMBBL replays show deviating choices.
**D17 — Stand Firm always-on** (no decline window; declining is never beneficial absent edge interactions). Same for auto-attempting cost-free single-candidate interceptions (D10).
**D18 — Kick auto-applies** (halve deviation) when any on-pitch kicking-team player has Kick — kicker nomination (not adjacent to LoS/wide zone) is folded into the fans/nomination TODO. **Break Tackle** is always-on per-dodge (rules: once per activation) — flagged for the FUMBBL differential. **Secret Weapon** send-off uses on-pitch-at-drive-end as "took part" approximation.
**D19 — Interrupt auto-policies.** Tentacles: every eligible tentacled marker attempts (cost-free, compulsory-shaped); one attempt per step. Diving Tackle: auto-applied when the -2 flips a passing dodge (the only rational use), never with a ball-carrying diver; first eligible marker dives. Shadowing still pending (needs per-turn MA-use counter). These become real decision windows if the RL action space wants them; FUMBBL differential will adjudicate fidelity.
**D20 — Apothecary casualty pick auto-selects the better band** (strictly dominant given equal in-match effect); KO-patch remains a real decision (saving the apo matters). Casualty outcomes now recorded in spp_game for league mode.
**D21 — More auto-policies (Drop B):** Trickster auto-relocates only when it fully escapes the blocker (else stays); Dump-Off auto-throws to the least-marked quick-range teammate; Saboteur always triggers (cost: auto-KO — debatable, FUMBBL will adjudicate); SPOH places in the first empty adjacent square; Solid Defence/Quick Snap/Charge roll their D3 for dice-stream fidelity but reposition no one yet (decision windows TODO); Dodgy Snack's stat debuff persists for the match (drive-end restoration comes with procedural squads); Bloodlust thrall-bite + Animosity keyword targeting need keyword data (gate fires on declaration as approximation). Multiple Block + Pile Driver deferred (no default-roster carriers).
**D22 — Phase 5 design pivot per policy research** (docs/policy-research.md): compact ~640B entity-centric obs (NOT board planes — 20GB rollout buffer at bf16 otherwise); ACT_SIZES {type, arg, fused-391-square} each with a null index; stock Linear→MinGRU×3 policy (config-only, ~3.8M params); env-phase decision decomposition (the engine already provides it).
**D23 — Decode snap-to-legal has a low-x bias under pure-random heads.** When all 3 sampled heads form an illegal combo and no same-type match exists, decode falls back to `legal[0]`; engine enumeration order biases that toward low-x squares, which favors the away team (perf 0.38-0.40 at 99.8% illegal, two seeds). Irrelevant under the CUDA masked sampler (per-head legality keeps illegal_frac near 0 and passes 1-2 respect type+square), and vanishes as the policy sharpens. Documented, not fixed — randomizing the fallback would cost a per-step RNG draw for a transient artifact.
**D24 — Mac practice-run path (torch backend).** Three Mac-only walls, all worked around without touching upstream semantics: (1) `SIMD_FLAGS=(-mavx2 -mfma)` is a hard error on arm64 clang — guarded in the gitignored vendored build.sh; (2) torch bundles its own libomp, homebrew's in `_C.so` makes two OpenMP runtimes → segfault in `__kmp_suspend_initialize_thread`; `tools/mac_practice_build.sh` builds _C WITHOUT -fopenmp (pragmas degrade to single-thread; vecenv uses no omp_* API); (3) the selfplay pool raises RuntimeError on non-CUDA backends and pufferl exits cleanly-but-silently → practice runs need `--selfplay.enabled 0`. Verified: 147.5K steps / 12 PPO epochs end-to-end on M-series CPU at 14.7K SPS, stats flowing, exit 0.
**D25 — Setup discipline (amends D1).** Reserves-first placement: until 11 are placed (or reserves exhausted), re-placing/removing placed players is illegal — the spectator showed undertrained policies shuffling one player between two squares for the whole budget. Every final formation stays reachable (fill the line, then rearrange). Budget 64→24. Side effect: setup's legal-action enumeration shrank ~15x, doubling whole-match throughput (176K→353K steps/sec/core standalone). Deployed AFTER the A/B runs (mid-experiment engine changes confound); profiles from round 2 (gamma ladder) onward use it.
**D26 — Bootstrap curriculum: stage-1 works, cold anneal fails.** Profile D (fetch/carry potentials, 10B) escaped the 0-0 avoidance basin both pure arms died in (tds 0→0.06 mid-run). Stage-2 cold anneal (D2: same weights, potentials hard-off) decayed back to tds 0.000 by 5.4B — the scoring behavior was scaffold-supported, not value-internalized. D2 cut at 5.4B (info value of the tail ~nil). Conclusions: curriculum needs GRADUAL anneal (e.g. halve potentials per chained stage) and/or much longer stage-1; the BC arm is the priority path. Both 10B checkpoints retained for puffer match baselines.
**D27 — Cross-population tournament (4096 games/match): the avoidance equilibrium is universal, and PPO erodes priors into it.** All cross-matches ≈100% draws (BC/A/D/BC-init — nobody scores on anybody). The one directly informative result: BC-init BEATS BC-final (0.510 in decisive games) — 10B steps of selfplay PPO made the human-derived policy strictly worse at football. Confirms the tds-decay reading: with win/TD rewards unreachable at this defensive skill level, the gradient prunes scoring behavior as wasted entropy. Indicated fixes, in order: (1) BC-regularized PPO (KL/aux-CE anchor to the human policy during RL — the AlphaStar solution); (2) gradual potential anneal (halve per stage, never cold-off); (3) asymmetric curriculum (train offense vs frozen weaker defense). Also fixed tonight: our Log now exports slot_0/slot_1/draw_rate so puffer match works at all.
**D28 — Gradual anneal GRADUATES: the curriculum works.** Chain (each 10B, warm-started): 50% potentials → tds 0.185 (record, still climbing at cutoff); 25% → 0.035 (sustained, no surge); 0% → 0.045 and GROWING all run (0.009→0.045). Control: D2's cold-cut died (0.000 by 5.4B) from a weaker base. Conclusion: scaffold-taught scoring consolidates into the value function when removed gradually — the true reward's event density at handoff is the survival condition. Caveats: selfplay tds is confounded (tournament arbitrates); the whole lineage trained under the [-1,1] reward clamp (D27 addendum — outcome hierarchy was distorted but potentials were unaffected); deep-setup habit fossil noted by Alex on the spectator (eval-suite metric added).

**D33 — blocks 0.000 on the synthesis run is REAL behavior, not a broken counter — and the mechanism is quantified.** Suspicion: bc_acc 0.80 (teacher-forced, on human pairs full of blocks) with on-policy blocks 0.000 looked like instrument failure. Probe (puffer/bloodbowl/bbe_microstats_probe.c, masked-random policy, 200 eps): blocks 1.875/ep, blitzes 6.14/ep — the counter ticks fine under any non-degenerate policy; verified wired at c_step→bbe_count_action on every applied decision. So the synthesis policy has actively zeroed block declarations. WHY: the same probe shows random contact is net self-harm — kd_own 1.75 vs kd_inflicted 0.61 (~3:1 against). PPO descends that gradient immediately ("all blocks bad") and cannot climb to "selective 2dB-with-Block blocks are +EV" — a textbook shaping valley, exactly Alex's spectator observation. The BC anchor doesn't prevent it: block declarations are a thin slice of the pair distribution, so the policy keeps 0.80 aggregate accuracy while zeroing them on-policy (knowledge-behavior gap; anchor CE is state-averaged, not behavior-coverage-weighted). Implications: (1) Profile C decision-time exposure pricing (k_kd × P(knockdown) etc. — spec in docs/reward-audit-decision-time.md Addendum 3, 2dB(2.8%)-vs-3d(3.7%) inversion test) is now empirically motivated, not just theorized — ungated. (2) Candidate anchor upgrade: weight BC loss by decision type (or oversample DECLARE pairs) so block judgment transfers; pairs already carry the action type. (3) Eval-suite metric: blocks/ep on demo-started episodes is the cleanest "does it fight when it should" probe.

**D38 — THE UNMASKED-SAMPLER BUG: the torch backend never applied action masks; every BC-anchored run played via decode fallback (illegal_frac 1.000).** Found chasing synthesis+C's blocks 0.000 AND blitzes 0.000 at 200M (exact zeros — structure, not behavior). Mechanism: bc_pretrain (and the bc_acc aux loss) train/score MASK-RESTRICTED logits; the torch backend samples RAW logits (masks were CUDA-only); the BC policy never had to learn raw-logit legality, so on-policy it sampled ~100% illegal and bbe_decode's fallback (same-type → legal[0]) played a MOVE-biased shadow policy. Measured: bc_v3b lr~0 probe — unmasked: illegal 0.999, blocks 0.000, blitzes 0.000; MASKED: illegal 0.235 (residual = joint arg×sq misses across independent head masks), blocks 12.4/ep, blocks_thrown 13.6/ep, blitzes 2.8/ep — HUMAN-RANGE contact from the same weights. Fix (training/torch_pufferl_bcreg.patch + puffer_dict_capacity.patch regenerated): bindings expose vec action_mask (cpu+gpu); torch_pufferl applies per-head masked_fill(-inf) BEFORE rollout sampling, stores masks in experience, and re-applies at train-time recompute (mask-consistent ratios/entropy; all-zero head row guard). REINTERPRETATIONS: D33's knowledge-behavior gap = largely this artifact; D32/synthesis-v4 "anchor holds" results stand as experiments but measured fallback-shadow dynamics (their tds/pickups arose through legal[0]-snapping, with PPO slowly re-learning legality in raw logits); the avoidance-basin conclusions (D26-D28, CUDA, masked) unaffected; D34's Profile C result (CUDA, masked) unaffected. Fleet k-grid provisioning deferred to daylight (3 AM unattended multi-box provisioning = zombie risk); morning read compares halved-k's first ~2B against the full-k curve.
**D41 — Wave 2 launched (the 3-arm masked-world experiment).** Per the morning read (halved-k found a different contact equilibrium ~29/ep vs full-k's 40, still tds 0 — knob magnitude moves the brawl pole, not scoring): (1) box-2 repurposed to the TRUE anneal chain — stage 2 warm-started from the full-k 3.4B checkpoint at half-k, 3B cap, then quarter→zero (D28 doctrine applied to exposure); the fresh constant-half run's 1.3B is retained as the mid-pole reference. (2) bb-kzero (48c 4090): anchor-only masked control — the missing baseline for whether exposure pricing HURTS scoring. (3) bb-ballhawk (64c 4090): Alex's super-ballhawk arm — anchor + dist_ball 0.1/sq + dist_endzone 0.2/sq (5x D-profile potentials, telescoping/unfarmable), no k-knobs: the offense pole, untested in the masked world where the original D-escape predates both masks and anchor. Bootstrap via new tools/setup_arm.sh. Corpus crossed 11,595 replays overnight.
**D42 — Ballhawk v1 postmortem (the scrum standoff) + the scrum-literate v2 (Alex's insight).** v1 (fetch 0.1/carry 0.2, k=0) at 3.4B on the 766K-SPS box: pickup_attempts COLLAPSED to 0.36/ep (vs ~1.0 baseline), gfi 17/ep, dodges 16.7, knockdowns_own 8.8, pass 0.000, tds 0.000, episode_return +0.67 — diagnosis: both teams sprint to the loose ball (fetch potential is side-symmetric), form a TZ forest around it, and HOVER — in-traffic pickup EV is deeply negative (-1/TZ, turnover on failure) and the potential income stops at adjacency. Alex's reframe: the scrum is CORRECT Blood Bowl; humans resolve it by BLOCKING markers off the ball before scooping — and v1 was pacifist BY DESIGN (k=0), removing the exact tool that resolves its own equilibrium. Also: 17 gfi/ep under bc_coef 1.0 proves the potentials behaviorally out-shout a full-strength anchor. Premortem of v2 caught a second flaw before launch: ball_gain 0.3 vs loss -0.2 breaks the |loss|>gain anti-farming invariant (pickup-drop laundering, team-level possession pays re-scoops) → v2 ships 0.3/-0.4. BALLHAWK-V2 = scrum-literate: fetch 0.05, carry 0.2, gain 0.3/loss -0.4, k-knobs at HALF (blocking the scrum becomes +EV) — converging back toward synthesis+C with the ball channel amplified and farming-proofed. Expected failure mode (premortem, ~60%): the carry-phase wall — straight-line carrier rushes into a mirror defense that co-evolves; its cure is ASYMMETRIC training (offense vs frozen defense), torch-side freeze support to be built in parallel. Also: 766K SPS on the 64-core/3.4GHz box (7x box-2) — cores_effective x clock is the fleet filter henceforth.
**D43 — The possession annuity (Alex's reward-chain redesign) + the from-kickoff zero.** Probe result that forced it: kzero@1.7B, from-kickoff-only, masked — pickup_attempts 0.000 (the bc prior attempts 0.36-1.0; PPO trained the FREE kickoff scoop away), possession_rate 0.052 (≈ touchbacks), full games of blocking around an untouched ball. Mechanism: the critic prices the possession FUTURE — under mirror defense, pickup (+0.1 once) → targeted → stripped/sacked (loss -0.2, injury -0.15, turnover) nets negative every time; refusing the free ball is the rational policy under lump-sum+fine pricing. Alex's chain audit exposed the inversion: possession was priced as a coupon with an exit fine when it IS the game's income stream. NEW KNOB reward_possession: ending your own team turn holding pays +p/-p ZERO-SUM at the turn boundary (implementation: the possession_rate detector). Funds the whole chain with one knob: want-the-ball (stream entry), protect-the-carrier (protect income), defense bleeds until takeaway; ball_loss fine DELETED in annuity configs (loss = lost stream + opponent's gain — no double fine); 16 binary events/side/game = unfarmable; known trade: mildly rewards stalling (real Blood Bowl). POSSESSION-SPINE ARM live on ex-kzero box: possession 0.03, gain 0.05, loss 0, fetch 0.05/carry 0.2, k-half, anchor 1.0. The kzero-1.8B no-shaping result stands recorded: B-knob fines alone reproduce ball-avoidance.
**D44 — Asymmetric training shipped: the frozen-defense arm is live.** torch trainer grew frozen_enemy_path (training/torch_pufferl_bcreg.patch): non-learner rows play a frozen policy (deepcopy + state_dict, no grad, masked sampling, own LSTM state), learner alternates home/away by env parity, PPO slices to learner rows only (ratio/prio/batch math on train_rows). Deployed as PROFILE-POSS-ASYM on the 64-core box (647K SPS, learner 2048/4096 rows): the full possession-annuity config (D43) vs FROZEN bc_v3b defense — the first run where the learner's offense faces a defense that cannot co-evolve. Rationale chain: D39 (no win progress symmetric) → D43 (possession futures net-negative under mirror play) → premortem (carry-phase wall ~60%) → this. Sister arms: possession-symmetric (control for the asymmetry variable), anneal-s3, ballhawk2 retained at 10B as the scrum-literate reference. Spectator gained the color-coded event-feed sidebar (bbe_feed_hook, POD-only cross-thread per the memorial doctrine) — pickups/blocks/dodges/passes/TDs streaming live.
**D45 — Asym 10B verdict: behavioral divergence WITHOUT win conversion; the prior is the bottleneck.** poss-asym (annuity config vs FROZEN bc_v3b, 647K SPS, 10B in ~4.5h): EIGHT consecutive nonzero tds ticks (0.004-0.018 band) and pickup_success up to 0.14-0.22 while the symmetric twin held absolute zero tds with possession decaying — the asymmetry effect is real and directional. BUT the arbitration tournament (4096 games vs its own frozen opponent, both bias-drop-converted): 97.1% draws, decisive 48.5/51.5 — after 10B steps of practice against a defense that NEVER ADAPTS, the learner cannot beat it. Synthesis of the week's evidence (D35 capacity, D39/D43 possession poison, this): the binding constraint is THE PRIOR — a 0.40-exact iid imitation is a bad Blood Bowl player; the anchor (bc_acc pinned at its 0.396 ceiling throughout) holds the policy at that level; and PPO cannot discover multi-step drives from there even unopposed-by-adaptation. Levers, ranked: (1) anchor RELEASE — bc_coef_floor now configurable (was hard-coded 0.1); ASYM-RELEASE launched overnight from the asym-10B checkpoint with floor 0 (does the policy outgrow its teacher when allowed to leave the human manifold vs a static defense?); (2) sequence-context bc_v4 (the D35 lever — iid zero-state BC is the known ceiling); (3) bigger policy. Tournament caveat noted: CUDA bias-drop conversion applied to both sides equally.
**D46 — Discovery-vs-artifact doctrine (Alex, 2026-06-07): do not patch out inhuman behaviors by aesthetics.** RL's value is uncovering inhuman-but-optimal play (TD-Gammon's doubles, AlphaStar's worker saturation); "looks absurd" is not a valid filter. Discriminator before patching any weird behavior: (1) does it survive GROUNDING — persist when wins/TDs against a competent opponent are the binding currency, not shaped income? (2) is its profit causally routed THROUGH the objective or around it? (3) human rates are evidence, not law. Case study, GFI-spam (~17/ep vs human ~2-5): currently routed AROUND the objective (farms potential income while degrading drives; failed GFIs priced ~zero because under scoring scarcity the opponent can't convert turnovers) — so PRESUMED artifact, but the verdict belongs to the tournament, not taste. Consequences: reward_rush_cost is ANTI-DEGENERACY SCAFFOLDING (k-knob category, to be annealed away once the economy works), never a permanent value statement; deploy taxed-vs-untaxed as an A/B; if the untaxed twin keeps high GFI AND wins, absurd is correct and the tax dies.
**D46-addendum (Alex, 03:32): the real GFI price is positional, and that unifies the disease.** GFIs are individually high-success (5/6); IRL the binding cost is TZ-coverage preservation — a prone player projects no tackle zones, so you GFI only when the squares net something AND that player being down is acceptable. Standing presence is defensive currency (constrains opponent ball movement); under scoring scarcity defense has nothing to defend, so the agent CORRECTLY prices prone-ness at ~zero — GFI-spam is accurate pricing of a worthless asset, not ignorance. Unifies ball-avoidance, scrum-hovering, and GFI-spam as ONE disease: positional value is denominated in points and there are no points. Flat rush tax therefore doubly a crutch (true GFI price is context-dependent: last screener vs idle player); cure remains a working scoring economy. GFI gradient observed across arms: anneal 8.5 → possession 14 → asym-10B 29.7/ep — rushing scales with optimization depth in the broken economy, not with winning (artifact signature per the D46 discriminator).
**D46-addendum-2 (Alex, 03:33): standing presence is protection currency on BOTH sides of the ball** — TZs constrain opponent runners (defense) AND screen your own carrier from a straight rush (offense); a prone screener is an open lane to your ball. Corollary: the annuity arms already mint the OFFENSIVE half (standing screeners protect the +p/turn stream), the defensive half stays unpriced until opponent scoring exists. Testable prediction: GFI discipline should emerge FIRST on the carrying team (sober cage, reckless others) — watch the event ticker / per-team gfi splits.
**D47 — Anchor release verdict: NO breakout, NO collapse — the anchor was never the binding constraint.** asym-release2 (from asym-10B ckpt, frozen bc_v3b defense, bc_coef 0.5 -> 0.000 corrected cosine, capped ~6.03B continuation; stop-condition overshoot noted: runner global_step advances train-batch-width under asymmetry — patch with epoch-based stop or full-width accounting): bc_acc HELD ~0.39-0.42 throughout including ~1.3B steps at bc_coef<0.1 (no manifold drift — PPO updates too local to leave the basin), tds band unchanged (0.004-0.018), gfi ~30/ep unchanged. Tournament 4096 games vs frozen bc_v3b: 96.8% draws, decisive 48.4/51.6 — IDENTICAL to the anchored result (97.1%, 48.5/51.5). D45's anchor-over-binding hypothesis REFUTED: with the leash fully off, against a defense that cannot adapt, PPO still cannot find multi-step scoring play from this prior at this capacity. Remaining levers, now cleanly ranked: (1) BACKPLAY CURRICULUM — filter the demo bank for carrier-near-endzone states so the policy EXPERIENCES scoring densely, expand backward (the bank was literally built for this pattern; cheapest lever, untested); (2) bc_v4 sequence-context prior (D35); (3) bigger policy. The asym infrastructure + annuity economy remain the training architecture; they removed every confound that used to hide this conclusion.
**D48 — BACKPLAY WORKS: first sustained scoring growth in project history.** Stage 1 (demo 0.9, maxdist 6, frozen bc_v3b defense, annuity economy, from bc_v3b): tds 0.045 -> 0.094 -> 0.152 over 2.3B (three rising ticks; every prior run flat ≤0.018), score_diff nonzero and growing (decisive games exist in training at last), and gfi_attempts FALLING (28.8 -> 25.6) as touchdowns become real — the D46 grounding test starting to bite exactly as predicted (recklessness costs points now). Mechanism confirmed: the TD gradient never had mass; placing carriers ≤6 squares from the endzone (90% of starts) gives PPO dense scoring experience to amplify. Stage plan: hold stage 1 until tds plateaus, then maxdist 12, then uniform bank, then kickoff starts — watching for retention at each backward expansion (the Backplay literature's failure mode is forgetting the endgame as the start recedes). Possession-symmetric twin flickered its first nonzero (0.005 @ 8.9B, footnote).
**D49 — The backplay program: three-arm controlled experiment from one checkpoint.** Anneal chain closed (s1-s4, full->zero k, tds 0.000 throughout: exposure-anneal alone never scores) and possession-symmetric capped at 10.1B scoreless (the annuity alone, mirror play: rational ball-avoidance persisted) — both boxes reassigned. ALL THREE FLEET ARMS now branch from the SAME backplay-s1 checkpoint (5.24B, tds ~0.29 rising): bp_s1 flagship (ballhawk box, maxdist 6, untaxed — how far does stage 1 climb), bp_s2 preview (possession box, maxdist 12 — does skill survive backward expansion, parallel instead of serial staging), bp_tax twin (box-2, maxdist 6 + rush_cost 0.015 — the D46 A/B: does pricing GFIs help or does the grounding effect alone suffice). Tier-distribution exports (2d:2d-red) live on all three after fixing a stale binding.c on the flagship box (header synced, binding didn't — partial-sync footgun; counters existed but were never exported). Sweep tracks tds/gfi/2d/2dred per arm.
**D50 — Mid-curriculum tournament calibration: training-tds does not equal winning until starts reach kickoff.** backplay-s1 @ ~7B (training tds ~0.29 from maxdist-6 starts) vs frozen bc_v3b, 4096 full games from kickoff: 96.4% draws, 48.2/51.8 — statistically the predecessors' result (whisper: decisive 119->147, draws 97.1->96.4, not claimable). Mechanism, plainly: the policy converts near-endzone STARTS; full games never reach near-endzone positions because early/mid-game play is unchanged — the endgame skill exists but is unreachable from kickoff. This is the expected mid-curriculum state, not refutation: the backward expansion (s2 maxdist 12 -> uniform -> kickoff) is precisely the machinery meant to connect the opening whistle to the learned endgame. RULE: grounded win-rate arbitration is the graduation exam for the FINAL curriculum stage; per-stage progress is measured by tds-at-stage-starts + retention probes of earlier stages.
**D51 — Curriculum step-size finding: 6->12 overshot, stepping to 9; tax twin OUTSCORING untaxed.** bp_s2 (maxdist 12 from the s1 ckpt): tds flat 0.03-0.07 through 2.1B, no slope (flagship at same depth: 0.15 rising) — 12-square starts demand open-field traversal the policy lacks; known scoring states too rarely reached to bootstrap. Backward expansion needs SMALL steps: relaunched as s2b maxdist 9, same shared checkpoint. Meanwhile bp_tax @1.2B hit tds 0.285-0.349 with gfi ~25-26 — matching/exceeding the flagship's per-step pace WITH fewer rushes: early D46 A/B read says the rush tax costs nothing and may help (cleaner positional play -> better conversion). Flagship grinding 0.30-0.37 @12.7B, slope shallow but alive.
**D52 — Stage 1 closed at tds 0.380 (8x pre-backplay best); s2-DEEP launched (stage-depth experiment).** bp_s1 capped at 15.0B (asymmetric stop overshoot — known): tds ground 0.29 -> 0.380 over the resumed leg, gfi easing 28 -> 27. The 64c box now runs S2-DEEP: maxdist 9 from the STRONG 15B checkpoint, racing s2b (maxdist 9 from the EARLY 5.24B checkpoint, currently ~0.13 @ 0.64B) — two stage-2 entries differing only in stage-1 depth, measuring whether longer stage-1 grinding transfers downstream or is wasted compute (curriculum-design question with direct cost implications for stages 3+). Tax twin at 1.6B: tds 0.303-0.311, gfi down to 23.0 — still matching the untaxed lineage's pace with ~4 fewer rushes/ep; D46 A/B continues to lean pro-tax.
**D53 — bc_v4: val exact 0.508 (bc_v3b: 0.371, +37% relative) — the obs-v4 information-parity prediction CONFIRMED.** 60K cosine steps, 2,085,330 v4 pairs from 12,304 replays (corpus doubled since bc_v3), by-replay split (1.67M/413K). Heads: type 0.949 / arg 0.840 / sq 0.668. **D54 — FIRST SIGHTED ARM LIVE: profile-v4-backplay.** s2-deep capped at 15.0B (stage-2-deep band ~0.20-0.22 — converged faster than s2b but to a similar level so far; the depth question stays open in the v3 lineage while v4 supersedes). The flagship box now runs the full v4 stack: obs-v4 probability planes + bc_v4 anchor (val 0.508) + bc_v4 FROZEN enemy + 2.09M-pair BC aux corpus (pairs symlink -> pairs_v4) + backplay stage 1 (demo 0.9, maxdist 6) + annuity economy + k-half. Final checkpoint 0000014942470144.bin on the stopped disk. FLEET FULLY HIBERNATED 06:10 after the balance ladder executed flawlessly: box-2 @$5 -> possession @$3.50 -> box-1 @$2 -> ballhawk stopped manually post-cap with ~$0.55 left — zero data loss, the highest-value run protected to the last dollar, exactly the priority order designed at 01:05. **D56 — Sighted stage-1 tournament: 98.8% draws (49.5/50.5) — the D50 rule holds; curriculum position, not prior quality, gates the kickoff exam.** v4_s1_final (15B, tds 0.42-0.49 from maxdist-6 starts) vs bc_v4, 4096 games from kickoff: no conversion — endgame skill remains unreachable from the opening; early-game play is still prior-shaped. Draws actually ROSE vs the v3-era exams (96.8 -> 98.8): a stronger prior on both mirror sides means fewer accident-decided games — the bar rises with the player. Confirms running the exam mid-curriculum is a calibration, not a verdict; graduation remains stage-by-stage backward expansion (s2 maxdist 9 live on two boxes, taxed + untaxed). The +1 lever if stages stall: frozen-opponent LADDER (weaker defense first) to manufacture decisive games earlier.
**D57 — THE 4x LEVER FIRES: native anchor-free asymmetric training at 2.1M SPS.** profile-v4-native-asym on box-1 (24c judge box!): native CUDA backend, NO bc aux (D47 license), frozen bc_v4 pinned as the selfplay-pool teacher (1-seed league_preseed pool, swap_winrate 1.1 = unreachable, opp_timeout 100B = never; frozen_bank_pct 0.48 — the apb/2 cap means ~48% of envs are vs-teacher, the rest mirror: an accidental but reasonable hybrid), learner warm from v4_s1_final_cuda, same annuity+backplay-s2 env knobs. SPS 2.1M vs torch twins' 0.6-0.77M — 3x on the WEAKEST box; the 64c boxes should exceed it. Early tds 0.229@0.5B sits in the stage-2 band = anchor-free learning parity plausible; the real test is the curve vs the torch flagship at matched steps over the next hours. If parity holds, the program's step budget just tripled at constant cost and the torch backend retires to bc_vN training only.
**D58 — THE 4x LEVER SHIPS: native anchor-free architecture verified at parity, 3.42x throughput.** parity_report.py (tools/, new) on the live A/B at matched steps to 5B: SPS 2.10M (native) vs 0.61M (torch) = 3.42x ON THE WEAKEST BOX (24c); tds PARITY (native 0.318 vs torch 0.355 at 5B, -10.4% within band, native slope STEEPER 0.080 vs 0.049/B — anchor-free learning holds, confirming D47's release-is-safe license at production scale); wall-clock-to-0.45-tds native ~13min vs torch ~23min (native needs more STEPS but far less TIME). Anchor-free training is correct AND ~3.4x cheaper per unit progress. SHIPPED: tools/run_native_asym.sh (TEACHER/WARM/STEPS contract, pinning knobs hardcoded + snapshot_interval 1e12 to suppress the ~600MB/hr pool pollution the audit caught, off-box refusal, LIVE check), tools/parity_report.py (the verdict harness), fleet-ops skill "Native anchor-free architecture" section (native=all RL stages, torch=bc_vN+aux-research ONLY; one backend per box — --float and native artifacts are mutually exclusive). 9-agent ultracode audit verdicts SOUND/ISSUES/SOUND; teacher provably immutable (every selfplay rotation trigger unsatisfiable at swap_winrate 1.1 / opp_timeout 1e11). OPEN/CONFOUNDED: block_2dred_frac native 0.116 vs torch 0.171 (-32%) — both warm-started from v4_s1_final ~0.20, so native TRAINS THE RED-DICE HABIT AWAY where torch holds it; HYPOTHESIS (the bc anchor pulls block selection back toward the noisy human prior; without it PPO+planes rationalize faster) is confounded with the opponent mechanism (pool vs frozen-enemy-path) — isolate before claiming (torch-no-anchor or native-small-aux arm). Box-1's installed build predates the SPS pass (55b43f3): live run is correct but pre-optimization; a future native rebuild picks up both — documented, do NOT rebuild mid-run.
**D59 — Hyperthreading/thread-pool answer: we were NOT using the cores optimally on quota-limited boxes; fixed +4.4x.** Alex's question, investigated empirically: the possession-tax box read 114K SPS vs the IDENTICAL-config flagship's 592K. Root cause (measured, not theorized): `nproc` reports VISIBLE logical CPUs, but vast.ai containers cap CPU TIME via cgroup CFS quota. possession box: nproc=255 (128 physical x2 HT) but cfs_quota_us 6120000/100000 = 61 CPUs allowed. With OMP_NUM_THREADS unset, PyTorch + OpenBLAS auto-size their intra-op pools to nproc=255, so the trainer ran 641 threads thrashing on 61 CPUs of real time. ballhawk: nproc=64 ~ quota 61, only 162 threads, mild 2.7x oversub, fine. FIX: cap OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL/NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS to the detected cgroup quota (v1 cpu.cfs_quota_us AND v2 cpu.max, clamped <= nproc) at launch — baked into tools/run_synthesis_c.sh + tools/run_native_asym.sh. The env-stepping OMP is INDEPENDENT (vec num_threads=20, explicit pragma) — this only tames the math-library pools. MEASURED on tax twin relaunch: 641->186 threads, 114K->~500K SPS (4.4x), now matching the flagship. The env step's own HT usage (loadavg 64 on 64 threads) is fine; physical-only vs HT for env stepping is the remaining Tier-4 A/B (lower priority). Flagship left undisturbed mid-A/B (it picks up the cap at stage-3 relaunch). NOTE: native backend (box-1) was already optimal (nproc=24=quota, GPU-bound).
**D60 — The native arm's low 2d-red is REAL and PERSISTENT but stays CONFOUNDED — do not promote to "anchor suppresses rationality."** block_2dred_frac on profile-v4-native-asym held 0.106-0.109 across the whole run to 9.4B (5+ consecutive stable ticks), vs torch v4 arms 0.17-0.20 — both lineages warm-started from v4_s1_final (~0.20), so the native config actively TRAINS THE RED-DICE HABIT DOWN where torch holds it. Tempting headline ("the bc anchor was pulling block selection back toward the noisy human prior"), but the native arm differs from torch in TWO ways simultaneously: (a) NO bc aux loss, (b) opponent = selfplay pool vs torch's frozen-enemy-path. Per D46 discipline this is NOT a clean finding. ISOLATION EXPERIMENT to settle it (queued, not urgent): a torch arm with bc_coef 0 (anchor off, same frozen-enemy-path) — if ITS 2dred also falls to ~0.11, the anchor is the cause; if it stays ~0.18, the opponent mechanism is. Until then: persistent phenomenon, cause unattributed. (Other scheduled-check reconciliation: SPS diagnosis -> D59 fix, tds parity -> D58, v3_tax left as legacy straggler/box-2 repurpose candidate, native caps ~15:30, balance $91.50.)
**D61 — Human baseline MEASURED (12,722 games, 453,617 team-turns) — corrects guessed priors, especially GFI.** Per-game / per-team-turn rates from the FUMBBL corpus: blockRoll 88.8/game (2.49/turn — Blood Bowl is constant violence, high contact is NORMAL not pathological), dodgeRoll 25.7/game (0.72/turn), **goForItRoll 17.4/game (0.49/turn)**, pickUpRoll 7.3/game (0.21/turn), passRoll 2.0/game, foul 2.9/game, pickup_success 0.670, block tiers 77.5% 2d / 1.7% 2dred / 8.5% 3d / 12.4% 1d. KEY CORRECTION: the D46/D52 "gfi artifact" narrative assumed humans GFI ~2-5/game; the TRUE figure is ~17/game (once per ~2 team-turns). Our agents' GFI rate is therefore much closer to human than the artifact framing claimed — the rush tax may be solving a smaller problem than thought, and per-team-turn (not per-curriculum-episode) is the only valid agent-vs-human GFI comparison. DELIVERED: tools/game_stats.py (agent dashboard vs docs/human-baseline.json, marks toward-human / PAST-human / context per metric — human is a plausibly-optimal REFERENCE, not a ceiling; superhuman SHOULD diverge on context axes) + tools/eval_game_stats.sh (full-game-from-kickoff frozen measurement, the ONLY human-comparable mode; training dashboards use curriculum starts and are NOT comparable). Methodology note: human is plausibly-optimal, not optimal — a superhuman policy may legitimately throw fewer/better blocks, hold the ball more, GFI less.
**D62 — Native stage-2 capped at 30B; stage-3 (maxdist 12) launched. Native arch verdict reaffirmed.** profile-v4-native-asym final (30B, anchor-free, frozen bc_v4 teacher, 2.0-2.1M SPS throughout): tds 0.432, block_2dred_frac 0.111 (HALF the torch arms' ~0.17-0.19 — the cleanest block-rationality of any arm, still confounded per D60 but persistent to 30B), possession_rate 0.195 (best recorded, ties the torch flagship), pickup_success 0.275, gfi 22.6. **D66 — D60 confound RESOLVED: the 2dred gap is TWO-FACTOR, opponent/backend mechanism the larger share (~60%), bc anchor the smaller (~40%).** Isolation arm v4-d60-bccoef0 (taiwan, torch --float obs-v4, frozen-enemy bc_v4.bin, bc-coef 0 = single variable vs torch_s3's 1.0, maxdist 12, warm from v4_s2tax 15B): at 10.9B block_2dred_frac settled at mean 0.145 (last-30 band 0.124-0.154). Reference points: torch-with-anchor arms ~0.16-0.18, native anchor-free ~0.108-0.111. Removing ONLY the anchor moved 2dred from ~0.17 to ~0.145 — about 40% of the native-torch gap; the remaining ~60% comes from the opponent/backend mechanism (selfplay-pool teacher mix vs head-on frozen-enemy, plus any bf16-vs-fp32 effect — these two remain bundled; a further isolation would be a native arm with head-on frozen enemy, LOW priority). Neither early hypothesis was right alone: "the anchor pulls block selection toward the noisy human prior" is TRUE but explains a minority; who-you-practice-against shapes block-dice taste MORE than the imitation pull does. Arm stopped at verdict (served its purpose); taiwan box stopped to conserve (nothing unique on it: big bank now on Mac+possession+japan, bc_v4 anchors on japan+ballhawk). SPS: native fp32 (no --slowly) ~190K vs torch --slowly ~115K — native wins here too, USE IT. Per-core ~12K vs vast native's ~91K/core (WSL + consumer-CPU overhead; the plan's 1-2M guess was optimistic by ~10x). **D89 — possession_rate is CONFOUNDED — do NOT read agent 0.184 vs human 0.47 as a ball-security weakness (Alex correction, 2026-06-10 D46 catch).** Measured human possession_rate = 0.47 (turn-ends holding the ball, 300-game sample; tools/human_possession.py, full-corpus running). Initial (WRONG) read: "agent holds ball <half as often = possession is the next frontier." Alex's correction, which is right: a TOUCHDOWN ends the drive with the scorer NOT holding (ball resets to kickoff), so possession_rate is MECHANICALLY suppressed by scoring efficiency — efficient scorers show LOW possession by construction. Compounded by the OPPONENT confound: agent games (self-vs-self in eval; agent weak on defense) have no real defensive resistance, so drives are SHORT (score-reset-repeat) → few mid-drive holding turn-ends; human-vs-human games have both sides defending, so possession is CONTESTED across many turns before converting/turning over → many holding turn-ends. So human 0.47 vs agent 0.184 reflects drive LENGTH (= defense quality + scoring speed), not ball security. DOCTRINE: possession_rate is only comparable between policies measured against the SAME opponent at the SAME scoring rate; the human figure is from human-vs-human and is NOT a clean agent target. The real ball-security question needs agent-vs-STRONG-opponent (v5 flagship as its own teacher) where drives are contested — at which point possession_rate becomes informative. Leaving possession OUT of the human-comparable target set in game_stats.py (mark context, not higher/lower).
**D90 — THE CONTESTED ERA BEGINS (Alex root-cause + directive, 2026-06-11: "No one is contesting the ball. No one is fighting to stop the opponent from scoring."). Diagnosis: every observed pathology — no defense, uncontested loose balls, aimless defensive movement, suspect record-ladder — traces to the DEAD OPPONENT POOL: since D57 all arms trained vs the frozen bc_v4 teacher (51% clone), which the learner outgrew long ago; defense and ball-denial have had ZERO gradient because the opponent never threatened anything. Four actions fired:**
1. **Possession metric fixed (env + human tool, same definition):** a turn ending in your own TD counts as ending WITH possession (you carried it in). Annuity unchanged (still requires HELD; reward_td pays the score). Pre-D90 possession_rate numbers are NOT comparable to post-D90. Human baseline re-measuring under the new definition (old-definition human = 0.476 over 14,285 games / 1.07M turns).
2. **v5-contested LAUNCHED (ballhawk):** TEACHER = the v5-kickoff 1.625 flagship cap ITSELF (first non-bc_v4 opponent ever), WARM from same, macro on, kickoff-pure, 30B. v5-kickoff2 (gen-3 vs the dead teacher) killed — low marginal value. PRE-REGISTERED: training tds CRASHES initially (real defense exists for the first time); pickup_attempts rise (loose balls contested); defensive behaviors (marking, screening, ball-denial) become visible on BBTV within a generation; from-kickoff eval may dip while defense develops — head-to-head is the honest score.
3. **Head-to-head tournament = the new scoreboard:** training-tds records vs a static teacher are NOT cross-lineage comparable (partly exploitation of a fixed target). v5-kickoff cap vs v4 kickoff-8 cap, 2048 games x TWO env configs (macro on = v5 semantics / macro off = v4 semantics) because the action-space asymmetry handicaps one side per config — bracket the truth. Running on the 2070 (v5-balloon killed — replicate purpose served; rig_relaunch.sh disabled pending new role).
4. **League unpinning = the structural end-state (design):** after v5-contested proves the shape, switch to the existing-but-pinned league machinery (training/selfplay_league.patch, run_league.sh): seeded bank {bc_v4, v4-kickoff8 cap, v5-kickoff cap, + run snapshots}, swap_winrate 0.55 (the ini's intended default), snapshot_interval live — opponent grows with the learner permanently; no more static-target overfitting. The frozen-teacher era (D57→D90) ends deliberately. Non-move (doctrine): NO defensive reward shaping — D67-D69 proved distributions teach and bribes distort; defense needed an opponent, not a bounty.

**D97-A — CODEX REVIEW of the H1/H2/H3 pivot (.codex-reviews/growth-plan.md): catches a NUMERIC ERROR in D97 and rewrites the gen-4 decision rule before it fires. The error: D97 read tournament `A=0.550 draw=0.419` as "55% decisive," but `puffer match`'s A/B fields already split draws 50/50 into each side's rate — the correct decisive-rate formula (the one bt_fit.py implements) is `(A - 0.5*draw)/(1-draw)`. Recomputed: D97 (gen3-vs-gen2) = 58.6% decisive, not 55%. D95 (gen2-vs-gen1, A=0.631 draw=0.337) = 69.8% (matches the "70%" claim — that one was read correctly). D96 (dead heat, A=0.505 draw=0.418) = 50.9% (also correct). REVISED slope: 69.8% -> 58.6%, an 11.2pt drop — still meaningful deceleration, but 58.6% is NOT "near the 50% plateau" as D97 implied; the "near-plateau" framing was an overcall. REVISED gen-4 decision rule (replaces D97's 50%/60% thresholds), defined on decisive-rate-after-draw-conversion (printed-A equivalents at draw~0.42: 50%dec~=0.500A, 53%dec~=0.514A, 60%dec~=0.558A): <=53% decisive AND H1 ladder shows gen4 not clearly above gen3/league2 -> retire clean ratchet, both boxes to H2/H3. >=60% decisive with CI clear of 55% -> keep one ratchet slot (gen-5). 53-60% decisive (a range that NOW INCLUDES gen3's own 58.6%) -> "slowing but alive," do not retire on this tournament alone; corroborate via H1 ladder + league2-vs-gen3 before deciding. STRUCTURAL fixes adopted: (1) H2 pool capped at <=8 frozen banks (selfplay.py hard RuntimeError above 8; frozen_bank_pct must drop to ~0.06 for 8 banks vs 0.08 for 5 to stay under the apb/2 cap) — curated composition (one weak anchor, one kickoff-era specialist, one v5/macro artifact, one older ratchet, one latest ratchet, one league cap, one skill-exposure cap if league-2 passes, one H3-exploiter slot), NOT literal "every cap ever made." (2) H3 gets staged 5B/10B/15B go/no-go reads (not a single 15B verdict), warm-start preference league2 > league1 > v5-contested (favor a real contender over stylistic-purity-only). (3) bt_fit.py being enhanced (bg, .codex-impl/btfit-enhance-run-*.md) with Wilson 95% CIs, a score-based (non-draw-stripped) Elo table alongside decisive-only, and a full pairwise residual table to catch non-transitivity before crowning a single H1 champion — use a TOP CLUSTER for warm-start selection unless the gap is clearly outside noise. **D98 — H1 ANCHORED LADDER RESULTS + a major methodological finding: single 2048-game tournaments can swing ~95 Elo between identical re-runs, larger than the entire top-cluster spread. Round-robin of 7 lineage caps (bc_v4, kickoff8, v5contested, gen1-3, league1; 21 pairings, 2048 games each, stepwise/macro=0; ~1200-1600 decisive games/pairing) fit via tools/bt_fit.py (anchor=bc_v4=0 Elo, scale 400):

DECISIVE-Elo ranking: gen2 4930.0 > gen3 4883.7 ~= league1 4882.7 (1.0 apart) > gen1 4803.0 (-80 from cluster) > kickoff8 4685.8 (-117) > v5contested 4435.8 (-250) > bc_v4 0.0 (effectively dead: raw_strength 1e-12, loses 100% of decisive games to ALL SIX other anchors, including v5contested).
SCORE-BASED (draws=0.5) ranking AGREES on ordering except gen3/league1 swap (league1 282.2 > gen3 274.4, 7.8 Elo apart) -- the two metrics corroborate each other everywhere except inside the noise-dominated top cluster.

TOP CLUSTER {gen2, gen3, league1} spans only 47.3 Elo and is statistically INDISTINGUISHABLE at this sample size -- the two largest residuals in the full pairwise table are gen2-vs-league1 (fit 0.568 vs empirical 0.508, |err| 0.059) and gen3-vs-league1 (fit 0.501 vs empirical 0.554, |err| 0.053), i.e. the noisiest pairings are exactly the ones INSIDE this cluster.

THE HEADLINE FINDING: this ladder's gen2-vs-gen3 pairing (A=gen2 0.530, draw=0.404 -> gen2 decisive 55.0%, 95% CI [52.3%,57.8%]) DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS D97's gen3-vs-gen2 tournament from ~1 hour earlier on the SAME checkpoints, SAME config (A=gen3 0.550, draw=0.419 -> gen3 decisive 58.6%). Converting both to Elo: D97 said gen3 +60.3 over gen2; this ladder says gen2 +34.9 over gen3 -- a ~95 Elo swing on nominally the same measurement, and D97's 58.6% falls FAR outside this ladder's [52.3%,57.8%] CI for the reverse direction. 95 Elo exceeds the ENTIRE top-cluster's 47.3 Elo span. CONCLUSION: a single 2048-game `puffer match` has MUCH larger true variance than the naive per-pairing Wilson CI suggests (the CI assumes i.i.d. Bernoulli over ~1200 "decisive games" but the effective independent sample size is evidently far smaller -- likely correlated outcomes within a run, e.g. shared procgen/seed structure across the env batch). NO SINGLE TOURNAMENT, including the queued gen4-vs-gen3 and league2-vs-gen3, can be decision-grade alone for anything inside a ~100-Elo band.

PROTOCOL AMENDMENT (supersedes D97-A's single-tournament gray-zone language): when gen-4 and league-2 cap, do NOT rely on one gen4-vs-gen3 / league2-vs-gen3 pairing for the retire/keep call. Instead EXTEND THE LADDER -- add each new cap via EXTRA_ANCHORS and run it against all existing anchors (7-8 new pairings each, reuse --resume). A cap's fitted Elo from ~8000+ decisive games across 7-8 opponents averages out single-pairing noise far better than one pairing's ~1200 games. Decision becomes: does the new cap's fitted Elo clearly exceed the {gen2,gen3,league1} cluster (by visibly more than the cluster's own ~50 Elo internal spread, with the full-ladder CIs as support), land WITHIN the cluster (= "still in the pack," itself meaningful for the retire/keep call per D97-A's spirit), or fall below it? Single pairwise tournaments remain useful as quick informal reads but are demoted to non-decisive.

OTHER FINDINGS: bc_v4 is now a "free win" for everything (confirms H4/bc_v5-refresh motivation -- it's a fine pool FLOOR but contributes zero gradient as a "contender"). v5-contested confirms its D93 retirement (clearly weakest non-dead anchor). gen1 sits clearly (~80-127 Elo) below the {gen2,gen3,league1} cluster -- the contested-era ratchet DID produce a real, ladder-visible jump from gen1 to {gen2,gen3}, even though gen2-vs-gen3's internal order is noise. Raw output: /tmp/anchored_ladder.csv + bt_fit.py on the 2070.**

**D107-A — CLAUDE ADVERSARIAL REVIEW of D107 (codex's first attempt produced 1600+ lines of file-exploration with no synthesized verdict -- retrying with a tighter prompt as secondary opinion, .codex-reviews/d107-gen2-dominance-v2.md). Re-examining the raw Elo gaps with noise in mind:

(1) GEN2-VS-GEN3 GAP IS NOISE (6.1 Elo: 100.3 vs 94.2) -- the D107 framing "gen2 is uniquely #1" OVERSTATES this. gen2 and gen3 form a TOP TIER, indistinguishable from each other. The REAL signal is the gap from this top tier DOWN to league1 (78.8, -15 to -21.5 Elo) and further to gen4/league4/exploiter1 (57-63, -31 to -37 Elo from top tier) -- these gaps are larger than a typical multi-pairing BT standard error (~12 pairings x ~1000-2000 games/node = ~12-15K decisive games informing each node's Elo) and likely reflect SOME real signal, though D98's single-pairing ~95-Elo variance means individual large gaps still warrant caution. REVISED leaderboard structure: TIER1 {gen2, gen3} ~94-100 > TIER2 {league1} ~79 > TIER3 {gen4, league4, exploiter1} ~57-63 > TIER4 {league2, exploiter3} ~21-46 > gen1 (0, baseline) > TIER5 {exploiter2, kickoff8, v5contested, bc_v4} all negative. This RECOVERS D98's original "{gen2,gen3,league1} cluster" finding -- the cluster has partially resolved (league1 separated downward) but TIER1 (gen2/gen3) staying flat across a full additional ratchet generation (gen2->gen3, the SAME 30B-vs-frozen-self recipe that produced gen3 from gen2) is consistent with D97/D97-A's "slope flattening" finding, now corroborated at the absolute-ladder level: the FIRST ratchet jump (gen1->gen2/gen3, +94-100 Elo from baseline) was real and large; nothing since has added to it.

(2) NON-TRANSITIVITY IS REAL, NOT NOISE. league4-vs-gen2: empirical gen2-win=47.1% vs BT-fit-predicted 55.7% (8.6pp gap on n=1133, ~3 SDs). exploiter2-vs-league4: empirical exploiter2-win=55.2% vs fit-predicted 36.8% (18.4pp gap on n=909, ~5.6 SDs) -- this one is STRONGLY non-transitive, not explainable by sampling noise. RIGHT FRAMING: BT/Elo is a useful AVERAGE-RANKING diagnostic (and the ladder tooling stays valuable for spotting tier structure and flagging non-transitive pairs), but "is training progress happening" should ALSO be read against the ABSOLUTE human-baseline eval suite (tools/eval_game_stats.sh from-kickoff vs docs/human-baseline.json, D61) -- a scale the BT ladder doesn't capture and that ISN'T relative to a possibly-drifting opponent pool.

(3) THE PATTERN IS REAL AND HAS A MECHANISM: warm-starting from a checkpoint and continuing self-play (ratchet-vs-frozen-self OR league-pool) tends to PLATEAU-OR-REGRESS on the cross-anchor ladder even when IN-RUN internal trackers (tds, possession, per-run hist_score/elo) look flat-to-improving. Ratchet: gen2->gen3 flat (94.2 vs 100.3, noise-band), gen3->gen4 REAL decline (-31.3 Elo). League: league1(78.8)->league2(45.9) sharp decline ->league4(60.7) partial recovery, still -18 below league1. MECHANISM (distributional drift / self-play overfitting): each arm's opponent population (frozen self, or a pool seeded mostly from the SAME lineage's recent generations) is a NARROW slice of the full strategy space. The learner specializes against THAT slice -- in-run trackers (which measure performance against exactly that slice) improve or look fine -- while drifting away from effectiveness against the WIDER population the ladder samples (gen1, kickoff8, v5contested, and now also each OTHER lineage's checkpoints). D96's "league Elo never plateaued (84.9->224.3)" was this exact illusion: a per-run internal tracker measuring fit-to-its-own-training-population, NOT cross-population strength -- D102-B's note that this tracker "resets on relaunch, not persistent" actually UNDERSTATED the problem; it isn't just non-persistent, it was NEVER a strength measure in the first place.

(4) LEAGUE-5 DECISION: DO NOT ABANDON (it is ~10min in, cheap to let ride) -- AND its design is ALREADY PARTIALLY RESPONSIVE to this finding: league-5's 8-bank pool (D106-A) includes BOTH gen2 AND gen3 (the TIER1 checkpoints) alongside gen4/league2/exploiter1/etc. If gen2/gen3 are genuinely strong pool opponents, league-5's learner now trains under pressure FROM the strongest known checkpoints -- a direct (if late) fix to the narrow-pool mechanism in (3). ACTION: at league-5's next ladder-worthy checkpoint, the critical NEW measurements are league5-vs-gen2 and league5-vs-gen3 specifically (does training WITH tier1 opponents in the pool let the learner approach/exceed tier1?). Separately, queue a CHEAP DIAGNOSTIC for ballhawk after exploiter-4: a short (10-15B) "gen2-continuation" arm (warm=gen2, teacher=gen2, the EXACT ratchet recipe that produced gen3) -- if a SECOND independent gen2->gen3-equivalent run ALSO lands flat/below gen2, that's strong evidence the gen2->gen3 transition is at a genuine local-optimum/plateau for this recipe, not a one-off; if it instead EXCEEDS gen2 this time, gen3's specific underperformance may have been a bad-draw artifact.

(5) DOCTRINE INCONSISTENCY FLAGGED: D102-B framed "more total training from a strong checkpoint (relaunching league3 for another 30B after the disk-crash) is a net positive from the crash" -- D107 suggests this assumption needs revisiting: MORE continued self-play from an already-decent checkpoint is NOT unconditionally good and can regress ladder-measured strength. This doesn't make D102-B's RECOVERY ACTION wrong (the alternative was losing the run entirely) but the "net positive" framing should be read as "recovered the run" not "more training = more strength."

PRACTICAL UPSHOT for the next several cycles: (a) keep league-5 + exploiter-4 running (both already informative, both cheap relative to total runway); (b) the LADDER, not internal trackers, is the persistent scoreboard -- re-extend it at every new cap, anchor=gen1 (non-degenerate); (c) the стандарт "warm-start from the most recent cap" heuristic is now SUSPECT -- future warm-start choices should be the LADDER-TOP checkpoint among recent caps, which as of D107 would be gen2 or gen3 (not league4/league3) -- this may mean some future arm warm-starts from gen2/gen3 directly rather than continuing the league/exploiter chains, once league-5/exploiter-4 report back.**

**D111 — DOCTRINE: "HARD OPPONENTS" POOL-COMPOSITION PROTOCOL (codifying D109's lesson as a standing rule, not a one-off). The root cause of league1-4's non-monotonic drift was that NO league pool ever included the genuinely-strongest checkpoints as training opponents -- each generation trained against weaker/drifted descendants of itself. League5 (first pool to include gen2+gen3, the ladder-top at the time) produced the largest jump in program history (+116.8 Elo). GOING FORWARD, every new league/pool build follows this protocol:

POOL COMPOSITION (8 banks, the selfplay.py hard cap, frozen_bank_pct ~0.06):
- 2-3 TIER1 slots: the current ladder-top checkpoint(s) by fitted Elo (anchor=gen1, the stable non-degenerate anchor) -- the "hard opponents."
- 2-3 TIER2 slots: the next tier down -- a difficulty gradient so not every game is a wall (D97-A's H6 rationale: some learnable losses/wins consolidate gains).
- 1-2 DIVERSITY slots: stylistically distinct lineages even if lower-ranked (exploiters, retired-macro v5 lineage, old kickoff-era) -- prevents pool homogenization, the same logic that made exploiter1/v5contested useful pool members despite sub-tier1 Elo.
- 1 FLOOR slot: gen1 (Elo 0, the stable reference point) -- NOT bc_v4/v5-style degenerate anchors (D98: bc_v4 is 0% vs everything, zero training signal).

REFRESH CADENCE: at EVERY new cap (every ~30B generation, both lineages), extend the anchored ladder (EXTRA_ANCHORS --resume) and refit BEFORE deciding the next launch. If the new cap enters TIER1 (top-3), it joins the next pool's TIER1 slots (possibly evicting a bank that has fallen toward TIER2/3). WARM-START = current ladder-top checkpoint (D107-A's rule, already adopted) -- not necessarily "the cap that just finished," though those often coincide when the lead generation IS the new ladder-top.

DURABILITY: the ladder CSV (currently /tmp/anchored_ladder.csv on the rig, ephemeral) gets committed to the repo as tools/anchored_ladder.csv after every extension, so the ladder survives rig reboots/session loss and any future agent can read it. A checkpoint REGISTRY (docs/checkpoint_registry.json, mapping ladder-names like "gen2"/"league5" to B2 keys + local filenames + one-line provenance) is also added -- the durable lookup table that lets pool-building be mechanical rather than requiring an agent to remember "gen2 = v4_contested2_cap.bin."

AUTOMATION: tools/build_pool_from_ladder.py reads the committed ladder CSV + registry, applies the slot-allocation rule above (with override flags for diversity/floor picks), and emits the build_league.py seed-list + recommended warm-start -- turning "pick 8 checkpoints" from a manual judgment call into a mechanical step. Dispatching to codex now (.codex-impl/brief-pool-automation.md).

CURRENT STATE (as of D109's 15-node ladder, anchor=gen1): TIER1={league5 +178.7}, the next tier ={gen2 +101.2, gen3 +98.3} (note: league6/league6b are CURRENTLY TESTING whether gen2/gen3 belong in TIER1-with-league5 or get superseded). TIER2={league1 +77.5, gen4 +64.0, league4 +61.9, exploiter1 +58.0}. DIVERSITY candidates={league2 +47.1, gen2cont1 +43.9, exploiter3 +22.0, exploiter4 +13.2, exploiter2 -31.7, kickoff8 -111.5}. FLOOR={gen1 0.0}. DEGENERATE/RETIRED={v5contested -330.3, bc_v4 -1571.4}. The league6/league6b pools (D109-A) already approximate this protocol (gen2,gen3,league5 as the "hard" core + gen4/league2/exploiter1 as tier2/diversity + gen1 floor + kickoff8 diversity) -- this entry formalizes it as the STANDING rule for league7+ regardless of league6/6b's outcome.**
**D112 — LEAGUE5 FROM-KICKOFF MIRROR EVAL: tds=0.667 (30% of human 2.217), a NEW LOW -- below even the now-retired v5-kickoff's 1.625 (73%, D87). possession_rate=0.245, the HIGHEST mirror possession ever recorded (prior bests ~0.22-0.23). Sample is SMALL (8M steps, ~6-10 games, D87-equivalent caveat applies -- wide CIs). Other deltas: blocks_thrown 7.0 vs human 88.8 (-92%, lowest ever), pickup_attempts 1.917 (-74%), pass_attempts 0.000.

THE LADDER-VS-MIRROR DECOUPLING: league5 is the all-time #1 on the anchored ladder (+178.7 Elo, D109, beating gen2/gen3/league1/etc. by 20-80+ Elo each) yet posts the WORST from-kickoff mirror-tds ever measured. HYPOTHESIS (not yet verified): a policy this optimized for possession/ball-security, played against an EXACT COPY OF ITSELF, may produce a low-variance defensive standoff -- neither side takes the dodge/GFI risk needed to score, even though against a DIFFERENT policy (the ladder's diverse opponent pool: gen1-4/league1-4/exploiter1/kickoff8) it dominates. If true, the mirror-from-kickoff eval -- our historical "vs human" proxy since D61 -- may have become MISLEADING specifically for pool-trained checkpoints, and the ladder (diverse real opponents, far more human-like in variety than a self-clone) may now be the better proxy for "vs human" strength. NOT YET VERIFIED -- needs (a) a larger-sample mirror rerun to rule out the n~8 variance explanation, and (b) a league5-vs-OLDER-WEAKER-checkpoint from-kickoff eval (e.g. league5 vs kickoff8/v4_kickoff9_cap via puffer match with demo_reset_pct 0) to test whether league5 scores normally against a non-self, non-pool-trained opponent.

CONTEXT for the live timeline discussion with Alex (re: Opus's forecast): this finding ADDS uncertainty rather than resolving it in either direction. It does NOT confirm "we're closer to human than the relative jump implied" (the raw mirror number got WORSE, not better) -- but it also doesn't cleanly mean "further from human," because the METRIC ITSELF may be broken for this checkpoint. Launching a larger-sample (32M-step) rerun + a league5-vs-kickoff8 cross-checkpoint from-kickoff eval on the idle 2070 now to disambiguate.**
**D112-A — DISAMBIGUATION: gen1's mirror eval (tds=1.111, 50% of human; possession=0.176) supports the POSSESSION-SPECIALIST hypothesis over the "general contested-era degeneracy" hypothesis. Side-by-side (all from-kickoff mirror, small samples n~9-13):
  v5kick (D87, dead-teacher era):       tds 1.625 (73%), possession 0.184
  gen1   (D112-A, ladder floor, Elo 0): tds 1.111 (50%), possession 0.176
  league5 (D112, ladder #1, Elo +178.7): tds 0.667 (30%), possession 0.245

This is MONOTONIC and DIRECTIONAL, not flat: as possession_rate climbs (0.176->0.245), mirror-tds falls (1.111->0.667). gen1 is NOT in league5's depressed range -- it sits in a "normal," moderately-below-v5kick band, consistent with gen1 being an ordinary contested-era checkpoint. league5 is the OUTLIER, and it is ALSO the most possession-optimized checkpoint ever measured (highest possession_rate ever recorded). The mechanism from D112 (two highly possession-focused copies of the same policy produce a low-variance defensive standoff -- neither risks the dodge/GFI needed to score) is SUPPORTED, though still n=2 (gen1, league5) at small per-arm samples.

IMPLICATION FOR THE LIVE TIMELINE DISCUSSION (Alex's "Opus's quarters/year estimate doesn't scan given our ~2M SPS / 4h-per-30B-generation throughput"): the mirror-from-kickoff metric -- the ONLY "vs human" proxy this program has ever had -- appears to DEGRADE precisely as the policy gets MORE possession-optimized, i.e. precisely as the ladder says it's getting STRONGER. The metric and the (likely-true) underlying strength signal are anti-correlated for the current champion. This means: (1) league5's mirror-tds drop is probably NOT evidence of "further from human" -- it's a measurement artifact; (2) the ladder's +178.7 (biggest jump ever, achieved in ONE ~4-8h generation) is more likely the trustworthy "real progress" signal, supporting Alex's faster-than-quarters intuition; (3) BUT we have NO WORKING absolute "vs human-like-opponent" eval for the current champion -- v5kick's 1.625/73% is retired AND was measured under a different (non-possession-annuity-dominant, dead-teacher-era) regime, so it's not a clean baseline either. THE REAL GAP is now: build a cross-checkpoint from-kickoff eval (league5 vs an old/weak frozen opponent like kickoff8, NOT mirror) -- this avoids the self-clone degeneracy and would give the first genuinely informative absolute-scale read on the current champion. Not yet built; eval_game_stats.sh is mirror-only. Queued as the next disambiguating step once league6/6b cap (the generalization-test verdict takes priority for the next launch decision).**
**D113 — RESEARCH: reward-inference from human replays (Alex's IRL question). Two independent research efforts (a direct opus dispatch covering GAIL/AIRL/ValueDICE/AlphaStar/MimicBot, and a /research-skill agent on classic IRL tractability) converged at high confidence (9/10): full IRL (Ng-Russell LP, MaxEnt/Ziebart) is INTRACTABLE for this setup -- both require an RL-solve-to-convergence per reward-update on what would need to be a stationary MDP; self-play is the opposite of stationary, and the 454-way factored action space / 2782-dim obs is far beyond any scaled IRL precedent (even Google Maps' ICLR-2024 "massively scalable IRL" relies on DAG road-graph structure BB doesn't have).

THE TRACTABLE WINNER (independently arrived at by both research paths): AGGREGATE-STATISTIC / FEATURE-EXPECTATION MATCHING (Abbeel & Ng 2004's apprenticeship-learning framing == AlphaStar's productionized "pseudo-rewards": episode-end reward = -distance(agent's cumulative game stats, human target stats)). This is the literal match to Alex's framing ("look at every step in aggregate, derive what reward would produce this behavior"). Implementation: NO engine/C changes needed (episode-boundary hook exists); compute agent stats via the same machinery as game_stats.py (possession_rate, tds, dodges, pickups, passes, blocks per game), compute distance to docs/human-baseline.json / docs/per-team-baseline.json, add as an episode-end pseudo-reward term. Fully interpretable and auditable-per-statistic against D90's anti-farming doctrine (unlike a discriminator logit).

SECOND PRECEDENTED OPTION: MimicBot (the actual Bot Bowl III winner for THIS GAME, arXiv 2108.09478) used interleaved BC-gradient updates during RL (behavioral anchor toward bc_v4) -- pure trainer-loss term, also no engine changes, the BB-native version of AlphaStar's KL-to-human-policy anchor.

GAIL/AIRL (discriminator-as-learned-reward) was assessed and DEPRIORITIZED: it's the "formal" version of the idea but adds a SECOND opaque reward channel at exactly the moment D112 showed our FIRST (hand-tuned) reward channel produced degenerate possession-obsessed behavior -- either frozen (exploitable/reward-hacking) or co-trained (GAN instability on top of self-play non-stationarity).

SEQUENCING: TD-maniac (queued, zero possession annuity / big reward_td / zero rush_cost) is the CHEAP PROBE -- if a 5-minute hand-retune fixes D112's degeneracy, aggregate-stat-matching may be unnecessary; if it doesn't, aggregate-stat-matching is the principled follow-up (lets HUMAN DATA set the target mix instead of hand-guessing). Relative to D111's pool-composition lever: orthogonal axis, but D109's biggest-ever jump came from POOL not REWARD changes, and D90 already warns against opaque shaping ("defense needed an opponent, not a bounty"). PRIORITY: pool-composition (D111) remains primary; TD-maniac launches when a box frees (league6/6b cap, ~1.5-2h); aggregate-stat-matching is a queued PARALLEL low-priority research track, design pending TD-maniac's result.**
**D113-A — Aggregate-stat-matching refined to an implementable spec (confirms+extends D113). GAIL/AIRL angle: confirmed deprioritized -- no 2023-2026 work solves discriminator instability for >100-way factored action spaces under self-play; the closest success (AMP, frozen discriminator) is continuous/single-agent/fixed-opponent, and the RLHF frozen-reward-model literature documents the EXACT failure mode self-play would trigger (policy diverges from training distribution -> frozen classifier becomes unreliable -> exploited). If tried at all: small auxiliary bonus with a DECAY SCHEDULE, never primary.

Aggregate-matching angle: STRONGLY reinforced with new grounding. (1) Waymo Open Sim Agents Challenge (2023-2025) validates the exact pattern (aggregate behavioral-statistic matching) at industrial scale. (2) "Of Moments and Matching" (Swamy, ICML 2021) gives the formal bound: matching moments of demonstrator behavior bounds the imitation gap regardless of the TRUE unknown reward. (3) "Correlated Proxies" (Laidlaw 2024) is the KEY justification for why JOINT matching avoids D112's single-stat degeneracy: optimizing an ENSEMBLE of correlated proxies jointly is robust because gaming one metric while tanking others requires orthogonal exploitation of ALL simultaneously -- possession_rate is SAFE as one dimension of a joint target even though it was UNSAFE as an isolated annuity (D90/D112).

IMPLEMENTABLE SPEC: episode-end pseudo-reward = -scale * sqrt(sum_i ((agent_stat_i - human_mean_i)/human_std_i)^2) [diagonal-Mahalanobis/Z-score L2, NOT PBRS -- raw episodic term]. Stat vector: {tds, dodgeRoll, pickUpRoll, passRoll, goForItRoll, block_2dred_frac, possession_rate_d90} -- all 7 jointly (possession_rate INCLUDED but only as one of seven, not isolated). scale ~0.2-0.5x typical episode return (start small). MUST zero reward_possession (the 0.03 annuity) -- cannot coexist with possession_rate in the joint target (annuity has denser gradient, would dominate). Activate ONLY at kickoff-start (demo_reset_pct=0) -- curriculum-stage episodes are too short for full-game stat targets to be meaningful. Use docs/human-baseline.json as a FIXED exogenous target (not the live opponent's stats -- in contested self-play the opponent's defense affects your tds/dodges, but the human baseline is fixed and correctly anchors the optimization). Gotchas: untracked-dimension exploits (the 7 stats don't cover everything -- monitor post-hoc), sparse episodic credit (keep coefficient small relative to dense per-step rewards), small-sample eval noise (track running averages over 1000+ episodes during training, not single evals).

This is now a near-ready brief for a codex-implementer dispatch -- queued as the parallel low-priority research track per D113, behind TD-maniac (cheap probe) and D111's pool-composition primary lever.**

**D113-B — MimicBot deep-dive: NOT usable as a tournament contestant (no code/weights exist, BB2016/wrong-edition, 8116-way flat-conv action space vs our 454-way factored), but yields THREE transferable techniques. (1) EV-BASED MASK SHAPING (the most actionable): MimicBot's biggest lever beyond BC was deleting no-brainer-bad actions from the LEGAL ACTION MASK at decision time -- specifically, blocks with >70% turnover probability were masked to -inf pre-softmax (plus forcing ball-carrier-blocks-last). We ALREADY COMPUTE the exact probabilities needed (obs-v4's A1/A2/B planes, tools/blockev_mc.c) -- this could be added as a cheap, ANNEALABLE binding-level mask filter (per D28/D46's gradual-anneal-never-cold-off doctrine), a candidate anti-degeneracy A/B independent of reward changes. (2) INDEPENDENT VALIDATION of our obs-v4 probability-plane design -- MimicBot (SOTA at the time) independently arrived at the same "put roll/block-dice probability planes in the observation" idea; no design change needed, just external corroboration. (3) INTERLEAVED-BC-DURING-RL (alternating whole optimizer steps between RL and BC, hard-cutting BC at a step threshold) is a DISTINCT technique from our current bc_coef aux-loss (cosine-annealed auxiliary loss term) -- a legitimate ablation if BC-anchoring (D113's Option B / MimicBot-recipe) ever shows gradient interference.

THE "MIMICBOT-STYLE BASELINE" recommendation: replicate the RECIPE (BC warm-start + interleaved-BC + EV-mask-shaping) trained on OUR BB2025 corpus (validation/pairs_v4) -- drops into the ladder/registry with ZERO new infra (same obs-v4/454-head/flat-fp32 format). Medium value: likely lands near the bottom (D98 found bc_v4-style pure-imitation is degenerate, 0% decisive vs everything) but serves as (a) a reproducible NAMED baseline node, (b) a testbed for techniques (1) and (3) above. LOW PRIORITY -- queued behind TD-maniac and D111's pool lever.

FOR AN EXTERNAL BB2025 CONTESTANT (the original ask's "at minimum"): NOT MimicBot/botbowl (wrong edition, no bot exists there either). FFB (the BB2025 reference engine) has NO bot/AI player currently -- NUFFLEBOT (the headless FFB-client bridge, docs/nufflebot-feasibility.md) remains the right long-term path, and ~70% of its code overlaps the already-planned Phase-4 replay-differential harness (task #6). No shortcut exists; this is a multi-week project already on the roadmap, not a quick win.**

**D114 — IMPLEMENTED: D113-A's aggregate-statistic-matching pseudo-reward (the principled "let human data set the target mix" follow-up to D112's hand-tuned-reward degeneracy). New env knob `reward_statmatch_scale` (CLI `--env.reward-statmatch-scale`, default 0.0 = OFF = bit-identical to existing arms; binding.c:90, bloodbowl.h struct field). When >0, `bbe_finish_episode` adds an episode-end term `-scale * sqrt(sum_i z_i^2)`, z_i = (agent_stat_i - human_mean_i)/human_std_i over the 7 D113-A stats {tds, dodgeRoll, pickUpRoll, passRoll, goForItRoll, block_2dred_frac, possession_rate} (diagonal-Mahalanobis / Z-score L2 -- a RAW episodic term, NOT PBRS, per spec). New dashboard field `statmatch_term` (the per-episode term, <=0; binding.c dict_set) so it is directly observable.

KEY IMPLEMENTATION CHOICES (reviewable design calls):
(1) MATCH-LEVEL, SYMMETRIC, not per-agent. The 7 stat counters in the env (ep_dodge_attempts, ep_block_tier, ep_turns/ep_turns_with_ball, etc.) are tracked match-level (both teams summed) -- which is EXACTLY how human-baseline.json was measured (dodgeRoll_per_game etc. are both-teams-per-game totals, see tools/game_stats.py METRICS). So I compute ONE term on the match-level vector and apply it SYMMETRICALLY to both self-play agents. The spec said "per-agent from that agent's counters"; I deviated because per-agent half-game stats are NOT what the baseline measures, and self-play means both agents jointly authored the game's statistics. Flagged for review: if a future asymmetric (learner-vs-frozen) statmatch arm is wanted, the term should switch to per-team counters and apply only to the learner -- not done here (statmatch1 is symmetric frozen-self).
(2) GATE: term activates ONLY when reward_statmatch_scale>0 AND demo_started==0 (kickoff-pure episode). Curriculum/demo-reset episodes never receive it regardless of the flag (safe-by-default; full-game stat targets are meaningless on truncated curriculum starts). statmatch1 also forces --env.demo-reset-pct 0 so EVERY episode is a full game.
(3) reward_possession FORCED to 0 in the launch (cannot coexist -- the 0.03 annuity's dense per-turn gradient would dominate the joint possession_rate target; D90/D112 already showed isolated possession shaping is poison, D113-A's Correlated-Proxies result only rehabilitates possession_rate AS ONE OF SEVEN jointly).

human_std DERIVATION (the open methodology question -- DEFENSIBLE-BUT-ARBITRARY, documented per Alex's review rule): NO per-game stats table exists anywhere in the repo (searched validation/ tools/ docs/ for any per-replay JSON/CSV with these 7 stats -- only the AGGREGATE docs/human-baseline.json from D61 exists; the corpus was reduced to means over 12722 games / 453617 team-turns, per-game values not retained). Re-deriving a per-game corpus from raw replays is a much larger task (>>30min) so I used the spec's principled FALLBACK: count stats (tds, dodgeRoll, goForItRoll, pickUpRoll, passRoll) are event-counts-per-game, treated as Poisson => std = sqrt(mean); fraction stats use std = sqrt(p(1-p)/n) with n = the per-game denominator (block_2dred over ~88.83 blocks/game = blockRoll_per_game; possession_rate over ~35.66 team-turns/game = 453617/12722). Computed stds: tds 1.489, dodgeRoll 5.068, pickUpRoll 2.700, passRoll 1.404, goForItRoll 4.169, block_2dred_frac 0.01368, possession_rate 0.0812 (hardcoded HB_STD[7] in bloodbowl.h alongside HB_MEAN[7]). CAVEAT WORTH REVIEW: block_2dred_frac's std (0.0137) is SMALLER than its mean (0.0169), and the agent sits at ~0.12-0.15 (~10x human), so that single dimension's z is ~9-10 and contributes ~84% of the squared norm -- the term is effectively "stop taking 2d-red blocks" with the other 6 stats as minor seasoning. This is DIRECTIONALLY correct (the planes-working doctrine wants 2dred falling toward human) but means statmatch1 is NOT a balanced 7-way pull in practice. If we want a balanced pull, floor the fraction stds (e.g. min 0.03-0.05) or switch counts to a real empirical per-game std -- left as-is for the first probe, monitor whether 2dred collapses while the other 6 stay stuck (= over-domination) vs all 7 converging.

SCALE = 0.01 chosen (the launch default), calibrated EMPIRICALLY not guessed: a scale=1.0 smoke run (warm league5_cap, native, 40M steps, kickoff-pure) measured mean statmatch_term = -13.4 => mean per-episode ||z|| ~ 13, and base episode_return ~0.45-0.65 (statmatch off). 0.01 => mean term ~ -0.11 to -0.13 = ~0.2-0.3x of base return, the LOW end of the spec's 0.2-0.5x band ("start small" -- sparse episodic credit must stay subordinate to the dense per-step rewards). (Note: hand-computing ||z|| from the mean stats gives 10.45, but the per-episode-then-averaged term is -13.4 by Jensen -- episode-to-episode noise inflates E[||z||] above ||E[z]||. Both are sane; implementation verified correct.)

SMOKE-TEST EVIDENCE (rig, RTX 2070, native --float build, warm league5_cap): builds CLEAN with the changes (only the pre-existing benign _XOPEN_SOURCE redefinition warnings; math.h/sqrtf added to bloodbowl.h). scale=1.0 run: statmatch_term -13.4, demo_episodes 0.0 (kickoff gate confirmed -- all episodes full games), no crashes, term finite/sane. REGRESSION CHECK: a scale=0 run (15M steps, otherwise identical) gave statmatch_term EXACTLY 0.0 and episode_return 0.456 = base economy only, proving the default-off path is inert (additive 0.0f is an IEEE no-op; the `>0.0f` gate excludes the default). Code committed atomically (knob+pseudo-reward; launch script separate). POOL-COMPOSITION CHOICE: statmatch1 runs FROZEN-SELF (no D111 league pool) deliberately -- to get a CLEAN single-variable read on the REWARD change without entangling D111's orthogonal pool lever (per the launch guidance). A pool-enabled variant is a later follow-up.**
