**D115 — NEXT-STEPS BACKLOG: reward-economy "extreme variant" candidates (Alex's "what would an extreme TD/win reward look like, and what's the downside" discussion, 2026-06-14). These are FOLLOW-UPS, contingent on results from the three currently-active probes (statmatch1 running on the rig per D114-A; TD-maniac and stakes1 staged at /tmp/launch_tdmaniac1.sh and /tmp/launch_stakes1.sh, both warm=league5_cap, both pending a freed Vast box). Not launched -- documented so the reasoning survives even if the next session doesn't have this conversation's context.

TD-REWARD AXIS (current default reward_td=0.4; TD-maniac=1.2):
- Axis-1 (magnitude) extreme: reward_td 3.0-5.0+. At this scale a single TD swing (+/-3 to +/-5, zero-sum per bloodbowl.h:1919-1922) dwarfs every other term (dist_endzone 0.2, k_value/k_ball/k_kd/k_seq 0.25/0.15/0.03/0.01, win 0.6, possession 0.03/turn) -- the game reduces to "TD differential, weighted huge."
- Axis-2 (structure) extreme: zero ALL other shaping (dist_endzone, k_*, ball_gain, possession, win/draw) so reward_td is the ONLY signal -- sparse TD-differential-only RL.
- DOWNSIDE (both axes): (1) TDs are RARE (human ~1.1/team/game over ~100 turns) and arrive after long sequences -- making the rarest, latest event also the LARGEST reward maximizes return variance on exactly the hardest-to-credit signal, especially destabilizing against a non-stationary self-play opponent. (2) The dense shaping terms teach the PREREQUISITE skills (positioning, ball security, dodge selection) that human TDs are built on; swamping them in the value-function loss could paradoxically SLOW TD growth, not accelerate it. (3) Directly amplifies the existing "Hail Mary" pattern (GFI/dodge attempts already 5-10x human at reward_td=0.4) -- pushes FURTHER from human on the exact axes D113-A's statmatch term is pulling TOWARD human. (4) Same Goodhart shape as D112 (possession), mirrored: over-weighting one proxy optimizes that proxy at the expense of what it's a proxy FOR, with no guarantee the result generalizes (echoes D107/D108 non-transitivity). RECOMMENDATION: only pursue axis-1 (3.0-5.0) as a follow-up if TD-maniac (1.2) shows TDs moving in the right direction but too weakly to matter; axis-2 (sparse TD-only) is a last resort, not a first move.

WIN-REWARD AXIS (current default reward_win=0.6 spread 1.2; stakes1=1.4 spread 2.8; reward_draw=0):
- Axis-1 (magnitude) extreme: reward_win 3.0-5.0+ (spread 6-10). bloodbowl.ini:40's "reward_td + reward_win <= 1.0 on the winning-TD step" invariant is already broken by stakes1's 1.4 and would be badly broken here (5.4 on that one step vs 0.01-0.25 elsewhere).
- DOWNSIDE (axis-1): (1) Long-horizon discounting: a ~100-team-turn episode means gamma^(steps-to-go) may shrink an even-bigger terminal reward into near-irrelevance at turn 1 anyway -- cranking the NUMBER doesn't fix a problem that's really about HORIZON LENGTH; what it reliably does is dominate the last few turns disproportionately (normal play for 90% of the game, erratic/extreme in the endgame). (2) Win/loss is NOISY (a late dice roll flips close games) -- huge magnitude on a noisy binary outcome inflates variance on otherwise-similar trajectories, destabilizing PPO's advantage estimates. (3) AMBIGUOUS effect on D112's stalling problem: raising stakes SYMMETRICALLY could make a policy that's AHEAD stall EVEN HARDER (bigger downside to blowing the lead) while a policy BEHIND gets more desperate -- net "liveliness" could be unchanged, just redistributed by game-state rather than reduced.
- Axis-2 (punish draws specifically): leave reward_win alone, make reward_draw meaningfully NEGATIVE (both sides, symmetric) -- e.g. -1 to -2. More SURGICAL than axis-1: D112's finding wasn't "winning isn't valuable enough," it was "drawing/low-scoring-stall is currently a perfectly acceptable outcome (reward_draw=0)." Making any non-decisive result actively costly targets that directly without disturbing the win/loss spread or the reward_td+reward_win<=1.0 invariant.
- Axis-2b (the genuinely-extreme option): zero ALL shaping entirely -- no dist_endzone, no k_*, no possession, no ball_gain, no per-TD reward -- pure +/-W at episode end (AlphaZero-style). Removes essentially ALL Goodhart/proxy-gaming risk (nothing to game except the actual win condition) but reintroduces the cold-start problem dense shaping was ADDED to solve -- EXCEPT we are not training from scratch; league5 is already a competent, win-capable policy. Stripping scaffolding from a strong warm-start and letting pure win/loss take over is the natural endpoint of D28/D46's "anneal scaffolding away" doctrine taken to its limit in one step rather than gradually. The most STRUCTURALLY INTERESTING of the extreme options -- a real "next era" candidate (post-statmatch1/TD-maniac/stakes1, from whichever checkpoint wins that 3-way readout), not a first move.

SEQUENCING: all of the above are gated on the outcomes of the THREE currently-active probes (D114-A statmatch1, staged TD-maniac, staged stakes1). Revisit this entry once those resolve -- the winner/loser pattern among those three should inform WHICH of these follow-ups (if any) is worth a box.**

**D119 — RESEARCH BACKLOG: "skill-aware role assignment" is weakly-or-non represented in the reward economy (Alex's passing digression, 2026-06-15). Three related findings, unified by one theme: Blood Bowl strategy constantly asks "WHICH PLAYER should do this," and our reward function mostly can't see player identity/skills at all -- it sees positions and ball state.

(1) PASSING'S PRECONDITION-OF-A-PRECONDITION: a Pass requires (a) the ball-carrier to have Pass/be a Thrower, AND (b) a Catcher already positioned downfield, in range, unmarked -- BEFORE the pass is even attempted. In human play, "get the ball to the Thrower" (often via kickoff retrieval routing, sometimes a hand-off) is itself a deliberate early-game decision, made turns before any pass. CONFIRMED IN CODE: `reward_ball_gain` (bloodbowl.h:1945) is completely skill-agnostic -- picking up the ball with the Thrower vs. any Lineman gives an IDENTICAL reward. The reward function cannot represent "this pickup matters more because of who made it."

(2) THE FORMATION PROBLEM: pushing a Catcher into open space downfield, BEFORE the ball arrives near them, changes none of {dist_ball, dist_endzone, k_value, k_ball} (all ball/carrier-centric) -- it is reward-NEUTRAL at the moment it happens, with the payoff (enabling a future pass) several turns away and uncertain. Blood Bowl strategy is substantially about TEAM SHAPE (screens, cages, spreading receivers) independent of where the ball currently is -- there may be NO existing reward term with this in its domain at all.

(3) PICKUP RISK SHOULD BE SKILL-CONDITIONAL: 4+AG and/or Sure-Hands players should preferentially contest loose balls -- minimizing failed-pickup turnovers is foundational risk management (a failed pickup roll = immediate turnover, ending the whole remaining turn). PARTIALLY may already be addressed by EXISTING machinery: obs-v4's probability planes encode per-square pickup-success odds (docs/obs-v4-spec.md, "AG/TZ/weather grids -> expected plane-B"), and `k_seq` = `P(turnover of this roll) * pending_safe_activations` (bloodbowl.h:276) is a generic turnover-probability-weighted penalty that SHOULD already discourage low-AG players from contesting risky pickups when better options exist. OPEN RESEARCH QUESTIONS: (a) is the probability plane computed per-ACTING-PLAYER (so the agent can see "if I move THIS specific low-AG player here, my odds are worse than if my Sure-Hands player went instead") or is it a generic/shared plane that doesn't vary by who's being asked to act? (b) is k_seq's gradient strong enough RELATIVE to the other dense terms to actually shape "send the right player" -- given D46's standing finding that GFI/dodge attempts run 5-10x human rates, the EXISTING turnover-probability machinery does not appear to be producing human-like risk aversion in general, so (3) may be a SYMPTOM of that broader unsolved problem rather than a missing feature per se.

SEQUENCING: this is a RESEARCH track (per Alex, "backlog entry to research") -- queued alongside D113-B's MimicBot-style-baseline and D115's reward-economy-extreme-variants as parallel low-priority threads, behind the three currently-running probes (statmatch2, TD-maniac, stakes1). Candidate next steps when picked up: (i) audit whether obs-v4's probability planes are per-acting-player or generic (quick code read); (ii) if generic, that's a real obs-v4 gap worth its own design doc; (iii) if per-player and k_seq's weight is the bottleneck, that's a cheap knob to A/B; (iv) the formation problem (2) likely needs either a new reward term (team-shape/spread metric) or the D115-axis-2b sparse-objective route -- no cheap fix exists yet, needs design work before any launch.**

**D121 — AndyDavo corpus synthesis vs reward-economy pressure test (research, 2026-06-15).** Read all 16 AndyDavo coaching-video packs in `docs/vendor/andydavo/*.md` (344KB; numbered by playlist position) for anything mapping onto a reward term, curriculum/demo-bank design, or BC-anchoring target. The packs each carry a doc-author "RL-mapping" section, but those were treated as SECONDARY — the load-bearing content is the timestamped dialogue/board-states (the actual source). Two prior artifacts frame this: the codex/Opus **pressure test** (pending as D120) and the in-repo **`docs/reward-design-coaching-wisdom.md` memo (R1–R11)**, which I discovered IS itself a prior synthesis of much of this same corpus — a comprehensive but as-yet-UNIMPLEMENTED design (the live header only has `k_kd/k_value/k_ball/k_seq` + `surf_taken/inflicted` [DEFAULT 0=OFF] + `possession` + `dist_*` + `ball_gain/loss` + `rush_cost` + `statmatch`). Reconciliation below is against BOTH the pressure test AND the R-memo, since they overlap.

**CODE-LEVEL GROUND TRUTH (verified in `puffer/bloodbowl/bloodbowl.h` this pass):** (a) `k_seq` is block-declaration-only AND turn<8-gated (line 1812: `act.type == BB_A_BLOCK_TARGET ... && m->turn[bteam] < 8`); dodges/GFI/pickup pay ZERO sequencing charge — pressure-test #1 finding CONFIRMED still true at code level. (b) Crowd-surf terms (`reward_surf_taken/inflicted`) ARE coded (header 255–258, applied 2044–2053) but ship DEFAULT-OFF — not in the settled v4 economy. (c) NO term has off-ball formation/screen/cage/spread in its domain (D119-2 confirmed). (d) NO per-step reroll-management term exists, and the R-memo (line 82) deliberately EXCLUDES "reroll budgeting beyond R9" as a value-network job.

### Part A — the 9 pressure-test principles

1. **Risk-sequencing / action-order ("safe things first").** CORROBORATED, overwhelmingly — the single most-repeated theme in the corpus. "Stand up downed players FIRST (0-risk) before rolling any dice" (#09 12:59, #01 08:00 "flat mistake" blitzing-before-standing-up). "Screen/cover the ball BEFORE throwing LoS blocks" (#01 03:01 "I should have covered and screened the ball first"). "Secure the ball carrier's safety before non-Block blocks" (#22 12:12, #29 12:12, #08 12:12 — the Str-5-no-Block-blocks-first blunder recurs across 3 packs of the SAME Chaos/Skaven game). EXTENDS the pressure test in one concrete way: AndyDavo repeatedly frames the cost as **scaling with unactivated players left** ("two-thirds of my turn's resources for precisely zero," #01 29:27; "spent two-thirds... a mistake") — which is EXACTLY R1's `pending_safe_activations` weighting that `k_seq` already implements for blocks. So the corpus strongly endorses EXTENDING `k_seq`-style pricing to dodge/GFI/pickup declarations (the pressure-test #1 gap), NOT just leaving it block-only. **But see D117-A caveat: the gfi/dodge-spam this was meant to explain no longer appears in the current lineage.**

2. **Caging.** CORROBORATED + EXTENDED with hard mechanics. Anti-leap "elongated X-cage" = put a 5th player DIRECTLY BEHIND the carrier to deny the leap-landing square (#02 11:20). "Never leave a cage CORNER open — agile opponents dodge in / the 2d-uphill out lives there" (#08 19:14, #22 15:53 "loose cage with open corner," #29 15:53). "Sideline three-prong cage" uses the sideline as the 4th wall, freeing one player (#01 33:51). "Loose cage" intentionally trades tightness for carrier escape-mobility when based (#06 08:33). Keep the ball on a Str-4 piece so cage-breaking needs multiple assists (#01 18:00 "keeping the ball on a Str-4 piece is always preferred"). NONE of this is representable today (no formation term). R-memo's **R6 (carrier-exposure, min-dodges-to-reach == 0)** is the formation-agnostic proxy and is its stated answer (memo line 80 explicitly refuses cage-shape templates).

3. **Cage-breaking.** CORROBORATED + EXTENDED with the most quantitative heuristic in the whole corpus: **to strip a caged ball, mark the cage corners in 2 tackle zones FIRST — a bouncing ball that an AG3 corner would catch on 4+ becomes a 6+ in two TZs, so they drop it and it bounces OUT of the cage** (#06 22:26, near-verbatim repeated in the #06 frame catalog). "Crush something IN: chain-push an adjacent player INTO the carrier to dislodge them" as an alternative to pushing a corner out (#32 03:49). "Rolling 8–12 block dice on the carrier in one turn makes a strip mathematically guaranteed even with no rerolls" (#26 39:35, the Frenzy-Werewolf double-blitz stack). Leap-sack into the open landing square behind the carrier (#02 12:45). Not representable; would emerge from R6/R7 + the exposure transfer if the agent ever learned to set it up.

4. **Screening.** CORROBORATED + heavily EXTENDED. The recurring concrete rule: **screeners stand on DIAGONALS / 2-squares-apart (knight's-move) so tackle zones overlap and no straight-line lane exists, WITHOUT giving the opponent a free block** (#10 "S-shape," #07 "column defense," #06 18:33 "2-square horizontal gap," #31 12:40 "Space Invader screen, staggered columns 2 apart"). "Maintain a 1-square gap — do NOT stand base-to-base on the opponent's turn; force them to spend their blitz for any contact" (#06 18:33, #10 takeaway-3). "Wide/flat denies the wings; the Boat/Chevron each have specific counters" (#07 whole pack). Today: no screen term. R-memo's **R7 (conceded-2D contact)** prices "do not stand where the opponent gets a free ≥2d block on you," which is the inverse-side of the same coin. **NEW nuance R7 does NOT capture: the "1-square air-gap" is about denying contact ENTIRELY (zero blocks), not just denying 2-dice — corpus is emphatic that 1-dice free blocks are also to be avoided on defense.**

5. **Screen-penetration.** CORROBORATED. "Stretching the rope": with a player advantage, spread WIDE to thin the opponent's screen, then concentrate locally against one thin section and flood through (#31 11:35 — a genuinely new, named concept). "Offset/split the LoS to open a 7-square gap, then punch through with Guard/Str4/AG5" (#07 04:30, #06 12:47). "Faking the score" — send runners deep to force the defense to spread, opening the center (#16 02:50, #29). Chain-push your OWN blitzer forward through a T/box to gain 1–2 squares of reach and blitz an out-of-range carrier (#09 12:59, the out-of-range-chain-push puzzle). No term; needs path-actions (v5) or formation reward.

6. **Basing / tie-up trades.** CORROBORATED + EXTENDED + one CORRECTION to the pressure test's "partially-and-possibly-mis-signed" worry. The corpus is crystal-clear on the SIGN: **base on a KNOCKDOWN (follow up, pin the prone player); on a PUSH do NOT follow up (step back, keep the air-gap, deny the free return-block)** (#02 28:30 "Basing on Knockdown, Free on Push," #16 38:00 invariant). Base with HIGH-strength / grouped-assist pieces so any block-back is 1-die/uphill; never base with a weak piece that gets blocked back free (#01 25:53, #02). "4-vs-7 trade": tie up 7 opponents with 4 cheap Zombies to win the numbers war elsewhere (#26 30:52). "Pseudo-stun": knocking down a MA3 Mummy costs it 3 MA to stand = effectively removed (#02 18:50). This is a clean, consistent sign and matches R7's "1D-marking-is-fine, concede-no-2D" framing — the pressure test's mis-sign worry looks RESOLVED by the corpus: the doctrine is "marking is good when it's 1-dice-for-them, bad when it's 2-dice-for-them," which is exactly R7's dice-based (not adjacency-based) predicate.

7. **Re-roll management.** CORROBORATED with the SPECIFIC NUMBER the pilot hoped for. Pack **#13 (FiveWaysToImprove) Tip 4, [03:01–04:13], verbatim: "Try to save one or two team rerolls for the final three turns of a drive (the 'business end')."** Corroborated by #02 09:08 ("preserve a reroll for the Turn-8 one-turn-score attempt") and #31 15:10 ("rerolls wasted early on low-impact actions left none for the critical end-game dodges"). Decision heuristic, repeated: **"If this fails, does it screw me? Do I even NEED to do this action?"** (#13, #08 06:40, #26 16:37) and **"Would I take this 3+ dodge if I had ALREADY used my team reroll?" — if no, it's sub-optimal** (#26 18:10). PRESSURE-TEST AGREED this is "not representable as a per-step reward (needs BC/curriculum)" — corpus CONFIRMS: the "save for the last 3 turns" rule is a clock-and-trajectory value judgment, exactly what the R-memo (line 82) says to leave to the value net. R-memo's **R9 ("no greed rerolls" — don't burn a RR on a pool that already has a zero-turnover face)** is the ONLY per-step slice that's cleanly priceable, and the corpus directly supports it (#26 18:10, #29 06:43). **The "reserve 1–2 RRs for the final 3 turns" heuristic is a BC-anchoring / curriculum target, not a reward term.**

8. **Game-management / tempo.** CORROBORATED, ubiquitous (every replay pack). The "Turn-8 stall" / "2-1 grind" is stated in #01, #02, #08, #09, #16, #22, #29, #31 — universal across races, with the execution-timing varying by speed (fast teams wait in the backfield; slow teams like Dwarfs/Orcs must START advancing by turn 2–3, #02 00:00, #31). Defense has exactly two win-conditions: force an EARLY score (you get turns to equalize) OR prevent scoring entirely (#01 24:31, #02 14:00). EXTENDS: **"two-turn planning horizon — never play turn-by-turn; every move must set up where you go next turn AND the turn after"** (#31 09:10, #10 "working backwards from where you want to be on Turn 8"). This is precisely R-memo's **R11 (clock-aware potential Φ, FUMBBL-fit win-prob)** and is its strongest corpus endorsement. The possession annuity (live `reward_possession 0.03`) is the zero-sum-symmetric partial version; corpus implies R11 (margin×clock-aware, NOT symmetric) is the real target — directly relevant to the D112 mirror-stall the pressure test flagged.

9. **Skill-value hierarchy / removal-snowball.** CORROBORATED + EXTENDED with skill-conditional targeting numbers. "Snipe the high-mobility POSITIONALS (Wights/Ghouls/Gutter Runners), NOT the high-Str Mummies — kill their maneuver, not their muscle" (#10 07:40 "don't get obsessed with Mummies; Wights and Ghouls are the stars"; #26; #31 03:30 "target the Claw players every turn, and remove low-AV non-Regen support"). Quantitative skill-conditional EV: Frenzy vs a Dodge target raises knockdown from 55%→80% IF assists are cancelled first (#26 08:41); a Claw block breaks AV10 Mummy armor on a flat 8+ (#26 33:57); MB density "34 MB blocks → 9 removals" (#16 38:00). This is the `k_value` (price-weighted attrition, `def_cost_k/100`) story — but the corpus says removal value is about SKILLS/ROLE (mobility, Claw-matchups), which gold-cost only partially proxies. EXTENDS toward a skill-aware (not just cost-aware) `k_value`.

### Part B — D119's three findings

- **D119(1) passing precondition-chain ("get the ball to the Thrower first").** CORROBORATED but with a DECISIVE CAVEAT that downgrades passing's importance in BB2025. The corpus repeatedly notes **passing is largely DEAD in current rules**: "Under BB2020 rules, passing stats are decoupled from agility, making vanity passing without a dedicated thrower highly risky and non-viable" (#01 22:46). Real games are won by RUNNING the ball in a cage/screen; passes appear only as (a) safe SPP-farm patty-cake when the ball is 100% secure (#02 33:55, #06 00:57), or (b) desperation end-of-half plays at ~20–36% (#01 20:30, #09 20:19). The "get the ball to the right carrier" theme IS real but is about HANDOFFS to a Str-4/scoring piece and "score with the right player" (#13 Tip 3, #08 17:34, #18, #22/#29 17:34 — "score with a Chaos Warrior to buy Block, not the Beastman"), NOT downfield passing. **Implication: the D119(1) "pass needs a Catcher pre-positioned" precondition-chain is a real human pattern but a LOW-VALUE target in BB2025; the handoff-to-the-right-player version is the live one, and our `reward_ball_gain` skill-agnosticism (D119-1's code finding) bites on handoffs/score-selection more than on passes.**

- **D119(2) the formation problem (off-ball positioning is reward-neutral).** CORROBORATED — this is the LARGEST gap the corpus exposes. A huge fraction of every pack is off-ball shape: screens, cages, spreads, sweepers, Guard-walls, lane-coverage, "safe corner" positioning (#26 43:48 — overlap opponents' threat-grids to find the unreachable corner and park the carrier there). All of it is reward-neutral at the moment it happens under the current ball/carrier-centric economy. The R-memo's stated ANSWER is the **R6/R7/R8 settled-turn-end exposure trio (carrier-exposure, conceded-2D, surf-zone)** — formation-as-FUNCTION, not formation-as-shape (memo line 80 explicitly refuses shape templates; line 67 "goal-side containment" is a flagged last-resort). The corpus VALIDATES that the underlying invariant ("min dodges for an opponent to reach the carrier") is what coaches actually compute, so R6 is well-targeted. This is the cleanest "should-be-a-reward-term" finding and it already has a designed-but-unbuilt home.

- **D119(3) pickup risk should be skill-conditional.** PARTIALLY CORROBORATED, with a strong REFRAME. The corpus barely discusses contested PICKUP-roll selection (because expert play AVOIDS contested pickups: **"don't attempt a risky 4+ pickup in tackle zones — just stand a tackle-zone ON the loose ball and make the OPPONENT roll the bad odds,"** #02 12:45, #06 08:33). The corpus's actual loose-ball doctrine is bigger than pickup-AG: **"When the ball is on the floor, the focus HAS to be on that — every action dedicated to securing or screening it; no greedy blocks elsewhere"** (#26 19:48, a hard-stated rule). And **"design the turn so the FAIL STATE is acceptable: set screens BEFORE rolling the risky pickup so a failure leaves the ball protected"** (#26 21:56, #01 22:46 fail-safe spacing, #08 27:15 "air gap"). So D119(3)'s "send the Sure-Hands/AG4 player" is real but secondary; the dominant heuristic is "loose ball = drop everything + pre-screen the fail-state." Neither is representable today (the obs-v4 plane question from D119(3) is still open and worth the quick code-read).

### Part C — GENUINELY NEW findings (not in pressure test or R-memo's main list)

- **N1. "Minimize dice rolled per turn" as a first-class objective.** #26 26:46 states it as a rule: "Frenzy forces a 2nd block, DOUBLING your turnover chance — if you don't NEED the 2nd block, use a plain Block player instead. Minimize the number of dice rolled per turn." Echoed #06 04:08 ("roll the absolute minimum dice to make the ball unsackable"), #26 23:27. This is subtly DIFFERENT from sequencing (R1) and reckless-block (R5): it's about not taking OPTIONAL successful-looking actions at all. R5 partially prices it (each extra block pays its own p_turnover) but the Frenzy-specific "second forced block" is a concrete sub-case. Candidate: a Frenzy-aware tweak to R5, or just confirm R5's per-block charge already covers it.

- **N2. "Safe corner" / threat-grid-overlap parking.** #26 43:48: click each opponent, union their movement+blitz threat ranges, find the square no opponent can reach, run the carrier there. This is the *positive* construction whose *negative* is R6 (carrier-exposure). Strongly suggests the obs-v4 should expose a per-acting-player "min-opponent-reach" / threat-union plane if it doesn't already — ties directly to D119(3)'s open obs-v4 question.

- **N3. Wizard/positional-hazard clustering (out of current scope but flagged).** Repeated across #01, #08, #09, #10, #14, #16, #29, #31: don't clump ≥3 players (Fireball template), don't carry near the sideline (Lightning-Bolt-into-surf), keep the carrier deep when the opponent holds a Wizard, push the ball into the OPPONENT's half early so a bolt-drop can't be converted to a defensive TD (#31 02:10). Inducements/wizards aren't in our engine's training scope yet (CLAUDE.md tasks 23–24), so this is a FUTURE curriculum note, not a near-term term.

- **N4. "Activate volatile players EARLY."** #31 05:40: activate Big Guys / Really-Stupid / Bonehead pieces early in the turn on non-critical actions, so if they fail you can still re-plan the turn to cover the gap. A turn-ordering nuance ORTHOGONAL to risk-sequencing (it's about information-revelation timing, not turnover-exposure). Hard to price cleanly; a BC/demo-bank pattern.

- **N5. "Mini-games" board decomposition + "two dice on the ball" puzzle framing.** #26 05:11, #31 14:10, #32 — experts decompose the pitch into independent zones and treat "how do I get 2 dice on the carrier" as the recurring core puzzle. This is a STATE-REPRESENTATION / curriculum hint (the demo bank could over-sample "2-dice-on-the-carrier-available" states), not a reward term.

- **N6. Kickoff sweeper/safety discipline.** #08 21:02, #22 20:31, #29 20:31 — leaving the backfield empty on a receiving setup is a recurring blunder punished by Blitz!/deep-kick. The R-memo argues the critic should learn this via R6/ball-loss back-propagating to the setup action (memo §5), rather than a hard "sweeper" reward. Corpus agrees it's a setup-phase consequence, but it's worth a CANARY (track empty-backfield setups vs Blitz!-conceded-TDs).

### Part D — prioritized next-experiment candidates (given pressure-test + D117-A caveat + this corpus)

Ranked by (corpus corroboration strength) × (cheapness/representability) × (NOT-already-stale-per-D117-A):

1. **R6 (carrier-exposure, min-dodges-to-reach == 0/marked, −0.05, endzone-dash-exempt) — BUILD IT.** This is the single highest-value candidate: it is the formation-problem (D119-2) answer, the cage/screen corroboration (Part-A 2/4) target, the "safe corner" positive's negative (N2), the leading indicator of the −0.5 sack (fixes credit assignment a full turn earlier), and — critically — it is NOT touched by the D117-A "D46 is resolved" caveat (it prices POSITIONING, not gfi/dodge volume). The R-memo already specs it as the priority of its positional trio and it reuses the existing possession-knob settled-turn hook. Cheapest high-impact build in the set. A/B vs the league6 lineage; canary = sack-rate-against (should fall), stall-length, contact-rate.

2. **R11 (clock-aware potential Φ from FUMBBL win-prob) — DESIGN/FIT next.** The tempo/Turn-8-stall doctrine is the most universal theme in the corpus (every replay pack) and directly addresses the D112 mirror-stall the pressure test attributed to the symmetric possession annuity. It's heavier (needs the FUMBBL-corpus win-prob fit, must retire or decouple the possession feature to avoid double-count) so it's phase-2, but it's the principled fix for "the annuity is zero-sum-symmetric." Also unaffected by the D46 caveat.

3. **Extend k_seq to dodge/GFI/pickup declarations (the pressure-test #1 gap) — DO, but DEMOTE in urgency per D117-A.** The corpus' strongest, most-repeated single lesson IS risk-sequencing (Part-A 1), and the code gap is real (`k_seq` block-only, verified). BUT D117-A shows all three current arms already run gfi/dodge AT-OR-BELOW human — the pathology this was meant to cure appears gone in the league6 lineage. So: keep it queued as a CHEAP knob-extension A/B (it's the same `pending_safe_activations` machinery the block path already has), but it is no longer the #1 fire — run it AFTER R6, and gate the decision on whether a fresh tournament (D109-A) shows the current lineage actually plays sequencing-clean or just gfi-quiet. If gfi/dodge stay human-like without it, this is a no-op and the discriminator (D46) says don't add scaffolding for a non-problem.

Deliberately NOT recommended as near-term reward terms (corpus-confirmed as value-net / curriculum jobs, not per-step rewards): reroll-budgeting beyond R9 (Part-A 7), passing precondition-chains (Part-B D119-1, low-value in BB2025), wizard-clustering (N3, out of engine scope). Crowd-surf terms (`surf_*`) are already CODED — flipping them on is a separate cheap A/B if removal-via-surf is judged under-explored, but they're default-off by design and the corpus treats surfing as opportunistic, not foundational.

UNCERTAIN / for the lead to sanity-check: (i) several packs (#08, #22, #29) analyze the SAME Chaos-vs-Skaven game — corroboration "across packs" there is partly the same source video, so weight it as one observation, not three. (ii) #29's own header flags a title/transcript mismatch (labeled Amazons-vs-DarkElf, content is the Chaos-Skaven game) — I cited its content as-is. (iii) I did not independently re-derive the R-memo's claim that R6–R8 reuse an existing settled-turn hook cleanly — that's the memo's assertion; verify the hook before scoping the R6 build. (iv) the D119(3) obs-v4 question (are probability/threat planes per-ACTING-player or generic?) remains open and is a prerequisite for both N2 and any skill-conditional-pickup work — still worth the quick code-read flagged in D119.**

**D120 — RECONCILIATION: codex + Opus pressure-test + D117-A + D121, final prioritized verdict (research, 2026-06-15).** Two independent code-level reviews (Opus, recorded inline this session; codex, `.codex-reviews/d119-article-pressure-test.md`, ~2h runtime) both audited the reward economy against the same 9-principle article. AGREEMENT is strong on STRUCTURE: both confirm `k_seq` is block-declarations-only (codex: extend to `BB_A_STEP`/dodge/GFI/pickup/catch/pass/handoff, skill-aware, as "the most promising reward-side fix for D46"); both confirm formation/caging/screening has NO representation and that a simple scalar reward is the WRONG tool for it (Opus: "needs new machinery, a formation-shape potential"; codex independently: "likely needs BC anchoring, demo-bank curricula, or auxiliary imitation targets... brittle and team-style dependent" -- codex arrived at the SAME "this isn't a reward-knob problem" conclusion via a different route); both confirm skill-agnostic ball-acquisition explains D119's passing gap; both confirm re-roll management is NOT a per-step-reward problem (codex: "needs decision-time EV or learned/imitation priors that understand board context").

**D123 — R6 REFINEMENT (Alex, 2026-06-15): graduated + adversarial exposure, staged as v1/v1.5/v2 in `docs/reward-design-coaching-wisdom.md`.** Before any R6 implementation starts (R6 was just identified as the 4-way pressure-test consensus #1, D120), Alex flagged that the table-row spec (binary "0-dodges-or-marked = -0.05") is too coarse in two ways:

(1) **Dodge-count isn't binary risk** -- "you can position a player so someone needs ONE dodge to get to you, and that's fine [relatively]. That's objectively worse than THREE dodges, or needing multiple GFIs." 1-dodge, 3-dodge, and GFI-gated access represent very different P(opponent actually converts the threat this turn) -- compounding independent-roll failure probabilities, plus GFI paths carry the ATTACKER's own turnover risk too. **R6v1.5** (addendum, same BFS as v1, richer scoring): price `-scale * P(best opponent reaches+dislodges carrier this turn)` using the SAME probability-pricing philosophy as `k_kd`/`k_value`/`k_ball`, replacing hand-picked dodge-count tiers with a continuous probability. Reproduces Alex's ordering naturally (0-dodge >> 1-dodge > 3-dodge > GFI-gated ~ 0).

(2) **Screeners are displaceable, not fixed obstacles** -- Alex's example: a single Dodge-skill Halfling "providing" a 1-dodge buffer for a ball carrier, standing next to a Block/Mighty-Blow/Grab Chaos Warrior about to throw 3 red dice. "You're not actually safe -- he's just getting displaced." VERIFIED in code: `BB_SK_GRAB` (`proc_block.c:447`) cancels the defender's Side Step, so a Grab attacker CHOOSES the push direction -- can deliberately clear the screener out of the lane. v1/v1.5's BFS treats friendly pieces as fixed obstacles; the TRUE exposure when a screener is one good block away from being cleared is much higher than the nominal dodge-count suggests. **R6v2** (addendum, a separate later iteration): for screeners whose removal would reduce `min_dodges`, run the existing `bb_blockev` routine on their adjacent opponents to fold `P(screener cleared) * P(then reach carrier)` into the exposure. Genuinely harder (1-ply lookahead, different timing than k_kd's block-declaration hook) -- ship with its own canary (does the v1.5 policy rely on screens a competent opponent would blow through? divergence between priced-exposure and actual sack rate is the trip-wire).

STAGING: v1 ships first per D120/the R-memo's A/B-3 (unchanged -- it IS Alex's "first thing: make it so no dodges can get you"). v1.5 is a low-risk in-place refinement (same BFS, different scoring fn) once v1's canaries are read. v2 is gated on evidence, not built speculatively. Full technical detail in `docs/reward-design-coaching-wisdom.md`'s new "R6 refinement" subsection (inserted between R6's and R7's implementation sketches).**

**D123-A — R6 spec corrected (v1: dual dodge/GFI counters) + R6v2 reframed around per-screener "fragility" to tame the combinatorial-displacement problem (Alex, 2026-06-15).** Both edits landed directly in `docs/reward-design-coaching-wisdom.md` (the R6/R6-refinement sections), this entry records the WHY.

**v1 correction (folded into R6's table row + sketch, not a new version)**: the original BFS labeled GFI-only squares as "free" (non-dodge), so a path needing 0 dodges but 1+ GFIs scored `min_dodges==0` -- the SAME full -0.05 as a true free walk-up. This is backwards from Alex's stated minimum bar: *"make them dodge to get to you, OR make them GFI to get to you -- do those things at a minimum."* Fix: BFS now tracks `(min_dodges, min_gfis)` as two counters; "free walk-up" (full -0.05) requires BOTH zero. One-line change to edge-cost bookkeeping, but load-bearing -- without it v1 doesn't actually implement what was asked.

**v2 reframed**: Alex correctly identified that the original v2 sketch (Grab lets the attacker choose the push square) is only ONE of FOUR ways a screener stops being an obstacle: (a) even non-Grab pushes have up to 3 attacker-chosen destination squares; (b) Blitz changes the attack angle, rotating which 3 squares those are; (c) Frenzy forces recursive follow-up blocks, each with its own (a)+(b) branching; (d) a no-push knockdown (Both Down/Defender Down) leaves the screener prone IN PLACE, removing its TZ without any push geometry. The cross-product is exponential -- "a really big exploding combinatorial problem" as stated.

THE REFRAME (avoids enumeration entirely): compute, once per screener, a single scalar `fragility = P(this piece stops projecting a TZ on the relevant square this turn, via knockdown-in-place OR being pushed off, vs its single best CURRENT adjacent threat)` -- reusing the existing per-pair `bb_blockev` math (same inputs as k_kd/k_value/k_ball, no new EV engine). Feed `fragility` into the BFS as a CONTINUOUS edge-cost (fragile screener ~ free square; solid screener ~ full obstacle) rather than enumerating where pieces end up. This is "is this obstacle solid" as ONE NUMBER from EXISTING machinery.

SPLIT: **v2a** (shippable) = fragility restricted to current adjacency, covers (a)+(d) -- already catches Alex's literal Halfling/Chaos-Warrior example (Warrior is already adjacent, no repositioning needed to matter). **v2b** (research, not scoped) = folding in (b) Blitz-angle + (c) Frenzy-chains -- if ever needed, via SAMPLING (Monte Carlo rollouts a la `tools/blockev_mc.c`), not exact enumeration, and only if v2a's canary proves insufficient (a SECOND, more specific trip-wire than v2's general one).

STAGING UNCHANGED: v1 (corrected) ships first, unblocked by any of this -- it IS "make them dodge or GFI to get to you, at minimum." v1.5 and v2a/v2b remain staged refinements per D123.**

**D126 — R6v1 ARCHITECTURE RECONCILED: no blocker, revision pass applied, implementation-ready (Opus architect + Opus review + Codex review + lead review, 2026-06-15).** Three independent reviews of `.codex-impl/brief-r6v1-carrier-exposure.md` converge:

**Priority item (the `p->moved` reset-timing question) is CLEARED, 3-way confirmed.** Codex's trace is the most precise: `turn_start` for the about-to-act team `1-t` (resetting `moved=0`/`rushes=0`, `proc_turn.c:9,23`) runs INSIDE the same `bb_advance` loop that processed team `t`'s turn-end, BEFORE `bb_advance` returns control to Puffer (`bb_match.c:255`, `proc_match.c:56-63`, `proc_turn.c:101-122`) -- so by the time the settled-turn-end hook (`bloodbowl.h:1894`) observes the flip, `1-t`'s `moved`/`rushes` are ALREADY zeroed. `budget = p->ma - p->moved == p->ma` holds. (Codex's residual note: if the engine ever auto-settles through MULTIPLE turn-flips before the next decision, this hook-style hits an EXISTING `reward_possession`-class limitation, not R6-specific -- out of scope.)

**BONUS FINDING (Opus): `bbe_macro_reach` (`bloodbowl.h:794-867`) already exists** -- a proven 2D Dijkstra over the pitch (movement budget, obstacles via `m->grid`, dodge-on-exit, GFI boundary), built for v5 path-actions. Resolves the spec's proposed 3D `(x,y,squares_used)` state space (use 2D, matching this precedent) AND Q5 (Sprint via `bb_max_rushes`, `bb_skills.c:11-13`, already exists).

**CONCRETE FIXES (revision appendix added to the spec, §8) -- all SMALL, none requires re-architecture:**
1. File references: `bb_types.h`/`bb_match.h`, not `bb_state.h` (doesn't exist) -- codex.
2. **SIGN BUG (codex catch, real)**: spec's `-0.05` example + `-=` sketch double-negates = REWARDS exposure. Fix: positive magnitudes (`reward_carrier_exposure = 0.05`), subtracted -- matches `reward_rush_cost` exactly.
3. **AGGREGATION BUG (codex catch, real)**: §1.4's "lex-min `(dodges,gfis)` across opponents, then threshold" can hide a different opponent's `{1,0}` (one-dodge, soft-tier) behind another opponent's `{0,2}` (zero-dodge-two-GFI, lex-smaller, scores as "safe" under thresholding). Fix: compute boolean ORs across opponents -- `any_free = OR(dodges==0 && gfis==0)`, `any_one_roll = OR(dodges+gfis==1)` -- then `full = marked || any_free`, `soft = !full && any_one_roll`. Replaces the single-lex-min-then-threshold aggregation.
4. Q8 extended (codex): exclude ROOTED opponents from the BFS-movers list too (`can_step` already rejects `BB_PF_ROOTED`, `proc_move.c:45`), not just the carrier's exemption -- rooted-but-adjacent opponents still mark via the unchanged `bb_is_marked` short-circuit.
5. Architecture: `bb_reachability.c` lives in `engine/` (Opus's testability rationale) but MUST be added to Puffer's engine-amalgamation include list (`bloodbowl.h:61` directly includes engine `.c` files -- codex's catch, the spec omitted this wiring step). Core algorithm adapted from `bbe_macro_reach`'s proven 2D approach (Opus).
6. Q3: carrier's endzone-exemption budget = `ma + bb_max_rushes(m, carrier)` (Sprint-aware, both reviewers converged here independently), gated on `!BB_PF_ROOTED` (Q8).
7. Q1 (`is_blitz`): keep dropped from v1's compute (Opus's "free adjacent access" reading matches §0's literal text), but RENAME the metric/comments away from "sack threat"/"blitz threat" framing to avoid implying blitz-cost semantics codex's reading would require -- documentation-only, no logic change.
8. Add a downed/prone-carrier test case (symmetric to the marked-opponent prone case) -- Opus.
9. Telemetry: `ep_carrier_exposed_full/soft` -- unanimous yes, capacity headroom confirmed (~36-37/64 keys used).
10. Fix the "tight cage" test case (codex): all-8-adjacent-occupied = UNREACHABLE, not "must dodge" -- use occupied corners + open-but-TZ'd adjacent squares to test the dodge-cost path.

**VERDICT**: implementation-ready after these 10 fixes (applied as a revision appendix to the spec, not a rewrite). **D128 — D124 A/B VERDICT (head-to-head, 2026-06-15): proven economy (league7b) BEATS statmatch-continued (league7) at matched 30B + same pool.** Both arms capped cleanly at 30.0B (league7 ~18:55 PDT, league7b ~19:22 PDT), both backed up to B2 (`league7_cap.bin`, `league7b_cap.bin`) and staged on japan. Ran the head-to-head on japan's judge GPU (`puffer match bloodbowl --load-model-path league7_cap.bin --load-enemy-model-path league7b_cap.bin --num-games 4096`): **`A=0.464 B=0.536 draw=0.460`** (A=league7=statmatch-continued, B=league7b=proven-economy). Score-style (half-draws split, the pufferl winrate convention): league7b 0.536 vs league7 0.464. Decisive-only: total decisive = 0.54, league7b won 0.306/0.54 = **56.7%** vs league7 0.234/0.54 = **43.3%**.

INTERPRETATION: this answers D124's question directionally — **the aggregate-stat-matching reward did NOT compound with the D111 pool lever; the settled v4 economy (possession annuity + k-half + dist potentials) is the stronger CONTINUED-training signal.** The conclusion is *strengthened* by the warm-start confound cutting AGAINST it: league7 warm-started from statmatch1 (D122 ladder #1, +326.5) — the HIGHER-rated checkpoint — while league7b warm-started from league6 (#2, +248.3), yet league7b still won. So statmatch1's D122 #1 placement was most likely a fresh-perturbation/measurement artifact (D122's own "soft #1" flag: 5B vs 15-28B, lopsided floor-node wins) rather than the statmatch reward producing a durably stronger policy. Statmatch as a one-shot perturbation reward may still have value; statmatch as a continued-training objective does not beat the proven economy here.

CAVEATS (this is PRELIMINARY pending confirmation): (i) single head-to-head, n=4096 games but 46% draws → decisive n≈2200, so the 56.7/43.3 split has real but not overwhelming separation; (ii) no full-ladder Elo yet — league7/league7b haven't been round-robined against the anchor set, so their absolute ladder positions (and whether league7b is the new #1) are unconfirmed; (iii) warm-start + reward differ together (not a single-variable isolation), though the confound direction strengthens rather than threatens the conclusion. A Codex review of this verdict + a full anchored-ladder extension (round-robin both new caps vs anchors on japan/2070) are the confirmation steps before D128 is treated as final. Per CLAUDE.md, the verdict is NOT yet a ship recommendation — but it does not block league8, which tests R6v1 on the proven economy regardless of the statmatch comparison.**

**D128-A — CODEX REVIEW of D128: H2H win is real, but the CAUSAL claim is not proven and "statmatch-reward is dead" is PREMATURE (2026-06-15, `.codex-reviews/d128-verdict-review.md`).** Read + accepted. Codex agrees the head-to-head result is statistically solid (league7b beats league7 with confidence) and that the proven v4 economy is the correct DEFAULT mainline (so league8's economy choice stands). But it correctly tempers three things D128 over-stated:

1. **The warm-start "confound strengthens the conclusion" argument is WEAKER than D128 claimed.** D128 argued league7 losing despite warm-starting from the higher-rated statmatch1 (#1) is evidence AGAINST statmatch. Codex's correction: *starting Elo is not a sufficient control for CONTINUATION potential* — a checkpoint can be higher-rated yet have less headroom to improve under further training. So league7's loss is "additional negative evidence for this exact recipe" but does NOT eliminate the warm-start confound. Compounding this: D122's league6 was a 28.03B checkpoint (the D116 KeyError ate ~2B); if the missing 2B would have raised league6, then "statmatch1 was the clearly stronger warm-start" is even less secure — which weakens the confound-cuts-against-me argument further, not the H2H itself.

2. **D124-A's "same pool" is only true for the INITIAL preseed banks (pool-drift confound).** The selfplay code uses the preseed dir as the LIVE pool dir, so interval/winrate snapshots accumulate per-arm after launch (`tools/build_league.py`, `training/selfplay_league.patch:17`). league7 and league7b therefore trained against IDENTICAL starting pools but DIVERGING full distributions (each accumulating its own statmatch-/v4-flavored snapshots). Fine for "which full recipe trains better," a real confound for "which reward signal alone is better." (This is the same 25-bank-vs-8-bank issue I noted for league8's pool — the accumulated snapshots, not just the seeds.)

3. **The 2×2 is incomplete — only 2 of 4 corners tested.** D124 tested league6+v4 (=league7b) vs statmatch1+statmatch (=league7) — the diagonal. The missing arms: **league6+statmatch** (isolates the reward change against league7b's OWN warm-start — the single most valuable missing cell) and **statmatch1+v4** (tests whether statmatch1 was a good perturbation worth handing back to the proven economy). Without these, "v4 reward is causally superior to statmatch continuation" is unproven.

REVISED D128 STATUS (per Codex's recommendation, accepted): proven v4 economy / league7b lineage is the default next mainline (unchanged — league8 correct). D128 = **strong negative DIRECTIONAL evidence against the EXACT league7 statmatch-continued recipe**, NOT proof that human-stat-matching rewards are dead as a family (D114/D118-A's formulation is one engineered instance — symmetric, match-level, terminal, non-PBRS, possession-off; a failure has many candidate diagnoses). Also note: "56.7/43.3 decisive" overstates the gap — the score-style 0.536 vs 0.464 (~+25 Elo) is the honest framing for ladder decisions; use that, not the decisive-only split. Confirmation order before any "statmatch continuation is dead" entry: (1) full anchored ladder for league7+league7b incl. the direct row + a reversed-order/fresh-seed H2H rerun as cheap insurance; (2) ladder statmatch2 when it caps (it's the D118-A CORRECTED formulation — the most relevant statmatch data point); (3) train league6+statmatch (matched-warm-start reward isolation); (4) optionally statmatch1+v4. Tasks #53/#54 updated to carry this order.**

3. **BUT "statmatch-as-reward is dead" is REFUTED — exactly as Codex cautioned.** statmatch2 (the SAME statmatch reward + D118-A formulation, but MIRROR selfplay, 8B, no hard pool) is **#2 at 161.3 — above league7b**, and only ~8 Elo below statmatch1 (minimal regression from its warm-start). So the statmatch reward in a mirror/short regime produces a TOP node; it's the combination **statmatch reward × hard-opponents pool × 30B** that regressed league7. Plausible mechanism: the hard pool forces adaptations that the human-stat-matching penalty actively fights (the penalty pulls toward human aggregate distributions while the pool rewards whatever beats strong opponents — a tug-of-war that over-regularizes over 30B), whereas mirror selfplay has no such conflict.

**REVISED DOCTRINE:** (i) D128/D129's "proven economy is the safe default mainline" STANDS (league7b #3 is the strongest 30B-hard-pool node). (ii) statmatch-as-reward is NOT abandoned — statmatch2's #2 placement REOPENS it as a promising MIRROR/short-continuation perturbation (candidate: a statmatch3 mirror run, longer, or statmatch×pool at SHORTER horizons to find where the conflict kicks in). (iii) statmatch1 remains the single strongest checkpoint (#1) — the natural warm-start for future arms per D107-A (league8 used league7b #3, fine but not optimal; not changing a live run). (iv) league7 is a dead-end recipe; do not continue it. CAVEATS: ladder omits league6b/tdmaniac1/stakes1 as league7/7b/statmatch2 opponents (rig lacked them — they're anchored via the D122 graph, so their Elo is still placed, just with fewer direct edges to the new nodes); the statmatch2-vs-league7 comparison still co-varies pool AND steps (not a clean single-variable isolation of "why league7 regressed" — that needs a statmatch+pool+8B or statmatch+mirror+30B arm). A Codex sanity-check of this nuanced finding is a worthwhile follow-up before it hardens into doctrine, but the full-ladder evidence is far stronger than D128's single H2H.**

**D133 — BACKLOG (Alex design, 2026-06-16): R12 = defensive scoring-lane threat — the DUAL of R6v1 carrier-exposure.** Alex flagged a real asymmetry: R6v1 prices only OUR ball protection (when WE hold the ball, is the carrier reachable without a dodge/GFI?). There is NO corresponding DEFENSIVE term — when the OPPONENT holds the ball, have we left a free lane to our endzone? Nothing currently prices defensive positioning at all (why untrained defenders clump/ball-chase instead of screening). The symmetry is sound: if pricing "is my carrier exposed" drives offense, pricing "can the enemy score for free" should drive sane defense.

**v1 (Alex's stated minimum = one turn):** reuse R6v1's `bb_reach_field_compute` (already a `(dodges,gfis)` Dijkstra from any mover to every square) as the DUAL — mover = enemy ball carrier (fires only when opponent holds the ball, mirroring R6v1's gate), target = our defensive endzone LINE (`x = bb_endzone_x(enemy_team)`), classify min `(dodges,gfis)` cost over that line within carrier `MA + bb_max_rushes`: `(0,0)`→FREE WALK-IN (defense breached), total==1→soft (one dodge OR GFI to score), ≥2/unreachable→screened. Fire at MY-turn-end when the opponent holds the ball (symmetric to R6v1's own-turn-end). Connection: R6v1's endzone-EXEMPTION already does a CRUDE version (Chebyshev distance ≤ MA+rushes, but IGNORES tackle zones) — R12 is that upgraded to real screen-aware reachability.

**Why potentially HIGHER value than R6v1:** offense exposure = one opponent reaching one carrier; defense = carrier reaching a whole LINE, so a SINGLE hole anywhere breaches the screen. "Cover every lane" is strictly harder than "protect one piece" and is exactly where RL defenders fail — a free-lane penalty would directly teach screen/deep-safety discipline.

**REFINED STAGING (Alex, 2026-06-16) — the v2 split is the key insight: carrier-only stays POLYNOMIAL, only v3 explodes:**
- **v1** — binary free-lane (0-dodge/0-GFI for the current carrier this turn). One Dijkstra.
- **v1.5** — graded by the NUMBER of dodges/GFIs required (continuous threat probability vs binary). Same engine, richer cost readout. Mirrors R6v1.5's graduated-probability refinement → keeps offense/defense symmetric.
- **v2** — two-turn, **CARRIER ONLY** (no passing, no handoffs): can THIS carrier reach the endzone in two of its own activations? Still SINGLE-PIECE pathfinding, just a larger budget (≈ 2×(MA+rushes), counting dodges/GFIs en route) — polynomial, NO explosion, because the ball never changes hands so no new movers enter. Catches the most common real defensive failure ("you left a two-move-deep hole"). Caveat to make explicit: v2 implicitly assumes the defense does NOT re-screen between the opponent's two turns (in real BB you'd get an intervening turn to plug it) → v2 slightly OVER-estimates threat, but that's the SAFE direction for a shaping signal (teaches "don't even leave a two-move lane"); modeling the re-screen turns it into a game-tree, defeating the point. Canary, not exact-solve.
- **v3** — the EXPONENTIAL case: any handoff or pass. THIS is what blows up — the ball can transfer to a fresh piece (new mover, own MA) or teleport via a throw, so it's no longer single-piece pathfinding but a search over which teammate gets the ball and from where. Defer; if ever built, via SAMPLING (à la tools/blockev_mc.c), only if v2's canary proves insufficient.

STAGING DISCIPLINE matches R6 exactly (v1 → v1.5 → v2a/v2b). Ship v1 first once the R6v1 line (D132) is validated — offense + defense from the same reachability core. Implementation cost is low given R6v1 landed; v1/v1.5/v2 all reuse `bb_reach_field_compute` with no new EV engine.

**D133-A — R12 REFRAMED (Alex, 2026-06-16): measure PLAYERS not the BALL — dissolves the v3 exponential entirely; the simpler model is also MORE defensively correct.** Alex's key insight: humans don't compute the ball's exponential branching to assess scoring threat — they look at which OPPOSING PLAYERS can get downfield. Shift the question from "where can the ball go?" (branches through handoffs/passes = the v3 blowup) to "who can reach my endzone by movement?" (per-player, O(players)). LEGITIMATE because ball-delivery is cheap and player movement is the binding constraint — a fast deep player is a scoring threat BEFORE it holds the ball (the ball can be handed/thrown to it). Measuring players instead of the ball DELETES the need to model ball-transfer, which was the entire source of the v3 explosion.

**THE METRIC (replaces the carrier-reachability v1):** per opposing player `p`: `reach_per_turn(p) = MA(p) + max_GFIs(p)` (≈+2, +3 w/ Sprint); `turns_to_score(p) = ceil(dist_to_our_endzone(p) / reach_per_turn(p))`; count `n_threats_1turn`(≤1) and `n_threats_2turn`(≤2). Two turns = "same thing, ×2 budget" — O(players), one subtract + divide each, NO Dijkstra, NO ball model. **Mitigation = the defensive job:** a MARKED deep player has reduced effective reach (must dodge to leave, costing tempo + turnover risk), so the live signal = **unmitigated deep threats** = count players who can score in ≤N turns AND are unmarked. Minimizing that = "mark/cover the deepest movers" = the human heuristic; policy learns to body the fast deep piece instead of clumping on the ball.

**WHY MORE CORRECT THAN THE CARRIER-CENTRIC VERSION:** the defensive failure vs fast teams isn't the carrier strolling through your screen — it's an UNCOVERED DEEP RECEIVER your carrier-lane screen never accounted for. Player-centric "how many pieces can get deep" is the right object. HONEST TRADE: drop tackle-zone-aware PATH precision (raw distance vs screened path) for ball-agnosticism + O(players) cost — but for deep coverage that's correct, because a screen between carrier and endzone does NOTHING to cover an open downfield receiver, so path-cost was measuring the wrong thing. Marking, not lane-pathing, is how you address a deep mover.

**SUPERSEDES the reachability-dual as R12 v1.** Revised ladder: v1 = unmitigated deep-threat count (1-turn); v1.5 = graded (margin = reach − distance, and/or degree-of-marking); v2 = 2-turn (just ×2 reach budget); v3 (handoff/pass) DISSOLVED — never needed. Also a natural **obs FEATURE, not just reward** — "this enemy is a 1-turn scoring threat" is exactly the state a defender needs (per-player threat flag in the entity rows). The reachability-dual framing (D133 above) stays as the OPTIONAL lane-denial complement (cover the carrier's walk-in path) but is secondary to deep-mover coverage.

**D135 — R12 v1 IMPLEMENTED (Opus agent, 2026-06-16, Alex-authorized parallel build): per-player defensive scoring-lane threat, default-0.0 inert, 374 tests pass.** Per D133-A (the per-player reframe). Extended `engine/src/bb_reachability.c`/`.h` with `bb_def_threat_turns` (per-player: reach = MA + `bb_max_rushes`; dist to the player's OWN scoring endzone = our defensive endzone via `bb_endzone_x(BB_TEAM_OF(slot))`; ceil(dist/reach); −1 sentinel for ineligible off-pitch/down/rooted/immobile) + `bb_def_threat_eval(m, team)` (counts the team's OPPONENTS who are UNMITIGATED — `!bb_is_marked` — and reach in ≤1 / ≤2 turns). LEAD REVIEW (sign/team/endzone-direction/soft-disjointness) = all correct. Default-0.0 = fully inert (hook guarded, eval not called when off) — safe to land like R6v1. **D136 — R12 DUAL REVIEW (Codex + adversarial Opus, 2026-06-16, Alex-requested pre-live): geometry CORRECT, but ONE BLOCKER (kickoff-gate) + 2 follow-ups before the live arm. Both reviews converged independently; Codex empirically reproduced the bug.** Verdict from BOTH: NOT ready to train as-is.

**BLOCKER (both, HIGH) — R12 fires on setup/kickoff active-team flips, not only settled own-turn-ends.** R6v1's hook was safe only because `bb_carrier_exposure_eval` early-returns unless the just-ended team holds the ball — that ball-gate doubled as a turn-boundary filter. R12 is ball-agnostic BY DESIGN (D133-A), so it inherits the generic `active_team`-flip hook's broader semantics and charges the KICKING team for the receiver's SETUP formation at the setup→kickoff flip. Codex's runtime probe against the exact `c_step` path: `seed=2 pre-turn R12 reward=(-0.14,0.00) active 0->1 before=SETUP after=KICKOFF ep=0/7 ball=0` — a penalty with turn counters still 0/0, ball off-pitch. Also reachable via kickoff `Charge!` active-team changes (proc_match.c:594/701). FIX (Codex's exact pattern): capture, BEFORE `bb_apply_trusted`, whether the pre-apply stack is inside a real `BB_PROC_TEAM_TURN` for the active team (`bbe_in_team_turn` helper), and gate the R12 reward+telemetry block on it. Stack-based (not counter-based) so kickoff-event flips don't count.

**FOLLOW-UP 1 (Opus HIGH / Codex MEDIUM) — clamp-stacking from unbounded count.** R12's threat count is unbounded (~11); R12 lands on the same step as win/loss terminal bonus + possession + carrier-exposure. Opus's worst case: terminal LOSS + 8 deep threats ≈ −1.08 → clips the [−1,1] clamp (ini lines 35-40 warn about this), silently corrupting the loss gradient. Codex: R12-alone max 0.55 is under the clamp, but budget against same-step rewards. RESOLUTION: cap the charged count (`hard=min(n1,4)`, `soft=min(n2−n1,4)`) → bounds R12 at −0.20/−0.08, keeps the terminal stack inside [−1,1]; loses ~no fidelity (rarely >4 truly-unmarked 1-turn movers). Telemetry stays uncapped (true counts).

**FOLLOW-UP 2 (both) — no hook-level tests.** The 13 tests exercise the pure evaluator only; none drive `c_step`/the reward hook, so none would catch the gate bug. Add 2 Puffer-level tests: (a) setup→kickoff transition asserts NO R12 reward + no `ep_def_threats_*` increment before the first real team-turn end; (b) a controlled own-turn-end asserts `reward[t] == -(hard*scale + (n2-n1)*soft_scale)` and the telemetry increments.

**CONFIRMED CORRECT by both (ships as-is):** endzone direction (`bb_endzone_x(BB_TEAM_OF(slot))`, traced for home+away), sign (positive subtracted, no double-negate), soft-tier disjointness vs inclusive telemetry, integer ceil `(dist+reach-1)/reach`, eligibility filters (off-pitch/down/rooted/marked), `bb_is_marked` excluding no-TZ markers. Post-fix canary (both): watch contact rate / blocks / def-TDs-conceded for over-marking, and `ep_def_threats_1t/2t` dropping WHILE win-rate improves. Apply the gate (blocker) + cap + hook-tests, re-verify `make test`, THEN box-build for the live arm (still gated behind league9).

Setup→kickoff / `Charge!` flips have no TEAM_TURN frame → skipped; normal own-turn-end still fires. MUTATION-TESTED: neutering the gate → 179 failures incl. "R12 charged on opening setup/kickoff flip". R6v1 block untouched (its ball-held check already gates). (2) CAP: reward uses `min(n1,4)`/`min(n2−n1,4)`; telemetry records TRUE uncapped counts — bounds R12 at −0.20/−0.08 so the terminal-step stack stays inside [−1,1]. (3) TESTS: +4 engine (`bb_in_team_turn` seam true/false across team-turn vs setup/kickoff stack states; cap arithmetic) + a hook-level `--r12test` driving real `c_step` with the mutation check. `make clean && make test` 378/0, ASan/UBSan clean, default-0.0 still fully inert. **D141 — CONTACT-ECONOMY FINDING (Alex, watching BBTV, 2026-06-17): the league lineage trains with `injury_inflicted=0`, which removes the reward for the ENTIRE attrition game (blocking-for-removal AND fouling) — contradicting the canonical `run_league.sh` + the reward memo, which both specify injury ±0.15 / value_scaled 1. This reframes the "no defense" problem and demotes R12.** Chain of observation→diagnosis this session: (1) Alex on BBTV: "they literally don't play defense." (2) Telemetry confirms: blocks_thrown 6.8/game vs human 88.8 (−92%), block_2d_frac 0.44 vs 0.77 (under-throws FAVORABLE attacker's-choice blocks), block_2dred_frac 0.115 vs 0.017 (over-throws desperate ones), ~0 fouls (no foul telemetry surfaced). (3) Root insight (Alex): blocking is the COUPLED core of BOTH phases (offense blocks to make lanes/protect cage; defense blocks to slow cage/force turnover) — so when neither side contests, the whole melee collapses into a mutual non-aggression pact. This is a ~stable equilibrium: unilateral deviation toward contact doesn't pay (turnover risk + zero attrition reward + low marginal value in a fast score-trade), so MORE self-play TIME won't fix it (game-theory property, not exploration budget) — escaping needs an external perturbation. (4) Mechanism found: live league9 (and the league7→8→9 + statmatch lineage) launch with `--env.reward-injury-inflicted 0 --injury-taken 0 --injury-value-scaled 0`; NOT a resume regression (the ORIGINAL run_league9.sh had it 0 too, warm from league8_cap — the lineage carried injury=0 forward). The CANONICAL `tools/run_league.sh:190-191` has `injury_inflicted 0.15 / injury_taken -0.15 / value_scaled 1`; the reward memo (`docs/reward-design-coaching-wisdom.md:3,110`) lists injury ±0.15 as a SETTLED term and names injury-inflicted rate "the designated PASSIVITY CANARY." So zeroing it predicts EXACTLY the observed no-block/no-foul passivity — and the "fix" Alex remembers (injury 0.15 + value_scaled 1) exists in the canonical script + design but the mainline arms never actually ran it. Alex's fouling point (D141 trigger): a foul's only upside is the injury it causes (memo R3: "the injury knob pays the foul's upside +0.15 KO/CAS"); with injury=0 fouling is all-downside (send-off risk) no-upside → agent never fouls. CALIBRATION NUANCES before acting: (a) restoring injury 0.15 risks foul-SPAM unless the memo's R3 send-off PENALTY (designed, NOT implemented) prices the downside; (b) attrition reward is ~zero-sum in mirror self-play (D34) — teaches the SKILL, the winning EDGE needs asymmetry (→ the scripted contact opponent, doubling as the absolute-signal anchor the triple-review/D140 wanted); (c) D34/D39 documented the contact-vs-scoring tension — Profile-C k-values (k_kd 0.06/k_value 0.5) CURED never-blocking (D34) but crowded out scoring (tds 0.000) so they were HALVED (D39, live: k_kd 0.03/k_value 0.25); today's lineage scores FAR better than the D34/D39 era, so it can likely afford more contact reward now — that's the re-test. CONSOLIDATED EXPERIMENT (after league9 caps, gated on Alex): restore injury 0.15 + value_scaled 1, optionally raise k-knobs toward Profile-C, add R3 send-off penalty to keep fouling calibrated, A/B vs league9 watching the SCORING-retention canary (the D34 failure) + block volume/quality + foul rate climbing toward human. This is better-founded than R12 (D133/D140): R12 is a one-sided defensive bounty that doesn't restore the COUPLED offensive blocking and is distortive; the injury/contact economy is the actual collapsed lever, has prior proof it works (D34), and needs no new code. R12 stays demoted per D140.

**D142 — CONTACT-ECONOMY DESIGN PRESSURE-TEST (Codex + adversarial snickerdoodle EAP, 2026-06-17, Alex-requested): the strategic-blocking "threat-weighting" proposal is REWORKED — static threat scalar KILLED, no new positive contact term built, work sequenced behind the D141 injury-restore A/B (which was AMENDED to isolate its variable). Full design + verdict in `docs/contact-economy-design.md`.** Alex enriched the threat concept (assist/tackle-zone economy, Guard-cancels-your-assist, Diving Tackle, follow-up/tempo, matchup-dependent avoidance: elves dodge away from ST4 Block/MB chaos). Both reviewers converged: (1) the v0 STATIC threat scalar (ST+skills) is the trap — `bb_blockev` already computes ST-after-assists both directions (`bb_count_assists`), so threat is relational/contextual, not intrinsic; a Guard lino beside a Treeman outranks the Treeman but is irrelevant in the backfield. (2) The assist/TZ SECOND-ORDER value (knock the Guard so your other blocks become 2-dice) already has a designed home: R6v1.5/R6v2a "fragility" (reward memo 51-59) — penalty-side, bb_blockev-based, current-adjacency-only, no enumeration; don't build a parallel positive term. (3) SEQUENCING/ISOLATION (both, + snickerdoodle CRITICAL): my committed `run_league9_attrition_ab.sh` restored injury AND bumped k to Profile-C (0.06/0.5) simultaneously = two density increases → re-triggers the D39 contact-crowds-out-scoring failure + confounds the A/B. AMENDED to keep k-HALF (0.03/0.25); injury-restore + send-off is the single isolated variable; Profile-C k-bump is a separate gated follow-up. Also fixed: the script logged to /tmp/league9.log (would clobber the running arm) → /tmp/league9_attrition_ab.log. (4) Diving Tackle is NOT a bb_blockev skill (movement/dodge interrupt, proc_move.c) — belongs in R6v1.5 reach-path, not block-EV; doc corrected. (5) Goodhart: a "remove the assist-provider" bonus becomes an unconditional Guard-bounty unless folded into the SAME declaration's EV; per-knockdown/threat bounties reintroduce the D36/memo-line-92 "win the fight lose the game" LOS-punch-fest (D34: contact-seeking but tds 0.000; D39/D40: full-k harvested without win progress → halved). (6) snickerdoodle CRITICAL — NO measurable success criterion: attrition is zero-sum in mirror self-play, so win-rate can't move on assist-economy alone → need scenario boards (Guard/Treeman, elf-vs-chaos) + metrics (block-tier mix, dodge-away rate, sack rate, carrier exposure, voluntary follow-up, next-turn free-2D conceded, TD/win) AND the asymmetric/scripted-contact opponent (the D141 through-line). WHERE I PUSHED BACK: R6 is carrier-DEFENSE-centric and does NOT price OFFENSIVE assist-clearing or matchup-avoidance — so it's not literally a superset — but the right response is still "let it emerge from restored EV+win+a contact opponent, TEST via the scenario probe, don't add a term." Follow-up/tempo is the one behavior that likely won't emerge from current EV (no voluntary-post-push pricing) = the sole future explicit-term candidate, gated on the probe. NET PLAN: (a) isolated D141 injury-restore A/B after league9 caps [ready: tools/run_league9_attrition_ab.sh + R3 send-off, committed]; (b) scenario-eval harness + scripted contact opponent (doubles as the D140 absolute-signal anchor); (c) only then, if the probe shows a real hole, extend R6v2a (defense) / add a tempo term — NEVER a static scalar or positive contact bounty. R12 (D140) and this both demoted to "gated experiments behind controls," consistent.

**D145 — KICKOFF "always touchback" is a LEARNING gap, not an engine bug (Alex observation on BBTV, 2026-06-18). The center-square tactic is faithfully modeled and the agent CAN select it; nothing teaches it to.** Alex: kicking team always touches back; the dead-center of the receiving half is the unique zero-touchback-risk placement (without Kick) because a max D6 scatter can't leave the half or go off-pitch. Investigation (subagent, file:line verified): (1) PLACEMENT is a real agent decision — `BB_A_KICK_TARGET` (bb_actions.h:23), kicking team chooses (proc_match.c:644), legal = EVERY square of the receiving half (proc_match.c:759-768, ~195 squares), encoded in the 391-wide spatial square head (each square independently maskable). (2) SCATTER = single D6 distance + D8 direction (proc_match.c:648-665); Kick skill halves it. NOT inflated. (3) TOUCHBACK fires correctly (proc_match.c:619-623/694-705): ball off-pitch OR in the kicking team's half → receiving team gives ball to any standing player. Matches BB2025. (4) CENTER-SQUARE math confirmed in our model: home-kicking safe center = x=19,y=7 (away-kicking x=6,y=7); max D6=6 from center reaches at most x=13/25, y=1/13 — all on-pitch, all in the receiving half. Zero touchback risk, exactly as real BB. (5) Agent CAN select center (distinct legal maskable square). VERDICT: pure LEARNING gap — placement is a genuine policy choice over ~195 squares, most carrying touchback risk, and **nothing rewards placement quality or penalizes touchback**, so an under-trained/exploratory placement head touches back most of the time. FIX CANDIDATE: a small `reward_kickoff_touchback` penalty charged to the KICKING team when its kickoff touches back — clean + targeted (touchback is unambiguously bad for the kicker; kickoff placement is a single isolated decision with a clear correct answer = low distortion risk, unlike positional shaping). Fold into a future arm (NOT the live attrition A/B). Alternative: leave to emerge from longer training (slower, uncertain). Recommend the penalty — it's the cleanest "teach the obvious tactic" signal and the mechanism is fully there for the agent to exploit.

**D146 — Two BBTV-observed behaviors diagnosed (Alex, 2026-06-18): (1) "blitz but no block" = REAL ENGINE BUG (missing reachability gate on Blitz declaration); (2) "grail knight oscillation" = the known over-rush policy pathology, faithfully rendered (NOT a bug).** 
**(1) BLITZ BUG.** BB2025 (`docs/vendor/bloodbowlbase/.../the_game_of_blood_bowl/index.html:7448`): declaring a Blitz MUST nominate a target the player can REACH (incl. Rush squares); may NOT declare if no opponent is reachable. The block itself is NOT mandatory once declared ("never required to perform the Block Action"). OUR ENGINE: `proc_turn.c:354-355` offers Blitz whenever `!m->blitz_used` with NO target arg and NO reachability check (contrast `proc_turn.c:351` BLOCK, gated on adjacency). So a player can legally declare a Blitz with ZERO reachable opponents → necessarily ends with no block = ILLEGAL in BB2025. `bb_reachability.c` exists (R12 uses it) but isn't wired into blitz-declare legality. This is a validation-layer miss (the kind the deferred FFB differential would catch). FIX: gate the Blitz declaration in `bb_legal_actions`/proc_turn on ≥1 reachable opponent (MA + max rush, dodge/GFI-path aware); do NOT force the block (keep END_ACTIVATION available). Engine change → changes the legal-action mask → goldens will change (expected, D6) → goes into the NEXT build, not the live attrition A/B. 
**(2) OSCILLATION (m_1781768323).** Macro-moves are OFF in the league9 STEPWISE lineage (server.py `--macro` defaults off; v5 macro retired D93), so the back-and-forth-then-GFI-turnover is genuine per-step policy choices = the documented over-rush/positional-mispricing pathology (D46 gfi 33/game vs human 17; D141 blocks 6.8 vs 88.8). NOT an engine bug, NOT a stream artifact. Only the reward-economy work fixes it — the live D144 attrition-restore A/B is the current attempt.

**D147 — REWARD AUDIT: decision-time (EV-at-declaration) vs outcome (post-dice) — 5 SHAPING TERMS VIOLATE THE CARDINAL RULE (Alex, 2026-06-18, after the attrition A/B's pathetic blocks_thrown 6.8→7.8).** Alex's principle: "reward the DECISION at decision time, then the dice roll — don't reward on injury (outcome)." Two parallel sub-agents audited every reward term for WHERE it fires relative to `bb_apply_trusted` (the dice) and WHAT it reads (EV/settled-state vs realized result). Verdict:
- **COMPLIANT (A, decision-time/EV/potential/geometry):** `k_kd/k_value/k_ball/k_seq` (priced from `bb_block_ev` EV at BB_A_BLOCK_TARGET, pre-dice — bloodbowl.h:1935-1964), `rush_cost` (declaration tax), `surf_inflicted/taken` (deterministic crowd-push, no dice laundered), `dist_ball/dist_endzone` (telescoping potentials), `carrier_exposure±soft` (R6 reachability geometry), `def_threat±soft` (R12 geometry), `setup_done/autofix` (pre-apply action read).
- **OBJECTIVE/terminal (C, outcome correct — it IS the goal):** `td`, `win`, `draw`, and `possession` annuity (zero-sum settled-turn-boundary mini-terminal, not dice shaping).
- **VIOLATORS (B, outcome-based shaping — MUST convert to decision-time):**
  1. **`injury_inflicted/taken/value_scaled`** (bloodbowl.h:2213-2241) — read the realized KO/CAS box AFTER apply. THE textbook anti-pattern: two identical 2d+Block declarations pay wildly different rewards based on injury-dice variance. FIX: price `ev.p_def_removed` (inflicted) / `ev.p_att_removed` (taken), cost-weighted when value_scaled, at block declaration — the engine ALREADY exposes these (`bb_blockev.h:44`); injuries are literally the realized version of what `k_value` already prices as EV. Cleanest fix = fold injury shaping into the k_value channel, DELETE the post-apply scan. (This is why restoring injury_inflicted only nudged blocks 6.8→7.8: a sparse rare-injury signal can't drive contact; the dense EV-at-declaration k-knobs are the lever — D34.)
  2. **`send_off`** (R3, bloodbowl.h:2257) — reads realized SENT_OFF post-Bribe/Argue dice. FIX: price `P(send-off)=P(caught: doubles)·P(no bribe)·P(no argue)` at FOUL declaration (all inputs known pre-roll).
  3. **`kickoff_touchback`** (just added, bloodbowl.h:1848) — reads realized off-pitch scatter. FIX: price `P(touchback)` at KICK-PLACEMENT by convolving the D8+D6 scatter distribution over the aim square; needs a new pure `bb_kick_touchback_ev(m,x,y)` helper (the ONLY violator whose EV isn't already exposed).
  4. **`ball_gain/ball_loss`** (bloodbowl.h:2179-2193) — pay on realized possession transition (pickup/strip/scatter die result) = the "measured poison" that converged every masked arm to ball-avoidance. FIX: fold into the possession annuity (ball_loss already 0 in v4; set ball_gain 0 too) OR price `k·P(pickup success)` at the pickup/pass declaration.
  5. **`statmatch_scale`** (B, qualified, lowest priority) — episode-end penalty on realized match stats; intentional human-prior regularization, not per-decision dice shaping; most components are attempt-counts (decisions) not successes. Leave unless it misbehaves.
