**D151 — THREAT A/B DIVERGENCE ROOT CAUSE: NOT the threat reward — a latent `exp()` overflow in the native PPO loss that affects EVERY native run (2026-06-18). FIX: clamp `logratio` before `exp` + skip non-finite minibatches in `torch_pufferl.py`.** The `league10-threat` arm (D150) trained HEALTHY (possession 0.11→0.21 stable, blocks/blitzes/knockdowns climbing — NOT camping; the camping canary did NOT fire) then SUDDENLY went `policy=inf` → all-losses=nan at 661M. Isolation ruled out every env-side suspect: reward is finite (`episode_return 0.018` at the NaN step — the T_max cap `min(T,T_max)` clamps even a NaN `uncapped_total` to a finite reward), obs is **uint8** (`(unsigned char)(p_def_down*255)` — physically cannot carry a NaN float into the forward pass), legal-action masks are **never empty** (0 empties over 12M random decisions), the D146 blitz gate is **pure** (stack-local `bb_reach_field`, clones for prone — no enumeration side effects). The tds 0.548 at the NaN point is the post-NaN dying policy, not learned camping. ROOT CAUSE in `vendor/PufferLib/pufferlib/torch_pufferl.py:599-600`: `logratio = newlogprob - mb_logprobs; ratio = logratio.exp()` with **no clamp**. The native CUDA rollout and the torch train-time recompute (`sample_logits`) disagree on a handful of masked-action log-probs every minibatch (even WITH the existing mask-recompute LOCAL PATCH), so `old_approx_kl = (-logratio).mean()` runs **~110-180 on EVERY native run** (verified: kickoff5-9 = 104-132, s4 = 113, all trained fine) — a chronic heavy-tailed `|logratio|`. Negative tails underflow to `ratio≈0` harmlessly; a single `logratio > 88` overflows `exp()` to **+inf** → `pg_loss1 = -adv*inf` → backward NaN → every weight NaN → all losses NaN (and post-corruption garbage: `illegal_frac 0.265`). Healthy runs survived only by luck of staying under the `exp(88)` cliff; the threat reward's net-positive injection nudged old_kl 130→180, closer to the edge, and a batch tipped over at 661M. FIX (Python-only, no rebuild): (1) `logratio = logratio.clamp(-20, 20)` before `exp` → ratio ∈ [2e-9, 4.85e8], far below inf and far wider than any legitimate PPO ratio (real per-epoch moves keep |logratio|<~3), so it never touches learning dynamics — it only defuses the overflow; (2) belt-and-suspenders `if not torch.isfinite(loss): zero_grad; nonfinite_skips++; continue` so no single bad minibatch can ever poison all weights again. This is a genuine harness robustness bug latent in all native training, relevant to the upstream PufferLib match-mode PR (task #58). FOLLOW-UP (not blocking): the chronic old_kl ~110-180 means rollout/train log-probs are systematically inconsistent (mask-mismatch on a few actions/minibatch) → those samples are silently zeroed (ratio≈0) = wasted gradient = training is mildly inefficient, not broken; worth a separate investigation into the CUDA-kernel vs `sample_logits` masking parity (D38 lineage). The threat-annuity design (D148/D149/D150) is VINDICATED — it never caused the NaN; relaunch with the patched harness to get a real verdict. Regression: `engine`/`make test` unaffected (Python harness); add a unit test asserting a synthetic `logratio=200` minibatch produces a finite loss + a recorded skip.

**D151-addendum — FIX REVIEWED (adversarial Opus) + REVISED to v2 + RELAUNCHED LIVE (2026-06-18).** Adversarial Opus review of the diagnosis+fix found 2 HIGH issues, both applied: (F4) the original `clamp(-20,20)` still lets a mask-mismatched NEGATIVE-advantage sample (ratio=exp(20)=4.85e8) dominate the minibatch mean — PPO's `max(pg1,pg2)` only clips the ratio on the positive-adv branch — so tightened to **`[-10,10]`** (ratio ≤2.2e4, contributes O(1) after averaging, still far under exp(88)); (F8) my in-place clamp made `old_approx_kl/approx_kl` read the CLAMPED logratio, erasing the ~180 heavy-tail canary that IS the diagnostic — fixed by clamping only the copy fed to `exp()` and keeping **raw `logratio` for the kl metrics**. Review CONFIRMED the diagnosis: obs is genuinely uint8 (cannot inject float NaN), `ep_carrier_threat` telemetry never feeds training, V-trace re-clips ratio to rho/c=1.0 so the advantage kernel is insensitive to the ratio blow-up → `pg_loss1=-adv*inf` is indeed the sole NaN entry. NOTED non-blocking: (F6, MEDIUM) on a skip the per-loss accumulators aren't incremented but the end-of-loop average divides by full `num_minibatches` → logged losses read low DURING a skip storm — moot in practice because the clamp makes the finite-loss backstop ~never fire; (F9, MEDIUM→upgraded) the chronic old_kl ~110-180 is a real rollout/train **logprob-parity bug** (native bf16 kernel rollout vs float32 `sample_logits` recompute + the `nan_to_num(probs,1e-8)` floor) — the clamp is a band-aid; proper fix = store/reuse the rollout kernel's logprob or match precision (the true follow-up, not "mildly inefficient"). v2 RELAUNCHED on japan (same `/tmp/run_threat_ab.sh`, warm threat_warm.bin): LIVE, steps advancing 0→2.9M, SPS ~270K, policy/value/entropy/total all FINITE, old_kl visible + climbing (23→43, canary intact) — overflow defused. Codex second-opinion review dispatched (`.codex-reviews/ppo-nan-clamp-fix.md`). NEXT: confirm it survives PAST 661M (original death point, ~40min), then watch the threat-annuity verdict + camping canary (D149/D150). FOLLOW-UP TASK: bf16/float32 logprob parity (F9) — affects every native run's sample efficiency.

**D151-v3 — v2 FIX FAILED IN PROD; v3 grad-norm guard deployed (2026-06-18).** The v2 `[-10,10]` clamp + finite-LOSS backstop survived the early run (validated to 2.9M) but NaN'd AGAIN at **675M** — past the original 661M death but same signature (old_kl→194 finite, then policy inf, **zero `nonfinite_skips`** = the loss-level backstop never fired). Root cause of the bypass: a finite-but-HUGE `pg_loss` (minibatch advantages normalized by a near-zero std via `(adv-mean)/(std+1e-8)`, times `ratio` up to exp(10)=22026) PASSES `isfinite(loss)`, then `loss.backward()` produces an **inf INTERMEDIATE gradient**, and `clip_grad_norm_` computes `inf*0 = NaN` → NaN weights before the next forward. A loss-level check structurally cannot catch a finite loss with inf grads. Codex's review INDEPENDENTLY flagged this ("other non-finite entry paths worth guarding, especially value and advantage normalization") and correctly predicted v2 would pass a short validation but risk a 600M+ run. v3 FIX: capture `grad_norm = clip_grad_norm_(...)` (it returns the pre-clip total norm) and **skip `optimizer.step()` when `not torch.isfinite(grad_norm)`** — a universal catch for inf/NaN grads from ANY component (advantage-norm, value, entropy, BC), dynamics-preserving (clean minibatches untouched), only skipping the rare catastrophic update. Editable install verified (single file, .pyc regen confirmed) so the patch IS loaded. Relaunched on japan. LESSON: validate a NaN fix PAST the known death step, not at 2.8M — armed a Monitor this time. The bf16/float32 logprob-parity bug (F9) remains the true upstream cause; the clamp+grad-guard are the robust band-aids that let the threat A/B produce a verdict.

**D152 — THE NaN IS A NEW-BUILD TRAINING INSTABILITY, NOT THE THREAT REWARD AND NOT THE PPO LOSS. Three guard-fixes (D151 v1/v2/v3) were chasing the wrong layer. Box idle; needs a revert/bisect decision (2026-06-18).** Decisive disambiguation run (threat term OFF, `reward_carrier_threat 0`, everything else identical on the same v3 build) ALSO went NaN — at epoch 729 (~190M steps) vs the threat arm's epoch 391 (~102M). Evidence chain:
- **Both configs NaN; threat only accelerates it** (102M with threat vs 190M without). The threat reward is NOT the cause — it changes WHEN, not WHETHER.
- **My D151 v1/v2/v3 torch_pufferl patches never engaged the real path.** The ORIGINAL unpatched threat run and the PATCHED v3 run NaN'd at the IDENTICAL epoch 391 / old_kl 183.759 / log line 12046. `nonfinite_skips` never incremented in EITHER the threat or control run → the NaN does not flow through a non-finite `loss` or `grad_norm`; it is entirely upstream of ratio/loss/gradient (the clamp + both backstops are downstream and inert against it). D151's "exp() overflow" root cause is WRONG (or at most a symptom): the real failure is upstream in the forward pass / data.
- **The signature is always the same:** `old_kl` climbs to ~185-190 (vs the healthy old-build ceiling ~104-132 on kickoff5-9/s4 — a ~47% higher mismatch), then `policy → inf` in a single epoch, then all losses NaN, then the policy is dead. old_kl IS the rollout-vs-train logprob mismatch (native CUDA kernel rollout vs torch `sample_logits` recompute over the legal-action mask). The new build inflates that mismatch until a logit overflows.
- **What changed vs the healthy billions-of-steps runs (league9, kickoff5-9):** the engine REBUILD folding in D146 (blitz reachability gate, `has_reachable_blitz_target`/`bb_reach_field_compute` in proc_turn.c) + D149 threat-eval code. The CONTROL has the threat eval disabled (`reward_carrier_threat 0` → `bb_carrier_threat_eval` never called), so the active engine delta in the failing control is **the D146 blitz-mask change**. PRIME SUSPECT: D146 made `bb_legal_actions`' blitz-declare legality state/path-dependent in a way that is nondeterministic OR differs between the CUDA rollout mask and the torch train-time mask → logprob mismatch (old_kl) inflates → overflow. (Candidates: uninitialized read in `has_reachable_blitz_target`/`bb_reach_field` stack struct; reachability result depending on scratch garbage; or a mask the rollout kernel and `sample_logits` compute differently.)
- **NOT yet ruled out:** value-function shock from warm-starting league9_cap (which trained under R6 carrier-exposure) into a different economy (R6 off); but old_kl (policy/mask), not value loss, is what climbs first — points to mask, not value.

**D152-addendum — MASK NONDETERMINISM RULED OUT (2026-06-18). The D146 reachability path is clean; the old_kl inflation is logprob non-parity (bf16 rollout vs fp32 train), not a mask bug.** Two zero-blast-radius Mac probes: (1) INSPECTION — `reach_field_compute_ordered` (engine/src/bb_reachability.c) FULLY initializes the field (opening double loop sets every cell cost=`reach_unreachable()`, len 0, prev -1, done 0) before the Dijkstra; `has_reachable_blitz_target`'s stack `bb_reach_field` is therefore never read uninitialized → no uninit-memory nondeterminism. (2) EMPIRICAL — `/tmp/maskdet.c`: called `bb_legal_actions` TWICE per decision on independent memcpy copies (one after poisoning 4KB of stack with 0xAA, one after zeroing it) over **6.0M decisions** → **0 mask mismatches, 0 blitz-bit mismatches**. The legal-action mask is deterministic. CONCLUSION: the rollout-vs-train logprob gap (old_kl ~190 fatal / ~130 healthy) is NOT mask nondeterminism — it is the **bf16-precision native rollout vs fp32 `sample_logits` train-recompute non-parity** (review finding F9), which the new build's D146-shifted (more peaked) masked action distribution likely amplifies past the overflow threshold. REMAINING LIVE HYPOTHESES for Alex: (1) bf16/fp32 logprob parity — store/reuse the native rollout kernel's logprob instead of recomputing in fp32 (the real F9 fix); (2) build bisect — rebuild the engine at the exact league9 (pre-D146) commit, rerun the control; if stable, re-add deltas one at a time (cheap at ~850K SPS, ~5min/run to 250M); (3) warm-start economy shock (league9_cap trained under R6, restarted with R6 off) — less likely since old_kl/policy, not value loss, leads. Four hypotheses now REFUTED with evidence (threat-reward-cause, my-PPO-patches, reach-uninit, mask-nondeterminism); the field is narrowed to logprob-parity vs a build-delta bisect. Recommend (2) first (decisive + cheap) then (1) as the durable fix. Box idle, awaiting steer — not guessing further autonomously after 3 wrong root-cause calls.

**D153 — ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (Codex gpt-5.5 xhigh, 2026-06-18): unclamped `__expf(logratio)` overflow in the NATIVE CUDA PPO kernel + bf16/fp32 logprob non-parity. My D151 patches were DEAD CODE for native runs; D152's "upstream of the ratio" conclusion was WRONG.** The decisive correction (`.codex-reviews/newbuild-nan-diagnosis.md`): the native bf16 league runs execute the PPO loss in the **CUDA kernel `vendor/PufferLib/src/pufferlib.cu` `ppo_loss_compute` (~L869)** and step via **`muon.cu` `muon_step` (~L159)** — NOT the Python `torch_pufferl.py train()` loop I patched in D151 v1/v2/v3. Proof: `pufferl.py:203` selects native `_C` unless `--slowly` (the launch scripts omit it); `torch_pufferl.py:21` REFUSES a bf16 `_C` build (the "PyTorch backend requires float32" error seen when probing). So `nonfinite_skips` never incremented and patched==unpatched onset because **the guards were on the wrong backend**, not because the NaN bypasses the ratio. This INVALIDATES D152's inference ("NaN is upstream of ratio/loss/gradient"); the original D151 MECHANISM (unclamped `ratio=exp(logratio)` overflow when the rollout/train logprob gap makes `|logratio|` huge) is almost certainly CORRECT — it just lives in `pufferlib.cu`, where `__expf(logratio)` is unclamped. CODEX RANKED CAUSES: (1ancy HIGH) native rollout stores **bf16** logprobs, train recomputes via a different fp32/log-space recurrent path → systematic non-parity → `old_kl` climbs to ~190 → a single `logratio>~88` overflows `__expf` to +inf → policy inf → all NaN (matches the observed signature exactly); (2-5 LOW) self-play frozen-row leakage (`compute_prio_normalize` +1e-6 samples frozen rows at tiny rate), stale/illegal-mask (would show `newlogprob<-1000` not a smooth climb — native masks with -1e4 not -inf), value/economy warm-start shock (rewards clamped + V-trace clipped, and policy-KL leads not value — so unlikely). The D146 mask change isn't a bug; it shifts the action distribution more peaked, widening the bf16/fp32 gap so the threat arm tips sooner (102M) than the control (190M) — both fail because the unclamped-`__expf` + bf16-parity gap is precision/build-wide, NOT threat-specific. FIX (native, needs GPU rebuild): in `pufferlib.cu` clamp `logratio` to [-10,10] before `__expf` (keep RAW logratio for the old_kl/approx_kl metrics), and guard `ppo_loss_compute` to zero policy/value grads + set ratio=1 + bump a debug counter when `!isfinite(total_log_prob||old_logp||adv_normalized||val_pred)`; guard `muon_step` to skip on non-finite grad norm. DURABLE FIX: bf16/fp32 logprob PARITY — store the rollout kernel's logprob and reuse it in train (don't recompute), or run native fp32 until parity lands. CHEAPEST CONFIRM (no rebuild): print `_C.precision_bytes` (expect 2 = bf16, proving the torch guards were off-path) + add native first-minibatch debug metrics (`mb0_old_kl`, `logratio_min/max`, `count(logratio>80)`, `count(newlogprob<-1000)`, `count(!isfinite)`) — if mb0_old_kl is already large pre-update it's rollout/train parity; if `count(logratio>80)` flips on in the fatal epoch the first non-finite is native `__expf`. STATUS: my D151 torch_pufferl.py patches are harmless for actual torch-backend (`--slowly`) runs but IRRELEVANT to native — keep as torch-path robustness or revert; they do NOT fix the native runs. **D154 — NATIVE-CUDA NaN FIX IMPLEMENTED (Codex), REVIEWED (Claude), VALIDATED, COMMITTED (2026-06-18). The threat A/B now runs CLEAN past both death points; fork commit f14b71c.** Per D153, the real bug was the unclamped `__expf(logratio)` in the native CUDA PPO kernel (`pufferlib.cu`) — NOT the Python `torch_pufferl.py` I'd patched 3x (dead code for native bf16 runs). Codex (gpt-5.5 xhigh, plan tool + CUDA-doc lookup) implemented + Claude reviewed:
- **`vendor/PufferLib/src/pufferlib.cu` `ppo_loss_compute`:** `raw_logratio = total_log_prob - old_logp; ratio = __expf(fminf(10, fmaxf(-10, raw_logratio)))` — bounds ratio to [4.5e-5, 22026] (far below the exp(88.7) cliff) while the RAW logratio still feeds the `old_kl`/`approx_kl` diagnostics (so the heavy-tail canary stays visible). Plus a non-finite-input guard (new `ppo_zero_element_grads` helper): if old_logp/total_log_prob/adv_normalized/val_pred is non-finite → ratio=1, zero all grads (logits+logstd+value), `goto reduce` (element contributes 0 to losses). Value-loss block relocated after the guard.
- **`vendor/PufferLib/src/muon.cu`:** new `muon_norm_ok(sum_sq)=isfinite&&>=0`; `muon_nesterov`+`muon_weight_update` take the global grad-norm ptr and EARLY-RETURN (skip the weight update, momentum buffer preserved) when the norm is non-finite; `muon_clip_norm`/`muon_norm_apply` write 0 on a bad norm. Belt-and-suspenders against any residual non-finite grad.
- **CLAUDE REVIEW:** both edits correct — clamp keeps raw logratio for metrics (F8-consistent), guard neutralizes cleanly, `goto reduce` is legal (label outside the block scope), muon skip preserves momentum. APPROVED.
- **BUILD:** clean rebuild on japan, `precision_bytes 2` (native bf16 confirmed — THE path the Python patches missed), no compile fixes needed.
- **VALIDATION:** relaunched the threat A/B (warm threat_warm.bin, identical config); ran to **181.9M+ steps with ZERO nan/inf** (independently re-verified by Claude: 0 nan/inf lines in the whole post-fix log, policy 0.007/value 0.005/entropy 0.258 all finite, tds 0.74 healthy), past BOTH the 102M (threat) and ~190M (control) death points. `bad_nonfinite_count 0` → the element/muon guards never fired; the CLAMP alone is the operative fix (the logratio was finite-huge, not non-finite). old_kl still swings 40-300 (raw, unclamped diagnostic) but ratio is bounded → no overflow. The threat-annuity A/B is now LIVE and will produce a real verdict (its first ever clean run) + the camping canary watch (D149/D150).
- **COMMIT:** fork (vendor/PufferLib, branch 4.0) `f14b71c` "Clamp native PPO logratio and guard non-finite grads", scoped to ONLY src/pufferlib.cu + src/muon.cu (unrelated pre-existing fork mods left untouched).
DURABLE FOLLOW-UP (not blocking, per D153 F9): the clamp is a band-aid; old_kl 40-300 means the native bf16-rollout vs fp32-train logprob NON-PARITY is real and large — many samples get clamped to ratio=22026/4.5e-5 = bounded but noisy gradient. The durable fix is logprob parity (store/reuse the rollout kernel's logprob in train, or train native fp32). This affects EVERY native run's sample efficiency (not just threat) and is worth an upstream PufferLib fix alongside task #58. LESSON CODIFIED: for native-backend numerics, the loss/optimizer math lives in `src/pufferlib.cu` + `src/muon.cu`, NOT `torch_pufferl.py` (which native runs never execute — `pufferl.py:203` selects `_C` unless `--slowly`; `torch_pufferl.py:21` refuses a bf16 `_C`). Confirm `_C.precision_bytes` and that the patched path actually executes BEFORE concluding a fix is inert.

**D155 — BALL-ADVANCEMENT TELEMETRY added (Codex impl, Claude review) to diagnose threat-arm camping; restart baseline fwd_adv ~7 sq/possession = healthy advancing, NOT camping at start (2026-06-18, main-repo 5525a9e).** Alex's camping diagnostic: "from pickup, how many squares did the ball move?" Two per-episode dashboard stats (puffer/bloodbowl/bloodbowl.h + binding.c), averaged over the episode's possessions:
- **`ball_fwd_adv`** = net squares the ball advanced toward the holding team's ATTACKING endzone, pickup→possession-end. Camping ⇒ ~0; advancing ⇒ high.
- **`ball_path_len`** = total ball path (Σ per-step Chebyshev) over the same window. Pairing the two separates camping (low fwd, low path) from the OSCILLATION/shuffle pathology (low fwd, HIGH path) from clean advance (high fwd, path≈fwd).
IMPL: Codex refactored the existing inline possession-transition logic into a shared `bbe_update_ball_possession(env, scored)` serving BOTH the ball gain/loss reward AND the telemetry, reusing the `possessor` state machine (no parallel detector). `bbe_start/end_ball_possession` record pickup-fwd (in the team's attack orientation via `bbe_forward_coord`) and accumulate fwd_adv + path; ball tracked via carrier position; TD captured before score-reset. CLAUDE REVIEW: (1) REWARD-PRESERVING — `possessor` is used ONLY by ball_gain/loss (gated `pay_rewards`); the threat run has ball_gain 0.05 so behavior is identical to pre-refactor; for zero-ball-reward configs possessor now updates unconditionally but nothing else reads it → no reward-dynamics change (Alex's "telemetry must not change rewards" constraint SATISFIED). (2) telemetry correct — orientation empirically validated (fwd_adv POSITIVE ⇒ advancing-toward-endzone direction right), Chebyshev king-move distance, clean possession state machine matching the original transitions, no path double-count. (3) no obs/action/RNG impact. BUILD: native bf16 rebuilt on japan, `precision_bytes 2`, the D154 NaN fix (fork f14b71c `raw_logratio`/clamp) confirmed still present + losses finite. RESTART: threat A/B relaunched UNCHANGED (k=0.03, warm threat_warm.bin) — lost the prior ~699M (Alex approved; only way to instrument given one-GPU/no-checkpoint; scientifically a re-run of the same early arm). FIRST VALUES: **ball_fwd_adv ≈ 6.7-7.2, ball_path_len ≈ 8.8-9.1** (path≥|fwd|, ratio ~0.78 = fairly direct, little wasted motion) — the warm-started policy advances the ball ~7 squares/possession at restart = HEALTHY, not camping. This is the BASELINE; the camping test is whether fwd_adv DROPS (toward 0, or path/fwd ratio rises = oscillation) as the threat reward shapes the policy over training. Commit 5525a9e (main repo, bloodbowl.h+binding.c only), pushed. WATCH: ball_fwd_adv + tds together to the ~10-14B verdict window; if fwd_adv collapses while possession_rate spikes ⇒ camping confirmed ⇒ halve k to 0.015 (D149/D150 canary).

Mechanism: k_kd scales reward ∝ p_def_down for ALL blocks; the RATIO between a 2d and a 1d reward is scale-invariant, so more k → more blocks of every kind (incl. ~10% unfavorable 2d-red), not more-selective blocks. To move the MIX you need either convexity (super-linear in p_def_down) or pricing the DOWNSIDE (p_att_down → attacker falls → turnover; currently UNPRICED — a 2d-red has high p_att_down that nothing penalizes at decision time). That turnover-risk pricing is the cardinal-rule-clean lever for discipline (bb_block_ev already exposes p_att_down) — but it's a REWARD-ECONOMY change → defer to Alex review per CLAUDE.md (do not ship a new reward term autonomously).
- CAVEAT: 2d-red isn't necessarily bad — blitzing the CARRIER on a 2d-red to force a turnover is often correct. Can't distinguish "undisciplined" from "aggressive carrier-pressure" without carrier-targeting telemetry (task #64) — which is exactly why #64 matters.

**D158 — violence2 (k_kd 0.2/k_value 1.0) CONFIRMS scale-invariance: doubling k → MORE blocks, WORSE mix. NET-EV block reward (turnover downside) is the real discipline lever (Alex directive, 2026-06-20).** violence2 capped 12B clean (VIOLENCE2_EXIT 0, 0 nan/inf — native fix holds): blocks_thrown 15.7→**21.1**, knockdowns 7.2→**9.7**, but block_2d_frac 0.49→0.47 (flat) and block_2dred_frac 0.11→**0.13 (WORSE)**. Doubling k bought ~35% more blocks of EVERY kind and did NOT improve selection — exactly the D157 scale-invariance prediction (k scales every block's upside equally; the 2d:1d:2dred ratio is invariant). k-cranking is exhausted as a discipline lever.
ROOT CAUSE of the mix problem: the block reward (bloodbowl.h:2105) is **UPSIDE-ONLY** — `exposure = p_deliver*(k_kd*p_def_down + k_value*p_def_removed*value + k_ball*p_ball_out)`, zero-sum att/def. The only downside is the weak `seq` term (k_seq*p_turnover*pending, k_seq=0.01) which prices wasted ACTIVATIONS, not the turnover. So the agent never sees the actual cost of a 2d-red: its high attacker-down → high **`ev.p_turnover`** (engine already computes it, bb_blockev.h:47) is UNCHARGED. Nothing makes a 2d-red net-negative.
ALEX'S FIX (net-EV at declaration, cardinal-rule clean — all pre-dice EV): block_reward = TAKEDOWN VALUE − TURNOVER COST = `(k_kd*p_def_down + k_value*p_def_removed*value + k_ball*p_ball_out) − k_turnover*p_turnover`. New knob `reward_k_turnover`. MECHANISM: p_turnover(2d-red)≈0.30 vs p_turnover(2d)≈0.03 (≈10×) → charging k_turnover*p_turnover makes 2d-red net-much-worse than 2d → policy shifts the MIX (not just volume). ELEGANCE (Alex's earlier point): it does NOT ban 2d-red — against the ball carrier or a star, p_def_removed*value / p_ball_out is big enough to justify the turnover risk (2d-red-on-carrier-to-spring-the-ball stays +EV); against a backfield lineman it goes net-negative. Self-sorts by target value — the exact behavior we want, and the reason carrier-targeting telemetry (#64, committed 89fa711) ships in the same build to SEE it. NEXT: implement reward_k_turnover (Codex + adversarial review per reward-economy standing pattern), rebuild, launch "netblock" arm warm from violence2_cap (k_kd 0.1, k_value 0.5, k_turnover ~0.15 first guess — SWEEPABLE), carrier telemetry live. Watch block_2dred_frac → toward human 0.017, block_2d_frac → toward 0.77, AND blocks-vs-carrier (is the residual 2d-red carrier-pressure or sloppiness). Box idle ~1h for build is acceptable vs launching another known-dead k-variant.

**D163 — ROOT CAUSE of the agent's poor block dice-mix: it UNDER-ASSISTS (Alex's H2 CONFIRMED, 2026-06-20). The agent brings ~HALF the offensive assists humans do on every tier — it blocks without ganging up, so more dice land unfavorable.** Measured via a new `block_tier × {is_carrier, off_assists}` telemetry crossing (env, commit 15f44c5) — agent eval on netblock_cap (513 games) vs the human corpus (32,483 blocks / 401 games, 1.4% engine-tier-vs-recorded mismatch audit). Matched mean offensive-assists-per-block:
| tier | agent | human |
| 1d   | 0.28  | 0.55  |
| 2d   | 0.52  | 0.94  |
| 2d-red | 0.09 | 0.17 |
Agent ≈ 0.5× human assists UNIFORMLY. This is the structural cause of both elevated 2d-red (0.05-0.06 vs human 0.017) AND depressed 2d-frac (0.54-0.59 vs human 0.77): humans turn marginal blocks favorable by bringing assists; the agent throws the same blocks with half the gang-up support. H1 (carrier-pressure) only PARTIAL: agent 2d-red IS more carrier-concentrated than human (0.26 vs 0.11) so SOME red dice are deliberate pressure, but 74% of agent 2d-red is NOT on the carrier → carrier-pressure can't explain the bulk (Claude's "probably carrier pressure" was mostly WRONG; Alex's skepticism correct). CORROBORATION: netblock2 (k_turnover 0.30, D162) made blocks more SELECTIVE (1d→2d) but couldn't FLOOR 2d-red → the residual isn't under-priced, it's structural (no better option in-policy because no assist was set up). WHY the agent under-assists (hypothesis): the block-EV reward (k_kd/k_value) already makes ASSISTED blocks more valuable (more assists → higher p_def_down → more reward), so the gradient EXISTS — but the SETUP move (positioning a teammate adjacent to the enemy to provide the assist) is UNREWARDED and DISTAL from the terminal block; the assist-provider isn't credited, so the agent doesn't learn the multi-step "gang up THEN block" coordination. This is a credit-assignment/positioning gap, not a pricing gap → raising k_turnover/k_kd won't fix it (proven by netblock2). CANDIDATE INTERVENTIONS: (a) **assist-EV reward** — credit a move by the offensive-assist EV it provides to a teammate's potential block (the bb_block_ev p_def_down DELTA the assist enables, decision-time/pre-dice, anti-farming-disciplined) — the mirror of pricing the block; (b) **BC-toward-human positioning** (humans assist; block-decision-weighted BC-CE would teach gang-ups — connects to the reward-discovery plan's BC-CE direction + D33's "state-averaged BC misses block behavior"); (c) obs feature: an "assistable enemy" plane so the agent SEES assist opportunities. Telemetry committed (block_2dred_carrier_frac, offassist_{1d,2d,3d,2dred}) + tools/bb_blockstats.c (human-corpus parser, reusable). NEXT: design + review the assist-EV reward (standing reward-economy review pattern), warm-start probe to test if it raises offassist toward human.

**D164 — ASSIST-POTENTIAL probe LAUNCHED (the D163 fix; bidirectional design from Alex's pressure-test, 2026-06-21).** After D163 (agent under-assists ~0.5×human), designed an assist reward and pressure-tested it with Alex. KEY DESIGN MOVE (Alex's bidirectionality question): a one-directional "reward providing an assist" is WRONG — it ignores removing ENEMY assists (blitzing an enemy off my blocker to free up my block), which is half of real BB. Fix = a **zero-sum telescoping potential** Φ = team aggregate contact block-favorability (Σ over my standing pieces adjacent to a standing enemy of max p_def_down), measured at settled own-turn-end (possession-annuity pattern). BIDIRECTIONAL by construction: adding my assist raises a contact's p_def_down (d0↑); blitzing an enemy that was defensively-assisting my contact raises my p_def_down (d0↑) AND drops the enemy's favorability (d1↓) → doubly credited via r0=k*(d0−d1). PBRS-ish (telescoping, can't double-pay k_kd by accumulation) + cardinal-rule clean (pre-dice bb_block_ev). CHEAP (learned from the threat-annuity 8× scar): Φ bounded to EXISTING adjacent contacts only — O(≤16 pieces × 8 squares), bb_block_ev on real adjacencies, NO per-square clones. Impl: `bb_team_contact_favorability` (bb_blockev.c), hook at the possession/threat turn-boundary site (bloodbowl.h:2412), `reward_k_assist` knob default 0, mutual-exclusion guard with reward_carrier_threat, `ep_contact_fav` telemetry. Committed 9d5a736; native built (precision_bytes 2, NaN fix raw_logratio intact), default-0 SPS not regressed. PROCESS NOTE: the Codex + adversarial-Opus pressure-tests both FAILED on infra (Codex over-explored 8h no verdict; Opus API ConnectionRefused) — pivoted to treating the LIVE probe + canaries as the empirical pressure-test (more reliable than stuck agents); Claude reviewed the diff directly (Φ bounded ✓, hook zero-sum/telescoping ✓, bidirectional ✓). PROBE (league10-assist): warm netblock_cap, netblock economy (k_kd 0.1/k_value 0.5/k_seq 0/k_turnover 0.15) + **reward_k_assist 0.03**, 12B. EARLY (32M): LIVE, finite, **SPS 609K** (~28% slower from Φ eval — bounded design avoided the threat-annuity 3× hit), 2d 0.506, 2dred 0.058, tds 1.40. CANARY (watch to cap): block_2d_frac UP toward human 0.77 + block_2dred_frac DOWN toward 0.017 (the GOAL — assists convert bad→good dice) AND tds/ball_fwd_adv HELD (not Φ-camping/farming). If 2d-red drops + 2d rises + scoring held → the assist potential works → graduate (cross-ancestor + from-scratch gate per D161). DISK: box healthy 63% post-D162-prune; standing-fix (launch-script snapshot pruning) still TODO so disk-full can't recur.

**D165 — ASSIST POTENTIAL FAILED (k_assist 0.03): did NOT raise the agent's assists. Clean negative + a strategic fork (2026-06-22).** league10-assist capped 12B clean (ASSIST_EXIT 0, 0 nan, SPS 609K — bounded Φ cost ~28%, NOT the threat-annuity 3x). DIRECT off-assist measure (training telemetry) vs netblock_cap (D163) and human:
| tier | netblock_cap | assist_cap | human |
| 1d   | 0.28 | 0.22 | 0.55 |
| 2d   | 0.52 | 0.50 | 0.94 |
| 2dred| 0.09 | 0.06 | 0.17 |
Off-assists FLAT/slightly-DOWN; block_2d_frac flat (0.543→0.540), 2dred flat (0.056→0.062). The bidirectional telescoping assist potential did NOT make the agent gang up. (It DID raise block volume 14→16.8 and tds 1.46→**1.66** — more aggressive/higher-scoring, but via more blocks, not better-assisted ones.)
LEADING EXPLANATION — PBRS optimum-invariance (the flip side of the design's elegance): a TELESCOPING potential can only SPEED learning of behavior the base reward ALREADY favors; it CANNOT create a new attractor. The base economy (k_kd 0.1 etc.) apparently does NOT make committing a teammate to assist worth its opportunity cost, so the optimum-invariant potential couldn't induce assisting — it just reshaped credit timing (+ slightly more aggression). Cranking k_assist likely won't help if this is right (telescoping nets out regardless of magnitude). This is the deep lesson: to CHANGE behavior toward human (vs speed learning of already-optimal behavior), you need a NON-PBRS push.
THE STRATEGIC FORK (Alex's call — touches the human-like-vs-win-maximal question he's been driving):
(A) **The assist gap may be a FEATURE, not a flaw (D46 discipline: ground inhuman behavior in WINS, not human-stat aesthetics).** The low-assist agent SCORES MORE (tds 1.66). Under self-play win-maximization it may be correctly finding that throwing more blocks + scoring beats slowing down to gang up like risk-averse humans; humans may over-assist out of convention/risk-aversion our win-maximizer doesn't share. TEST: does a higher-assist agent actually WIN more (tournament vs anchors)? If not, the agent is right and "match human assists" is the wrong goal.
(B) **If we DO want human assists, a telescoping potential is the wrong tool** — need either (b1) a NON-telescoping standing assist bonus that genuinely SHIFTS the optimum toward assisting (risk: farming/camping, no longer double-count-free), or (b2) BC/KL-toward-human positioning (the principled way to instill a human CONVENTION that isn't optimal under our reward — connects to the reward-discovery plan's BC-CE direction; humans assist, BC pulls there). (b2) is heavier (native CUDA) but addresses the root: this result is EVIDENCE that human assist behavior is NOT optimal under our current reward, which is exactly when BC-toward-human (not reward shaping) is the right lever.
RECOMMENDATION: don't reflexively crank k_assist (optimum-invariance says it won't work). Either accept the finding pending a strength test (A), or commit to the BC-toward-human path (b2) if we believe human-like blocking is worth instilling. assist_cap backed up. reward_k_assist code stays (default 0, inert). Box idle.

**D166 — DEFENSE RESEARCH SYNTHESIZED → root cause is OPPONENT-QUALITY, not reward design; first move = scripted offense bot, NOT a new reward (2026-06-22).** Alex: human beats the bots 3-0 to 6-0 (worst vs fast teams = defense is the bigger hole than blocking). Gathered defense knowledge: existing AndyDavo #07 Defensive Setup Guide (reviewed) + 4-agent web fan-out (`analysis/defense/defense-research-collected.md`, sources: grumbbl, bbtactics, thetacklezone, goonhammer, bloodbowlstrategies, Bonehead). CONVERGENT CORE: force-the-dodge (more dice=more failure), screen-don't-blitz, two-deep columns at 2-sq spacing, **keep a DEEP SAFETY** (the 6-0 failure mode — one broken screen = walk-in), mark-carrier-from-endzone-side + the one-good-blitz/turn, roster-conditioned mark-vs-screen (gated on relative speed + Tackle skills). Codex synthesis (`.codex-reviews/defense-paths-forward.md`) — OPINIONATED BOTTOM LINE: **"don't invent 5 more defensive rewards; make the agent defend against something that can actually score."** ROOT CAUSE: defensive skills ARE optimal vs a competent attacker, but the agent only ever faced its weak self-play mirror (can't punish a missing screen) → no gradient toward defense; per D165 PBRS can't induce behavior the opponents don't make necessary. So the lever is OPPONENT-QUALITY first, reward-shaping only as bounded scaffold after. RECOMMENDED FIRST EXPERIMENT (cheapest decisive test, answers the causal question): (1) build a scripted **offense_bot** (heuristic cage/advance/score) via the existing `scripted_opponent` hook (beside contact_bot.h); (2) add defensive-canary telemetry (deep_safety_count/zero, carrier min-dodges/GFIs-to-our-EZ, carrier-path zero-TZ squares, carrier_marked, bot turns-to-score, bot TDs); (3) baseline champion vs the bot; (4) train 3-5B warm-started vs the offense bot with the CURRENT reward economy, NO new defensive reward; (5) re-eval. PASS/FAIL: defense improves w/o reward changes → opponent-quality is the lever → graduate to hard-opponent/asymmetric-frozen-attacker curriculum; else layer bounded scaffolds IN ORDER: R12 reward_defensive_threat (already built, off — cheap A/B) → obs scalars (opp_carrier_min_dodges_to_ez, deep_safety_count, carrier_path_zero_tz, cage_corners_marked — spare obs bytes, no BBE_OBS_SIZE change) → narrow NON-PBRS deep-safety + lane-coverage rewards (lane = zero-TZ squares on carrier→EZ min-cost path via ONE bb_reach_field_compute Dijkstra, NOT per-square clones — avoid the D150 threat-annuity 8x scar) → BC-toward-human defense only if hard-opponent training still won't produce human screens. OBS GAP confirmed: agent can't directly SEE scoring lane / deep-safety / cage corners (must derive from raw rows under sparse pressure) → the scalar obs features are a real complement. Promote ONLY by anchored-strength (win/score vs frozen anchors + held-out scripted offense), never self-play TDs or prettier columns (D46). SEQUENCING: finish the block/turnover thread (turnover3, promising — 2d 0.625/2dred 0.045 at 1.1B) first per Alex, THEN the defense pivot starts with the scripted-offense stress test. NOTE: the scripted offense bot is the crux + non-trivial (cage/advance/score heuristic) — get Alex's input on its design/strength before building.

**D167 — OFFENSE BOT (bashy cage-advance) BUILT + RIGOROUSLY VALIDATED (2026-06-22, commit e27ecaa + tools/bb_offense_test.c).** The defense-curriculum keystone: a scripted bashy cage-advance attacker (puffer/bloodbowl/offense_bot.h, `bbe_offense_bot_pick`, selected via scripted_opponent + scripted_opponent_type=1). BLOCKING RULE (Alex, corrected): throw blocks ordered by p_def_down, gated on SKILL-AWARE own-turnover risk `ev.p_turnover <= 0.17` (BBE_OB_BLOCK_TURNOVER_MAX) — admits 1d-WITH-Block (~0.167, only skull turns over), excludes 1d-no-skill (~0.33) and 2d-red (defender picks). NOT a crude ndice>=2 rule (that bug — banning all 1d — was caught + corrected). RIGOROUS BEHAVIORAL SUITE (tools/bb_offense_test.c, 300 games each, Alex's 3 questions): (1) vs PASSIVE (does-nothing) opp: terminates 300/300, 0 non-termination, bot 1.34 TD/game, scored-in 73%, SHUTOUT 27%; (2) vs RANDOM: 1.65/game, shutout 17%; (3) BOT-vs-BOT: terminates 300/300, 0 infinite loops, HOME 0.83 / AWAY 0.48 TD/game, BOTH score (197 & 118 games) — not a stalemate; defense-probe: 0.0% immediate-END_TURN (never degenerates to passing turns). VERDICT: passes the critical pathology gates (termination, no deterministic loop, both-score, no passivity, zero red blocks 190/190 gated). The 27% shutout-vs-nothing is BALL-RECOVERY (its defense), NOT a finishing flaw — proven by: vs RANDOM (which fumbles → hands the bot the ball more) it scores MORE + shuts out LESS, so shutouts = games where the kicking opp received and the bot couldn't pry the ball loose. The bot is a competent ATTACKER, mediocre BALL-RECOVERER. CURRICULUM IMPLICATION (confirms D166/Codex): run the defense stress test ASYMMETRICALLY / from opponent-has-ball demo states (agent ALWAYS defends vs the offense bot holding the ball) — bypasses the bot's ball-recovery weakness, isolates the agent's defense vs a competent cage-advance. NEXT (after turnover3 caps): baseline current champion vs offense_bot from opponent-has-ball states + defensive-canary telemetry (D166), then train ~3-5B asymmetric defense vs offense_bot with NO new defensive reward → test if defense emerges (the opponent-quality hypothesis).

**D168 — STANDING RULE: probe run-length is set by PLATEAU, not a fixed step budget (Alex, 2026-06-22).** The fixed 12B/28B budgets were a pragmatic default, NOT principled — they can stop a run mid-trajectory. NEW STANDING RULE for reward-economy / behavioral DIAGNOSTIC probes:
- **Extend-on-still-improving, stop-on-plateau.** Do NOT declare a verdict at a fixed budget. Track the primary metric(s) the probe is testing (e.g., block_2dred_frac, offassist_2d). At each cap, compare the metric's value over the last ~2B-step window to the prior ~2B window. If still moving beyond noise → **warm-restart from the cap (chained) and continue** until it flattens. If flat (Δ < ~noise) OR the verdict is already decisively clear (clearly working / clearly dead) → stop + record.
- **Judge "still improving" on the metric that MATTERS:** for a behavioral probe, the behavioral curve (off-assists, dice-mix); for a STRENGTH/final run, Elo-vs-frozen-anchors — and there also stop on the OVEROPTIMIZATION downturn (EvalStop, k=2 consecutive Elo drops; D161), not just plateau, because a proxy can keep climbing toward human while true strength stalls/regresses.
- **Probe vs production:** probes stop at behavioral plateau / clear verdict (cheap, answer the question); final policy runs go to a real budget / Elo plateau for maximum strength.
- Mechanism: chained warm-restart from the latest snapshot/cap with the same reward config + pool preseed (the lineage continues seamlessly; total-timesteps can't be raised mid-run). LIVE CASE: turnover3 off-assists still climbing 0.52→0.60 (3.6B→4.7B) → it will NOT have plateaued at the 12B cap → on cap, evaluate the trajectory and CHAIN-EXTEND if still moving, rather than calling the verdict at an arbitrary 12B. Longer-term: automate plateau/EvalStop detection instead of eyeballing (the reward-discovery-plan guardrail).

**D170 — DEFENSE BASELINE: the trained champion's defense concedes ~2× what a simple scripted bot's defense concedes (2026-06-22). Alex's "I'd win 3-0 to 6-0" thesis CONFIRMED empirically.** Ran turnover3_cap (the settled-economy champion) FROZEN (lr=0) vs the scripted bashy cage-advance offense_bot (D167), bot = team1, full games, def-canary build. Over n=379 dashboard frames (≈196M steps of rollout): **tds_t0 (champion offense, vs bot defense) = 0.565 · tds_t1 (bot offense, vs CHAMPION defense) = 1.156** → the bot outscores the champion **2.05:1**. Symmetric read: the champion's DEFENSE allows 1.156 TD/ep; the *bot's* defense allows only 0.565 — the champion is ~2× leakier on defense than a deterministic script that just forms a cage and grinds forward. This is the opponent-quality failure (D166): self-play from a weak prior plateaus at a mutually-incompetent equilibrium — the champion never learned to screen/keep-a-safety/wall-lanes because no self-play opponent ever punished the absence. The offense_bot is the missing "competent offense." MECHANISM NOTE: the def-canary fields (def_deep_safety, def_carrier_path_zerotz, def_carrier_min_dodges, def_carrier_marked_frac — bloodbowl.h:209-213) ARE computed in-env (ep_* sums L500-504) but are NOT yet wired to the Log struct/dashboard, so this baseline rests on the scoreboard (tds_t1) not the mechanistic readout; wiring them is a deferred nice-to-have (the scoreboard already settles the question). **D170-CORRECTION — the block-economy lineage is NATIVE, not torch (I misread turnover3's 399K SPS as torch; it's native-on-the-slow-judge-GPU).** turnover3_cap.bin starts with raw float bytes `\xe7\xbaR>` (a native weight blob, biases not stored separately), NOT a torch zip (`PK\x03\x04`). (2) `training/convert_checkpoint.py --to-torch` converts the native champion → torch state_dict (turnover3_torch.bin, hidden 512×3, obs 2782) — **biases zero-filled** (D45 native↔torch limitation), so the warm-start is mildly degraded and re-learns biases in the first frames. **D172 — BC BOTTLENECK SETTLED: it is NOT data volume (the ~25k-game corpus is saturated), and NOT mainly the discarded biases. The ceiling is the BC recipe/representation (2026-06-22).** Alex asked why 25k human games isn't enough for a functional bot and whether to scrape every FUMBBL game ever (incl. older rules). Ran two controlled experiments on box-1 (fixed val set = 413,130 pairs / 2,446 replays, checksum-verified identical across all 6 runs; 3000 steps cosine, seed 42; both defense1 + the BBTV server ran undisturbed). (1) **DATA-SCALING CURVE = SATURATED:** val exact 0.448 / 0.451 / 0.450 / 0.451 at train-frac 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75 / 1.00 (424k → 1.67M pairs). Quadrupling the data buys ZERO (0.003 spread, inside noise); per-head acc constant to 3 decimals. **More data — including a mass older-rules scrape — is NOT justified.** (2) **BIAS-IMPACT = real-but-minor:** zeroing bc_v4's biases (the ones the native/CUDA bias-free pipeline discards at warm-start; decoder bias max |4.8|) costs only **−0.0133 val exact** (0.5077 → 0.4944, ~2.6% rel), spread across heads (type −1.5pts). So my earlier "bias-drop is the headline culprit" hunch was OVERSTATED — it's a measurable edge worth recovering if cheap (and defense1, being torch, already avoids it), NOT a dominant lever. CONCLUSION: the BC ceiling (~0.45–0.51 val exact) is bounded by the **model/recipe** — capacity, the **iid zero-recurrent-state (no-memory) BC formulation** (consistent with D35: sequence context > more data > bigger policy), and the inherent label noise of imitating diverse human play — not by dataset size or biases. The real levers for a functional/defending bot are therefore: (a) sequence-context BC (bc_v5, D35) to break the no-memory ceiling, (b) preserve the human prior THROUGH RL (KL-to-bc, stop annealing to zero) so self-play stops eroding it (the turnover3 "looks untrained on defense" = D170 erosion), (c) explicit defensive shaping + competent opponents (the cage-bot fix + defense pivot). Caveat: single seed, cosine-endpoint noise ~±0.02 (flatness robust to it); bias eval is exact/deterministic. Artifacts in box `/tmp/` (curve_*, bc_v4_nobias.bin, edited bc_pretrain.py); original bc_pretrain.py restored.

Conceded **tds_t1 1.156 (D170 frozen baseline) → 0.718 final (−38%)**; champion offense tds_t0 0.565 → ~0.474 (slight dip). So facing a competent-ISH attacker does pull the champion's defense down toward the bot's own ~0.565 allowance — the D166 opponent-quality thesis holds directionally. THREE confounds keep this from being the verdict: (1) it trained against the **pre-fix** cage-bot (D167/offense_bot 150a1fb fixed AFTER launch — the old bot walked its carrier into contact, so the champion partly "learned to punish a bad ball-handler," not general defense); (2) zero-biased warm-start (D170-corr); (3) one deterministic opponent (overfit risk). For any keeper run, set `--train.checkpoint-interval`/`--selfplay.snapshot-interval` AND back the cap to Mac (D160). The long-standing "sequence context" lever is, empirically, not the lever (2026-06-23).** Path-A cheap screen (context features computed from the ordered pairs at BC-load time, NO engine change; built by Codex, 2 review loops + a loop-3 obs-redundancy check; iid arm reproduces D172's 0.451 EXACTLY, checksum-pinned identical val set, strict --head-loss legacy ablation). Four arms, val exact: **iid 0.451 · structural 0.450 (−0.001) · structural+last-action 0.453 · last-action-only 0.453**. All within the ±0.02 cosine-endpoint noise band (D172). READS: (1) **structural features = NULL** — because the within-turn context they encode is ALREADY in obs-v4: per-player `BB_PF_USED`("activated this turn")/`BB_PF_ACTIVATING` flags (player bytes [4][5]), the [784+8..13] blitz/pass/handoff/foul/ttm/secure-used-this-turn scalars, rerolls [784+5/6], deciding/active [768+10/11]. A linear layer already reads all of it. (2) **last-action history** (the only signal NOT in the pre-action obs) gives a negligible +0.002 (within noise) AND is the copycat-prone feature — so even that hair is suspect and would need a Path-B rollout to trust. CONCLUSION: the BC ceiling (~0.45–0.51) is NOT from missing observable/temporal context — the obs is already information-rich. This triangulates with the loop-1 research (AlphaStar Unplugged: "no-memory ≥ LSTM for BC"; MimicBot single-frame won) and D172 (data-saturated). The "we keep naming sequence context and never build it" tension (D35/D45/D47/D140) is RESOLVED: we finally built it (the cheap, correct version) and it does ~nothing — so we can stop naming it. IMPLICATION for recurrence (the queued A/B): its cheap win (short history) just showed negligible, and its remaining value (long-horizon intent memory) is exactly what AlphaStar found doesn't beat no-memory for BC → recurrence is LIKELY low-ROI; recommend NOT spending the multi-day build, pivot instead. THE REAL LEVERS (re-confirmed, research-backed): (b) **KL-to-bc anchor THROUGH RL** — stop annealing to zero so self-play stops eroding the prior (AlphaStar persistent-KL, MimicBot hybrid-loss, Diplomacy piKL all independently endorse this; it's the turnover3 "untrained on defense" = D170 erosion fix); (c) **defensive shaping + competent opponents** — the fixed cage-bot (150a1fb) + defense2 vs it. **D176 — KL-ANCHOR A/B VERDICT: the BC anchor FAILS; OPPONENT QUALITY is the defense lever (2026-06-23). **D182 — THE COMPLETED POSSESSION/GAIN SCREEN IS REJECTED; ITS ONE CLIP ALSO EXPOSED AN UNSAFE TERMINAL-COMPOSITION PATH (2026-07-14).** The cleanly redeployed `500M × 2` possession/gain screen completed all eight training/evaluation arms and preserved every final checkpoint/result, but no `SCREEN_COMPLETE.json` was published. Its final cumulative train counters were `reward_clip_episodes=1/351253`, `reward_clip_excess=0.015/351253`, with zero non-finite, engine-error, demo, or fallback counters; final eval had 10,047 games and zero integrity counters. The acceptance gate therefore behaved correctly. The retained schema records neither the clipped sign nor terminal/non-terminal context, so the exact historical co-firing components cannot be claimed after the fact; `0.015` equals the rush-cost coefficient but does not prove causation. A code audit nevertheless confirmed an independent structural defect: `bbe_finish_episode` added win/draw/loss to the current action's entire shaping subtotal, so an arbitrary terminal-action scaffold could distort or exceed the learner's `[-1,1]` emission even though TD+result passed static validation. DECISION: reject the whole screen as causal evidence; do not manufacture completion, relax the any-clip gate, run transfer from it, or promote its preliminary factorial. Terminal composition now discards incidental same-action shaping, preserves only explicitly tracked objective reward (TD), then adds result utility; explicitly episode-terminal terms such as quarantined statmatch remain separate and clip-visible. Episode-return accounting follows the reward actually emitted. New telemetry splits terminal from non-terminal clipped samples so recurrence is classifiable. Rerun every compared arm under this single corrected semantic contract before interpreting possession/gain effects; any recurrence still fails closed and requires its own diagnosis. Canonical rejected evidence remains immutable at `runs/reward-screens/possession-gain-screen-20260713-v2` on the audit host; screen manifest SHA `e2c09590483f5703c03b53128b86535b35e08ada5a2a039abfa83b74e8133816`, rejected checkpoint SHA `9d368986f49903171cb563c48c02371d620159f0fc4260c903dedb0b10eca7f2`.

**D183 — THE SIX-DAY VACATION RUN IS A CLOSED TWO-LINEAGE CONFIRMATION QUEUE, NOT AN AUTONOMOUS REWARD SEARCH (2026-07-14).** The unattended system may consume already-reviewed evidence but may not invent candidates, change thresholds, promote a reward, or mutate production. Learned transfer is exactly `4096` games per cell with candidate/reference, seeds 42/43, exactly four identical pinned anchors, and both native backend orientations; per-cell outputs are atomic and hash-bound. Its mean, per-training-seed, per-anchor, per-orientation, and worst-cell thresholds are a deterministic fixed-stratum routing rule—not a confidence interval over pseudoreplicated cells. The typed queue pins every executable, runner, config, checkpoint, manifest, evidence file, and directory tree; enforces disk/inodes, progress, maximum runtime, three-poll thermal, validator, and completed-evidence revalidation gates; and halts with later jobs pending on any failure. PPO screens are non-resume-safe; only atomic, restart-validating transfer/gate jobs may resume. Queue-owned screens set `ARM_DETACH=0`, keeping the screen, arm wrapper, trainer, and descendants inside the queue job's new-session process group so a guard cannot strand GPU work. BBTV remains observational only: it may stream each newest completed checkpoint, but its output is never scientific input. No unattended result changes a production default; post-vacation promotion still requires human review.

**D188 — CORRECTION: D187 MIXED ENDPOINT MASKS AND OMITTED PANEL EPISODE WEIGHTS FROM STATIC-POOL SCORE; ITS QUALITATIVE VERDICT STANDS (2026-07-14).** Puffer normalizes every environment field by each dashboard panel's completed-episode count `n`, including both `hist_score_bank_*` and `hist_n_bank_*`. Static-pool score must therefore be `sum(hist_score_bank_i * n) / sum(hist_n_bank_i * n)`, while ordinary fields are `sum(metric * n) / sum(n)`. The first band contains 3,810 panels, 365,615 episodes, 175,000.000869 frozen-bank games, and score sum 93,401.500416; the last has 3,815 panels, 395,560 episodes, 183,050.000779 games, and score sum 113,599.000447. **D189 — BBTV'S GPU-BUILT MATCH SERVER WOULD STRAND THE PINNED VACATION OVERFLOW; MOVE ONLY THE VIEWER TO A PROVEN CPU BUILD (2026-07-14).** The primary/overflow autonomy review initially inferred that BBTV could not block the handoff because checkpoint conversion sets `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""`. A spare-port probe established a second constraint: hiding CUDA removed the probe PID from the parser, but the current viewer has `pufferlib._C.gpu=1`, so PuffeRL failed with `RuntimeError: No CUDA GPUs are available` while moving the policy. DECISION: neither queue, its pins, nor its gates may be weakened. Build a separate fp32 CPU Blood Bowl viewer in `/home/rache/bloodbowl-rl-bbtv-cpu/vendor/PufferLib` with `./build.sh bloodbowl --cpu`; require the launcher to prove that the imported `_C` resides in that tree and reports `env_name=bloodbowl`, `gpu=0`, and `precision_bytes=4`; hide CUDA from each match child; and before switching only `bbstream`, require a real spare-port `hello`/`match_start`/`snapshot` cycle plus the exact pinned parser showing only the live trainer. Preserve the existing GPU viewer and static stream as rollback, and roll back only by removing the entire follower service override; pairing the CPU-hiding follower with the old GPU viewer is the confirmed crash mode. After the switch, verify public HTTP/WebSocket freshness, no BBTV compute PID, unchanged primary PID/service/progress, and byte-identical primary/overflow pins. BBTV remains observational and this changes no reward, trainer, queue, scientific input, or promotion decision.

**D190 — ADD A BEHAVIOR-NEUTRAL EMITTED-REWARD COMPONENT LEDGER FOR FUTURE RUNS; DO NOT RETROFIT THE ACTIVE VACATION QUEUES (2026-07-15).** D187 could observe total reward integrity and behavior but could not say whether distance, possession, block EV, sequencing, Rush, or another term supplied the learner's return. Summing agents is forbidden because zero-sum channels would cancel. A signed residual records float refolding error, while mismatch and non-finite counters fail integrity. Terminal reconstruction discards incidental same-action shaping, preserves explicit touchdown reward, and adds result/statmatch once; the ledger follows that actual emission rather than inventing counterfactual credit. The dashboard contract grows from 88 to 123 environment keys, so both vector dictionaries and the visible metric limit are raised from 96 to 160 with install/check migrations and a machine-readable contract test. Fable's headless architecture review approved the core arithmetic and its requested dashboard-capacity, call-site-label, draw/objective-bypass, and vector-path checks were resolved. This ledger enables causal diagnosis in newly built runs; it does not validate any component, alter a reward coefficient, promote R0, or support retroactive attribution. **D193 — IMPLEMENT BB2025 STALLING AS ENGINE LAW, NOT A REWARD PENALTY (2026-07-15).** The reward/rules audit described the current Third Season rule, but a focused executable search and failing regression proved the engine never enforced it: a turn-1 carrier one free square from the end zone could end their activation standing with the ball, consumed no crowd die, and continued without a Turnover. DECISION: at carrier activation start, snapshot whether any occupied-pitch scoring path exists with zero Dodges and zero Rushes and no compulsory activation-gate, Bloodlust, Animal Savagery, or Ball & Chain die. If that player finishes the activation still standing and holding the ball without an earlier Turnover, roll a non-rerollable D6 through `bb_rng`; `D6 >= current team turn` pushes the existing `BB_KD_OTHER` chain. Voluntarily ending the team turn before activating an eligible carrier marks that carrier used and performs the same check. A prior Turnover that ends the turn first and a successful Pass/Hand-off that transfers possession are exemptions. The roll is still consumed on turns 7–8 even though it cannot succeed. Reusing KNOCKDOWN preserves one owner for Steady Footing, ball release/bounce, armour/injury, Turnover, and stack unwinding; a Steady Footing 6 therefore prevents both the knockdown and Turnover per the May 2026 FAQ. Nine behavioral tests cover the success path, turn threshold, Rush/Dodge/gate exemptions, Hand-off transfer, whole-turn forgoing, prior Turnover, and Steady Footing; a query-purity canary proves gate inspection does not mutate Skill coverage, and the touchdown canary proves a real score does not fall through into Stalling. All 411 engine, 37 reward, 2 contact-bot, and 1 loader tests pass optimized and under ASan/UBSan, and golden replay resimulation stays exact. No match field or procedure identifier was added, so the BBS1 match layout/fingerprint is unchanged. Residuals remain explicit: Fumblerooski is not implemented; Steady Footing's broader FAQ-permitted team-reroll choice is still an existing engine approximation; and the 454-way policy interface can end the whole team turn but does not yet expose the finer rulebook choice to forego only one player and continue activating others. This fix must not be deployed over the source-pinned live vacation experiment; it enters only future reviewed builds.

**D194 — AUTHOR RARE-DECISION DRILLS BY LEGAL ENGINE TRAJECTORY WITH EXACT TWO-STREAM REPLAY, NEVER BY STATE SURGERY (2026-07-15).** The strict historical bank is rich in opening opportunity states but sharply censored for Pass, Hand-off, second-half/late-drive, contextual-reroll, and score-now-versus-Stall decisions. Each recipe initializes through `bb_match_init_forced_p`/`random_p`, saves the initialized raw bytes, reaches captures only through enumerated legal `bb_apply` actions, and records packed actions plus every in-match die's sides and face. Verification reruns procgen from the same seed/stream, requires initialized byte identity, scripts the game-die faces, checks decision team and legal membership before every action, requires exact dice consumption/sides, and accepts only byte-identical loader-valid decision states. Direct writes to players, grid, ball, score, turn, half, resources, status, or procedure frames are forbidden. Authored BBS metadata uses the reserved `0xA.......` source-ID namespace; train/dev/test grouping is by recipe template; counterfactual branch outcomes remain evaluation-only and never become BBS fields, observations, rewards, masks, or BC labels. The serializer consumes recipes and internally exact-replays them into private storage, so callers cannot substitute a separately mutated raw match after verification; it also rejects any declared capture decision index that differs from the verified recipe action count. Nested Pass/Hand-off target and reroll windows remain rejected until their complete resumable stacks receive explicit shared validators. The phase-1 executable proof reaches the first genuine post-kickoff team-turn with a const deterministic setup controller, rejects illegal actions, missing/extra/wrong dice, decision-team drift, initialized/captured byte drift, false capture indices, malformed BBS records, and is accepted byte-for-byte by the hardened Puffer loader. **D198 — ENFORCE PA-DASH AND NO BALL IN ENGINE LEGALITY, NEVER AS REWARD SHAPING (2026-07-15).** F1 adversarial review proved two broader engine gaps behind the authored predicate's defensive checks. `activation_legal` exposed Pass declaration to PA-dash players even though `proc_ball` immediately rejected them, and `bb_can_catch` omitted No Ball even though catch resolution auto-failed it. DECISION: require `pa > 0` before `BB_ACT_PASS` is offered; Hand-off declaration remains available. Make `bb_can_catch` exclude No Ball so scatter, throw-in, kickoff landing, Dump-off selection, and ordinary catch resolution share the actual catch-eligibility rule. Keep Hand-off target eligibility distinct: any adjacent Standing team-mate with a Tackle Zone remains selectable, including No Ball, which then automatically fails the required Catch without consuming a catch die before the Bounce and ordinary Turnover. A Pass may still target any legal square occupied by a No Ball player and then Bounce without a catch die. Exclude No Ball from interception candidates and Touchback recipients; Touchback falls back to legal empty-square placement when no eligible Standing recipient exists. Five focused tests cover PA-dash Pass masking while preserving Hand-off, No Ball Hand-off auto-failure/dice flow, accurate Pass-to-No-Ball target/bounce dice flow, No Ball interception exclusion, and Touchback recipient/fallback enumeration and resolution. The deliberate rule change altered deterministic controller choices in the Dwarf/Skaven, Goblin/Halfling, and Amazon/Norse goldens; all eight goldens were regenerated twice byte-identically and now resimulate exactly. All 423 engine, 37 reward, 2 contact-bot, and 4 loader tests pass optimized and under ASan/UBSan; Clang static analysis and diff checks pass. No match layout, BBS fingerprint, reward, coefficient, observation shape, or action-space width changed. D198 supersedes D197's noted pending mask/helper gaps but does not widen the BBS boundary, publish an authored bank, alter the frozen vacation checkout, or authorize training/deployment.

**D201 — ADMIT ONE EXACT FAILED-DODGE REROLL STACK THROUGH THE PRODUCTION LOADER WITHOUT WIDENING SCENARIO OR WRITER SEMANTICS (2026-07-15; exact-head review closure).** F4 cannot be represented at a fresh team-turn boundary because the reroll choice exists inside a live generic TEST procedure. DECISION: split raw BBS validation into (a) `bb_state_bank_boundary_valid`, retained by historical scenario scanners and the current authored writer, and (b) `bb_state_bank_resumable_valid`, used only by production reset admission and the canonical continuation canary. The resumable union admits the ordinary fresh-team-turn state plus exactly one five-frame nested shape: `MATCH -> TEAM_TURN -> ACTIVATION(Move) -> MOVE -> TEST(Dodge)` at the pending choice after a failed first-step, non-Rush Dodge. The procedure-specific validator checks exact lower-frame fields, a Standing active mover with zero movement/rush use and ordinary MA remaining, absence of Rooted and activation-cleared Distracted/Eye Gouged flags, an adjacent empty destination, a marked origin, no held carrier or destination ground ball, exact pending-test latches, `match.ret == 0`, failed die, a target recomputed with implemented modifiers, valid generated skill bits, and a legal set containing real Use Re-roll and Decline choices and nothing outside the reroll family. A legally resolved Rush is intentionally a different shape: before its pending Dodge, moved/rushes remain zero but the successful Rush result persists in `match.ret`; an exact legal fixture proves that shape is rejected. Direct skill-bit validation also closes a broader raw-snapshot gap that the ordinary skill iterator could not reveal because it intentionally stops at `BB_SKILL_COUNT`. A legal fixture reaches the admitted state through ACTIVATE, DECLARE MOVE, and STEP with an exactly scripted failed Dodge. Tests prove input preservation and reject malformed stack depth, parent procedures/phases/slots/data, destination, TEST kind/phase/target/die/latches, Rooted/Distracted/Eye Gouged/Used movers, exhausted or negative MA, movement/rush counters, destination ball, and unknown skill bits. A team-reroll branch succeeds and continues the Move with exactly one D6; a Decline branch consumes exactly the two scripted Armour dice, leaves the mover Prone, preserves the reroll, and turns over. Because reroll masks are nonspatial and a reset has no preceding STEP history, observation context bytes 9/12 expose the parent MOVE destination egocentrically without changing the 2782-byte shape; a metamorphic Puffer test proves two accepted same-target/same-mask states with different destinations no longer alias and that the identical successful reroll reaches different squares. The production Puffer test reloads byte-identically, exposes TEST target 3 plus the pending destination, masks Use/Decline only to the deciding coach and null only to the waiting coach, and repeats both continuations plus the canonical canary. All 428 engine, 37 reward, 2 contact-bot, and 7 loader tests pass optimized; sanitizer and hosted exact-head review results are recorded on the PR before merge. No writer or discovery controller yet emits this state, every other nested shape remains rejected, and no reroll action, outcome, regret, reward, BC label, bank artifact, training input, deployment, or frozen-queue change is authorized. The next separate tranche must legally discover and exact-replay one F4 recipe before selectively widening the authored writer.

**D202 — TACKLE SUPPRESSES THE DODGE SKILL REROLL AT THE ORIGIN WITHOUT SUPPRESSING TEAM RE-ROLL OR PRO (2026-07-15).** The BB2025 Tackle rule prevents an opponent leaving the Tackle player's Tackle Zone from using Dodge. The generic reroll hook previously granted Dodge from test kind alone, so a newly admitted pending-Dodge state could expose a rules-illegal skill reroll. DECISION: while querying a Dodge reroll, skip `BB_SK_DODGE` when `bb_has_tackle_adjacent` finds an opposition Tackle player exerting a Tackle Zone on the mover's live origin square. The Dodge TEST occurs before movement, making that coordinate the correct origin. Do not suppress the generic Team Re-roll or Pro paths: they remain independent reroll sources under BB2025. A focused four-cell contract consists of the existing no-Tackle Dodge control plus Tackle with (a) Dodge only and no pool, where the failed Dodge resolves without a reroll window, (b) one Team Re-roll, where Team+Decline are offered and Team succeeds, and (c) Pro, where Pro+Decline are offered and the 3+ gate plus rerolled Dodge succeeds; every Tackle cell excludes the Dodge skill action with exact scripted dice. This is a global rules-law correction, not an F4-only loader filter, and any golden changes must be explicitly regenerated and reviewed rather than silently accepted.

**D203 — PROVE ONE F4 PENDING-DODGE REROLL OPPORTUNITY BEFORE THE POLICY CHOICE, AND WIDEN ONLY THAT AUTHORED WRITER PATH (2026-07-15).** The fixed F4 recipe uses controller seed 1 and reaches D201's exact loader-valid five-frame pending-Dodge shape only by applying 384 enumerated legal engine decisions and recording 110 in-match dice. DECISION: preserve the three semantic logits heads but transport the current ragged joint support as packed 10-bit head values. Native and Torch rollout sample type, then argument conditioned on type, then square conditioned on both. Each sampler writes the selected conditional slices into the existing 454-wide rollout mask, so PPO recomputation uses exactly the behavior distribution without storing ragged support across the horizon. Inactive heads canonicalize to singleton `arg=32` and `square=390`, contributing zero log-probability, entropy, and gradient. Touchback recipient and fallback forms remain disjoint; macro destinations are explicit virtual env actions in joint support. `bbe_decode` now accepts only an exact, unambiguous tuple and fails closed on marginal cross-products, non-finite/fractional/out-of-range heads, or distinct engine actions that collide under projection; scripted bots still choose directly from `legal[]`. The transient vector allocation reserves at most `BB_LEGAL_MAX+391` tuples per agent but copies only each buffer's compact current count; measured support therefore avoids expanding rollout storage. Agent permutation now resets, re-emits, and uploads vector state immediately after repointing so self-play cannot sample identity-layout observations or supports on its first rollout. Fresh replay extraction advances to BBP v4: identical physical records now carry selected conditional masks and canonical inactive targets, so v1-v3 action corpora and historical marginal-mask checkpoints are not exact-action inputs by shape coincidence. Future reward screens bind the exact-action patch and both native/CPU binding sources into their implementation provenance. Optimized and sanitizer C suites, Python corpus/backend tests, a fresh Puffer patch install, local C/CPU-binding compilation, Torch support-membership and rollout/recompute log-probability+entropy equality, zero-repair full games, and deterministic FNV are merge gates. This tranche remains source-only and does not touch the occupied RTX 2070 recovery run or BBTV. A reviewed post-boundary deployment must prove the exact installed module and zero integrity violations before a paired learning screen; recurrent rollout/recompute state parity remains the next independent harness tranche.

D218 entropy/provenance clarification: the entropy scalar is a sampled/pathwise conditional-entropy estimate. Its expectation matches factorized joint entropy, but ordinary backpropagation does not send downstream conditional-entropy gradients through earlier-head probabilities. This bounded approximation does not affect exact behavior log-probabilities or PPO ratios. Native CUDA compilation for the pinned target architecture is a source-merge gate; native CUDA graph-capture and finite rollout/recompute ratio, entropy, and gradient execution remain a post-boundary deployment gate so this source tranche does not contend with or mutate the occupied recovery experiment. The installed native/CPU module must expose the exact backend-source digest compiled into it; source timestamps alone are insufficient provenance.

**D219 — ZERO SCIENTIFIC CONTAMINATION WITH A BOUNDED FAIL-FAST COMPUTE BUDGET (2026-07-21).** D218 makes sampled/executed action identity exact, but first-transition native aborts alone do not bound compute lost to telemetry-visible reward, non-finite, component-reconciliation, engine, demo, or fallback failures. DECISION: accepted exact-action runs have a contamination budget of exactly zero. Every integrity-bearing schema-2 machine panel must report finite, numerically exact zero for one frozen hard registry including `illegal_frac`; no epsilon, averaging, or rare-event allowance applies. `tools/live_integrity_guard.py` consumes only new complete log bytes, preserves partial live records for the next poll, rejects malformed/schema/step/key/value/state/log replacement or truncation, writes one atomic failure artifact, and exhausts liveness after 180 seconds without an integrity-bearing panel. Legitimate metadata-only panels before any episode completes are consumed but do not reset that clock. Reward screens enforce the same registry again over train/eval acceptance and rescan completed/recovered logs without applying a live silence deadline; any unterminated completed-log tail is invalid. The guard and status wrapper hashes, registry, poll interval, and silence budget are frozen into screen/run/queue provenance. A redundant watchdog runs inside the trainer's durable detached supervision tree, so loss of the outer SSH/screen orchestrator cannot remove bounded detection; the outer screen and durable watchdog maintain independent incremental state files so overlapping reads cannot race or regress one another. On failure the watchdog marks the arm, terminates the exact trainer, and forces nonzero atomic status when the wrapper survives. No later arm or completion artifact may advance after a failure. A new repaired runtime receives no multi-day budget until static/install/module provenance, CUDA construction/graph capture, zero-update ratio/log-probability/entropy/gradient, deterministic exact-support full-game smokes, and then one reward-frozen `exact-action-canary` arm of exactly 50M requested steps pass with zero hard failures. The canary is qualification-only: never warm-start from its checkpoint or treat its metrics as causal/reward evidence. This tranche changes no reward, optimizer, opponent, production default, BBTV process, or occupied pre-repair recovery run; deployment remains gated on that run's immutable boundary.

**D220 — REQUIRE ONE IMMUTABLE TARGET-GPU VERDICT BEFORE THE EXACT-ACTION CANARY (2026-07-21).** Source and CPU tests cannot prove that the repaired recurrent CUDA path is clean under graph capture or that PPO recomputation samples only learner-owned rows. A separate sampler defect also made frozen rows eligible at `prio_alpha=0`, because zero advantage raised to the zero power has unit weight. DECISION: explicitly assign literal zero sampling probability to every frozen row, normalize only the native primary-row partition, and reject invalid or empty primary layouts. Before the disposable 50M exact-action canary, `tools/qualify_recurrent_cuda.py` must run fresh isolated subprocess cells on the target GPU and independently validate one atomic, qualification-only artifact. Qualification is fp32-only: BF16 rounds stored behavior log probabilities before recomputation, so no strict near-unity ratio claim is accepted without a separately reviewed quantization-aware contract. Acceptance requires predeclared clean source/module/backend/environment identities; exact-zero state in every primary and frozen bank/buffer at construction; graph-on/off first-rollout parity; automatic terminal reset parity against an explicit all-bank zero control; bounded repeated real PPO calls covering every primary row with no frozen selection, finite near-unity ratios, and byte-identical weights at learning rate zero; exactly zero hard-integrity counters; and throughput within ten percent of a same-host/config/precision predecessor artifact whose module/backend/environment identities were predeclared both when captured and consumed. Missing, malformed, non-finite, incomplete, drifted, or nonzero evidence fails; failure reporting may write only to a prevalidated external new/empty output directory. Qualification artifacts and optimizer state are never checkpoint ancestry or scientific reward evidence. This is source-only while the recovery queue owns the RTX 2070: it does not authorize a rebuild, service restart, live deployment, canary, reward change, checkpoint promotion, or BBTV mutation before the immutable boundary.

Qualification advances to schema 3, binds the league patch in its source-file closure, and explicitly rejects schema-2 qualification and predecessor artifacts. The operator must predeclare the full replacement-candidate commit; the schema-3 runner requires that value to equal its own clean `HEAD` and the separate clean candidate checkout, while the predecessor remains the exact isolated `afc8008933548438ca93c41341f5f08fdd294386` runtime. Experiment patch provenance must include the same league patch, and launch preflight requires both its marker and complete reverse applicability.
