**D241 addendum — BOTH SIDES AND THE MIRROR: THE HOLE IS PLAY UNDER CONTACT PRESSURE, NOT THE OPENING PER SE (2026-08-18 13:30 PDT).** Contact bot as HOME (champion AWAY, 2,003 games): champion 0.035 TD/game, bot 1.276 — symmetric with the AWAY read (0.052 / 1.281), so side and receiving do not matter; the tiny-n mid-run panel that briefly showed 0.8–1.3 for the champion was noise. **Mirror from kickoff (10,018 full games, `demo_reset_pct 0`): 0.951 TD/game total (both teams), possession 0.199, blocks 9.2/game, dodges 7.8, gfi 3.9, pickups 1.32 attempted / 0.66 successful, passes 0, hand-offs 0.** So the policy CAN take a drive from kickoff to the endzone against itself (~0.48/team-game vs the human 2.2), i.e. the opening is not absent — but against a scripted opponent that simply blocks and marks it produces almost nothing while conceding 1.28. That is D166's finding on the new lineage: self-play from a weak prior settles into a mutually-permissive equilibrium and never has to play through contact; the ladder has taught scoring and ball acquisition, not pressure. Two implications, both cheap and both already tooled: (1) the kickoff graduation rungs must include a **scripted-bot opponent share** (`scripted_opponent` + pool mix, D166/D170 machinery) rather than pure pool self-play, or the graduation exam will keep failing for the same reason; (2) the contact-bot exam is the standing pre-registered graduation metric — champion TD/game and conceded TD/game vs the fixed bots, both sides — and every future checkpoint gets it (rig, ~45 min per side on the torch path). Recorded also: seed-42 replicate of the uniform chain launched on the rig 13:05 PDT (`rig-seed42-20260818`, warm Vast stage-1 rehosted, pool rung12/uniform/chain/stage1 `ce9042f6`, 138M steps in 20 min, `demo_episodes` 0.53). Vast r25 at 3.85B: windows 2-3.5B 0.585 → 3.5-4.2B 0.641 (+0.056, still climbing) — the pre-inserted `uniform-r25-chain` stays.

**D243 — NATIVE TRAINING AGAINST A SCRIPTED BOT VIA A SCRIPTED BANK (NO CUDA CHANGE), A `graft` LINEAGE BRIDGE FOR SOURCE CHANGES, AND THE FIRST KICKOFF RUNG WITH A CONTACT-BOT SHARE RUNNING ON A SECOND VAST BOX (2026-08-18, PR #94 branch `ab5c897`).** D241's exam said the missing skill is play under contact pressure, and the only way to train against a bot at native speed was guarded off (`pufferl_scripted_training_guard.patch`: no scripted-row exclusion on the CUDA path; the torch path with its row filter runs ~5K SPS on the rig — 30-100× too slow for a 5B rung). Scoping (Explore agent, 42 tool uses) found the seat identity that makes it cheap: in a tagged self-play env the frozen bank plays slot 1 (AWAY) and its rows are the bank's contiguous tail slice per buffer, which `puffer_frozen_prio_mask` already excludes from the prioritized minibatch sampler; the scripted opponent also plays slot 1 (`scripted_opponent_team=1`). So **`scripted_bank_tag = b+1`** makes the bot act ONLY in envs tagged for bank b, and its (never-executed-by-policy) rows are excluded from PPO by the SAME mechanism as frozen-bank rows — a two-line env predicate on `env->tag`, a kwarg, a guard relaxation, no `.cu` change; the learner rows in those envs (slot 0) train normally, and `hist_score_bank[b]` becomes a free per-rollout "learner vs bot" score. Built as `SCRIPTED_BANK_TAG`/`SCRIPTED_BOT_TYPE` through launcher → screen → ladder stage → marker; binding hard-fails on out-of-range tag or wrong team rather than falling back to global mode; guard v1 kept so `install_puffer_env.sh` upgrades an already-installed tree in place. **Because `bloodbowl.h` changed, `source_sha256` changed and every existing sidecar becomes ineligible on the new build; `rehost` refuses source drift by design.** So the reviewed bridge is now a first-class mode: **`BOOTSTRAP_MODE=graft-v6` / `SCREEN_PROFILE=graft`** — every sidecar among warm + 4 banks must bind either this build exactly or the operator-declared old (source, patch bundle) with any module; ≥1 old-build; all old-build modules identical; `GRAFT_REASON` required; all of it recorded in the run manifest and hashed into the accepted sidecar as `ancestry.grafted_from` (source/module/patch/warm-lineage/reason). Adversarial review (62 tool uses) found and we fixed before first launch: (1) BLOCKER — the first graft design deadlocked the ladder one rung later (warm new-build, pool three old-build banks: lineage-v6 refused the banks, graft/OLD refused the warm, graft/NEW was a no-op) — fixed by per-sidecar classification (`checkpoint_lineage.graft_bridge`), reproduced then tested against real 16 MB sidecars in exactly that mixed pool; (2) the new guard patch was neither applicable nor already-applied on any tree carrying the old guard — v1 kept, installer reverse-applies it, drift check now reverse-verifies both; (3) graft pool banks were validated against no build at all — now pinned to {this build, declared old build}; (4) the C predicate had no test — `test_contact_bot.c` now asserts digest equality/inequality by tag; (5) out-of-range tag silently fell back to GLOBAL scripted mode (the exact contamination the guard exists for) — now `exit(1)`; plus GRAFT_REASON, no-op→`rehost` message, env-scrubbed tests, docs. 160 Python tests + `make test` green; 15 commits. **Deployment:** rented a second Vast box `bb-ryzen2` (Ryzen 9 5950X @5.1 GHz, 32 threads, RTX 3090, $0.241/hr, instance 48055773) rather than rebuild under box 1's live trainer; built PR #94 head (`source 3ed6899e…`; setup gotchas: `--no-deps` pip skipped pybind11/rich_argparse — install PufferLib's declared deps minus torch), shipped bank + six sidecars from box 1, plan-only graft dry run verified (contract records `graft{from_source 21f20412, from_patch de77f6c0, from_module 72e1f94b, warm 82f34393}` and `ladder{maxdist 0, reset 0, scripted_bank_tag 4, bot 0}`), then campaign `vast2-20260818` launched 14:52 PDT: **kickoff rung (reset 0) grafted from chain2 (tds 0.652), pool uniform/chain/stage1/chain2 `cb769c10…`, bank 4 = contact bot (~12% of envs), 200K SPS, `demo_episodes 0.00`, `illegal_frac 0`, `hist_score_bank_3` live at ~0.21 early.** This is a deliberate A/B against box 1: same root (chain2), box 1 goes chain2→r25→r25-chain→kickoff with pure pool self-play, box 2 goes chain2→kickoff with the bot bank; the graduation exam (D50/D241: TD/game and conceded TD/game vs the contact bot from kickoff, both sides) decides. `hist_score_bank_3` is a training-distribution number and NOT the exam.

**D242 — r25 (RESET 0.25) ACCEPTED AT tds 0.695 WITH 75% KICKOFF STARTS AND STILL CLIMBING → r25-CHAIN; BOX-2 KICKOFF-WITH-BOT SHOWS THE EXPECTED PRESSURE DIP (2026-08-18 15:42 PDT).** `uniform-r25` (warm chain2, pool `e138c936`, 5B in 8h55m) accepted, sidecar `39c12405…`: eval **tds 0.695**, perf 0.539, draw 0.563, blitzes 13.9, blocks 11.2, possession 0.203, **pickup_attempts 1.17 / success 0.57** (up from 0.91/0.46 at chain2), dodges 7.7, gfi 3.2, pass_attempts 0.006, `demo_episodes` 0.244 as declared. Because three-quarters of these episodes are real full games from kickoff, this `tds` is much closer to a from-kickoff number than any 0.5-reset rung — and it went UP on halving the banked starts (0.652 → 0.695), which is the transfer signal D74's 0.5→0.25→0 step exists to show. Windows 0-1B 0.496 → 1-3B 0.632 → 3-5B 0.639; 2-3.5B 0.585 → 3.5-5B 0.663 (+0.08): still climbing, so the pre-inserted `uniform-r25-chain` launched 15:42 PDT (warm r25 accepted, pool chain/stage1/chain2/r25 `0339ccb4…`); kickoff@0 follows it. Standing rule from D240 held this time: the chain stage was pre-inserted while the rung was mid-run, so no tick was load-bearing. Box 2 (kickoff@0 + contact-bot bank, D243) at 0.86B: tds 0.80 → 0.54 → 0.49 across the first three 0.3B windows while possession fell 0.18 → 0.13 — the bot's pressure is now inside the training distribution and the pure-self-play habits are being un-learned, as intended; the learner-vs-bot score (`hist_score_bank_3`) is 0.163 → 0.174 → 0.188, i.e. the policy is beginning to take points off the bot at kickoff where the D241 exam measured 0.05 TD/game. Neither number is the exam; the exam runs on box 2 after the rung. Credit $15.17 at 15:57 PDT (~$0.45/hr for both boxes).

**D244 — THE FIRST r25-CHAIN COLLAPSED INTO THE ABSTINENCE BASIN AGAINST A FULLY-PROMOTED POOL; KILLED AT 2.06B AND RELAUNCHED AGAINST THE POOL r25 ITSELF CLIMBED ON (2026-08-18 19:57 PDT).** `uniform-r25-chain` (warm r25 accepted `7f5133…`, pool chain/stage1/chain2/r25 `0339ccb4…` — i.e. four banks that are all the policy's own last four checkpoints) did not dip and recover like chain2 did; it fell off: windows 0-1B tds 0.115, 1-2B 0.091, 2-2.06B 0.101 (r25's own final window was 0.663), pickups 0.24/episode (r25: 1.17), possession 0.126, episode length 243 (r25: 439), `episode_return −0.46`, and `hist_score_bank_{0..3}` = 0.036/0.047/0.049/0.051 — roughly 5% wins against every bank INCLUDING its own predecessor. `demo_episodes` 0.226 as declared, `illegal_frac` 0, `demo_fallbacks` 0, `error_episodes` 0: the run was healthy and honestly configured; the policy simply stopped playing. This is the D233 abstinence basin, reached this time not from a fresh start but by warm-starting a strong policy into a pool where every opponent is ≈ its own strength: the block-EV/possession scaffolds no longer pay against equals, terminal utility is ~0.5 whatever it does, and the PPO update walked it into passivity within the first billion steps. Chain2 survived the same shape (its 1-3B window dipped to 0.43 and recovered) — one recovery and one collapse is not a mechanism, but two facts stand: (a) the pool-promotion rule ("newest three + the last accepted") converges the pool onto four near-identical selves, which is exactly the mutually-permissive equilibrium D166 warned about and removes the weak-anchor diversity the June doctrine prescribed for the curated pool ("weak anchor, era specialist, older ratchet, latest cap"); (b) the campaign supervisor and the acceptance gate would have let this run to 5B and accepted its checkpoint (all hard counters zero), and `ladder_stage.sh` would have promoted the collapsed policy into the next pool. **Actions:** killed the run at 2.06B (its OUT dir `…-r25-chain` is abandoned; its screen fails closed on the 143 status); relaunched as `…-r25-chain-v2` (first-rung form: WARM = r25 accepted, PREV_POOL = r25's own pool `e138c936…` = rung12/uniform/chain/stage1, launched 19:57 PDT); repointed stage 3. **Two follow-ups this exposes, both queued rather than improvised mid-run:** (1) the pool-composition rule should keep a WEAK ANCHOR bank (a fixed early checkpoint, e.g. rung 6 or the genesis root) and rotate only the other three — the "curated pool" doctrine, cheap to add to `ladder_stage.sh`; (2) the acceptance gate should refuse a rung whose eval `tds` fell more than some fraction below its warm's rung (a regression gate — accepted-but-collapsed checkpoints must not become lineage), analogous to D168's EvalStop. Box 2's kickoff+bot rung is unaffected (its pool is uniform/chain/stage1/chain2 with a bot bank; vs-bot score flat at ~0.20 from 1B on, tds 0.55-0.60).

**D245 — r25-CHAIN COLLAPSED A SECOND TIME ON r25'S OWN POOL: POOL COMPOSITION IS RULED OUT; THE TRAJECTORY SHOWS A HEALTHY POLICY WITH STRONGLY NEGATIVE RETURN BEING OPTIMISED INTO PASSIVITY — A REWARD-ECONOMY FAILURE UNDER STRONGER OPPONENTS; BOX 1 HALTED (2026-08-18 21:06 PDT).** `uniform-r25-chain-v2` (warm r25 accepted `7f5133…`, pool `e138c936` = rung12/uniform/chain/stage1, the pool r25 climbed on) collapsed identically and faster: 0-0.05B tds 0.588 pickups 1.05 eplen 457 **return −0.83** → 0.05-0.1B 0.446/0.83/387/−0.73 → 0.1-0.2B 0.253/0.47/251/−0.50 → 0.2-0.35B 0.127/0.26/222/−0.44 → 0.35-0.55B 0.106/0.25/224/−0.45; `hist_score_bank_{0..3}` 0.065/0.040/0.052/0.041. So: the r25 policy arrives INTACT (it plays like r25 for the first ~50M steps) but its episode return in this configuration is deeply negative, and PPO does exactly what it should — it finds the less-negative behaviour, which is to stop playing (short episodes, no pickups, return −0.45 > −0.83). Pool composition is not the lever (two different pools, same collapse); the warm is not corrupted (it plays); the config is honest (`demo_episodes` 0.226, counters zero). What differs from the r25 rung that DID climb from the same reset (0.25) and pool: r25 warm-started from chain2 with return near chain2's positive level, whereas both chains warm-start from r25 whose own return at 0.25 against banks that are now ≥ its strength is dominated by losses — win/loss utility 0.6 per game plus the block-EV/possession/rush terms that are net negative when you lose most bank games — and the LR/entropy schedules restart at full on a settled policy. This is D233's mechanism ("the block-EV basin is a scaffold that became the objective") in the mirror image: when the scaffold's income turns negative under stronger opponents, abstinence is the optimum the reward economy actually specifies. It is the second time this campaign the ladder has been stopped by the reward, not by learning capacity, and it says the reward-economy work (D226/D229/D233 lineage) is now the binding constraint on graduation, not the curriculum. **Actions:** killed at 0.55B; box-1 campaign HALTED, not relaunched (a third try would only spend credit); box 1 is held for exams and for the box-2 comparison; the r25 accepted checkpoint (tds 0.695 at 0.25) remains the box-1 frontier and gets the D50 exam. The chain2 → r25 → collapse pattern will be re-tested from box 2's kickoff-with-bot checkpoint if that one accepts. Standing questions for the next reward step, recorded not answered: (a) is a warm restart's LR/entropy re-anneal (0.00028 / 0.009 from the top) too hot for a settled policy — the D168 "chain" mechanism has never been validated as return-neutral; (b) should the graduation rungs carry a return floor / terminal-utility-only reward (drop the scaffolds at reset ≤ 0.25, which D226 filed as "anneal the scaffold away once capability exists — never done"). Credit $12.75.

**D245 addendum — THE COLLAPSE IS A WARM-RESTART DIP THAT CAN RECOVER; I KILLED BOX 1'S TWO CHAINS TOO EARLY; SEED-42 REPLICATES THE UNIFORM RUNG AT 0.647 (2026-08-19 08:45 PDT).** The rig's seed-42 replicate accepted its uniform@0.5 rung at **eval tds 0.647** (pickups 1.00, possession 0.223, sidecar `69ef03a8…`; windows 0.553 → 0.650, climbing) — seed 43's comparable checkpoint (chain2) was 0.652, so the uniform-chain result replicates across seeds to within noise. Its r25 stage (warm = that checkpoint, pool rung12/chain/stage1/s42-uniform `5a831aa4…` — bank 0 kept as the D244 weak anchor) then showed the SAME shape as box 1's two killed chains: 0-0.1B tds 0.523 pickups 0.86 → 0.3-0.6B 0.157/0.29 → 0.6-2.0B 0.11/0.22 (return −0.40) — and then RECOVERED: 2-3B 0.159/0.33, 3-3.6B 0.260/0.55, return falling back to −0.50 as it re-engages. Chain2 (D240) did the same: 1-3B window 0.43 then 3-5B 0.61. So the phenomenon is a warm-restart DIP — a settled policy dropped into a pool of ≥-strength selves with LR and entropy re-annealed from the top walks into passivity in the first ~0.5B, and at least twice out of four it has climbed back out by ~2.5B. Box 1's r25-chain (killed at 2.06B, still 0.10) and r25-chain-v2 (killed at 0.55B) may simply not have been given the chance; the v2 kill in particular was premature — recorded as my error. D245's "reward economy is the binding constraint" stands as a hypothesis, not a finding: the dip is real and costs ~40% of a rung, but recovery says the basin is not absorbing. **Corrections to the operating rule:** do not kill a warm-restarted rung for a dip before ~3B; let the regression gate (D244, eval tds ≥ 0.5× warm rung) be the judge at cap; and treat "hot restart" (LR 0.00028 / ent 0.009 from the top) as the prime suspect for the dip — a chain should probably resume at the warm rung's FINAL LR/entropy (min-lr ratio 0.1 → 2.8e-5) rather than re-anneal, which is a one-line launcher knob to test next. Box 1 remains halted; its r25 checkpoint is under the D50 exam now (torch 2.10+cu128 installed on both Vast boxes for the `--slowly` eval path; the cu128 wheel needs the venv's own `libcudart` first on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and an unversioned `libcudnn.so` symlink in the venv cudnn dir — both boxes rebuilt `_C`, drift OK). Box 2's kickoff+bot rung accepted (eval tds 0.731 from pure kickoff, pickups 1.50, vs-bot 0.21 train and eval; return −1.51 → −0.59 with NO dip — the only warm restart this campaign that did not dip, on a pool of three older selves + the bot); its exam is running on box 2. Credit $7.47 at 08:13 PDT — box 1 idled ~11h on a broken torch upgrade while my tick was blocked behind a long pip install; that is ~$2 wasted and a monitoring lesson: never run a multi-minute install synchronously inside a tick.

**D246 — THE FIRST HEAD-TO-HEAD ON THE GRADUATION EXAM: ONE KICKOFF RUNG WITH A 12% CONTACT-BOT SHARE DOUBLES SCORING AND CUTS CONCEDING BY A FIFTH AGAINST THE BOT; MORE CURRICULUM ALONE (r25) DOES NOTHING (2026-08-19 10:30 PDT).** Same exam (frozen torch, full games from kickoff, vs `contact_bot` type 0, ≥2,000 games per side), three checkpoints of the same lineage: **chain2** (uniform@0.5, D241): AWAY 0.052 / bot 1.281, HOME 0.035 / 1.276. **r25** (chain2 → uniform@0.25, 5B more of pool self-play, eval tds 0.695): AWAY **0.038 / 1.150**, HOME **0.025 / 1.211** — statistically indistinguishable from chain2 on scoring, ~8% less conceded; the extra curriculum rung bought nothing on the exam that matters, exactly as D241 predicted. **kickoff+bot** (chain2 → kickoff@0 with bank 4 = contact bot, ~12% of envs, D243, eval tds 0.731): AWAY **0.102 / 0.997** (score 0.226 vs 0.774, draws 35%) — **~2× chain2's scoring and −22% conceded**, after ONE 5B rung in which the learner's training-time score vs the bot was only 0.21. Modest in absolute terms (the bot still wins three games in four) but it is the first movement on the graduation metric in this lineage and it came from opponent quality, not reward: the reward manifest, pool structure, and every other knob were identical to box 1's r25 path; the only declared factor was `scripted_bank_tag=4`. This is D166's thesis ("make the agent defend against something that can actually score / play through something that actually blocks") confirmed on obs-v6 with the cheapest possible intervention. HOME side and mirror for kickoff+bot, and r25's mirror, still running and will be appended. **Implications, in order:** (1) the kickoff graduation rung's default is now kickoff+bot-bank, not pure pool; (2) the next lever is the bot share and bot diversity — two scripted banks (contact + the D167 offense bot) at ~25% of envs, chained from the kickoff+bot checkpoint, is the obvious next rung on box 2; (3) the exam stays the only scoreboard; `hist_score_bank_3` tracked it in the right direction (0.16 → 0.21 train vs 0.05 → 0.10 exam) but is not a substitute. Box 1's r25-chain-v3 (cold restart, LR scale 0.1) launches after its mirror exam to settle the D245 dip question, then box 1 is retired to save credit ($6.85 at 09:35).

**D247 — SPEND MANDATE: NATIVE FROZEN EVAL (24× FASTER, SAME ANSWER), BOX 1 RETIRED, ONE PAID FRONTIER BOX; THE BOT-BANK GAIN HOLDS ACROSS BOTH SIDES AND GENERALISES TO THE OFFENSE BOT (2026-08-19 12:25 PDT).** Alex: "save our money. Your number one goal and memory and mandate is wise $ spend on GPUs." Audit of the waste: (a) a blocking pip install held my monitor tick overnight and box 1 idled ~11h on a broken torch upgrade (~$2); (b) every D50 exam ran on the torch `--slowly` path at 2-7K SPS — a 3-part exam took 3+ hours of a paid box, and box 2 (the only new-source box) sat not-training for ~4h waiting on it (~$2 and, worse, lost frontier time). Fix (b) structurally: `NATIVE=1` in `tools/eval_vs_contact_bot.sh` and `tools/eval_game_stats.sh` runs the frozen eval on the CUDA backend from the rung's own flat blob (validated sidecar, real biases, `lr 1e-12`; the scripted-training guard permits it because lr ≤ 1e-9), **165K vs 6.8K SPS — a full 3-part exam in ~3.5 min**; cross-check r25 AWAY native 0.043/1.118 (n=2032) vs torch 0.038/1.150 (n=2005) — the same answer. Committed `4d6ae27`/`a48fa58`; `/root/native_exam.sh` on the boxes runs away/home/offense/mirror. Fix (a) by rule: never block a tick; and the standing memory `gpu-spend-mandate`. **Box 1 (`bb-ryzen1`, 47967132) destroyed 12:09 PDT** after pulling its exam outputs, markers, campaign state and the r25 checkpoint+sidecar to the Mac (`scratchpad/box1-final/box1-final.tgz`, 15 MB); its open question (does a cold restart, LR scale 0.1, avoid the D245 dip?) moves to the free rig: `rstage3_s42_kick.sh` now carries `LADDER_CHAIN_LR_SCALE=0.1`. Steady state: one paid box (box 2, $0.24/hr) + the rig. **Native scoreboard (same weights, both checkpoints, ~2,000 games/cell):** r25 — contact AWAY 0.043/1.118, contact HOME 0.037/1.131, offense-bot AWAY 0.101/0.587; **kickoff+bot — contact AWAY 0.091/1.023, contact HOME 0.069/0.975, offense-bot AWAY 0.152/0.538.** The bot-bank rung improves every cell: ~2× scoring and −9 to −14% conceded vs the contact bot it trained against, and +50% scoring / −8% conceded vs the OFFENSE bot it never saw — some of what it learned is general pressure handling, not bot-specific. Still losing clearly (score ~0.21 vs 0.79 contact, 0.36 vs 0.64 offense). Box 2 now runs `kickoff-chain-offbot` (warm kickoff+bot, offense bot in bank 4, cold restart scale 0.1, anchor pool uniform/…, graft): first launch attempts failed on two of my own deploy mistakes, both caught by the tooling — the torch-2.10 rebuild changed the module digest so graft refused the warm ("a same-source/same-patch module difference is a rehost" — rehosted, fine) and torch 2.10's `libtorch_cuda` needs the venv's nccl/cudart first on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (now baked into the supervisor loop); live at 195K SPS since 12:22 PDT. Credit $5.64 at 12:05 → ~20h at $0.27/hr.

**D248 — COLD RESTART (LR/ENTROPY ×0.1) REMOVES THE WARM-RESTART DIP: TWO FOR TWO, ON DIFFERENT BOXES, LINEAGES AND START DISTRIBUTIONS; NOW THE DEFAULT FOR CHAINED RUNGS (2026-08-19 13:35 PDT).** Box 2's `kickoff-chain-offbot` (warm kickoff+bot, offense bot in bank 4, `LADDER_CHAIN_LR_SCALE=0.1` → lr 2.8e-05, ent 0.0009): 0-0.1B tds 0.693 pickups 1.27 return −0.59 → 0.6-1.0B 0.679/1.31/−0.60 — flat from step 0, no dip, and the learner-vs-offense-bot score already 0.37 → 0.42. The rig's `s42-kickoff` (warm s42-r25, reset 0, pure pool, old source, same ×0.1): 0-0.3B tds 0.40, pickups 0.85, return −0.45 — flat, no dip. Against that, the rig's `s42-r25` (HOT restart) dipped 0.52 → 0.11 and was accepted at eval tds **0.334** from a warm of 0.647 — a hot restart cost that rung half its value (the D244 regression gate was skipped because the warm's marker predates `eval_tds`; from now on every marker carries it). Four hot restarts dipped (chain2 recovered, s42-r25 half-recovered, two box-1 r25-chains killed), two cold restarts did not. `tools/ladder_stage.sh` now defaults `LADDER_CHAIN_LR_SCALE=0.1` whenever `PREV_COMPLETE` is set (first rungs of a chain keep 1; an explicit value wins) — `7802fa7`. Box 2 stage 3 pre-authored: chain from the offense-bot checkpoint back to the CONTACT bot (alternating bots each rung), cold restart, anchor pool. Credit $5.28 at 13:26.

**D249 — OFFENSE-BOT RUNG: CONCEDED-TO-OFFENSE-BOT DOWN 25%, CONTACT CELLS HELD, NO DIP; ALTERNATING-BOT CHAIN CONTINUES (2026-08-19 19:45 PDT).** `kickoff-chain-offbot` (warm kickoff+bot, offense bot type 1 in bank 4 ~12% of envs, cold restart ×0.1, anchor pool uniform/chain/stage1/chain2→kickoff+bot, 5B in 7h20m at ~195K SPS) accepted: eval tds 0.746 (from 0.731), pickups 1.44, possession 0.140, in-eval learner-vs-offense-bot score 0.423 (0.37 at rung start); `regression_gate` skipped (the warm's marker predates `eval_tds`; every marker from here carries it). Native exam (~2,040 games/cell): **offense-bot AWAY 0.151 / 0.405** (prev 0.152 / 0.538 — conceded −25%, score share 0.36 → 0.41, draws 0.51 → 0.56), contact AWAY 0.077 / 1.029 (prev 0.091 / 1.023), contact HOME 0.068 / 1.009 (prev 0.069 / 0.975) — contact play held within noise while the trained-against cell improved, so the bot share teaches against THAT bot first and generalises weakly (D247's offense gain from contact training was +50% scoring; this rung's contact carry-over is ~flat). Mirror from kickoff 0.765 TD/g total (chain2 0.951): the policy has become more defensive/conservative against itself as it learns to play under pressure — consistent with fewer free scores in a mutually-permissive mirror, not a regression on the exam. The cold restart held flat from step 0 for the whole rung (no dip). Stage 3 `kickoff-chain-contact2` (back to the contact bot, alternating) launched 19:37 PDT. Two rung-level levers left untested and queued: (1) two scripted banks at once (needs per-tag bot type — small C change) or a larger share (`FROZEN_BANK_PCT` is fixed 0.06 in the screen contract); (2) the rig's pure-pool `s42-kickoff` (cold, caps ~01:00 Aug 20) is the control for "kickoff training without a bot". **D250 — THIRD BOT-BANK RUNG (CONTACT AGAIN): CONTACT HOME SCORING +30%, OFFENSE CELL HELD, REGRESSION GATE ACTIVE AND PASSED; CREDIT EXHAUSTED, BOX 2 RETIRED WITH ALL ARTIFACTS PULLED (2026-08-20 06:45 PDT).** `kickoff-chain-contact2` (warm offense-bot rung ckpt, contact bot in bank 4, cold restart, anchor pool, 5B in 7h10m) accepted: eval tds 0.755 (warm 0.746; regression gate active for the first time: 0.755 ≥ 0.5×0.746, recorded in the marker), pickups 1.69, in-eval learner-vs-contact 0.212. Native exam (~2,030 games/cell): contact AWAY **0.083 / 0.993** (prev rung 0.077 / 1.029), contact HOME **0.088 / 1.028** (prev 0.068 / 1.009), offense AWAY **0.160 / 0.459** (prev 0.151 / 0.405), mirror 0.803 TD/g. **D252 - AUDIT: THE obs-v6 LINEAGE WAS FROZEN BY ITS OWN RECIPE, AND THE DISCARDED JULY POLICY IS ~6x BETTER ON THE EXAM (2026-08-20 23:00 PDT).** Alex asked for a rigorous audit of the training profile, weights and rewards, trusting nothing prior. Eight independent auditors (reward semantics, obs/action encoding, network + optimizer + schedule, self-play row masking, episode structure, rig-log telemetry, a skeptical read of D1-D251, engine rules with probes) ran in parallel; every load-bearing claim was re-verified against the code that runs or the rig logs. Full report: `docs/audit-2026-08-20.md`. The findings that change the program: (1) **The cold-restart default `LADDER_CHAIN_LR_SCALE=0.1` (D248, this session) froze training.** On the rung-1 log of `rig-s42-bot-20260820` `kl` and `clipfrac` print 0.000 on 38,206 of 38,207 updates and every game statistic is flat over 5B steps; the pure-pool control, the bot-bank rungs and tonight's rung 1 (exam: contact 0.056 / 1.224 AWAY, 0.046 / 1.224 HOME, offense 0.060 / 0.649, vs the control's 0.023 / 0.016 / 0.027) measured their warm checkpoints, not training. (2) **The optimizer is Muon** (`vendor/PufferLib/src/pufferlib.cu:2051`, `src/muon.cu`): updates are orthogonalised per matrix, so `lr` is the per-step relative change; ours (2.8e-4, from a 200M fine-tune sweep with a 1e-4 floor, D137) is 2x below chess.ini and 54x below default.ini before the 0.1 scale. `replay_ratio 0.25` gives exactly 2 gradient steps per 131k-sample epoch and `update_epochs` is ignored by the native trainer. No prior entry knew any of this. (3) **The reward is 94% shaping, 6% objective**, and because Phi_carry (up to 0.96 at d=1, larger than the 0.4 TD) collapses to zero in the TD apply, the touchdown step nets -0.56 to the scorer (161/161 TDs in a bot-vs-bot harness). PBRS invariance assumes a critic that represents V - Phi exactly; ours must do that on 2 Muon steps per epoch. (4) **The base policy is in a non-play equilibrium**: 1.25 pickup attempts, 0.15 possession, 0 passes, 8.4 blocks per game for both teams combined; the contact bot scores ~1.2 TD/game against a uniformly random policy and 1.0-1.3 against the obs-v6 frontier, so the frontier's defense is indistinguishable from random. (5) **Training `tds` is a both-sides mixture** (mirror 52% of games, banks 36%, bot 12%, bot TDs included) and `perf` is ~0.5 by symmetry; every rung acceptance in D235-D251 was read on it. (6) **The July R0 seed-42 checkpoint** (`runs/reward-transfer-20260713-v1/checkpoints/r0-s42-native.bin`, obs-v4 era, sha `4e97ba4f...`) re-examined FROZEN on tonight's obs-v6 / exact-joint build (lineage gate bypassed for a diagnostic, nothing published, `runs/diag-july-r0s42/` on the rig): **contact AWAY 0.354 / 0.438, HOME 0.346 / 0.447, offense AWAY 0.392 / 0.334 (match score 0.541)**, 18 blocks and 6.2 pickups per game. D228 restarted from random weights because the lineage tooling had no warm-start entry point, not because an experiment beat these weights; ~80B steps since have not come within 4x of them. Also found and verified correct: obs perspective symmetry (0 failures in 8.2M mask round-trips), row masking, frozen forward pass, tag arithmetic, scripted-bank exclusion, PBRS telescoping, terminal handling, dice conformance, exam harness; one engine rules bug (carrier follow-up into the endzone on POW/STUMBLE/crowd push is not scored, `engine/src/proc_block.c:684-693`, rare). Actions tonight: campaign `rig-s42-bot-20260820` halted (sticky) and both supervisor timers stopped; rung 2 stopped at 1.1B (frozen recipe, nothing lost); `LADDER_CHAIN_LR_SCALE` default returns to 1.0; a reviewed `bridge` initialisation is being added to `checkpoint_lineage.py` so the July blob can warm-start on the current build with its provenance in the sidecar. Plan (one variable per arm, native kickoff exam is the only acceptance metric): bridge July R0 s42 onto the contact-bot bank at LR 2.8e-4 (3B), then an LR probe under Muon (5.7e-4, 1.5e-3), then a reward-economy arm {td, win, draw -0.1} from the same warm, then bot share 0.12, entropy 0.02-0.05, gamma 0.999 / lambda 0.95, and representation last. Credit $0.65; the rig is the only compute.

**D253 - BRIDGE ARM 1: s0_both DISMANTLES THE JULY POLICY IN 500M STEPS; STOPPED, SPARSE ARM LAUNCHED (2026-08-20 23:50 PDT).** The first `bridge-v4` rung (`runs/ladder-d0-bridge-jul-s42-20260820`: July R0 s42 warm, pool `972c557d` of four current-build obs-v6 banks with the contact bot in bank 4, `s0_both`, LR 2.8e-4, ent 0.009, 2B requested) started where the July policy stands (first 50 windows: tds 0.96, learner tds_t0 0.63, pickups 3.4, possession 0.30, 79% wins vs bank 0, score vs bot 0.043) and moved monotonically toward the obs-v6 non-play equilibrium: at 522M steps tds 0.46, tds_t0 0.15, pickups 1.43, possession 0.16, 61% vs bank 0, score vs bot 0.021, episode length 700 -> 1163 decisions, while blocks thrown rose 15 -> 21 and the per-episode touchdown component went from +0.12 to -0.07. That is the direction of the s0_both gradient (block-exposure bounty up, ball-handling charges and the -0.56 touchdown step down), not random damage from a hot restart; kl/clipfrac printed 0.000 throughout, which under Muon says nothing about movement. Stopped at 522M (unit stop, exit 143, nothing published). Arm 2 launched immediately from the SAME warm, pool and LR with `LADDER_ARM=sparse` (`s4_sparse`: td 0.4, win 0.6, draw -0.1, every dense term 0; `runs/ladder-d0-bridge-jul-s42-sparse-20260821`). Scoring held far better than under s0_both (0.46 at 520M) but ball handling and blocking decayed anyway: with no block or contact terms and a TD 100+ c-steps away at gamma 0.995, the policy stops blocking first. Both arms share one confound: each changes the reward the warm's critic was fitted to, so the first hundreds of millions of steps run on a wrong value function at a hot Muon step. Two engineering findings from the same audit. First, `bbe_profile.c` sampled each action head independently, so every profile since 9217256 measured setup-error episodes. With that fixed (`fix/profile-joint-sampling-20260911`), legal enumeration is 67% of a 7.7 microsecond env step and ACTIVATION blitz reachability is nearly all of it. Second, an exact early-exit reachability query for blitz declarations makes env steps 2.29x faster per core, with bit-identical goldens, legal sets and masks (`fix/blitz-reachability-fastpath-20260911`, v6 port in progress). It changes the source digest, so it lands between rungs behind a graft and never inside a paired comparison.

The warm critic was fitted to the legacy stream, so the switched reward made pickups look negative-EV, and the policy stopped going for the ball while keeping its contact game. This is the D253 pattern (`s0_both` collapsed the July warm in 500M).

**Rulings.**
1. Chain 28 is rejected and must never be a warm start or pool bank.
2. D253 stands, restated: never switch a reward form on a warm checkpoint. A warm switch is not a neutral intervention, so chain 28 does not answer D391's question of horizon versus legacy distance bias. Only a lineage trained under exact PBRS from its root, or a gradual anneal between the forms, could, and neither is cheap.
3. The recipe stays legacy `r0_poss_half` at gamma 0.999 / lambda 0.95. Chain 25 stays the frontier.
4. The regression gate floor (eval tds 0.5) is too loose to catch a halving; tightening it is noted as tooling work.

**A three-lens adversarial panel then checked the claim before any action.**
- **Harness (not refuted, high confidence).**
  - Weight loading is exact (bias-free CUDA layers, so zero-filled torch biases are exact), and the gate kernel matches native formula by formula.
  - The env source hash equals training's 3ed6899e, and the sampler and recurrence match the native eval contract.
  - 12 replayed games reproduce bit for bit, an -mfma build gives identical observation bytes, and a chain 25 bot bench reproduces its exam cells within noise.
- **Statistics (partly refuted, high confidence).**
  - All counts, intervals and Elo recompute exactly, and the gap over chain 25 is robust under every model: chain 27 +100.8 +/- 7.2, chain 30 +108.3 +/- 7.2. With draws scored as half it is about +66.
  - **Chain 30 vs chain 27 is a tie:** +7.5 +/- 7.3, 95% interval [-6, +21]. Head to head chain 27 leads 0.517, and chain 30's rank-1 comes only from beating the 0.995 chains harder. Chain 31 vs chain 25 is also a tie.
  - The doc's leg correlation is uncentred: -0.087 there, -0.207 centred within pair. Its seed-cluster bootstrap had no committed code, and Kendall tau 0.60 over 6 points is not significant.
  - At 1400 games per pair the minimum detectable effect is about 30 Elo.
- **Confounds (partly refuted, medium confidence).**
  - The pool code shows chain 9's warm seat was the contact bot in d67d527b, so chain 9 was not a frozen opponent for chains 25 or 30, and the residuals show no chain-9 exploitation.
  - The field contains no opponent from outside the family, and the offense bot is the only opponent none of these rungs trained against.
  - Elo rank matches per-decision sampling sharpness exactly: mean logprob chain 30 -0.143 down to chain 14 -0.238.
  - The gain is concentrated on agile rosters and reverses on some bash rosters. Chain 30 vs chain 25: Undead 0.370, Chaos Chosen 0.375, Tomb Kings 0.381 of decisive games, against High Elf 0.933 and Dark Elf 0.927.
  - Uncertainty covers match noise only, with one training seed per chain.

**Rulings.**
1. Chain 30 (sha 41ecd998) becomes the frontier warm start. It holds the top decisive-Elo tier, matches chain 25 within the floor on every exam cell including the held-out offense AWAY (-0.0035), and has the best Elo per GPU-hour. This is a warm-start decision, not a production promotion, and not a claim that chain 30 is stronger than chain 27.
2. Replay ratio 1.0 does not become the recipe until a training-seed replicate confirms it, as D397's positive branch required. It costs 1.43x wall per rung.
3. D394 and D397 are superseded, not reclassified. Their exam rules were applied as written, but they are insensitive to in-family head-to-head gains. Chain 27's offense veto stands until a held-out re-test clears it.
4. The gate becomes two-part. The bot exam stays, with the offense AWAY cell as a veto on a drop greater than 0.02 on the mean and on both exam seeds; the contact cells are in-sample. It is joined by a pre-registered tournament against a fixed anchor panel: the frontier, existing seed replicates, and held-out opponents where available. Candidates are never scored against their parent alone. N comes from a power calculation (about 3100 games per pair for 20 Elo), intervals come from committed seed-cluster code, and draw-inclusive score is reported beside decisive share.

It is chain 30's exact recipe (warm chain 9 marker, seed 42, 3B, pool identity d67d527b, `r0_poss_half`, gamma 0.999 / lambda 0.95) with `LADDER_REPLAY_RATIO=2.0`: 16 Muon steps per 131K-step epoch instead of 8. - **Gate part 2, tournament:** chain 33 against chain 30, chain 32 and chain 25, with 3,200 games per pair on seed block 20400000 under D400 conditions. The same run adds chain 32 vs chain 26 (3,200 games), which completes D401's seed-matched contrast. The offense bot joins the panel as a held-out anchor if its harness seat first reproduces the exam cells.
The readings are applied in this order, and the first that matches is the result:
1. **Negative:** the veto fires, or chain 33's 95% interval against chain 30 lies entirely below zero.
2. **Positive:** chain 33 beats chain 30 by more than +40 decisive-Elo with its 95% interval above zero, and beats chain 32 with its interval above zero. A seed replicate follows before any recipe change.
3. **Flat:** chain 33's decisive-Elo against chain 30 lies within +/-40.
4. **Inconclusive:** anything else, for example more than +40 over chain 30 without a clear win over chain 32.

Neither a flat nor an inconclusive reading changes the recipe; replay ratio 1.0 stays, because 2.0 costs more wall time. The +40 cutoff is a screening threshold for funding a replicate, taken from the largest replicate-pair gap (+39.9 [+26.1, +53.6]). It is not a statistical bound on training-seed variation. At 3,200 games per pair the minimum detectable effect against zero is about 19 Elo (SE about 6.8), but a true gap of exactly +40 clears a point-estimate cutoff of +40 only about half the time, and about +46 is needed for 80%.

Caveats named in advance:

**Which parent.** Chain 36 starts speculatively from chain 34. D404's complete ordered readings are applied to chain 35. Chain 35 becomes the parent only if its reading is Replicated and the 95% seed-cluster decisive-Elo interval for chain 35 minus chain 34 has its lower endpoint strictly above zero. Otherwise chain 34 stays the parent after a valid completed verdict. Missing or invalid chain 35 evidence leaves chain 34 as the parent, and a chain 35 that never finished training has no checkpoint to continue from.
- **No peeking.** The keep-or-discard decision and its timing depend only on chain 35's registered evidence, never on chain 36's training metrics, intermediate checkpoints or evaluations. Until the parent is resolved, chain 36 is monitored only for operational progress and hard integrity.
- **If chain 35 is selected:** chain 36 and its exam waiter are cancelled. Its artifacts are kept for audit only, and it is excluded from scoring and from any future warm start or pool, whatever its apparent performance. The replacement continuation from chain 35 gets its own run identity, frozen manifest and pre-registered gate before it starts; this entry's gate is specific to a chain 34 parent.
- **Cost.** A wrong default costs about 1.5 GPU hours; waiting would cost the same 1.5 hours every time. Chain 35's tournament runs on separate compute (a DigitalOcean droplet) while chain 36 trains.

**Chain 36** (`runs/ladder-d0-r0chain36-cont34-rr1-20260917`, unit `r0chain36-cont34-rr1`, which runs `/home/rache/queue_c36.sh`).   - `exam-c36-waiter` is armed.
- **Pool** (identity 51a19cff, built by `tools/ladder_stage.sh`). The rotation keeps the kickoff anchor, retains the chain 9 marker and chain 30, drops `rung0warm2`, and appends chain 34 as bank 3 under the contact-bot override. **Chain 30 becomes an active learned opponent for the first time**, so the opponent set is stronger than chain 34's.
- **Verification.** SCREEN PLAN VERIFIED with manifest e13c6f26 and drift check 3ed6899e, run while chain 35 trained.

As D402 named for chain 34, this changes three things together: the warm checkpoint, the cumulative budget (9B from the chain 9 marker), and the active opponent set.

**Why a drift guard.** Both continuations lost offense-bot touchdowns: chain 27 tripped the veto against chain 25 (D394), and chain 34 sits 0.021 below chain 30, clear of the veto by 0.002 on one seed (D404). A veto measured only against the parent lets the offense cell ratchet down 0.02 per rung. The guard pins a fixed reference.

**Gate part 1, exam.** Rates are champion touchdowns per game in the offense AWAY cell at exam seeds 42 and 43, and the mean is their unweighted mean. The displayed three-decimal reference values are normative, and every inequality is strict. Either condition makes the reading negative:
- **Parent veto:** offense AWAY down more than 0.02 against chain 34 (0.557, 0.573; mean 0.565) on the mean and on both exam seeds.
- **Drift guard:** offense AWAY down more than 0.04 against chain 30 (0.581, 0.591; mean 0.586) on the mean and on both exam seeds.

| A gate fires only if all three hold | Chain 36, exam seed 42 | Chain 36, exam seed 43 | Mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| Parent veto | < 0.537 | < 0.553 | < 0.545 |
| Drift guard | < 0.541 | < 0.551 | < 0.546 |

The 0.04 is a prospective design choice informed by chains 27 and 34. It is not applied retroactively to their verdicts. Passing the guard does not establish offense non-inferiority or cap the mean decline: one seed can fall far while the other prevents the conjunction.

**Gate part 2, tournament.** Chain 36 against chains 34, 35, 30 and 27 and the offense bot, plus chain 34 against the offense bot on the same seeds so the held-out contrast is paired. 3,200 games per pair on seed block 20800000, D400 conditions, run off the Mac.

The readings are applied in this order, and the first that matches is the result:
1. **Negative:** the parent veto or the drift guard fires, or chain 36's 95% interval against chain 34 lies entirely below zero.
2. **Positive:** chain 36 beats chain 34 by more than +40 decisive-Elo with its 95% interval strictly above zero, and its interval against chain 27 lies strictly above zero. Chain 36 becomes the warm start. Chain 27 carries the second condition because it is fixed, already in the panel and absent from chain 36's pool. Chain 30 is now a training opponent, so the chain 36 vs chain 30 pair is an in-pool retention diagnostic, not a transfer comparator.
3. **Flat:** chain 36's decisive-Elo against chain 34 lies within +/-40, bounds included. Chain 34 stays the warm start, and a third continuation is not run on this recipe without a new idea.
4. **Inconclusive:** anything else with valid completed evidence. Chain 34 stays the warm start.

Missing or integrity-invalid evidence is not scored; it does not fall into "anything else".

Caveats named in advance:
- The +40 cutoff is D401's screening threshold, not a statistical bound on training-seed variation.
- This is one training seed, and the opponent-set change is confounded with the continuation.
- Chain 27 is a repeatedly used, lineage-connected benchmark, not an untouched external test.
- The paired offense-bot contrast is diagnostic. The rig exam stays the registered veto.

**D406 - GATE TOURNAMENTS MOVE TO DROPLETS AND TO A BATCHED POLICY FORWARD (32 GAMES PER WORKER), STARTING WITH CHAIN 35'S, DECIDED BEFORE ANY CHAIN 35 TOURNAMENT DATA EXISTS (2026-09-17 13:20 PDT).** **Amended 2026-09-17 13:45 PDT after a Codex review, still before any chain 35 tournament data.** The amendment adds the acceptance check, scopes the agreement claims, and fixes the retry rule.

This changes how gate tournaments are computed, not what they measure. Games per worker has a small observable numerical effect, so it is a registered implementation condition and not an invisible detail; D404's "under D400 conditions" now reads as D400's substantive evaluation conditions plus this declared computation amendment. D400's conditions are unchanged: sampling policies, every-step recurrence, random rosters that stay with the side, sides swapped per seed, per-game engine and sampling seeds derived from the seed block, and the same statistics code.

**Droplet runner** (`tools/droplet_tournament.py`, harness `feat/play-harness-20260913` at 0bf9ce0; doc `docs/play-harness/droplet-tournaments-2026-09-17.md`). It creates one throwaway DigitalOcean droplet per run, syncs the harness at a pinned commit plus only the needed checkpoints, builds the shim there, runs the tournament, copies the records back with sha256 verification, and destroys the droplet on every handled exit path (success, failure, Ctrl-C, SIGTERM). `--keep`, SIGKILL, host death or a failed teardown can leave one running, which is why every run ends with the `status` leak check. A `merge` subcommand joins shards split by pair and refuses shards that differ in commit, seed block, torch version, compiled shim or games per worker, that overlap in pairs, or that miss a scheduled game.
- **Size.** The account's largest usable size is `s-8vcpu-16gb-amd` (8 shared vCPUs, $0.167/h, sfo3).
- **Cross-machine agreement.** Against the Mac reference for chain 34's gate (seed block 20600000), 2,399 of 2,400 droplet games had identical action trails. The one that differed had the same 0-0 result, and every integrity counter was zero. What is established: every observed score matched, almost every observed action trail matched, and the implementation keeps the policy, state and RNG structure. That is engineering evidence, not a proof that outcome distributions are equal, and one diverged game is too little to state a divergence rate. `action_trail_sha256` is the discriminating hash; `final_digest` matched even in the diverged game.
- **Reviews and cost.** Codex reviewed the runner, and three droplet-leak paths were fixed. Build and test spend was $0.20, and the account leak check was clean afterwards.

**Batched forward** (`--games-per-worker N`, default 1; doc `docs/play-harness/batched-tournaments-2026-09-17.md`). With N above 1 a worker keeps N games in flight and runs one batched forward per policy per step. Each game keeps its own recurrent state and its own sampling generator, and a refilled slot gets fresh seats, so a game's actions depend on its batch only through float roundoff in the logits. On identical input states a single batched forward differs from batch 1 by at most 3e-5, measured as the largest logit error in a row divided by that row's largest magnitude (floor 1). That is not a per-logit bound, and it does not bound independently evolving recurrent trajectories.
- **Agreement on one droplet, same seeds, against N=1:**
  - checkpoint pairs: 1,200 of 1,200 games identical at N = 2, 4 and 8, and 1,199 of 1,200 at N = 16, 32, 64 and 128;
  - bot pair: 1,200 of 1,200 at every N from 2 to 64;
  - a full runner run at N=32: 3,200 of 3,200 action trails identical to the unbatched Mac reference.
- **Outcomes.** Every score and every W/D/L count matched at every N, with integrity counters zero.
- **The one differing game** is the same one each time (seed 20600020, chain 34 vs chain 30): a sampling draw lands in a 5.4e-6 probability gap while the logits differ by one part in a million. It ends 0-0 either way.
- **Throughput on the droplet** (8 workers, checkpoint pairs): 1.54 games/s at N=1, 7.74 at N=32 and 8.70 at N=64. A mixed two-pair shard at N=32 ran at 8.73 games/s. N=1 after the refactor reproduces the chain 34 reference records field for field.
- **Reviews and cost.** Codex reviewed the code (no state leakage, no RNG coupling, three lifecycle bugs fixed with tests) and the findings (every number reproduced, overclaims corrected). Validation spend was $0.34.
- **Not covered:** argmax and non-unit temperatures have structural tests only, with no droplet agreement run. No gate currently uses them.

**Ruling.** From chain 35's gate onward, gate tournaments run on droplets at 32 games per worker, split by pair across up to four droplets and merged with the verified merge. Every shard of one gate uses the same games-per-worker, which the merge enforces. Contrasts inside a gate are always computed within one run. Comparisons with earlier unbatched Mac runs stay descriptive, as cross-run comparisons already were. Each shard's manifest records `games_per_worker`, the harness commit and the torch version, and its checksummed `machine.json` records the compiled shim hash.

**Acceptance check** (`tools/gate_acceptance.py`, harness b0099fb, 15 tests). The merge validates shards against each other and takes the merged schedule to be their union, so a launch that omits a whole pair still merges cleanly; Codex demonstrated this on the proof artifacts. After the merge, every gate is therefore held to its registered plan: the exact pairs and games per pair, the seed block with both legs of every seed exactly once, games per worker, the pinned harness commit, each checkpoint's sha256, sample mode at unit temperature, natural endings and zero integrity counters. A gate is scored only if the check prints GATE-ACCEPTED. On the real chain 34 run it accepts the registered five pairs and rejects the same run against a six-pair plan.

**Retry and rerun rule.** A shard is rerun only if it failed to complete, and the first completed attempt of each shard is the one merged. A completed shard is never rerun, and a borderline verdict never triggers a discretionary unbatched rerun. The registered thresholds apply to the accepted N=32 run.

**Pairing across droplets.** The pairing unit is the shared engine seed, roster assignment and orientation, not an identical action trail, so rare float-driven action differences do not unpair the offense-bot contrasts. Those contrasts are computed by resampling engine-seed clusters jointly across both matchups, as D403's was. A systematic machine-dependent policy effect would be a separate confound that this screen cannot bound, and none has been observed.

**Why now.** Chain 35's gate is 22,400 games. Unbatched on four droplets it takes about 77 minutes; at N=32 it is budgeted at about 17 minutes and $0.17 (plus or minus 25%, single measurements). That shortens the window in which chain 36 runs from a default parent (D405), and it keeps tournament load off the owner's Mac, which reached load 47 on 14 cores on 2026-09-16.

**What does not change.** Chain 35's registered pairs, seed block 20700000, 3,200 games per pair, D404's ordered readings and the rig exam veto. Chain 35's gate runs at harness commit b0099fb.

**Context.** The rig had been idle since chain 36's exam on 2026-09-18. Neither chain 35's gate (D404) nor chain 36's (D405) had been scored: three of chain 35's four droplet shards died on 2026-09-17 and chain 36's tournament never ran. On 2026-10-01 the owner asked for a rigorous review and optimization of the training code and then a long run on the rig. This entry records the review, the build, and what the first rungs of that run are. It decides nothing about chains 35 and 36; their gates are running tonight and get their own entry.

**Review** (doc `docs/trainer-review-2026-10-02.md`). Six reviewers read the patched trainer exactly as it ran chain 36, the launchers and the rig's logs, and a separate verifier attacked each reviewer's findings: 48 findings. The ones that change how the ledger reads:
- **The dashboard "Forward" row is the train step.** Per 1,465 ms epoch on chain 36: rollout GPU about 619 ms, env about 180 ms, train about 604 ms. Rollout GPU time is about 252 ms plus about 86 ms per frozen-bank forward, nearly independent of row count.
- **The entropy coefficient has never annealed in a native run.** The annealed value is passed by value into a kernel inside the captured CUDA graph, so the capture-time value replays for the whole run (`pufferlib.cu` train capture region; no graph parameter update exists anywhere in the tree). Every native rung trained at a constant coefficient: 0.009 on the current recipe, 0.018 in D261, D259 and D271, 0.0009 in the D248 and D252 scale-0.1 rungs. The learning-rate anneal is live (it goes through a device pointer). Nothing is changed here: a live anneal is an untested algorithm change. Constant 0.009 is the proven recipe.
- **A warm start loads weights only**, so the learning rate jumps tenfold at every rung boundary and the priority-beta schedule restarts. In chains 34, 35 and 36 the in-run score against every frozen bank falls within the first 25 to 50M steps (scripted bot: 0.025 to 0.03 below the parent's last 100M) and regains the parent's level only at 2.1 to 3.0B; net change against the scripted bot per continuation rung is about zero (-0.002, +0.006, +0.003). The logs cannot separate "damage, then relearn" from "the score follows the current learning rate", and that in-run yardstick has not tracked the head-to-head gains.
- **The pool never contains the newest self as an active opponent**: `ladder_stage.sh` appends the warm checkpoint last and the scripted bot plays that bank's seats. The learner beats the anchor bank at about 0.91 and that bank takes about a quarter of frozen games. Recorded, not changed.

**How it runs.**
- `tools/campaign_supervisor.py` ticks every five minutes from a systemd user timer in the long-run checkout (`chain-supervisor@`). Each stage is `tools/chain_stage.sh`: it takes the shared GPU lock and waits for it without limit, runs the rung through `tools/ladder_stage.sh`, runs the six exam cells itself with every cell's exit status checked, and writes `EXAM_VERDICT.json`, plus `EXAM_VERDICT_PASS.json` only when the stage's rule passes. A written verdict is final and a failed trainer status is not retried; a host death is.
- GPU temperature, utilization and power are logged once a minute per rung. There is no thermal kill: the card holds 80 to 83 C under this load and 37 rungs have run there without a thermal or integrity failure.
- The two finished July queue units that started on every boot are disabled.
- **Tournaments compete with training for the rig's CPU.** A 15-worker gate running beside the trainer cost 19 to 22% of throughput tonight. Gates run on droplets when the account has room, and otherwise on the rig only when that cost is accepted and written down.

**What this entry does not decide.** The chain 35 and chain 36 verdicts; the parent for any gate-accepted continuation; whether the entropy anneal, the pool composition, the replay arithmetic or the seed spacing should change. Each of those is a separate declared factor.

**D415 - THE OWNER APPROVES REPLAY RE-SEATS FOR IMITATION DATA, WITH RESTRAINT; THE FIRST HUMAN PRIOR AND ITS OFFLINE AUDIT ARE STARTED OFF THE RIG (2026-10-05 16:45 PDT)**

**What was asked.** `AGENTS.md` forbids building game states by direct surgery: every banked state must be reached through legal `bb_apply` actions from an engine initializer. A prototype on branch `probe/lockstep-depth-20261003` (unmerged) restarts human-replay alignment at each team-turn boundary by writing the replay's recorded state into the engine, which is that surgery. On the 399 BB2025 replays held locally it takes usable human (observation, action) records from 115,939 to 565,033 and second-half coverage from 2.3% to 47.2%; the alternatives that avoid surgery recover nothing beyond the aligned prefix (as measured by the session that built it). The owner was asked to sign off on a contract change.

**The owner's answer, verbatim (2026-10-05 16:42 PDT):** "You can do reseats as often as you need just don't fo overboard".

**How that is applied.** The limits below are this ledger's reading of "don't go overboard", not the owner's words.
- New provenance: **replay-seated, observation only.** A re-seated state may be used to compute observations and conditional masks for imitation pairs. It is never a reset state for training, never an exam or tournament state, and never opponent data. The no-surgery invariant for banked reset states is unchanged.
- Re-seated records live in their own shard set with a per-record span stamp. A loader must ask for them explicitly. The default subset is prefix-aligned records plus re-seated records whose span closed equal to the replay.
- Any result says which subset it used.
- Scale follows evidence: the 399 local replays first; the 9,118-replay corpus only after the first prior and audit justify it.

**Started, off the rig, nothing wired into training.** A first human-imitation prior on the 399-replay set, and the audit the roadmap proposal named as the gate for any trainer work: on chain 41's own states, does the prior put clearly more weight on Block and Blitz declarations than chain 41 does, and on human states, where and how much does chain 41 depart from what the human chose. Thresholds are written before the numbers are read. If the audit says stop, no trainer term is built.

**Also recorded from the prototype, not acted on.** The engine departs from the BB2025 rules in at least four places: Grab on a Block action should allow any unoccupied adjacent push square and does not cancel Sidestep on a Blitz the way the engine does; Hit and Run is not offered after a Stab; a tied Brilliant Coaching roll should give both teams a re-roll; `ktm_used` is never reset. The engine's re-roll count differs from the human game's at 16.5% of otherwise aligned turn boundaries (as reported; not re-verified here). The build is frozen for the current lineage (D407), so these are batched for the next build change, each with a rules check and a regression test.


**D416 - AN INTEGRITY-GUARD FALSE POSITIVE HALTED THE CAMPAIGN FOR 27 MINUTES AND IS FIXED; THE EXAMS OF CHAINS 37 TO 49 RAN ON THE ORIGINAL BUILD'S MODULE; A NO-TRAINING TEST SHOWS THAT FORBIDDING AN EARLY END OF TURN IS WORTH ABOUT +32 TO +43 AT PLAY TIME; CHAIN 54, ONE TRAINING RUNG UNDER THAT RULE, IS PRE-REGISTERED ON A THIRD BUILD (2026-10-05 21:00 PDT, with chain 50 twenty minutes into training)**

**1. The halt.** Chain 49's stage ended at 20:13 PDT. Chain 50 launched at 20:15 and the live integrity guard killed it 34 seconds in ("machine panel is missing hard-integrity keys"). `chain_stage.sh` correctly treated the integrity failure as final, the stage exhausted its three attempts at 20:32, and the campaign halted. The GPU was idle from 20:16 to 20:40.
- **Cause.** The self-play league writes `historical_winrate` and `historical_winrate_bank_<b>` into the env panel on every epoch once any league game has ended. In chain 50 one game ended at epoch 2 and none at epochs 3 and 4, so those two panels carried league keys and no episode registry. The guard exempted only `elo` and read them as an env that published metrics without its registry. Every earlier rung's first game ended later, with games finishing in every epoch after it. The trainer is deterministic for a seed, so the same rung would have failed the same way on every relaunch.
- **Fix** (`39ec843`, tools only): the guard treats the league's win-rate keys like `elo`. Two regression tests; the real failed log replayed through the fixed guard gives 9 complete panels and no failure. An aggregated panel without its registry still fails. The long-run checkout was moved to that commit while nothing was running; the installed build is unchanged (drift check clean, module `3d8e5f72...`). Chain 50 relaunched at 20:40 as `screen-attempt2` and passed the point of failure. A Codex read of the fix is requested with this entry.

**2. A provenance defect in the long-run checkout, found by review and verified.** The long-run checkout's Python environment was made by copying the original checkout's. The copy's editable `pufferlib` finder was repointed to the new tree; the entry-point scripts' shebangs were not. Training goes through the environment's `python` and used the long-run module (its logs carry the long-run telemetry). `tools/eval_vs_contact_bot.sh` goes through the `puffer` entry point, whose shebang names the original checkout's interpreter (verified on the rig), and that interpreter resolves `pufferlib` to the original tree.
- **So the exams of chains 37, 38, 40, 41, 42, 46, 47, 48 and 49 ran on the original build's compiled module**, while their eval manifests record the long-run module's hash, which the launcher computes from the file path. The module actually imported was not captured in an exam process; this reading rests on the shebang, the finder, and the absence of long-run telemetry lines in the exam logs.
- **What it touches.** The original and long-run builds produced identical traces, weights and env digests in every check (D407 and its amendments), so the exam numbers are probably what the long-run module would have given; that is not proven for the exam path. No reading in D409 to D414 turned on an exam: no veto fired and no guard was within 0.03 of firing, except D416's own item 5 below.
- **What is done.** The long-run checkout is left as it is so the compounding test's exams stay comparable with the earlier ones. The new checkout (item 4) repoints the shebangs, and its exam refuses a foreign entry point.

**3. What the human-imitation audit and the masked-copy tests found** (off the rig; reports `docs/human-prior-v1-2026-10-05.md` on branch `probe/lockstep-depth-20261003`, and `docs/play-harness/masked-copy-2026-10-05.md`, `masked-copy-followup-2026-10-05.md`, `masked-copy-baselines-2026-10-05.md` on harness branch `feat/play-masks-20261005`; every threshold below was committed before its runs).
- **The registered gate for a human-prior trainer term read stop.** On chain 41's own states the first human prior puts less weight on Block declarations than chain 41 does (0.71 of chain 41's rate), and the Blitz gap fails the cross-check on human states. No declaration term is built.
- **The gap to human play is in the shape of a turn.** Per team turn, humans activate 7.16 players and chain 41 activates 2.97; a turn is ended by choice with a usable player left in 23.9% of human turns and 61.9% of chain 41's; a Block activation with a target on offer ends without a block 0.9% of the time for humans and 39% for chain 41.
- **A hypothesis, not tested.** Chain 41's training reward per game on the learner's side is +1.24 from distance to the end zone, +0.29 from touchdowns, +0.23 from the result, and negative from every block term (sequence -0.18, turnover -0.13, exposure -0.10) and from rushing (-0.14). The only dense reward is advancing the ball; nothing dense pays for using the other players.
- **Mask m1: END_TURN is not available while an activation is.** With no training, chain 41 under m1 against plain chain 41 is +32.5 [18.3, 47.1] decisive-Elo over 3,200 games (6.92 activations per team turn against 3.14). The same test on chains 42, 47 and 48 gives +37.3 [23.0, 51.8], +33.5 [20.4, 47.0] and +43.4 [29.1, 57.7]. As a paired contrast against a common opponent, m1 on chain 41 is worth +42.7 [23.5, 60.6] against chain 47, +37.8 against chain 36, +35.2 against chain 27, +20.9 [2.0, 39.5] against the contact bot, and -14.8 [-35.9, 4.6] against the offense bot (inconclusive). A null control, plain against plain with shifted sampling seeds, reads -11.1 [-25.4, 2.8].
- **Two other masks are worse** against plain chain 41: no activation ended at once, -25.4 [-38.3, -12.2]; no unthrown declared block, -24.5 [-36.7, -11.8].
- **What m1 adds.** About 4.2 activations a team turn, of which 58% end at once, 37% are moves only and 5% are blocks. With both sides under m1, touchdowns per side fall from 0.74 to 0.58 and a game takes 1,202 decisions against 695.
- **Under m1 the control shows no established edge over its parent:** chain 42 with m1 against chain 41 with m1 is +9.4 [-4.0, 23.5].

**4. The third build ("b3").** Branch `feat/no-early-end-turn-20261005` (head `5074b03` when installed): a default-off env flag `no_early_end_turn`, a launcher knob `LADDER_NO_EARLY_END_TURN`, exam support, and a lineage change that lets a graft declare more than one old build.
- **The rule.** In the env layer (the engine is untouched), on a seat played by the learner, END_TURN is removed from the legal list when an activation is also legal. Frozen-bank seats and scripted-bot seats keep the engine's list. Because the engine ends a team turn itself once nobody can be activated, this is in effect "the learner cannot end its own team turn by choice". It is a training and play restriction, not a Blood Bowl rule: a coach may end a turn at any time, and an empty activation is not a free skip (it can roll a negative trait, clear Distracted and move the Stalling check).
- **Flag off is identical** on the Mac and on the rig's CPU: observations, masks, legal lists, actions, rewards and terminals match the unmodified tree on four seeds; the C suites pass in the new checkout (459 / 51 / 14 / 12 / 34, 0 failures).
- **Installed** in its own checkout, `/home/rache/bloodbowl-rl-b3-20261006`, with its own environment copy (finder and shebangs repointed; both interpreters import this checkout's module). Env source `4c8a04b1...`, module `4156c9c3...`. The long-run checkout is untouched by it.
- **Lineage.** A rung on b3 from chain 41 declares two old builds: the original (`3ed6899e...`, `de77f6c0...`) and the long-run (`2ed3ffc2...`, `c1174af6...`). Plan-only preflights of the canary and of chain 54 verified with pool `cc9b201e...`.
- **Not yet shown, and gating everything below:** that the b3 CUDA build with the flag off reproduces chain 42's stored checkpoints at 131,072 and 50,069,504 steps byte for byte. That check, a flag-on trace and PPO smoke, and a 50M-step canary under the rule are supervised stages that fail closed. If the identity check fails, chain 54 does not run.

**5. Chain 49's exam veto fires.** Chain 49 (chain 42's rung with the bot on tag 1) scored 0.585 / 0.585 on offense AWAY against registered thresholds of below 0.594 and below 0.615, so its pair reads Negative by D413's ordered rule before its tournament is consulted. Its tournament is running and is reported in the next entry as the tournament half only. Both exams ran on the original module (item 2), the same for arm and control.

**6. Chain 54, pre-registered: one rung trained under the rule.**
- `r0chain54-noearlyend-from41-s42-20261006`: warm chain 41, training seed 42, pool `cc9b201e...`, bot on tag 4, standard recipe at restart scale 1.0, 3B steps, `LADDER_NO_EARLY_END_TURN=1`, on b3. **Control: chain 42**, the same rung without the rule.

- **Gate.** Tournament at harness commit `7d0d547` (branch `feat/play-masks-20261005`, whose unmasked path was shown identical to `b0099fb` game for game on a 64-game slice), seed block 22200000, 3,200 games per pair, 32 games per worker, T=1, accepted before scoring: (1) chain 54 + m1 against chain 42 + m1; (2) chain 54 + m1 against chain 41 + m1; (3) chain 54 + m1 against chain 37; (4) chain 42 + m1 against chain 37; (5) chain 54 + m1 against plain chain 42; (6) chain 54 + m1 against the offense bot; (7) chain 42 + m1 against the offense bot. Where both sides are masked, the two sides use different sampling seeds.
- **Ordered readings on pair (1):** Negative (interval entirely below zero) > Positive (point estimate above +40, that interval entirely above zero, and the paired contrast (3) minus (4) with its interval entirely above zero) > Flat (within plus or minus 40 inclusive) > Inconclusive. Missing, unaccepted or integrity-invalid evidence is not a reading. Pairs (2), (5), (6), (7) and the paired offense-bot contrast are descriptive.

If training under the rule produces more empty activations than the mask alone, it taught filler.

**D422 - CHAINS 58 AND 59 PRE-REGISTERED TO FOLLOW CHAIN 57: CHAIN 55'S RUNG WITH GAE LAMBDA 0.97, THEN CHAIN 55'S REPLICATE AT TRAINING SEED 2042; THE BLOCK-CHARGE REWARD ARM IS NOT RUN (2026-10-06 18:10 PDT; chain 57 is training, neither new rung has started, chain 57's gate has not been played)**

Chain 57 is the last stage in the plan and ends at about 01:40 PDT on 2026-10-07. Chains 55 and 56 both read Inconclusive (D419, D421), so nothing from this round changes the warm start so far. A design study (`docs/plans/next-rung-after-chain57-2026-10-06.md`, written by an agent on the session model and read by the operator) compared the candidates against the ledger's prior art. Two rungs are registered here, both one-variable copies of chain 55's stage on the same build, pool and warm start, so chain 55 is the control for both and no new control rung is needed.

**What was considered and not chosen.**
- **Removing the block risk charges (`reward_k_seq`, `reward_k_turnover`).** The operator's hypothesis in D416 item 3, that a block is net charged, is wrong as a general statement. The reward pays every declared block its expected knockdown, removal and ball-out value (`reward_k_kd`, `reward_k_value`, `reward_k_ball`, zero-sum against the defender), and the turnover and sequence charges fall on the attacker only. By hand arithmetic from the formulas, for equal strength, no skills, seven players still to act and a 50k to 100k target that is not the carrier, a two-die block comes out net paid and a one-die block net charged; the sign moves with the players still to act, the target's value, the ball and skills. The negative block-exposure line read in D416 is a zero-sum net that includes what opponents' blocks took, not a charge on the learner's own blocks. In the June panels (D156 to D169, another lineage) blocks fell by about a tenth when the charges were added; that is not a bound on what removing them would do now. Halving all five block terms lowered blocking (D278 to D281, exam only), but that halves pay and charges together and does not isolate the charges. The study's view that the gap to human blocking is mostly positional is a hypothesis. Not measured: the per-block numbers through `bb_block_ev`, the learner's gross block income, and the dice of the blocks it declines. An off-rig check of those comes before any reward rung. A reward arm also needs a tools change in the training checkout, which is not made while a stage runs from it.
- **Training under the rule at a second seed.** Barred by D416 and D421 without a new idea.
- **A second pool arm.** Chain 57 is the pool arm; a follow-up waits for its gate.

**Chain 58, pre-registered: chain 55's rung with GAE lambda 0.97.**
- `r0chain58-lam097-from49-s42-20261007`: warm chain 49 (`a2d1d10d...`), training seed 42, pool `2ae7448e...`, `r0_poss_half`, gamma 0.999, replay ratio 1.0, 4 banks x 0.12 with the contact bot on tag 4, restart scale 1.0, 3B steps, on the b3 build (source `4c8a04b1...`, module `4156c9c3...`), rule flag off, `LADDER_GAE_LAMBDA=0.97`. **Control: chain 55** (`f6ba3b44...`).
- **Hypothesis.** GAE weights a TD residual k steps later by (gamma x lambda)^k. One round of play is about 43 engine steps; at that distance the weight is 0.106 with lambda 0.95 and 0.259 with 0.97 (effective lengths 19.6 and 32.3 steps). These are geometric weights, not a hard window, and the critic's bootstrap and rollout boundaries carry credit too. The hypothesis is that the low weight is one reason an off-ball activation earns little advantage and the policy ends its turn after about three activations. If true, chain 58 activates more players per team turn than chain 55 in unmasked play, the added activations are not all empty, and it is no weaker.
- **Declared differences from chain 55, all of them.** GAE lambda. The wrapper sets one more variable. The rung runs about 27 hours later on the same checkout, build and hardware; the b3 checkout is at `fc25468`, the commit chain 55's stage ran from, was checked clean at 18:10 PDT and is not moved before either rung. The stage manifest must show the same source (`4c8a04b1...`), module (`4156c9c3...`) and Puffer patch bundle (`e3134e04...`) as chain 55's; a difference is an undeclared factor and the rung is unread until a new entry. Same stage rule (D405's chain 30 drift guard, same floors). No exam veto (D417).
- **Why D396 does not settle it.** Chain 29 changed gamma and lambda together and was read on the exam only, where one cell was 0.003 past the overshoot threshold. It has played no tournament, and the exam read chain 30 Flat (D397) a day before the round robin put it +108 over chain 25 (D399).
- **Gate.** Mask harness `7d0d547` for its activation log, seed block 22700000, 3,200 naturally completed games per pair, 32 per worker, T=1, kick-off starts, both legs, no sampling offsets, plan sha256 committed here before any shard is launched, accepted by `tools/gate_acceptance.py` and `accept_from_plan.py` before scoring. Eleven pairs, played without masks unless marked: (1) chain 58 against chain 55; (2) chain 58, (3) chain 55 and (4) chain 49, each against chain 37; (5) chain 58, (6) chain 55 and (7) chain 49, each against chain 46; (8) chain 58 against chain 49 (descriptive; chain 49 sits in the bot's seat in both pools); (9) chain 58 and (10) chain 55, each against the offense bot; (11) chain 58 + m1 against chain 55 + m1 (descriptive). Contrasts by `paired_contrasts.py` (sha256 `722ece95...`, 2,000 replicates, generator seed 0): chain 58 minus chain 55 against chain 37, chain 46 and the offense bot; retention, chain 58 minus chain 49, against chain 37 and chain 46.
- **Labels, applied in this order to accepted evidence only.** **Negative:** pair 1's interval entirely below zero, or the stage's chain 30 guard tripped. **Positive:** pair 1's point estimate above +40 with its interval entirely above zero, and both held-out contrasts (chain 58 minus chain 55, against chain 37 and against chain 46) with intervals entirely above zero. **Flat:** pair 1 within plus or minus 40 inclusive. **Inconclusive:** anything else. Missing, unaccepted or integrity-invalid evidence is unread. A trainer or integrity failure, or a marker refused for any reason but the guard, is unread for chain 58 only. A clean guard trip is Negative although the stage then writes no pass marker. A gate shard that aborts on the harness's 4,096-decision cap makes the gate unread, with no rerun before a new entry (D420).
- **Consequences.** Positive: lambda 0.97 is a candidate recipe component; adoption needs a second Positive pair at another training seed or parent, registered then. Chain 58 is a warm-start candidate only if both retention contrasts are also entirely above zero (D418 amendment item 6). Any other reading: lambda stays 0.95. Flat or Negative rejects this registered change in this context (one training seed, this warm start); it settles nothing general about D396's compound step.
- **Registered style diagnostics, not gates.** Pair 1, per team turn unless noted, each with the difference chain 58 minus chain 55 and a 95% seed-cluster interval: activations; empty activations; non-empty activations (the difference of the two); blocks (block targets chosen); turnovers; own decisions per game; touchdowns per game. Reference from D421's pair 9, another seed block: plain chain 55 has 2.965 activations, 0.537 empty, 0.466 blocks and 0.326 turnovers per team turn. The same table for pair 11, beside D421's masked values. In-run, from the logs: value loss, explained variance, deciding-row KL and clip fraction against chain 55's bands. Resemblance to human play is a diagnostic; the gate decides.

**Order and operation.**
