**D425 - A WHOLE-GAME OFFLINE COMPARISON OF ROLLOUT SEARCH IS PRE-REGISTERED: CHAIN 55 + m1 WITH A SEARCHING SEAT AGAINST ITSELF WITHOUT ONE, 1,600 GAMES PER ARM, ONE LOOK (2026-10-07 06:30 PDT by the machine's clock at commit; no game of it has been played; chain 58 is training and this uses no rig time)**

**Why.** Three gates in a row (D419, D421, D424) beat their comparator directly and left one held-out contrast spanning zero. Decision-time search is the roadmap's next lever (`docs/plans/superhuman-roadmap-2026-10-03.md`, M2). A design study and three offline measurements were made on 2026-10-07 (`docs/plans/search-probe-design-2026-10-07.md`, section 8 holds; `docs/search-probe-2026-10-07/FINDINGS.md`). All three measurements are exploratory: none had a plan committed before it ran, the third was extended in a second batch, and its intervals are nominal. What they suggest and do not establish: with chain 55 + m1 playing itself, a rollout search over the policy's own top candidates found an alternative with a large predicted gain (above 0.10 in shaped-return units) at about 1.5% of the sampled turn-level and after-declaration decisions, and those single deviations, played to the end of the match, showed +0.065 [+0.006, +0.122] touchdown difference and +0.028 [+0.006, +0.050] win score as means over 29 selected roots from 22 games. Small predicted gains showed nothing established, and deviations at the declare decision read negative on 6 roots. This entry registers the first test of a seat that searches at every in-scope decision of whole games. It decides whether the search seat is built into the tournament harness. It adopts nothing.

**Code and inputs, pinned in the plan file.** `docs/search-probe-2026-10-07/PLAN-d425.json`, sha256 `bae9549f6e5492f88630f9a282e6a959cb3158d93e0891af2e52a71850dfaf4c`. Branch `feat/search-probe-20261007` of the play harness at commit `544d5b3` (`tools/search_ab.py`, `play_harness/search.py`, the shim at ABI 5; code digest `69b20260...`). Checkpoint chain 55 (`f6ba3b44...`). Reward manifest `r0_poss_half` (canonical digest `433c7920...`) and gamma 0.999, both as in chain 55's stage manifest. The plan file fixes the game and search settings below (and the harness's 4,096-decision cap). The machine size, time limit, budget, relaunch allowance and labels are fixed by this entry, not by the plan file. The tool's launch, resume and report steps each refuse a plan file that does not hash to the value passed to them; passing the value committed here, and pushing that commit before any droplet is created, are the operator's part.

**Design.**
- Seat A and seat B are both chain 55 under m1, sampling at T=1, kick-off starts, seat B on sampling offset 1. Every engine seed is played in both orientations (A home, A away).
- Seed block 29200000 to 29200799: 800 seeds, 1,600 games per arm, the same seeds for every arm. One look: nothing is scored until every record is in, and there is no extension.
- Arm **P** (plain): seat A does not search. It is the speed reference and a calibration: if the two sampling streams are exchangeable, its expected decisive share is one half and its expected touchdown difference is zero.
- Arm **S10** (primary): seat A searches at every own decision that is turn-level (an ACTIVATE is legal) or the first own decision after its own DECLARE, when more than one action is legal. Not at DECLARE. Candidates: the action plain play sampled (a0) and up to three other legal joint actions with the highest policy probability, ties broken by a fixed action order. 16 rollouts per candidate with common random numbers across candidates. In a rollout both sides are played by chain 55 under m1 from rollout-only dice and generators; the real seats' generators, the real dice and the real recurrent states are never consumed or written. A rollout stops at the end of seat A's own team turn, or at the end of the match (no bootstrap), or after 200 steps (bootstrapped and counted). Its score is the discounted training reward collected plus the discounted value at the stop. Seat A deviates to the best alternative only if its paired mean gain over a0 exceeds delta = 0.10 and exceeds two standard errors, with the standard error no smaller than the square root of (the mean over candidates of the per-rollout return variance, divided by 16). Otherwise it plays a0.
- Identity sample: on every droplet, the first 5 seeds of its range in both orientations with delta set to infinity, so the full search runs at every in-scope decision and is discarded. Each game's action-trail digest and final state digest must equal arm P's for the same seed and orientation on the same droplet. This shows identity for that sample under that runtime, not in general.
- Machines: eight DigitalOcean droplets (`s-8vcpu-16gb-amd`) through the harness's droplet tooling, 100 seeds each. Each droplet plays both arms and its identity sample for its own seed range, with the arms interleaved, so no arm is tied to a machine. Records carry the native library hash, ABI, library versions, precision and thread counts.
- Statistic: seat A's decisive-Elo in arm S10 with a 95% percentile interval from a seed-cluster bootstrap (both orientations of a seed resampled together, all arms resampled jointly, 2,000 replicates, generator seed 0), computed by `search_ab.py report`. It is tested against zero. The seed-paired contrast S10 minus P, computed inside each replicate, is reported beside it and is not the label statistic.

**Acceptance, before anything is scored.** The report prints no outcome unless all of this holds; otherwise the comparison is unread.
- Every (seed, orientation, arm) of the plan present exactly once; code, checkpoint, manifest and plan hashes equal to the plan's; the native library hash equal across all droplets; ABI, library versions, precision and a single torch thread constant within a shard.
- Every real game naturally completed. A real game that ends on the decision cap makes the comparison unread, with no rerun before a new entry (D420).
- No integrity failure in a real game or in any rollout clone. What the tool checks, and records in every game's `integrity_checks` list: the engine's return code on every step; the five hard counters the shim exports (illegal actions, projection collisions, error episodes, rejected submissions, precheck collisions), after every real step and at the end of every rollout; finite logits and values on every forward, both views; both seats' emitted rewards finite and inside the manifest's clip threshold on every real and rollout step; a finite accumulated return for every rollout; no mask fallback. One such event makes its arm unread. Not checked: the env's own reward telemetry counters (clipped, non-finite, component mismatch), which the shim does not export; the checks on the emitted rewards stand in for them.
- Every identity game matched.
- A rollout that ends on the decision cap it inherits from the real game is a cap rejection: that decision plays a0 and is counted. If more than 1% of an arm's searched decisions have a cap rejection, the arm is unread.
- A droplet that dies or reaches its time limit may be relaunched once, for its unfinished games only, from the same plan. Finished records are never replayed. The relaunch runs on another droplet, which does not replay the identity sample; its runtime is covered by the library hash only, and the report shows which shards were relaunched. If records are still missing after one relaunch, or the budget is exhausted, or the run is stopped early for any reason, the comparison is unread, never Flat or Negative. The one-relaunch limit and the cumulative budget are kept by the operator from the runner's cost lines; the runner enforces the budget per launch only.
- If arm S10's statistic is undefined (no decisive game), the comparison is unread.

**Labels for arm S10, applied in this order to accepted evidence.**
- **Negative:** the interval entirely below zero.
- **Positive:** the point estimate above +20 with the interval entirely above zero. This establishes a gain above zero, not a gain above +20.
- **Flat:** the interval entirely inside -20 to +20.
- **Inconclusive:** anything else.

**Consequences.**
- Positive: the search seat is built into the tournament harness (the design's milestone M3) with this scope and delta, provided the measured slowdown against arm P on the droplets is at most 150; above that a new entry decides. A gate against chain 55 + m1 and the held-out opponents chain 37 and chain 46 is registered before it is played. This comparison is self-play, where the rollouts model the opponent with the opponent's own network; it says nothing about other opponents, and nothing is adopted from it.
- Flat or Negative: rollout search with this evaluator, scope and delta is closed. The next design is an outcome head as evaluator.
- Inconclusive: the seat is not built on this evidence. The result is recorded as unresolved, not as a rejection, and continuing needs a new registered entry on fresh seeds.
- Arm P's interval excluding zero is reported as a warning, since it happens one time in twenty with exchangeable streams. The S10 minus P contrast is then read beside the label, the label rule is not changed, and no fresh seed block is played to make arm P pass.
- A lower delta is not played here. The exploratory band (predicted gain 0.02 to 0.10) is about six times as frequent as the tail and its outcome interval touched zero; an arm for it would double the cost of this entry. It needs its own registered comparison on fresh seeds.

**Reported beside the label, none of it a gate:** W / D / L, win score and decisive share per arm; touchdown difference per game with its interval; the paired contrast S10 minus P; deviations per game by class and by action types; mean predicted gain at deviations; cap rejections and 200-step cutoffs; wall time per game and the slowdown against arm P.

**Spend.** A ceiling of $5 for everything in this entry, enforced by the runner as the sum over droplets of time limit times hourly price (eight droplets at 2.5 hours and $0.16667 an hour is $3.33). The expected spend is about $2.2: 1,680 searched games at about 215 seconds per droplet core. Droplets this entry creates are destroyed, partial records are fetched before a timed-out droplet is destroyed, and the spend is reported.

**Why +20.** +20 decisive-Elo is a decisive share of about 52.9%. The m1 mask was taken as a play-time option at +32 to +43 for no cost. Search cost about 3.6 minutes of one droplet core per game in the smoke below, 46 times plain play on the same droplet. It would be used where time is cheap (games against people, or as a teacher, which is untested), so a smaller gain than m1's is still worth building for. This is an engineering preference, and the slowdown condition above keeps the build decision tied to the measured cost.

**Two smokes were played before this entry and are not evidence.** Both on one droplet each at seed 29900000, which is outside this entry's block, to prove the runner and measure speed. The first (8 games at commit `79e466e`: plain, delta 0.10, delta 0.02 and identity, both orientations; `docs/search-probe-2026-10-07/droplet_smoke_report.txt`) passed acceptance; a searched game took 150 to 300 seconds on one core, 46 times plain play. The second (6 games at this entry's commit `544d5b3`, after the integrity checks were widened; `droplet_smoke2_report.txt`) passed acceptance with the 13 checks recorded, and its six games equal the first smoke's on action trail and final state, on another droplet with the same native library hash. In both, the identity games equalled the plain games on action trail, final state and sampling state. Both droplets were destroyed ($0.04 together). The reports printed two games per arm, which say nothing.

**Limits, disclosed.**
- The scope (no declare class), the delta of 0.10 and the 16 rollouts were chosen from the exploratory runs on seed blocks 29000000 and 29100000, which used chain 55 + m1 in self-play on other seeds.
- The evaluator is shaped training reward plus the value head, not match outcome.
- There is no lower-temperature control, so a Positive is not a claim that search finds more than sharpening would. The exploratory runs suggest it is not sharpening (the chosen alternatives had policy probability below 0.001 in 25 of 28 cases, by the agent's report), and that is not established.
- The design study's pilot rule D2 (an upper bound on false deviations from independent reference rollouts) is not met by the exploratory runs and is set aside for this entry: the whole-game result is the judge here. It applies again before any gate.

**Written down so it cannot be adjusted later.** I expect S10's point estimate between +10 and +60 decisive-Elo. With 1,600 games and about 59% of games decisive the interval should be near plus or minus 22. At that width Flat cannot be reached at all, since the interval must fit inside plus or minus 20; an estimate near zero would then read Inconclusive. I have no distribution over the true effect and give no odds for the labels. The labels are applied by the operator from the report's numbers.
- Reviewed by Codex twice before this entry was written (`.codex-reviews/d425-review.md`, `d425-review2.md`). The first review's changes: one fixed look in place of an optional extension, Flat by interval, arm P as a warning and not a gate, the rejection taxonomy, the spend and stopping rules. The second found the tool's integrity checks narrower than the draft's promise; the tool was widened (`b5904ea` to `544d5b3`) and the wording now lists exactly what is checked. Not re-reviewed after that last round: the four fix commits themselves, which the operator checked by rerunning 130 tests and the second smoke.

**D426 - THE WHOLE-GAME SEARCH COMPARISON (D425) READS POSITIVE: IN SELF-PLAY, CHAIN 55 + m1 WITH THE SEARCHING SEAT IS +47 [+28, +67] DECISIVE-ELO AGAINST THE SAME CHECKPOINT WITHOUT ONE; THE SEARCH SEAT IS TO BE BUILT INTO THE TOURNAMENT HARNESS AND A GATE REGISTERED BEFORE IT IS PLAYED; NOTHING IS ADOPTED (2026-10-07 10:01 PDT by the machine's clock at commit; chain 58's stage has ended, its gate has not been played, chain 59 is training)**

**What was run, against D425.** Plan `PLAN-d425.json` (sha256 `bae9549f...`), harness branch `feat/search-probe-20261007` at `544d5b3`, chain 55 under m1 in both seats, seat A searching in arm S10, seeds 29200000 to 29200799 in both orientations, 1,600 games per arm, plus the identity sample. One look, by the operator's statement: the report was run once, after every record was in, and nothing was tallied or scored before it. The artifacts are consistent with that and cannot prove it: the report's three files were written at 09:54:06, after the last record arrived at 09:53. The runner logs the operator read for progress print the latest finished game's result on their status lines, so single game results were exposed to the operator at 07:01 and during the relaunch. Beyond that the operator read game counts and wall times and counted records per arm in the partial files. No decision depended on any result: the relaunch was forced by the time limit and its terms were fixed by D425.

**A timing miss, and the one relaunch D425 allows.** The first launch (eight droplets, 06:30 PDT) was sized from a smoke in which a searched game took about 215 seconds. That smoke kept only 4 to 6 of the droplet's 8 worker processes busy. In this run the mean elapsed time per searched game was 370 seconds (363 on the first-launch droplets, 415 on the relaunch droplets), so seven of the eight shards reached the 2.5 hour limit at about 09:00 with 322 to 403 of their 410 games recorded. Shard s1 finished. The runner fetched the partial records and destroyed each droplet. The sizing error is the operator's. The likely cause is that the 8 vCPUs are hyperthreads and slow down when all are busy; processor time was not measured, so that is not established.
- Each of the seven shards was relaunched once, at 09:05 PDT, on a new droplet, from the same plan, for its unfinished games only (7 to 88 games; a game that was in progress at the limit had no record and was played from its start). No finished record was replayed. All seven finished, the last at 09:53.
- The relaunched droplets did not replay the identity sample, as D425 states. All 80 identity games were played on the first-launch droplets. The relaunched droplets' runtime is covered by the native library hash, which is the same on all fifteen droplets (`32632f03...`). The identity sample shows that a full search which is then discarded leaves those 80 games unchanged on those eight droplets; it is not a general proof.
- Of the 1,600 games of arm S10, 1,395 were played on first-launch droplets and 205 on relaunch droplets; of arm P, 1,450 and 150.
- Spend by the runners' cost lines: $3.317 for the first launch, $0.616 for the relaunch, $0.04 for the two smokes, $3.97 in all against the $5 ceiling and an expected $2.2. All fifteen droplets and their keys are deleted (HTTP 404 on each in the logs; the tool's status listing shows no tagged droplet, no key and no live local state).

**Acceptance.** `search_ab.py report` printed `ACCEPTANCE: PASS` (`docs/search-probe-2026-10-07/d425_report.txt`, sha256 `db1234ef...`; the report's SHA256SUMS lists the eight record files and the plan). Three layers, kept apart here. (1) At play time the tool runs the 13 integrity checks D425 lists on every real step and rollout and marks a record invalid, or not naturally completed, on any failure. As D425 states, the env's own reward telemetry counters (clipped, non-finite, component mismatch) are not exported by the shim and are not checked; the checks on the emitted rewards stand in for them. (2) The report's acceptance reads the records: every (seed, orientation, arm) present once; hashes equal to the plan's; the native library hash equal across droplets; every real game naturally completed; no record marked invalid; the list of checks on every record equal to the plan's 13; all 80 identity games equal to the plain games on action trail, final state and sampling state, with 1,020,752 rollouts run and discarded; cap rejections under the ceiling. It does not replay the checks. (3) A recount of the raw fields by the operator and by the reviewer: 3,280 records with unique keys, none on the decision cap (the longest real game is 1,922 decisions), no invalid record, no error rollout, no cap rejection (0 of 331,103 searched decisions), 711 of 19,576,320 rollouts ended on the 200-step cutoff.

| Arm | W / D / L | Win score | Decisive share | Decisive-Elo [95% seed-cluster] | TD difference per game |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P (plain) | 449 / 675 / 476 | 0.492 [0.475, 0.509] | 0.485 [0.456, 0.515] | -10 [-30, +11] | -0.035 [-0.081, +0.013] |
| S10 (search, delta 0.10) | 534 / 658 / 408 | 0.539 [0.523, 0.556] | 0.567 [0.540, 0.596] | +47 [+28, +67] | +0.114 [+0.067, +0.161] |

**Reading, labels applied in the registered order: Positive.**
- Not Negative: S10's interval is not entirely below zero.
- Positive: the point estimate is +47, above +20, and the interval [+28, +67] is entirely above zero. As registered, this establishes a gain above zero for the searching seat in this setting, not a gain above +20 (the lower bound happens to be above +20; the label does not rest on that).
- Arm P's interval contains zero, so the registered warning does not apply. Its point estimate is below zero, which is why the paired contrast (+57) is larger than the label statistic (+47). The label statistic is the one registered.
- The operator's written expectation was a point estimate between +10 and +60 with an interval near plus or minus 22. The result is inside it (+47, about plus or minus 20).

**Consequences, as registered in D425.**
- The measured slowdown is 41.3 times plain play on the same droplets (370.1 against 9.0 seconds per game), under the 150 limit. So the search seat is to be built into the tournament harness (the design's milestone M3) with this scope (turn-level and the first decision after the seat's own declaration) and delta 0.10. It is not built yet.
- A gate against chain 55 + m1 and the held-out opponents chain 37 and chain 46 is to be registered, in its own entry, before any of its games is played. The design study's pilot rule D2 applies again before that gate.
- Nothing is adopted. No checkpoint, recipe or play-time default changes on this entry.

**What this does not show.**
- It is self-play. In the rollouts the opponent is played by the network the real opponent uses, so the search's model of the opponent is exact here. Against chain 37, chain 46 or a person it is not. The gate measures that.
- There is no lower-temperature control, so this is not a claim that search finds more than sharpening the policy would.
- The evaluator is shaped training reward plus the value head, not match outcome.
- One checkpoint, one mask setting, one delta, one scope, 16 rollouts. The scope, delta and rollout count were chosen from exploratory runs on other seeds (D425, Limits).
- A lower delta was not played and nothing is known about it from this entry.

**Descriptive, not part of the reading** (`docs/search-probe-2026-10-07/d425_splits.txt`, raw counts without intervals, made after the report was read).
- What the search did: 99.5 turn-level and 107.4 after-declaration decisions searched per game; 2.42 deviations per game (1.24 turn-level, 1.19 after the declaration), 1.17% of searched decisions; 151 of the 1,600 games had no deviation. Mean predicted gain at a deviation 0.159 (median 0.133). The exploratory tail measured 1.46% and 0.159.
- Deviation types: 1,978 are another player activated; after the declaration, 953 are a different step, 319 a step in place of ending the activation, 207 a block in place of ending the activation, 146 standing up in place of ending the activation, 94 ending the activation in place of a step.
- Touchdowns per game: seat A scores 0.831 with search and 0.701 without; seat B scores 0.716 and 0.736. The gain is mostly seat A scoring more.
- By orientation, S10's raw decisive share is 0.547 with seat A at home and 0.587 away (plain: 0.470 and 0.501).
- By shard, S10's raw decisive share is above one half in seven of eight (0.575, 0.547, 0.582, 0.584, 0.559, 0.616, 0.496, 0.575); arm P's ranges from 0.405 to 0.561.
- By droplet: S10's raw decisive share is 0.573 on the 1,395 first-launch games and 0.528 on the 205 relaunch games; arm P's is 0.491 and 0.429. The relaunch games are not a random subset (they are the later games of each shard's order and the games in progress at the limit), and both arms read lower there.
- The same seed and orientation give the same result in both arms in 60.2% of pairs and the same game in 9.4%.
- Cost: the mean elapsed time per searched game is 370 seconds (median 365, longest 725) with eight worker processes on an 8-vCPU droplet. At that rate, with all eight workers busy throughout and no setup time counted, 3,200 searched games would take about 41 droplet-hours, about $6.9. The gate's size and budget are set in its own entry.

**Process notes.**
- A run on rented machines is sized from a smoke that loads every core, and the time limit is given real margin.
- Reviewed by Codex before this entry was written (`.codex-reviews/d426-review.md`): Positive is the only label the registration supports and no unread condition is triggered; its recount reproduced the report, the splits, the spend and the hashes; the seven relaunches carried the finished records over byte for byte and replayed none. Four corrections applied above: the one-look statement is attributed to the operator and says what the logs exposed, the acceptance paragraph separates what was checked at play time, by the report and by recount and restores D425's stated exclusion, the timing is described as elapsed time, and the consequences are worded as still to do.

**D430 - THE SEARCH SEAT'S GATE AGAINST HELD-OUT OPPONENTS IS PRE-REGISTERED: CHAIN 55 + m1 WITH THE SEARCH SEAT AND WITHOUT IT, EACH AGAINST CHAIN 37 AND CHAIN 46, 3,200 GAMES A PAIR, ONE LOOK (2026-10-07 13:58 PDT by the machine's clock at commit; no game of it has been played; chain 59 is training and this uses no rig time)**

**Why.** D426 read Positive in self-play: chain 55 + m1 with the searching seat was +47 [+28, +67] decisive-Elo against the same checkpoint without one. In self-play the rollouts model the opponent with the opponent's own network. D425 registered that a Positive is followed by a gate against opponents the rollouts do not model exactly, before anything is adopted. This entry is that gate.

**What was built since D426, and how it was checked.** Harness branch `feat/search-probe-20261007`; the gate's commit is `06f0a5f`.
- **The seat** (`b52ae45` to `33428b3`: `play_harness/search.py` `SearchSeat`, `play_harness/tournament.py --search`, `tools/droplet_tournament.py --search`, `tools/search_acceptance.py`), built by an agent on the session model and checked by the operator against git. The seat draws the plain action exactly as the masked seat does, keeps its own network's recurrent state on the opponent's observation row (it never reads the other seat), and applies D425's rule through the same rollout code.
- **Equivalence with the tool that measured D426**, by the build agent's tests and report (not rerun by the operator, except through the full suite): on the Mac, three tournament games of chain 55 + m1 + search against chain 55 + m1 (offset 1) equal `search_ab.py` arm S10's games field for field; against D425's droplet records the same three games have the same action trail, final state and counts (predicted gains differ in the sixth decimal across machines). With delta set to infinity the seat reproduces the plain masked game on 10 seeds.
- **First Codex review, of the seat** (`.codex-reviews/m3-review.md` in the harness worktree). No route from the real opponent's hidden state into the search, no difference from D425's decision rule, no way for the search to change the real game except through the action played. Two blocking findings, both reproduced by the reviewer: the acceptance tool could pass records whose seats were not the registered pair's, records with missing identity or integrity fields, and non-finite predicted gains; and a resume or a merge did not check existing records against their manifests. Fixed by two agents on the session model: `4437bdd` to `5965294` (the acceptance tool, each reproduced false pass with a regression test that failed first, merged at `d8c3a89`) and `ccba611`, `413291d`, `eee64f6` (resume and merge). A resume into a run written at another harness commit is now refused, which retires the "legacy manifests resume as before" line of two September docs.
- **A pair can be split across droplets by game index** (`--index0`, `70c6098`, `69b33cc`, `660886e`), because a searched game takes about six and a half minutes of one core, the tournament tool used to shard by pair only, and the account offers no machine above 8 vCPUs. In the tests a split pair merges into a run whose records equal the unsplit run's field for field (ignoring seconds and process id), for a plain and for a searched pair.

The earlier false passes are closed; the split and the merge hold seeds, ranges and settings; game play is unchanged from the reviewed seat; the reviewer built this gate's 12,820-record layout in memory and both acceptance tools passed it. One blocking finding: no tool required a record's final status to be the engine's match-over status. Closed for this gate in `accept_from_plan.py` (final status, and both sides' decision counts positive and adding up to the engine steps); the harness tools do not yet check it.

When the seat deviated to such an action it recorded a log-probability of minus infinity, and the fixed acceptance tool refused that record. `06f0a5f` records the finite log-space value in that case and the value it always recorded otherwise; it changes no decision. In three plain games on the Mac, half of the search's alternative candidates had a log-probability below -50 and 0.7% underflowed.
- **Full suite** at `d8c3a89`: 1,288 passed, 11 skipped, exit 0. At `06f0a5f`: 1,290 passed, 11 skipped, exit 0 (both runs by the operator, logs in the session scratchpad).
- **What acceptance cannot show**, by the acceptance agent's own list and the reviews: hand-edited scores, records spliced from another run with the same names, seeds and settings, and a seat that ran other search arithmetic than it declared. Those rest on the pinned code, its tests, and the droplet tool's own verification of what it copied back.

**Pilot rule D2, which D425 set aside and said applies before any gate.** The rule (design study, section 8): an upper confidence bound of 10% or less on the share of the seat's deviations that are false by fresh independent rollouts, a lower bound above zero on the mean gain, clustered by game, on held-out states. The count was fixed in `docs/search-probe-2026-10-07/D2_CHECK_PLAN.md` (commit `3dae118`, pushed) before a third batch of roots was run.
- Batches 1 and 2 (already seen when the count was fixed): 29 deviations in 22 games, 0 false.
- Batch 3 (seeds 29100067 to 29100199, 3,990 roots screened): 58 deviations in 45 games, 0 false; exact one-sided 95% upper bound 5.0% counting roots. All three batches counting games: 0 false of 67, upper bound 4.4%. Mean fresh gain in batch 3: 0.146 [0.120, 0.178]. Recorded in the same file and `d2_count.txt` (commit `7d6bed8`).
- So D2 is met by the count fixed in advance (the plan's commit `3dae118` is an ancestor of the result's `7d6bed8`; commit order cannot prove when the batch started). That is less than the statistical assurance section 8 asked for. Its limits: "false" means the fresh 128-pair estimate is at or below zero, which the reference's own error can get wrong either way; the root-level bound treats roots as independent though some share a game, and the game-level condition pools the two batches that had been seen; the reference is 128 fresh paired rollouts, not 256 (the weakest deviation's fresh gain is +0.021 with a standard error of 0.017; the next is +0.063 with 0.010); the roots come from plain self-play trajectories, one deviation at a time; it is about the evaluator (shaped return plus the value head), not about wins.
- Exploratory, entering nothing: played to the end of the match, the 87 deviations of all batches show +0.051 [+0.019, +0.085] touchdown difference and +0.019 [+0.007, +0.031] win score each; 87 control-band roots show nothing (`tail_all_report.txt`).

**Design.**
- **Players.** S = chain 55 (`f6ba3b44...`) + m1 + the search seat at D425's setting (scope turn-level and first decision after the own declaration; a0 and the three most probable other actions; 16 rollouts each on common random numbers; stop at the end of the own team turn, the end of the match, or 200 steps; deviate on a paired mean gain above 0.10 and above two floored standard errors; reward manifest `r0_poss_half` `433c7920...`, gamma 0.999; in rollouts both sides are played by chain 55 under m1). C = chain 55 + m1. Held-out opponents: chain 37 (`268f1db0...`) and chain 46 (`8eee9ac1...`), played plain, as in every gate since D418.
- **Pairs**, seed block 25100000 (unused), 3,200 naturally completed games each, kick-off starts, both legs of every seed, T=1, one game per worker: (1) S against chain 37; (2) C against chain 37; (3) S against chain 46; (4) C against chain 46. (5) Identity: the search seat with delta infinity against chain 37, the first 10 seeds, 20 games.
- S and C have the same sampling seeds, so on a given seed and leg the two games are identical until S's first deviation.
- **The self-play pair is not replayed.** D425 said the gate is "against chain 55 + m1 and the held-out opponents". D426 measured the self-play pair this morning on 1,600 games, the tournament seat plays that tool's games exactly, and replaying it would add half again to the gate's searched games, cost and hours without changing any label below. A replay would test replication on fresh seeds; this gate does not. This is a departure from D425's wording, made before any game.
- **Statistic.** The two paired contrasts S minus C, against chain 37 and against chain 46, in decisive-Elo with 95% seed-cluster intervals, by `paired_contrasts.py` (sha256 `722ece95...`, 2,000 replicates, generator seed 0).
- **Machines.** Eight DigitalOcean droplets `s-8vcpu-16gb-amd`, 8 workers each. Each droplet plays 200 seeds (game indexes 200(j-1) to 200j-1) of all four pairs, so no arm is tied to a machine; the first also plays the identity pair. Expected about 11.5 hours a droplet (800 searched games at about 400 seconds over 8 workers, 820 on the first); time limit 15 hours.
- **One look.** The operator does not inspect or tally outcomes, shard reports or game records, whole or partial, until every shard has finished and the merged run has passed acceptance. The runner writes a statistics report inside each shard's directory when the shard ends; those files are not opened. Progress lines carry game counts, rate and time left, no outcome. There is no early stop and no extension.

**Acceptance, before anything is scored** (plan file `PLAN.json` in the gate directory `srch-gate-20261007`, sha256 `7fb1591c8489518e5b4d11c841a5d5970aecf67d5157e99475c1fea6dd67dad1`, copied to `docs/search-probe-2026-10-07/gate/` with the hashes of the scripts beside it (`SCRIPTS.sha256`); this entry is committed and pushed before any droplet is created; the launcher and `score_from_plan.py` each refuse a plan file or a script that does not hash to the registered value).
- `tools/gate_acceptance.py`: the five pairs, their game counts, the seed block, both legs of every seed exactly once, one game per worker, the harness commit, each player's checkpoint hash, sample mode at temperature 1, natural endings, every integrity counter zero.
- `accept_from_plan.py`: each player's masks in the manifest and on its side of every game, no sampling offset, no truncation, no mask fallback; every game's final status equal to the engine's match-over status; both sides' decision counts positive and adding up to the engine's decisions and steps; the native kernel; `COMPLETE.json` saying complete; both harness acceptance tools equal to the hashes in the plan, on disk and at the registered commit.
- `tools/search_acceptance.py`: every record's seats are its pair's and leg's; each player's complete search setting (scope, k, n, delta, cutoff, horizon, gamma, reward manifest hash, opponent model, candidate rule, standard-error floor) in the manifest and on its side of every game; the reward manifest hash and the 13 integrity checks on every searched game; consistent search statistics, no failed rollout, one opponent-view forward per engine step; at most 1% of a pair's searched decisions with a cap rejection; all 20 identity games equal to C's games on action trail, final digest, log-probability sums, score, steps, rosters and sampling seeds, having run their rollouts.
- The merge requires the same commit, settings, torch, Python and compiled library on every droplet, and checks every shard's records against that shard's manifest.
- Not checked, as in D425 and D426: the env's own reward telemetry counters (clipped, non-finite, component mismatch), which the shim does not export; the checks on the emitted rewards stand in for them.
- **Relaunch, fixed now.** Only a droplet that dies, loses contact or reaches its time limit may be replaced. Its shard is launched again, whole, on a new droplet from the same plan (`launch_from_plan.py --relaunch-suffix r`); the failed shard's partial records are never read, merged or scored. Games are deterministic given the plan, so the replacement plays the same games. At most one replacement per shard and four in all, in the order the shards failed, and a replacement is launched only if the spend so far plus every running droplet's time limit plus the replacement's ($2.50) stays within the ceiling. The merged run uses, for each shard, its original run if that completed, else its one replacement; there is never a choice between two completed copies of a shard.
- **Unread, never Flat or Negative:** missing, unaccepted or integrity-invalid evidence; a shard that aborts on an integrity failure or on a real game reaching the 4,096-decision cap (no relaunch for those before a new entry, D420); a shard that fails again after its replacement, or a fifth failed shard; a budget stop. In each case the whole gate is unread.

**Labels, applied in this order to accepted evidence.**
- **Negative:** either contrast's interval entirely below zero.
- **Positive:** both contrasts' point estimates above +20 with both intervals entirely above zero. As in D425, this establishes gains above zero, not above +20. Why +20 again: m1 was taken as a play-time option at +32 to +43 for no cost; the search costs about 45 times plain play (smoke below) and would be used where time is cheap (games against people, or as a teacher, which is untested), so a smaller gain than m1's is still worth having. That is an engineering preference.
- **Flat:** both contrasts' intervals entirely inside -20 to +20. Flat is unlikely at the expected interval widths (about plus or minus 20); near-zero estimates will usually read Inconclusive.
- **Inconclusive:** anything else.

**Consequences.**
- **Positive:** this search setting on chain 55 + m1 becomes a play-time option, as m1 is, with its measured slowdown recorded beside it. It is not a claim that search finds more than sharpening the policy would: a lower-temperature control at plain speed is registered and read before any further entry builds on search (a C rollout kernel, search as a teacher, a larger rollout budget). Using it on another checkpoint needs that checkpoint's own gate. No training recipe, warm start or evaluation default changes.
- **Negative or Flat:** rollout search with this evaluator and opponent model is not carried to other opponents and is closed until one of the two changes. No escalation is registered.
- **Inconclusive:** not adopted. The contrasts are reported as measured and a further sample needs a new entry.

**Registered diagnostics, not gates.** W / D / L and decisive-Elo of the four pairs; the mean of the two contrasts (descriptive, no label); touchdown difference per game; the style table of D422 for S and C against each opponent; for S: searched decisions and deviations per game by class, deviation types, mean and median predicted gain, cap rejections, cutoffs, seconds per game and the slowdown against C on the same droplets.

**Spend.** Expected about $15.5 (12,820 games of which 6,420 searched, at about 400 seconds of one core each). Eight droplets at the 15 hour limit are $20. Ceiling $30 for everything in this entry (the eight originals and four replacements at their time limits), counted from the runner's cost lines; the runner enforces the time limit per droplet, and the operator keeps the sum and the count of replacements. Droplets this entry creates are destroyed and the spend is reported.

**Smoke, not evidence.** Two droplets at `d8c3a89`, seed block 29910000 (outside every block in use), 32 games a pair and 4 identity games, 132 games, with this gate's launcher and plan generator: launch from a hashed plan, index slices 0 to 7 and 8 to 15. The acceptance wrapper was changed after the smoke was launched (the final-status and decision-count checks of the second review), so the smoke's plan was written again with the new wrapper's hash before the merge, acceptance and scoring were run; the launched plan is kept beside it as `PLAN.launched.json`, and the two differ in the time stamp and the acceptance block only. Both droplets built the library `32632f03...` (D425's). The merge succeeded and the stock tool and the mask checks accepted the run; the search acceptance refused the one record with the infinite log-probability (above). On a scratch copy with that one number replaced (by the operator, outputs in the session scratchpad, not saved as artifacts), all three checks accept, the 4 identity games equal the plain games, and the report, the contrasts and the diagnostics run. The operator did not read the smoke's report; 32 games a pair say nothing. (The scores of the four games of seed 29910000 were printed while the fix below was checked.) Elapsed time with eight workers busy (not processor time): the 64 searched games of S take 397 seconds on average (401 against chain 37, 393 against chain 46; longest 562), the 4 identity games 441 (longest 574), a plain game 8.7; the slowdown is 48 and 43. S deviates 2.25 and 2.72 times a game. No cap rejection; 125 of 791,520 rollouts cut off, identity games included. Both droplets destroyed (HTTP 404), $0.21. The gate's commit `06f0a5f` differs from the smoked commit by the log-probability fix only and has not itself run on a droplet. The operator replayed seed 29910000's four games (S and C against chain 37, both legs) on the Mac at `06f0a5f`: the four action trails equal the droplet's records, and the log-probability sum that was minus infinity is -1110.5044.

**Limits, disclosed.**
- The two opponents are older relatives of chain 55 and about 200 Elo weaker than C under m1 (D421). Neither is a strong or a foreign opponent. A Positive says the gain carries to opponents the rollouts mis-model; it does not say it carries to a stronger one or to a person.
- The rollouts stop at the end of the seat's own team turn, so the opponent model matters only for the opponent's choices inside that turn; the value head at the stop was trained against the training pool, not against these opponents.
- One checkpoint, one setting, chosen from exploratory runs and one registered comparison in self-play.
- Chain 55 is very sharp at the searched decisions: in three plain games half of the search's alternative candidates had a log-probability below -50. The search therefore mostly weighs actions the policy all but rules out, which a lower temperature would make rarer still. That is a reason to expect the temperature control to show little, not a measurement of it.
- The standard-error floor in the rule is the error of one candidate's mean, not of a difference of two means (found by the build agent). It is the rule D425 registered and D426 measured, and it is unchanged.
- Acceptance checks declarations and counts. The records do not hold each decision's returns, so the decision arithmetic rests on the pinned, reviewed code and its tests.

**Written down so it cannot be adjusted later.** I expect both contrasts between 0 and +50, smaller than the self-play contrast (+57), with intervals near plus or minus 20. Positive and Inconclusive are about equally likely by my guess; I expect Negative to be rare.
- Reviewed by Codex before this entry was written (`.codex-reviews/d430-review.md`): the design is a fair test of the stated, narrow claim; the shared seeds and the per-droplet index slices do not bias the contrasts; neither the self-play pair nor a temperature arm is required for the claim as bounded here; its recount of D2 from the raw records and its check of the smoke's timings, the spend arithmetic and the commit hashes agree with the figures above. Its blocking corrections are applied: the one-look sentence now says what the runner writes by itself and what the operator does not open; the relaunch, replacement and budget rules are explicit; the acceptance list names the final-status, decision-count, kernel, completion and tool-hash checks and keeps D425's telemetry exclusion; the smoke's acceptance wrapper change is disclosed; D2's limits and Flat are qualified; the plan is hashed here before launch.

This rung is that control, and it also asks whether a plain continuation from chain 58 clears the gate.

**What was considered and not chosen.**
- **Chain 58's rung with lambda 0.97 first.** Chain 60's gate decides whether lambda 0.97 is adopted and cannot be read before chain 60 ends, which is when this rung starts. Under the present plan, with chain 58 the warm start, the control at 0.95 is useful under each reading of chain 60: if lambda 0.97 is adopted, a rung of chain 58 with lambda 0.97 would have chain 61 as its matched control (a third pair, at another parent); if it is not, later arms are at 0.95 and chain 61 would be their control. Holding the rig idle until chain 60's gate is read (about an hour) to choose between the two was the alternative, and under this plan both orders run chain 61. This can change: a selection that replaces chain 58 (for example chain 60 becoming a candidate and winning a registered comparison) or a failed or unread chain 61 would change which parent or control later work needs.
- **An entropy or exploration rung** (the lead in `docs/search-probe-2026-10-07/LOGIT_SCALE_NOTE.md`). A design study (`docs/plans/exploration-in-training-design-2026-10-07.md`) and its Codex review (`.codex-reviews/explore-design-review.md`) do not support running one now: the entropy knob has little or no gradient at the saturated decisions it would have to reopen (the review holds that "exactly zero" is too strong, and that deferring the rung is reasonable), a behaviour-policy change needs a new build, and the study's probe of END_TURN decisions, which is exploratory and prices outcomes with the policy's own critic, does not show that exploration is what limits activations. Off-rig tests come first. Such a rung would in any case need this control.

Chain 40 leaves the pool.

Declared, because it is not a one-factor step from chain 58's own training: chain 58 was trained with lambda 0.97 and this rung uses 0.95; the pool differs from chain 58's by the rotation (chain 49 becomes an active opponent, chain 40 leaves); the warm start is chain 58. - **Gate.** Mask harness `7d0d547` played without masks, seed block 23000000, decisive-Elo with 95% seed-cluster intervals, 3,200 naturally completed games per pair, 32 per worker, T=1, kick-off starts, both legs, no sampling offsets, plan sha256 committed and pushed before any shard is launched, accepted by `tools/gate_acceptance.py` and `accept_from_plan.py` before scoring. Nine pairs: (1) chain 61 against chain 58; (2) chain 61 and (3) chain 58, each against chain 37; (4) chain 61 and (5) chain 58, each against chain 46; (6) chain 61 and (7) chain 58, each against chain 59 (descriptive: a third opponent, nearer in strength, in neither training pool, a lineage relative chosen after its gate was read and so not an independent confirmatory holdout; pair 7 is also the first meeting of chain 58 and chain 59); (8) chain 61 against chain 49 (descriptive, in pool); (9) chain 61 against the offense bot. Positive: pair 1 above +40 with its interval entirely above zero, and both held-out contrasts (chain 61 minus chain 58, against chain 37 and against chain 46) entirely above zero. Flat: pair 1 within plus or minus 40 inclusive. Inconclusive: anything else. Unread: missing, unaccepted or integrity-invalid evidence; a trainer or integrity failure; a marker refused for any reason but the guard; a gate shard aborted on the 4,096-decision cap, with no rerun before a new entry.

**D435 - A LOWER-TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR THE SEARCH SEAT IS PRE-REGISTERED: CHAIN 55 + m1 AT TEMPERATURES 0.75, 0.5 AND 0.25, EACH AGAINST CHAIN 37 AND CHAIN 46 ON THE SEARCH GATE'S SEEDS, COMPARED WITH THE PLAIN CONTROL AND WITH THE SEARCH SEAT'S ACCEPTED GAMES; ONE LOOK; IT ADOPTS NOTHING (2026-10-08 02:53 PDT by the machine's clock at commit; no game of it has been played; it uses no rig time)**

**Why.** D434 read the search seat Positive against chain 37 and chain 46 (+45.5 [+28.3, +63.4] and +45.3 [+27.2, +64.5] decisive-Elo over the same checkpoint without it). D430 registered that a Positive is not a claim that search finds more than sharpening the policy would, and that a lower-temperature control at plain speed is registered and read before any further entry builds on search. This entry is that control. It costs about $1.40 and about two hours.

**What a lower temperature is here.** `play_harness/policy.py` `select_joint` divides every head's logits by T before masking and selection. That tempers each head's conditional distribution (type, then argument given type, then square given both). It is not the joint distribution raised to 1/T. Under m1 the mask is applied to the tempered distribution and renormalized. Three values are fixed here without a calibration run: 0.75 (mild; D400 used it for another purpose), 0.5 and 0.25. Strength need not vary monotonically with temperature, which is why there are three. Argmax is not an arm: the acceptance tools hold a gate to sample mode, and adding it would mean changing them again. That is a limit of the tooling, not an argument that argmax is uninteresting.

**The claim under test is narrow.** Whether the search seat at D430's setting beats per-head tempering at these three values, on chain 55 + m1, against these two opponents. It is not a test of sharpening in general (a schedule by decision type, tempering the type head alone, the joint tempered as a whole, argmax).

**Design.**
- **Players.** T075, T05, T025 = chain 55 (`f6ba3b44...`) + m1 at temperature 0.75, 0.5, 0.25. C = chain 55 + m1 at temperature 1, replayed. Opponents chain 37 (`268f1db0...`) and chain 46 (`8eee9ac1...`), plain, at temperature 1. No player searches.
- **Pairs.** Eight, 3,200 naturally completed games each, kick-off starts, both legs of every seed, one game per worker: T075, T05, T025 and C, each against chain 37 and against chain 46. 25,600 games.
- **Seeds: block 25100000, the search gate's, on purpose.** Sampling seeds are keyed by engine seed, side and episode, so C's replay must reproduce D430's C games exactly, and each temperature arm plays the seeds S played with the same sampling streams on both sides (common random numbers; once an action differs the games part and the streams no longer line up decision for decision). That gives a comparison of S with each temperature arm paired on seed without replaying S (about $14).
- **This is a follow-up on evidence that has been read, not an independent confirmation.** S's and C's results on these seeds are known (D434); the temperature arms' are not. On these seeds gain plus margin (below) is exactly the gate's S minus C, which is fixed at about +45. The gate was read Positive, so that figure is, on average, somewhat above its true value, and the bootstrap intervals do not correct for it: to the extent S was lucky here the margins are too high, and to the extent C was unlucky the gains are too high. There is no cheap correction. A fresh-seed replay of S large enough to matter costs about what the gate did, and is what a later entry would have to do if the reading below is close.
- **Statistics**, decisive-Elo with 95% seed-cluster intervals, `paired_contrasts.py` (sha256 `722ece95...`, unchanged; 2,000 replicates, generator seed 0), for each temperature arm T and each opponent:
  - **gain(T)** = T minus C, both from this run.
  - **margin(T)** = S minus T: S's games from D430's accepted records (`srch-gate-20261007/main/games.jsonl`, sha256 `b634d44b67110e1f96bb9a294f18f9038905b5cded124fe69cd277c832e8c536`), T's from this run. After acceptance `score_from_plan.py` checks that file's hash again, writes one record file per arm (this run's records plus the 6,400 records of the two S pairs, on this plan's seeds only) into its own sub-directory, and runs the same contrast script there. Six gains and six margins, each written to `gain_<arm>/<opponent>_contrast.json` or `margin_<arm>/<opponent>_contrast.json`.
- **Machines.** Four droplets `s-8vcpu-16gb-amd`, 8 workers, each playing 400 seeds of all eight pairs (6,400 games, about 100 to 125 minutes: D434's plain games took 7.5 seconds each with eight workers busy, and the smoke ran at 0.8 to 0.9 games a second with startup included), so no arm is tied to a machine. Time limit 4 hours each. All four are launched together if the account has four free slots; otherwise two and then two; with fewer than two free the launch waits. The plan and its hash do not change with the launch order.
- **One look.** As D430: the operator reads runner logs only (counts, rates, completion, cost, teardown) until every shard has finished and the merged run has passed acceptance. No early stop, no extension.

**Acceptance, before anything is scored** (plan file `PLAN.json` in the gate directory `tctl-gate-20261008`, sha256 `80dcbb558a1849c7ce1f33032df7b629a5602daab3a0e3f119f57958f6fed5ae`, copied to `docs/search-probe-2026-10-07/tctl/` with the scripts and `SCRIPTS.sha256`; committed and pushed before any droplet is created; the launcher and the scoring script refuse a plan that does not hash to the registered value, and each checks the gate's scripts, itself included, against the hashes in the plan; a script's check of itself is a guard against accidents only, and the committed copies are the record). Four checks, all required:
- `tools/gate_acceptance.py` at harness commit `5ab3ab6`: the eight pairs, their game counts, the seed block, both legs of every seed exactly once, one game per worker, the harness commit, each player's checkpoint hash, sample mode, natural endings, every integrity counter zero, and, new in `ad36a16` and `5ab3ab6`, each player's registered temperature in the manifest and on its own side of every game (0.75, 0.5, 0.25, and 1.0 for everyone else), with a registered checkpoint held to sampling. The change and its eleven tests were written by the operator on 2026-10-08; with a plan that registers no temperature the tool behaves as before.
- `accept_from_plan.py` (changed for this gate): masks, no sampling offset, no truncation, no mask fallback, final status, decision counts, the native kernel, `COMPLETE.json`, both harness acceptance tools at their registered hashes.
- `tools/search_acceptance.py` (unchanged): every record's seats are its pair's and leg's; each player's mode, temperature, masks and absent search setting in the manifest and on its side of every game. The droplet runner forwards the temperatures and does not itself verify them; these two tools do.
- **The replay check** (new, in `accept_from_plan.py`): all 6,400 games of C equal D430's C games on the same engine seed and leg in action trail hash, final digest, score, engine steps, both sides' decision counts, rosters, sampling seeds, turns, half and final status, and in their seats; D430's record file has the registered hash and its manifest the registered commit (`06f0a5f`); the compiled library of the merged run is D430's (`32632f03...`). Log-probability sums are not compared (a rounded float). If the replay differs anywhere the control is unread, and the difference is reported as a reproducibility discrepancy to be explained, not presumed to be an engine fault.
- The merge requires the same commit, settings, torch, Python and compiled library on every droplet.
- **Relaunch, as D430 fixed it:** only a droplet that dies, loses contact or reaches its time limit; its shard launched again whole, once, from the same plan (`--relaunch-suffix r`); at most two replacements in all, in the order the shards failed, and only if the spend so far plus every running droplet's limit plus the replacement's ($0.67) stays within the ceiling; the merged run uses a shard's original run if that completed, else its one replacement; a failed shard's partial records are never read. The scoring script takes the shard directories it is given, so this choice is kept by the operator and not enforced by the tool. **Unread, never a label:** missing, unaccepted or integrity-invalid evidence; an integrity abort or a decision-cap abort; a second failure of a shard or a third failed shard; a budget stop.

**Reading, on accepted evidence.** "Entirely above zero" means the interval's lower end is above 0; "entirely below zero" means its upper end is below 0; "inside -20 to +20" includes the ends. Each list is applied first match, in the order written.
1. **Search against the three temperatures** (the condition D430 set):
   - **A temperature is better:** for some arm, against at least one opponent, the margin's interval is entirely below zero. Nothing builds on this search setting; that temperature is carried to its own entry. (Six intervals are examined, so this can fire by chance more easily than one test would; it stops work and adopts nothing.)
   - **Search beats the three temperatures:** all six margins' intervals are entirely above zero. The condition D430 set is met for these arms: entries that build on search (a C rollout kernel, search as a teacher, a larger rollout budget) may be registered. Each still needs its own entry and its own gate. It is not a finding that sharpening in general cannot match search.
   - **Not separated:** anything else. Nothing builds on search until a new entry says how the two are to be separated (fresh seeds, more games, or another arm).
2. **Each temperature against C, descriptive.** D430's labels are printed for each arm's two gains: Negative (either gain's interval entirely below zero), Positive (both gains above +20 and both intervals entirely above zero), Flat (both intervals inside -20 to +20), Inconclusive (anything else). With three arms these labels are exploratory and adopt nothing. An arm that reads Positive is carried to a confirmation on a fresh seed block in its own entry before it can become a play-time option.
- No training recipe, warm start, play-time option or evaluation default changes under any outcome. Nothing here is a claim about another checkpoint.

**Registered diagnostics, not gates.** W / D / L, decisive-Elo and touchdown difference of the eight pairs; the D422 style table for T075, T05, T025 and C against each opponent. Mean log-probability per decision is in that table; it is the sharpness realised along each arm's own games, not a matched-state measurement.

**Spend.** Expected about $1.40 (four droplets for about two hours). Four droplets at the 4 hour limit are $2.67. Ceiling $4.50 for everything in this entry, including the smoke and two replacements. Droplets this entry creates are destroyed and the spend is reported.

**Smoke, not evidence.** Three runs at harness `5ab3ab6` on seed block 29910000 (the search gate's smoke block), with `srch-smoke-20261007` as the reference run.
- **Mac, 4 games a pair.** The stock, mask and search checks pass. The replay check passes on every field and refuses on the library hash (a Mac run records none), as it should. On a scratch copy with the hash written into the manifest by hand, the scoring path runs.
- **One droplet, 32 games a pair (256 games)**, launched from a hashed plan with this launcher. The 32 games the Mac had played (all eight pairs, two seeds, both legs) have the same action trails, digests, scores and decision counts on the droplet. Log-probability sums differ by up to 0.0012, which is why they are not in the replay check. This is the first Mac against droplet agreement run for temperatures other than 1 (D406 noted that none existed).

**D436 - AN OFF-RIG PROBE OF END_TURN DECISIONS IS PRE-REGISTERED: HOW EACH CHECKPOINT'S OWN CRITIC PRICES ONE MORE ACTIVATION AGAINST ENDING THE TURN, AND WHETHER THE REALISED SHAPED RETURN AGREES, ON CHAINS 49, 55, 58, 59 AND 60; IT ADOPTS NOTHING AND USES NO RIG TIME (2026-10-08 03:42 PDT by the machine's clock at commit; no game of it has been played)**

**Why.** The policy activates about three players a team turn where human play has about seven. The logit note of 2026-10-07 suggested that missing exploration at saturated decisions explains this. A design study and its Codex review (`docs/plans/exploration-in-training-design-2026-10-07.md`, section 8) left that open in both directions: an exploratory probe found that where chain 55 ends its turn, its own critic prices the most probable activation lower (-0.0117 [-0.0166, -0.0072], 120 roots), but that probe was small, had no plan, and cannot say why. D432 added that a seed change alone moves activations by +0.41 a team turn, so chain 58's style difference is not established as a lambda effect. The rung after chain 61 has to be chosen soon, and the candidates are objective-side arms. This probe is run to give that choice one more input.

**What is registered.** `docs/endturn-probe-2026-10-08/PLAN.md` and `PLAN.json`, sha256 `d6b829470bbd4eee3b78365b05c35f830de04a12edcba7ad8724d53fa1f0cbaa`, committed with this entry before any game. In short: 200 plain self-play games per checkpoint on engine seeds 29960000 to 29960199 (unused), harness `06f0a5f`, checkpoints by hash (chain 55 `f6ba3b44...`, chain 58 `a03ed608...`, chain 59 `73461254...`, chain 49 `a2d1d10d...`, chain 60 `da9a538f...`); at the decisions where the checkpoint played END_TURN with an activation legal, 64 paired rollouts of END_TURN against the three most probable activations, scored by the shaped reward to the end of the team turn plus the checkpoint's own critic (E1); a forced arm that allows exactly one more activation (E2); and a match arm that plays END_TURN and the first alternative to the end of the match and records the realised shaped return, the 28 reward components and the score. Intervals resample games. The reading rules (plan sections 5 and 8) are numeric conditions evaluated and printed by the analysis script. One look, after every accepted shard is in.

**What it can and cannot say.** It measures the critic's pricing and, in the match arm, whether the shaped return that followed agrees with it. It cannot show that ending the turn is right or wrong by match result, it cannot say whether the reward or the fitting of the critic causes a gap, it says nothing about exploration, and it is not an estimate of a lambda effect: each lambda has two training seeds at most. Its outcome is a pointer (a reward arm on the block and rush charges, lambda 0.97, gamma 0.9995, or none) and adopts nothing; the plan gives the outcome table, with lambda before gamma when both conditions hold. An effect on the match result of the size the m1 mask implies for one activation is below what the match arm can detect.

**Departures from unmodified harness code, disclosed.** The engine library is the pinned `bbplay.c` compiled together with three read-only accessors for the env's reward components (`endturn_shim.c`), and two hooks run in the probe's own process (the forced rule and the component capture). Every game checks that with the hooks idle the probe returns exactly what `Rollouts.evaluate` returns, and that the components sum to the reward. Those checks do not exercise the hooks while active and cannot show that the env attributes rewards correctly.

**Chain 60 is in the plan.** Its stage ended at 03:20 PDT and its exam passed at 03:28 (checkpoint `da9a538fb8b944efc2a37e10b7b50ea7b4df022bbfcabc7f4a183ac3f04134d2`, equal to the rung's completion marker; lineage file `2059bba1...`). `make_plan.py --with-chain60` changed `PLAN.json` only (the checkpoint and its shard), and the hash line of `PLAN.md`; no tool file changed.

The account has 9 of its 15 droplets in use (four are D435's temperature control, which ends at about 05:05), and chain 60's gate needs two free. So four shards (chains 58, 55, 59, 60) are launched now and chain 49's is launched under the same run name when the temperature control's droplets are gone. A shard is one checkpoint on its own droplet with its own seeds, so the launch time enters no estimate. The analysis is still run once, after all five shards are accepted.

**Cost and exposure.** One droplet per checkpoint; about 1.9 hours and $0.32 each by an estimate not measured at full size, about $1.60 in all; `--max-hours 3.5`. A dead runner, a lost create or a failed delete can leave a droplet billing until it is destroyed by hand; the cleanup commands are written before anything is created, and the scheduled check-ins list the account's tagged droplets.

**D437 - THE END_TURN PROBE'S FIRST LAUNCH (D436) IS UNREAD: ITS OWN FAIL-FAST CHECK STOPPED TWO SHARDS ON A CASE THE DESIGN DID NOT FORESEE (A KICK-OFF BLITZ TURN), AND THE OTHER TWO WERE STOPPED BY THE OPERATOR; NOTHING WAS ANALYSED; A CORRECTED PLAN NEEDS ITS OWN ENTRY (2026-10-08 03:58 PDT by the machine's clock at commit; chain 61 is training; chain 60's gate has not been played)**

**What happened.** Run `et1`, run id `472b85`, plan `d6b82947...`, four shards launched at 03:42 PDT (chains 58, 55, 59, 60; chain 49's was to follow).
- Chain 58's shard stopped at 03:46 after about a minute of play, and chain 59's at 03:51 after 13 games, each on the same registered integrity check: "forced arm: the rule ended a turn 2 times in one rollout" (engine seed 29960001 at step 26, and engine seed 29960027 at step 32). Both runners fetched the failure logs only and destroyed their droplets.
- The failure is deterministic. On the Mac, `endturn_probe.py run` with the registered settings on seeds 29960000 and 29960001 of chain 58 stops on the same message at the same step.
- The operator then interrupted the launcher (SIGINT to its process, 03:54), which stopped the chain 55 and chain 60 shards at 14 and 13 games. A rerun of any shard under this plan would stop on the same seeds, any fix changes a hash-bound tool and so the plan, and shards of two plans cannot be analysed together; the two live shards could no longer contribute to a reading.
- All four droplets and keys are gone (HTTP 404 on each in the runner logs; the status listing afterwards shows only D435's four). Spend $0.109 by the runners' cost lines. No record of any shard was fetched, and the analysis was not run.

**The cause, from a diagnostic run on the Mac** (the registered tool with a wrapper that prints the failing root's state; scratch output, not kept as evidence). At the failing root the half is 1, both teams' turn counters and completed-turn counters are 0, the searcher's team is both the kicking team and the active team, and the engine is inside its kick-off procedure. That is the kicking team's free turn from a Blitz kick-off result. Ending it does not advance the engine's completed-turn counter, which is what the harness's rollout uses to detect the end of the searcher's team turn (`play_harness/search.py`, `turns_completed`). So a rollout from such a root runs on through the receiving team's turn into the kicking team's first real turn, where the forced rule ends a turn a second time.
- This is a flaw in the probe's design, not an engine fault and not a fault of the check: the plan defines the turn arm and the forced arm by "the end of the searcher's team turn", and at a root inside a Blitz turn the harness's horizon is the end of the next real turn. The fail-fast check exists to catch a forced rule that fires more than once, and it did.
- The same horizon applies to the search seat of D430 and D434 at decisions inside a Blitz turn: its rollouts there run to the end of the next real turn. That is the registered behaviour of that seat (it stops where the completed-turn counter advances) and changes nothing in those readings; it is noted here because it was not written down before.
- Neither smoke caught it: the Mac rehearsals and the droplet smoke played two games each, and a Blitz turn with an END_TURN root did not occur in them.

**What the operator saw of registered seeds.** The diagnostic played chain 58's games on engine seeds 29960000 and 29960001 on the Mac. The operator read the worker's completion line of an earlier single-game run (a different game: its sampling differs with the game index) and the failing root's state and action trail header. No return, margin or count from any root was read.

**Status and next step.** The probe is unread and D436's reading rules have been applied to nothing. A corrected plan is a new entry: the tool must say what a root inside a Blitz turn is (the operator's proposal is that such a decision is not a root for any arm, since no horizon the plan names applies to it), with a test that reproduces seed 29960001, a new plan hash, a Codex review of the change, and the registered seed block reused only if the entry argues why that is sound (no result of it has been seen). It is not started in this entry. The rung after chain 61 is registered from chain 60's gate without the probe unless the corrected probe is read first.

**D439 - THE END_TURN PROBE IS PRE-REGISTERED AGAIN WITH ONE CHANGE: A DECISION INSIDE A KICK-OFF BLITZ TURN IS NOT A ROOT; NEW SEED BLOCK 29970000; EVERYTHING ELSE AS D436 (2026-10-08 04:14 PDT by the machine's clock at commit; no game of it has been played; it uses no rig time)**

**Why.** D436's launch is unread (D437): the probe's fail-fast check stopped two shards at END_TURN decisions inside the kicking team's free turn from a Blitz kick-off result, where ending the turn does not advance the completed-turn counter the rollout core stops on. **What changed.**
- **The root rule** (`endturn_probe.py`, `in_kickoff_turn`): a decision made while a kick-off frame is on the engine's procedure stack is left out of every class, before the class's count and its reservoir. Each game record counts the decisions left out per class (`kickoff_turn_decisions`). The estimands are therefore about decisions in ordinary team turns. One exception: the style rates the analysis prints per own team turn are whole-game rates and still include a Blitz turn's decisions. The match-end horizon would apply at such a decision; it is left out of every class so that all arms share one scope. This is the only change to a hash-bound tool; the forced-arm check, the acceptance, the analysis, the launcher and the shim are byte for byte as in D436.
- **The seed block** is 29970000 to 29970199 (unused). The first launch's block, 29960000 to 29960199, is retired: the operator has seen per-game decision counts and two failing roots' states on three of its games (no return, margin or critic value), and a fresh block costs nothing.

- **Registered descriptive addition:** the number of decisions left out per class and checkpoint is reported with the reading. The unchanged analysis and acceptance tools neither print nor validate the new field, so the operator tallies it separately from the accepted game records. It enters no rule.

**How much the rule removes.** In two 60-game runs on the Mac at 4 rollouts, on seeds outside both blocks: chain 58, 6 of 585 END_TURN decisions and 12 of 2,992 ACTIVATE decisions; chain 49, none of 579 and 47 of 2,789. Both complete, each leaves out one END_TURN decision, neither has a root at the step that failed, and the forced rule fires at most once on every root. **What this does and does not show.**

The reading rule is applied as registered and the permission to register work on search stands. What does not stand without that replay is any claim that rests on search being better than temperature 0.5 in particular; an entry that needs that claim has to bring the replay.

**What this says.**
- At the decisions where it ends its turn, each of the five checkpoints' own critics prices the most probable further activation below ending, by about 0.008 to 0.011, and that is the price of one activation.
- Played out to the end of the match, the shaped return does not establish a negative margin: all five realised-margin intervals span zero (they reach from -0.013 to +0.011). For chains 55, 58, 59 and 60 the critic's margin is below the realised one by about 0.01 (pointwise intervals). So for those four the critic prices one more activation, relative to ending, lower than the shaped return that followed. Whether that is the critic's fit or something the reward does later is not separated by this probe.
- The reward does charge an activation through the block and rush terms and pay it through the block exposure term, and the block pay's point estimate exceeds the magnitude of the charges in every checkpoint (about +0.009 against -0.004 at the match end). These are differences in components summed along the trajectories, not necessarily payment for the activation itself, and no registered interval tests their net.
- Nothing separates lambda 0.97 from lambda 0.95 beyond the seed gap in the margin itself. The critic's part of the margin is smaller in magnitude in both lambda 0.97 checkpoints than in their controls.

**What it does not say** (plan section 8, last paragraph, and D436). That ending the turn is right or wrong by match result: an effect of the size m1 implies is below what the match arm can detect, and its intervals are about plus or minus 0.01 touchdowns. Anything about exploration. A lambda effect. Which of reward and critic fitting causes the gap. What training at another gamma, lambda or reward would do. Anything about decisions inside a kick-off Blitz turn, which are left out. All intervals cover evaluation seeds on self-play games of one checkpoint each, not training seeds.

**Consequences.** None is adopted and no arm is pointed at. The rung after chain 62 is chosen without a pointer from this probe. The observation that the critic under-prices one more activation relative to the realised shaped return at four of five checkpoints is a lead for a later entry and nothing more: it diagnoses no cause and authorises no training change. A test that could separate the critic's fit from the reward would have to hold the actor and shared features, the reward, the root states and the continuation policy fixed and refit only the critic, judged on held-out roots; refitting a critic and probing newly sampled roots would not separate them. That test is not designed here.
