**D444 - SEARCH DISTILLATION, TEST 1, IS PRE-REGISTERED (ENTRY A): LABEL 10,000 SELF-PLAY GAMES OF CHAIN 55 + m1 WITH THE SEARCH SEAT'S OWN CHOICE AT SAMPLED DECISIONS, FINE-TUNE ONLY THE POLICY ROWS OF THE OUTPUT LAYER TOWARD THOSE LABELS AT THREE STRENGTHS, AND DECIDE BY A BATCHED PLAIN-SPEED GATE AGAINST CHAIN 37 AND CHAIN 46; THE REGISTERED ARM IS LAMBDA 4, NAMED HERE; IT CHANGES NO DEFAULT (2026-10-08 10:46 PDT by the machine's clock at commit; no registered game has been played; it uses no rig time)**

**Why.** D434 read the search seat Positive against held-out opponents (+45.5 and +45.3 decisive-Elo over chain 55 + m1 without it, at 48 times the cost). D442 read its lower-temperature control "search beats the three temperatures", which D430 had set as the condition for entries that build on search. This is the first such entry: can the cheapest possible student absorb what the search does, so that the gain is had at plain speed? It is also the cheapest test of "search as a teacher" before anything is tried on the rig.

**The plan is `docs/search-distill-2026-10-08/PLAN.md` (version 3, the narrow first slice) and is part of this entry.** Its hash-bound form is `docs/search-distill-2026-10-08/PLAN.json`, sha256 `7833952041c0d3b9e98bf42471408d0552e4fe9a04d90c13c700ad16cf8dae00`. Every tool refuses a plan that does not hash to the value handed to it and refuses when a tool file is not the one the plan names. Committed and pushed before any registered droplet is created. In brief:
- **Labels.** Chain 55 (`f6ba3b44...`) plays itself under m1 at temperature 1, engine seeds 26000000 to 26009999. At 15 sampled decisions per class per game in the seat's scope (30 roots a game) the label tool runs the seat's own computation (the same candidates, seeds, rollouts and rule, through the harness's own functions at `5ab3ab6`) and stores what the seat would play. A root where the seat deviates is a label (about 1.3% to 1.5% of roots, so about 4,000 to 4,400). Each label is judged on 128 fresh rollout pairs. 64 other decisions a game are sampled for the preservation term. Split by game: 70% train, 10% validation, 10% test, 10% reserve.
- **The student, recipe R1.** Only `decoder.decoder.weight` (the 454 policy rows of the output layer, 232,448 weights) is trained. The trunk and the critic stay chain 55's byte for byte. Loss: lambda times a cross-entropy toward the label at deviation roots, plus a KL to the original policy at every other loss decision, on the exact joint distribution. Three arms: lambda 1, 4 and 16, 2,400 Adam steps each, no stop rule.
- **Reading 1, the fit check.** The lambda 16 arm's weighted mean probability of the label on training deviation roots, from float32 logits as the harness computes them: FIT at 0.80 or more; NOT FIT stops the plan; Unread when the shards or the dataset are not accepted, that arm was not trained, its blob fails acceptance, or its fit value is not a finite number; read after milestone 1 (1,000 games, by `fit`, which writes no selection file) and again after milestone 2 (all 10,000, by `select`).
- **The registered arm is lambda 4 (`c55d1l4`), named here.** Version 2 as first written chose the arm by a no-rollout score J on validation games. On the Mac runs J was below zero for every arm and chose the smallest dose: at the sizes measured its first term cannot exceed about 0.0004 while its penalty was 0.0009 to 0.0015, so at sizes like these it picks the smallest dose whatever the arms do. The tools' author and the outside reviewer both recommended a named middle dose. J is still printed and decides nothing. This choice was made after seeing two Mac rehearsals' gate rehearsals (32 and 16 seeds a pair, eleven of twelve point estimates below zero, lambda 1 the least negative); they are not evidence and they did not favour lambda 4.
- **Held-out numbers** (label probability and change at other decisions on the test games) are reported for all three arms with no threshold.
- **Reading 2, the gate.** F1, F4, F16 and C (chain 55 + m1), each against chain 37 and chain 46, 12,800 naturally completed games a pair, seed block 25200000, 32 games per worker on four droplets, one look. For the registered arm, its two contrasts against C (decisive-Elo, 95% seed-cluster intervals, `paired_contrasts.py` `722ece95...`), first match: Unread; Negative (either interval entirely below zero); Positive (both point estimates at +15 or more and both intervals entirely above zero); Flat (both intervals inside -15 to +15); Inconclusive. The other two arms are a descriptive dose-response and carry no label. The gate's own plan hash, the three arms' blob and sidecar hashes and the selection file's hash are fixed in Entry B before any gate game.
- **Consequences** are PLAN.md section 5's table, each restricted to R1 at this label count. No default changes under any outcome: no training recipe, warm start, play-time default or evaluation default. The entry does register consequences: a Negative closes R1 at this label count; a Positive permits the next larger design, and a proposal of the registered arm as a play-time option, each in its own entry; a dose-response arm with both contrasts above zero may be carried to a confirmation on fresh seeds in its own entry. An arm is not eligible ancestry for training (the trainer's lineage tool refuses its sidecar, by design).
- **Stops.** Reading 1 Unread or NOT FIT; any arm's blob failing acceptance at the selection; a completed label shard whose records acceptance rejects; a label stage or a gate that cannot be completed within its two replacements (a replacement is only for a droplet that dies, loses contact or reaches its limit, or a refused launch: the shard whole, from the same plan and seeds); the gate unaccepted; the rate stop (T is the mean `wall_seconds` of the two accepted milestone 1 shards; if (3 x T + 240) / 3600 is above 6.0 hours milestone 2 is not launched as written). Each stops the plan until a new entry. A refusal of the gate's scorer (its scripts or the harness worktree not the registered ones, or a shard's manifest not there yet) is not a reading: no record of the run has been read, and the scorer is run again. A failure of the scorer after its acceptance lines have printed is not a refusal: the look has happened, the scorer is rerun on the same merged run with the same scripts and its reading stands, and if that cannot be done without changing a hash-bound script the gate is Unread with every printed number reported.

It is an allocation, not a ceiling any tool enforces, and teardown exposure is outside it. **Limits, disclosed** (PLAN.md section 10 in full). One recipe, one label count, one teacher setting, one checkpoint. **Written down so it cannot be adjusted later.**
- **Reading 1.** FIT at milestone 1: about two chances in three (the Mac runs fitted 0.93 at milestone 0 and 0.82 at the rehearsal, on 64 and 110 training labels, with each label visited hundreds of times; at milestone 1 each is visited about 270 times). FIT at milestone 2, given FIT at 1: about three in five (each label is visited about 30 times there, and there are ten times as many preservation examples for the same weights). A NOT FIT would say more about the step budget than about the recipe, and the entry that follows would have to say so.
- **Held-out, lambda 4, at the full label count.** Label probability between 0.03 and 0.12 over all test labels (the original gives them about 0.01 to 0.02). The top action changed at 3% to 8% of held-out screened roots (the Mac runs showed 10% to 12% with a tenth of the data or less).
- **The gate.** Both of the registered arm's contrasts between -30 and +10. Reading: Negative about 45%, Inconclusive about 30%, Flat about 15%, Positive about 10%. Dose-response: more negative the larger lambda.

**Why this rung.** Chain 62 is the last stage in the plan and should end at about 20:40 PDT. Its gate cannot be read before then, and D441 allows nothing to be launched from chain 60, chain 61 or chain 62 before a registered selection among the warm-start candidates, which needs chain 62's gate. So a stage that follows chain 62 without a gap starts from chain 58, the warm start, and is chosen before chain 62 is read. Leaving the rig idle until chain 62's gate is read and a selection is made was the alternative; it was not chosen. This rung is a precommitted experimental arm beside the adopted recipe, not a rung of it, and it runs whatever chain 62 reads. From chain 58 there are now two continuations on the same pool, seed and build that differ in GAE lambda alone: chain 61 at 0.95 (read Flat, D447) and chain 62 at 0.97 (training). A third at a higher value makes a three-point dose-response of the only factor that has read Positive on this ladder (D428 and D440: +44.5 and +40.07 for 0.97 over 0.95, both from chain 49). It is one-factor against chain 62, it needs no new build and no new pool, and whatever it reads it says whether more of the same change is worth having before the next generation's recipe is fixed.

**Why 0.99.** With gamma 0.999 the advantage estimator's weights decay by gamma times lambda a step, so the geometric horizon 1 / (1 - gamma x lambda), which is not a guaranteed length of credit, is about 20 steps at 0.95, 0.97 about 32, 0.98 about 48, 0.99 about 91. The step from 0.95 to 0.97 multiplied the horizon by 1.65. 0.98 would repeat a step of that size (1.47); 0.99 nearly triples it. The larger step is chosen because a rung costs about nine hours and one look: if the response is still rising, a larger step shows it more clearly; if 0.99 is worse than 0.97 on this comparison, an arm at 0.98 is the natural next question (one comparison does not locate an optimum); a step to 0.98 that read Flat would say little either way. The risk is the usual one for a long horizon, noisier targets. The stage's own guards stop a collapse: a clean trip of the chain 30 drift guard reads Negative, and a stop by the live integrity guard is unread, as the label rule below says.

No fine-tune was run and no fit value exists. The log is `results/m1-drift/dataset-m1.registered.log`. PLAN.md section 5's table says of this case: "Nothing is concluded. A new entry decides whether the stage is rerun." This is that entry.

**What was measured afterwards** (`results/m1-drift/`: `diag_logp.py`, `x86_replay_droplet.py`, `SUMMARY.json`). The diagnostic recomputes the registered comparison at every screened root of the 900 games that are not in the reserve group and records the differences. It writes no dataset. It parses the shards' records whole (shard acceptance does) and keeps, of a root, the step, a0, a0's recorded log-probability, the recorded candidates, support, class and flags; it keeps and prints nothing of a label, a gain or a judgment. Like the registered tool's own check it covers the roots of the test games (3,000 of the 27,000). The recorded log-probability is finite at all 27,000 roots and there are no cap rejections, so 27,000 roots are compared throughout.
- **On the Mac, 32 games per forward (the registered tool's arithmetic):** 1 root differs by more than 1e-3 (the one above, 1.138e-3, in a training game), 4 by more than 3e-4, 56 by more than 1e-4, 1,018 by more than 1e-5; the median is 2.9e-12; none exceeds 2e-3. The recomputed candidate list is the recorded one, in the recorded order, at all 27,000.
- **On the Mac, one game per forward against 32** (18 games, 540 roots: the ten games with the largest differences and games 0 to 7): the two differ from each other by up to 4.0e-4, and one game per forward differs from the droplets' record by up to 9.5e-4.
- **On a third droplet** (same size, image, torch and engine library as the two label droplets; created for this and destroyed, verified gone, $0.048): **with one game per forward, as the label tool runs the seat, all 27,000 recomputed values agree with the record to 2.2e-7** (none over 1e-6; the largest per shard is 2.18e-7 and 2.11e-7). On the same droplet with 32 games per forward they differ by up to 5.8e-4 (26 over 1e-4, none over 1e-3). The candidate lists are the recorded ones at all 27,000 either way. At game 162 step 929 the record is -2.288351059, the droplet at one game per forward gives -2.288351131, the droplet at 32 games per forward -2.288076914, and the Mac at 32 games per forward -2.287213188.
- **What this establishes and what it does not.** A machine that was not a label machine, replaying the recorded trails from the engine seed and running the original network one game per forward, recomputes every recorded log-probability within 2.2e-7 in absolute value (a residue consistent with the sampler's float32 arithmetic against the enumeration's float64 and the record's nine decimals; it was not decomposed). So the records are what the code computes on that kind of machine at one game per forward. The difference depends on the batching and on the machine and runtime: the same droplet differs by up to 5.8e-4 from batching alone, and the Mac at 32 games per forward by up to 1.14e-3 (processor, operating system, torch build and numerical libraries were not separated). It does not show by an independent route what the label droplets' processes held in memory; a fault there would have had to leave values that a third machine reproduces within 2.2e-7 at all 27,000 roots. One number per root is compared: this does not establish equal hidden states, equal logits, values or rollout judgments. No float64 reference was run (the harness's forward is float32 throughout).
- The 16-game droplet smoke (D444) had replayed on the Mac with a largest difference of 1.2e-4 over 480 roots (NOTES.md section 00); with 56 times as many roots the tail passed the limit. What is established: the registered build's default arithmetic (32 games per forward, on the Mac) is not the label tool's (one game per forward, on a droplet), and on this corpus it failed the registered check.

**What changes: where and how the registered build runs. What does not: any acceptance rule.**
- **The dataset is built on a droplet of the label stage's size and image, one game per forward, by the registered build function with its registered rule.** `docs/search-distill-2026-10-08/distill_dataset_b1.py` (sha256 `4be1369b4140390427dc97b0bf2efb7bebb1e3a135790e9f5a313b0dbe927ef5`) calls the registered `distill_dataset.build` unchanged: shard acceptance, replay to digest, score and observation hashes, supports and classes rebuilt from the replayed engine, the candidate rule, and the 1e-3 agreement of a0's log-probability at every root. It replaces only how the network is run over a game's observation rows: each game alone, the registered `Features.run` on a batch of one, which is what the registered tool's own option `--batch-games 1` computes, in worker processes so that the full plan takes hours. `distill_dataset_droplet.py` (sha256 `a89bc24cdbd5d09b4d9d8a99a8cf50e999fb351e682ba8536ff96c07b55ed7ec`) accepts the shards locally, runs that tool on one droplet with the label launcher's lifecycle calls, and fetches `DATASET.json`, `BUILD_B1.json` and the three split files into `OUT.partial`. **Nothing appears at the output directory until everything has succeeded:** only after the build exited 0, every split file has the hash `DATASET.json` records (no file is deserialised), `DATASET.json` names the plan and one engine library for the build, the shards and the droplet, and the cleanup is verified (the droplet gone, the lifecycle's teardown reporting clean, no ssh key of the run left listed), is `droplet_build.json` written and `OUT.partial` renamed to the output directory. The stage commands hand the downstream tools the output directory and nothing else, so a run that fails earlier leaves them nothing. The readers themselves take whatever directory they are given: that `OUT.partial`, `OUT.failedN` and `OUT.refused` are never given to them is the operator's procedure, not something the readers enforce. The teardown is attempted on every exit path the process survives; as with the label launcher, a killed process, a create whose answer is lost or a failed delete can leave a droplet billing, and the message printed then names the recorded id and the command.
- **No plan-bound file changes.** `PLAN.json` still hashes to `78339520...`; the six tool files are the registered ones; the two accepted shards stay valid; milestone 2's label command is the registered one.
- **Consequences worth stating.** The stored features, and the original policy's probabilities computed from the logits (raw logits are not stored), are then the droplet's one-game-per-forward values, not the Mac's 32-games-per-forward values the plan would have stored; the fine-tune and the evaluation read them as registered. This can move Reading 1's value, the fitted weights and so Reading 2; the thresholds, the named arm and the evaluation rules are untouched. `DATASET.json`'s `batch_games` field will say 32: under this tool it counts the games replayed between two rounds of forwards, and `BUILD_B1.json` beside it says one game per forward. Neither the new tool's hash nor `BUILD_B1.json` is bound into the fine-tune's or the selection's records, which bind the dataset's file hashes as before: that this tool built the dataset is recorded in `BUILD_B1.json`, `droplet_build.json` and this ledger, and is the operator's procedure.
- **Tests** (`results/d445-tests/`). `test_dataset_b1.py`, 6 of 6: on two dev shards the tool's three split files equal, byte for byte, those of the registered `distill_dataset.py --batch-games 1`, and its `DATASET.json` differs only in `seconds` and `batch_games`; a copy with one root's recorded log-probability 0.002 off and a copy with a recorded candidate replaced by another action of the support are each refused by both tools with the registered message, and no split is written. `test_dataset_droplet.py`, 32 of 32, with stand-ins for the lifecycle module and the remote while the script's own `claim_out`, `attempt`, `build_on_droplet`, `classify`, `collect` and `accept_shards` run for real, and `main()` with the preflight replaced (the preflight itself is not run, the setup and shim-build scripts are empty strings, the launcher's reconcile is a stand-in, no real signal is sent and no process is killed: a killed runner is represented by the directory it would leave): published only after the teardown; a teardown that raises after a complete fetch, a teardown that returns without verifying the cleanup, an ssh key of the run still listed, a rename that fails after a clean teardown, a result that cannot be written, an interruption, a fetch that fails after two splits arrived, a split whose bytes do not hash, and a build that exits non-zero without a registered check's message each publish nothing and exit 1; a failed attempt that cannot be moved aside stays as `OUT.partial` and is counted at the next start; a report stream that cannot be written does not change a publication; a registered check's refusal, another plan and another engine library each exit 3 and are kept as `OUT.refused`, after which the script will not start for that directory; a refusal followed by a failed teardown is still a refusal, and so is a refusal whose marker cannot be written (kept from the process's own record); a runner killed after it recorded a refusal, or after the build's log was fetched and before the marker, is kept as a refusal at the next start, and one killed without a refusal is counted as a failed attempt; the refusal marks count only at the start of a log line; local shard problems and an unreadable shard file are both refusals (tested with the acceptance function replaced, not with a real unreadable shard); `OUT.partial` is made in one step or nothing is made; `main()` exits 3 for a refusal before anything is created, 2 for every other stop before `OUT.partial` exists, and 1 for an interruption just after it is made; three failed attempts and the script will not start a fourth; a failed attempt followed by a whole replacement publishes. Not tested before the registered run: the script against a real droplet end to end (its lifecycle calls are the ones the label launcher makes, exercised by the label smoke, the two label shards and the diagnostic droplet above).
- **The stage commands.** In PLAN.md section 8 the two `distill_dataset.py` lines become, with the plan's shorthand:
  - milestone 1: `python $D/distill_dataset_droplet.py --harness-export $X --plan $D/PLAN.json --expect-sha256 $H --shard-dir m1-s1=$R/m1-s1 --shard-dir m1-s2=$R/m1-s2 --out-dir $R/dataset-m1 --max-hours 1.5`
  - milestone 2: the same with all eight `--shard-dir` arguments, `--out-dir $R/dataset --max-hours 7`.
  Every other command is literal. Expected: about half an hour and $0.10 at milestone 1, three to four hours and about $0.70 at milestone 2 (one process replays, seven run forwards). The time limits bound the work (the teardown follows them) and are not dollar caps: at the limits one attempt is $0.25 and $1.17 of droplet time, and three attempts at each milestone would be $4.26. That is not in D444's $14 worst case, so the allocation becomes $18.50; it is the operator's to manage, as before, and as in D444 the time a teardown takes, and a droplet left billing by a killed runner or a failed delete until it is destroyed by hand, lie outside it.

**The dataset build's outcomes.** Two things are kept apart: the state of a milestone's output directory, which is what the plan reads, and what one run of the script reports.

*The state of a milestone's output directory, in this order of precedence.*
1. **Refused: `OUT.refused` exists, or a leftover `OUT.partial` holds the refusal's marker or a fetched build log with a refusal line. The dataset is not accepted, Reading 1 is Unread, and the plan stops until a new entry.** A registered check of the dataset refused. On the droplet that is a line of the build's log that starts with one of the registered tools' own messages: `distill_common.IntegrityError:` (the replay to digest, score and observation hashes, a support, a class, the candidate rule, the 1e-3 agreement), `not accepted, nothing built` (shard acceptance) or `a game appears in two shards`. It is also a fetched `DATASET.json` that names another plan or another engine library. The build's log is fetched into `OUT.partial` before it is read; then the marker is written, `DATASET-REFUSED` is printed, and the attempt is kept as `OUT.refused`, by this process or, if it dies, by the next start. **What the next start can recover is what is in `OUT.partial`: the marker, or a refusal line in the fetched build log, even an incomplete one.** It cannot recover a refusal that exists only in the run's log (the poll prints the last line of the droplet's log before the log is fetched), nor, for the two refusals that come from the fetched `DATASET.json` (another plan, another library), one whose process was killed between that check and the marker: such a leftover is archived as a failed attempt. So the operator reads the run's log of a failed attempt before any replacement, and a refusal line there stands whatever is on disk. While a refusal stands the script begins no attempt for that directory. Nothing is widened, no record is dropped, the forward is not rebatched and the build is not run again under this entry. A refusal and a publication cannot both exist, because the script begins no attempt once either does.
2. **Published: otherwise, the output directory exists and holds `droplet_build.json`** (written into `OUT.partial` before the one rename that makes the output directory). The dataset is accepted and the stage goes on. Failed attempts that came before it stay beside it as `OUT.failedN` and change nothing.
3. **Open: otherwise.** `OUT.failedN`, and a leftover `OUT.partial` without the marker, are the failed attempts so far. An attempt begins when `OUT.partial` is made, one `mkdir`, the last thing the script does before the droplet's lifecycle starts; so a failure between that and the droplet's creation uses an attempt although no droplet existed. Whatever stops an attempt and is not a refusal leaves it a failed attempt: setup, an upload, the shim build, a worker's start or crash or any other failure of the build process, a build that stops on a provenance message (another harness commit, another checkpoint; these repeat and use up the attempts), a lost connection, the time limit, a fetch that fails, a transferred file whose bytes do not hash, a cleanup that is not verified after a complete and checked fetch, a signal, a failure to write the result or to rename, a killed process. An attempt is whole: no file of a failed attempt is published or reused. The whole build may be run again from the same command, **at most two replacements per milestone**: with three failed attempts the script begins no other, and the plan stops until a new entry. A failure that hides a refusal (the connection is lost before the log is read) is a failed attempt; the replacement runs the same deterministic checks.

*What one run reports.* Exit 0: it published. Exit 3: it observed a refusal as above, **or the shards failed acceptance on the Mac before anything was created** (problems returned, or a shard file that cannot be read or parsed; no marker, since nothing ran; it repeats on the same directories), which is the same reading: Unread, and the plan stops until a new entry, which is also where a mistyped directory would be put right. Exit 1: its attempt failed. Exit 2: it began no attempt and no `OUT.partial` exists (the arguments, the plan or a tool file not the registered one, the export or the checkpoint, an output directory already published, a standing refusal, three failed attempts, the account's droplet limit, an interruption before `OUT.partial`); a run that stops before the droplet's lifecycle while an `OUT.partial` exists, its own or an earlier run's, exits 1, because an attempt exists and has not published; for the droplet limit it is run again when slots are free, and nothing is deleted to make room.

*Operator's procedure, not enforced by the script.* After a cleanup that was not verified, or a killed runner, the droplet is destroyed by its recorded id and verified gone before the script is run again (a new attempt has a new name). `OUT.partial`, `OUT.failedN` and `OUT.refused` are never handed to a downstream tool.

*Not handled.* A filesystem on the Mac that cannot be written (a full disk, a permission): the directories above can then be wrong. In that case too the run's log decides: a refusal line there is a refusal whatever is on disk. Signals are ignored from the start of the teardown to the end of the script, publication included. A replacement can never depend on a fit or gate value: no fine-tune is run before a milestone's dataset is published, and once it is published the script begins no other attempt.

**Disclosed.** This choice was made after the refusal and after the measurements above, and before any registered dataset, fine-tune or fit value existed (dev and rehearsal datasets from before D444 exist; they are not this plan's). A first draft of this entry kept the build on the Mac and loosened the agreement rule (1e-3 at all but 1 root in 1,000, 0.05 at every root); the outside review blocked it (the cause was not established, and the looser constant also widened the registered candidate rule in the second pass), the x86 replay was run in answer, and that draft and its tool were discarded. The diagnostic script was given a `--slice` option between the Mac run and the droplet run; nothing else in it changed.

**What this entry does not change.** The plan hash, every plan-bound tool, the accepted shards, the label seeds, the split, the three arms, the fit threshold (0.80 on the lambda 16 arm), the registered arm (lambda 4), the selection, the held-out look, the gate and its readings, D444's stops (this entry adds the dataset build's outcomes above and changes none of them), the label relaunch rule, and the label stage's dollar guards. The allocation is raised as stated above. It changes no default.

**What happens next, in order.** (1) The milestone 1 dataset by the command above. (2) `distill_finetune.py` and `distill_eval.py fit` as registered: Reading 1 at milestone 1. NOT FIT or Unread stops the plan. (3) If FIT, milestone 2's labels by the registered command (six shards, `--max-hours 7 --max-total-usd 7.10`; if six droplets are not free at once the launcher is run again with the remaining shard names, as registered), then the dataset over all eight shards by the command above.

**Spend so far on D444.** Smokes $0.10, milestone 1 labels $0.50, the diagnostic droplet $0.05.

**Review.** Outside review (Codex, `gpt-6.1-sol`, read-only): the first draft, `.codex-reviews/d445-review.md` (blocked, see Disclosed); the second draft and its tools, `.codex-reviews/d445-review2.md` (blocked: the droplet script fetched straight into the output directory, several failure cases were undefined, and the script had no test of its own); the third, `.codex-reviews/d445-review3.md` (blocked: a killed runner could erase an observed refusal, publication did not require the teardown's own verdict, and the outcomes written here did not match the script's exit paths); the fourth, `.codex-reviews/d445-review4.md` (the three closed; blocked on the outcomes still not matching the script at its edges: local shard failures, what counts as an attempt, an exit code after publication, a failed attempt that cannot be moved aside); the fifth, `.codex-reviews/d445-review5.md` (blocked on a refusal whose marker could not be written, on `OUT.partial` made in two steps, and on the four states overlapping as written; the states now have an order of precedence and are kept apart from what one run reports); the sixth, `.codex-reviews/d445-review6.md` (blocked on two instants: a kill between observing a refusal and writing its marker, and an interruption just after `OUT.partial` is made; the first is now covered by the fetched log and its remainder is stated as a limit, the second exits 1); the seventh, `.codex-reviews/d445-review7.md`: no code blocker; no path found that publishes without the registered build, the fetched-file checks and a verified cleanup; the 32 saved checks exist and call the real functions; one blocking wording correction, that what a restart recovers is the marker or a refusal line in the locally fetched log and not a refusal seen only in the run's log. It is applied above and in the script's docstring (which changed the script's hash; its 32 tests were run again on the final file). This last wording was not sent back an eighth time.


**D449 - SEARCH DISTILLATION TEST 1 STOPS AT MILESTONE 1: READING 1 IS NOT FIT. THE LAMBDA 16 ARM PUTS 0.605 ON ITS TRAINING LABELS AGAINST THE REGISTERED 0.80; NO MILESTONE 2, NO SELECTION, NO HELD-OUT LOOK, NO GATE; IT SAYS THE RECIPE AS REGISTERED (2,400 STEPS) DID NOT FIT 370 LABELS, AND NOTHING ABOUT TRANSFER OR STRENGTH (2026-10-08 14:29 PDT by the machine's clock at commit)**

**What ran, after D445.**
- **The dataset**, by D445's command: published at 14:14 PDT on the first attempt. The registered build ran on one droplet, one game per forward, and refused nothing: 900 games replayed to their digests, scores and observation hashes; 27,000 root supports rebuilt and equal to the record's; no candidate list reordered; the largest difference of a0's log-probability from the label droplets' record 2.18e-7 against the registered 1e-3. Train 700 games, 65,800 loss decisions, 370 labels; validation 100 games, 9,400, 77; test 100 games, 9,400, 62 (written to `locked/test.pt` and not opened); reserve 100 games, not written. The droplet was destroyed and verified gone, its key gone, 17.2 minutes, about $0.048. Records: `docs/search-distill-2026-10-08/results/m1/dataset/`.
- **The fine-tune**, by the registered command, on the Mac: three arms, 2,400 Adam steps each, all three blobs accepted. (By the operator's record it ran from 14:18 to 14:25; the saved files do not carry the times or the command line.)
- **The fit check**, by `distill_eval.py fit`. The operator ran it once; the saved files cannot show that. It wrote no selection file, and by the records the test split was not deserialised (its bytes were written, fetched and hashed when the dataset was built). Records: `results/m1/finetune/`.

**Reading 1: NOT FIT.** The lambda 16 arm's weighted mean probability of the label on the 370 training deviation roots is **0.605** from float32 logits (0.605 in the float64 training arithmetic); the registered threshold is 0.80. By rule 2 of Reading 1 the plan stops. PLAN.md section 5's table: "R1 does not fit its training labels at this size. No selection, no held-out look, no gate. The test and reserve games stay unopened for a later entry." Milestone 2's 9,000 label games are not played.

**The numbers `fit` printed, none of which is a reading.**

| arm | lambda | training: label probability | training: change elsewhere (total variation, top action changed) | validation: label probability | validation: change elsewhere |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `c55d1l1` | 1 | 0.282 | 0.030, 1.8% | 0.078 | 0.056, 4.8% |
| `c55d1l4` (the registered arm) | 4 | 0.424 | 0.055, 3.6% | 0.114 | 0.084, 7.0% |
| `c55d1l16` | 16 | 0.605 | 0.082, 6.6% | 0.169 | 0.113, 9.8% |

Training: 370 deviation roots and 65,430 other decisions. Validation: 77 deviation roots and 9,323 other decisions, in 100 games the fine-tune did not see. J, the printed diagnostic, is below zero for every arm (-0.0008, -0.0012, -0.0016), as D444 said it would be.

**What it says, and what it does not.**
- It says that this recipe with this step budget did not reach the fit bar on 370 labels. It does not say that the output layer cannot fit them. When the fine-tune stopped it was still moving: over the last 400 steps the lambda 16 arm's distance from the original weights grew from 23.5 to 26.2, about as fast as over the 400 steps before (20.6 to 23.5); the chunk losses it reported at steps 2,000 and 2,400 were 0.51 and 0.31, on chunks that need not be the same; the other two arms' weights were moving likewise. I wrote beforehand (PLAN.md, the operator's expectation) that a NOT FIT would say more about the step budget than about the recipe. The trace shows continued weight movement and no more: whether the same recipe run to convergence would pass 0.80 at lambda 16 was not measured.
- It says nothing about transfer or strength. The validation columns are from 100 games and no rule reads them. They are set down because they are the registered run's first numbers on games the student did not see: at every dose the label's probability on validation deviation roots is well below its training value, and mean total variation and the share of top actions changed are lower on training decisions than on validation decisions.
- **Against what I wrote down.** I gave FIT at milestone 1 about two chances in three. It read NOT FIT.

**What is kept.** The two accepted label shards (1,000 games, 30,000 screened roots, 566 deviation roots each judged on 128 fresh pairs, 64,000 other decisions), the milestone 1 dataset, the three blobs and the tools. The labels are the expensive part and are not tied to this recipe. The test games' file exists and has not been opened; the reserve games were never written.

**Consequences.** As registered: the plan stops, no default changes, nothing is adopted and no recipe is closed. R1 is not closed by this reading: it did not fit at this step budget, and its gate was not played. A further test of search distillation is a new entry with its own registration. This entry decides none. What a follow-up could be, set down without choosing:
- the same recipe with a step budget fixed by a stated convergence rule (the registered fixed-feature loss is convex; convergence and its fit value were not measured);
- an exploratory look at convergence on the training games, which opens nothing;
- a recipe with more of the network trained (PLAN.md section 9's R2);
- nothing further, on the grounds of D444's own odds (Positive about one in ten) and of the rehearsal arms' gate smoke, which is not evidence.

**Why this rung.** Chain 63 is the last stage in the plan and should end at about 05:30 PDT. D451 read chain 62: both rungs from chain 58 (chain 61 at lambda 0.95, chain 62 at 0.97) beat chain 58 head to head, and against the held-out opponents both are below it: chain 62 against chain 37 and chain 46 on its one block; chain 61 against chain 37 on both of its blocks and against chain 46 on the second (on the first that interval contains zero, D447). The rungs of the generation before, from chain 49, were not established below their parent against either (D451 lists the contrasts). Between the two generations two things changed: the parent, and the learned opponents the rung trains against. Rungs from chain 49 trained against the anchor, chain 40 and chain 41 (pool `2ae7448e...`, with chain 49 in the bot's seat). Rungs from chain 58 train against the anchor, chain 41 and chain 49 (pool `59a6703f...`, with chain 58 in the bot's seat): the ladder's rotation dropped chain 40 and made chain 49 an active opponent. D451 says its gate separates neither explanation. This rung is chain 62's rung with the active opponents of the generation before. It tests one intervention, the earlier ordered pool, at one parent, one lambda and one training seed. If the rotation is what cost the held-out strength, this rung should do better than chain 62 against chain 37 and chain 46. That is the prediction tested. A rung that does better would not show that the parent plays no part: a loss that comes with the parent can sit beside a gain from the pool. The rung cannot tell a pool effect from a pool effect that exists only at this parent, and one rung is one training seed.

**The selection D441 requires is not run now.** The candidates standing are chain 60 and no other (D451). Nothing is launched from chain 60, chain 61 or chain 62 by this entry: chain 64 starts from chain 58, the warm start. A selection between chain 60 and chain 58 is left for the entry that next proposes to launch from chain 60, and it stays a condition of any launch from chain 60, chain 61, chain 62, chain 63 or chain 64. D448 wrote that the stage after chain 63 would be the next generation, chosen by that selection once chain 62's gate was read; this entry replaces that intention, for the reasons that follow, and breaks no rule of D441 or D448. **D454 - GATES AND PANELS ARE PLAYED ON THE TRAINING RIG FROM NOW ON, NOT ON DIGITALOCEAN DROPLETS (ALEX, 2026-10-09 01:54 PDT); THE RIG RUNNER `rig_gate.py` IS REGISTERED AFTER FOUR SMOKES IN WHICH THE RIG REPLAYED DROPLET-PLAYED GAMES AND EVERY RECORD MATCHED, ACTION TRAIL INCLUDED; A GATE NOW TAKES ABOUT FOUR HOURS BESIDE TRAINING AND, IN THE SMOKES, SLOWED THE TRAINER BY ABOUT 13 PERCENT WHILE IT PLAYED; THIS AMENDS D448, D452 AND D453 (2026-10-09 06:20 PDT by the machine's clock at commit; chain 64 is training)**

**The instruction.** Alex, 2026-10-09 01:54 PDT, to this session: "we need to move you off any digital ocean droplets and you only use the 2070 machine". By the report of another of his sessions the reason is the account's spend across all projects and a new cap on its droplet count; that report is not checked here. From that message on this work creates no droplet. Three shards of D453's panel were still playing when it arrived (launched 01:08:45); they were left to finish and delete themselves, the last at 02:15, and the droplet listing at 05:47 shows none. The operator's reading of the instruction, stated so it can be corrected: games are played on the rig; the Mac keeps the ledger, the scoring and the reviews, and plays no games.

**What changes.**
- **Machine.** The rig (`bbrig`: Ryzen 7 2700X, 8 cores and 16 threads, 12 GB of memory and 4 GB of swap), which is also training. Gates use its CPU only: the runner installs CPU-only torch in its own environment (`/home/rache/bbgate/venv`, python 3.12.13, torch 2.14.0+cpu, numpy 2.5.3, the droplets' versions of torch and numpy), asserts that CUDA is not available to it, and hides the GPU from the queue.
- **Runner.** `rig_gate.py` (sha256 `ba494088a95c604e7d9475ce3a6f9e922288b28bf4801eddde76f0fb6e3a638a`, `docs/rig-gates-2026-10-09/`, with a test of its own logic, 46 of 46) replaces `launch_from_plan.py` and `tools/droplet_tournament.py run`. It makes no cloud call and deletes nothing. It imports the droplet runner from the harness worktree at the plan's commit and uses its job script, its shim build and machine record, its tournament command line and the whole of its copied-run verification (file hashes, manifest, schedule, integrity counters), pointed at directories under `/home/rache/bbgate/<gate>/`.
- **Start.** Refused unless the plan hashes to the committed value; every gate, shard, player, checkpoint and mask name in it, the keys of its checkpoint table included, is a plain name checked as a whole string (they reach paths and shell lines); the plan registers this `rig_gate.py` by its sha256 as its launch script and the droplet runner by its sha256; both checkouts are clean at their commits; every checkpoint has its registered sha256 (checked on the Mac and again on the rig after upload); no shard has a local directory; the rig has at least 4,000 MB of memory available and 20 GB of disk free at that moment; and the gate's directory on the rig can be created new by one `mkdir`. `rig_start.json` is written beside the plan before anything is prepared or launched. Every command the runner runs on the rig, file transfers included, runs under `nice -n 19` and `ionice -c 3`; the shared environment is made under its own lock. A start that fails is not re-entered: the gate is started again under a new name from a new plan, and no game of the failed start is used.
- **Play.** One detached queue per gate. It first sets its own out-of-memory score to the maximum, which its jobs and workers inherit, so that if the rig runs short of memory the kernel prefers the gate's processes as victims. It then waits for a rig-wide lock, so gates play one at a time, and plays the plan's shards one after another with 6 workers. Each job and its tournament process inherit the lock, so it stays held while either lives even if the queue itself is killed. Nothing stays running on the Mac.
- **Collect.** Refused unless the harness worktree is still clean at the plan's commit and the runner file is the one `start` hashed. Each finished shard is copied to a `.partial` directory, verified as the droplet runner verifies a copied run, and only then renamed to the name a droplet shard would have. A queue that is gone with shards unfinished is reported as a failure, not as still playing.
- **Plan fields.** A plan played this way names the rig as its machine and `rig_gate.py` with its sha256 as its launch script, and records the droplet runner's sha256, which `start` checks. `max_hours` has no meaning on the rig.

**What does not change.** The harness commit and the play code; seeds, pairs, game counts, 32 games per worker, T=1, both legs; the plan's sha256 committed and pushed before any game; `droplet_tournament.py merge`, `tools/gate_acceptance.py`, `accept_from_plan.py`, `score_from_plan.py`, `paired_contrasts.py` and `gate_diagnostics.py`, all byte for byte as before; one scoring pass; every label rule. The gate settings and label rules registered in D448 (chain 63) and D452 (chain 64) stand; their gates are played by this procedure.

**This entry amends D448, D452 and D453.**
- **D452.** Its comparison of chain 64 with chain 62 was registered as one ordered-pool factor under a manifest condition. From here a gate plays beside chain 64 for part of its run (three of the smokes took about thirteen minutes of its time; chain 63's gate will play for about four of its hours), and chain 62 trained with none. That is an added training condition for chain 64 against its control. The trainer's command, seed, step count and manifest are unchanged, and unchanged manifest leaves do not establish unchanged training: the trainer's wall-clock speed and the timing of its threads differ, and whether that can change what it learns is not tested. **So D452's consequences are qualified: an improvement, or its absence, can no longer be laid to the ordered pool alone; the comparison includes this load difference, and chain 64's reading must say so.** Its manifest condition, readings and the rest of its consequences are as registered.
- **D448.** The first smoke played for about three minutes (02:02 to 02:05) while chain 63 trained; chain 62, its control, trained with nothing beside it. The same qualification applies to chain 63 against chain 62, for those three minutes of a run of eight and a half hours. Chain 63's reading names it. D448's gate, labels and consequences are otherwise as registered.
- **D453.** It said the panel used no rig time, which was true of that panel. Any later panel or side experiment is played on the rig through the same queue and waits behind whatever holds the lock.

**Evidence, four smokes of the runner (`docs/rig-gates-2026-10-09/SMOKES.json`). None is a gate and nothing is read from them about strength.** Each replays games of `c62-gate-20261008` that were scored and read in D451: the same pairs, seed block and game indices.
- `rigsmoke-20261009` (plan sha256 `58e52458...`, 02:02 to 02:05 PDT, chain 63 training): 256 games of pair 1 (chain 62 against chain 61) and 64 of pair 11 (both under m1).
- `rigsmoke2-20261009` (plan sha256 `b8664fd5...`, 05:49 to 05:54, chain 64 training): 512 games of pair 1 and 512 of pair 8 (chain 62 against chain 58).
- `rigsmoke3-20261009` (plan sha256 `12b99e09...`, 06:03 to 06:08): 512 games of pair 1 and 256 of pair 11.
- `rigsmoke4-20261009` (plan sha256 `07525962...`, 06:14 to 06:17), **with the runner as registered here**: 256 games of pair 1 and 128 of pair 11. The first two smokes used the runner's first version (sha256 `ac638e4a...`) and the third its second (`e41730af...`); the outside review's corrections lie between them.
- **All 2,496 replayed records (1,280 distinct games) match the droplets' records in every compared field:** 33 fields, among them the action trail's sha256, the final state digest, touchdowns, result, engine steps, decisions, teams, seeds and turns. Not compared as equal: wall time, process id, the recorded log-probability sums (largest difference 0.0005) and the per-game counters, which differ in one masked game in each m1 shard by 0.0001 in a summed probability mass. That is on another CPU, compiler (gcc 15.2 against 13.3), python patch release and compiled shim, and with 6 workers where the droplets had 8, which changes which games share a forward pass. It does not show that no game can ever differ; none of these did.
- **The scripts take rig shards unchanged:** `score_from_plan.py` on the second, third and fourth smokes merged the shards and printed `GATE-ACCEPTED` (1,024, 768 and 384 games) and `MASKS-ACCEPTED` (512 and 256 masked sides in the third and fourth).
- **Speed.** 3.62 games a second on plain games with 6 workers beside the trainer over 512 games, 1.79 on the m1 pair over 256 (by the shard logs of the earlier gates a droplet shard gave 5.3 to 6.8 on plain games, and four or five played at once). By the plain rate chain 63's 44,800 games are 3.4 hours, more with its two pairs against the slower bot and its m1 pair; chain 64's 51,200 are 3.9 hours. "About four hours" is an estimate.
- **Memory.** Summed over the gate's 10 processes, resident memory was 2,157 to 2,160 MB through the third smoke (9 samples) and 2,157 MB in the fourth, with 8.5 to 8.6 GB of the rig's memory still available. Shared pages are counted once per process in that sum.
- **Priority, as observed in the fourth smoke.** All 10 of the gate's processes were at nice 19, I/O class idle and out-of-memory score 1000, and the queue held the lock.
- **Cost to training, over minutes.** Sampled from the watch tool: the trainer ran at 98.7K steps a second before the second smoke (4 samples), 85.9K while it played (21 samples, 77.8K to 94.1K), 99.3K after (3 samples), and 86.0K during the third (9 samples). About 13 percent slower while a smoke played. The slowdown over a whole gate is not measured yet.

**Limits of the new arrangement.**
- About one gate per rung fits. A reading now arrives four to five hours after a rung ends, so the stage after a rung is always registered before that rung is read, as has mostly been the case.
- Priority, the out-of-memory score and the admission check lower the risk to the trainer; none of them guarantees it. The out-of-memory score makes the gate the kernel's preferred victim, not its certain one. The admission check is one reading taken before preparation, with nothing reserved and no second reading when a waiting queue starts to play. None of these is a hard cap on what the gate may use.
- The slowdown over a whole gate is read at the first gate and reported in its entry. If it is above 20 percent, the next gate is started with fewer workers.
- Nothing is resumed. A start that fails before its queue is launched leaves its directory on the rig and is started again under a new gate name from a new plan, committed before launch like any other. A queue that dies after launch is not resumed either: the shards it finished stay collectable, and a new entry decides about the rest. A shard that aborts on the decision cap stays unread, as D448 and D452 register.
- The runner writes under `/home/rache/bbgate`, except for uv's own cache when the environment is first made and the compiler's temporary files. Preparing a second gate while a first plays is possible and uses CPU at the same low priority beside it.
- A shim built in another directory on the rig has another sha256 (four smokes, four hashes). Every shard of one gate uses one build, which is what the merge requires.
- **Known and left as they are, so that the registered bytes are the bytes the fourth smoke ran.** Three strings in the tool say more than is true: `collect`'s message "Nothing more will be played" when the queue is gone (a job inherited from a killed queue may still be running; the right action is to collect again after it exits), the queue script's comment "the trainer is never chosen before it", and a test label "first choice of the out-of-memory killer" (the score makes the gate's processes preferred victims and guarantees no order). The liveness check trusts a process id and does not verify what the process is. A download is held whole in the Mac's memory before it is written. A first installation of the environment that failed halfway would have to be repaired by hand. None of these changes what is played or what is verified.

**Pair 1 has one checkpoint on both sides and is played without a sampling offset.** The harness keys each seat's sampling seed by engine seed and side, so in the two legs of an engine seed the two games are the same game until the first decision at which the mask changes what the masked seat samples. What changes is the dependence between the two legs of a seed and between the two pairs on a seed; the interval resamples whole engine seeds with every pair and both legs, which accounts for that dependence without promising exact 95% coverage, and a run with offsets would not give the identical numbers. **Why the two unfinished shards cannot simply be played and merged with shard 1.** The merge refuses shards that do not share one compiled shim (`tools/droplet_tournament.py`, `merge_shards`: "compiled shim ... differs"). Each start of `rig_gate.py` builds its own shim under the gate's own directory, and the builds do not hash alike: four gates at the same harness commit `7d0d547` recorded four different `library_sha256` values (`132167a9...` chain 63's, `95a3c38a...` chain 64's, `df0e368d...` chain 65's, `976a6dcf...` this first queue's). A new queue rebuilds the shim; if its hash differs, the registered merge refuses its shards beside shard 1. The four observed builds differ, and D454 provides no approved continuation procedure. Running the first queue's jobs again by hand in its own directory is outside D454's procedure (`rig_gate.py`: "A start that fails is not re-entered: the gate is started again under a new name, from a new plan") and would resume a games file that a host death may have left torn.
